It is designed to evaluate text embedding and classification models on real-world, colloquial movie-review language, supporting tasks like sentiment polarity or rating prediction and benchmarking representation quality for downstream supervised classification.

MTEB LCQMC (default) is the Large-scale Chinese Question Matching Corpus configured for the MTEB evaluation. It contains Chinese question pairs labeled for semantic equivalence (paraphrase vs. non-paraphrase) and is used to evaluate sentence embedding models on tasks such as binary semantic matching, semantic textual similarity, and retrieval. The dataset presents realistic lexical and syntactic variation in user queries, making it a focused benchmark for measuring embedding quality and paraphrase detection performance in Chinese.

MTEB MTOPDomainClassification (en) is an English domain-classification subset derived from the MTOP task-oriented parsing corpus and included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It contains user utterances labeled with their high-level task domains (e.g., music, weather, navigation, alarms), enabling evaluation of embedding and classification models on domain identification in task-oriented dialogue. The dataset is suitable for benchmarking semantic representations in supervised, few-shot, and retrieval-style settings where accurate domain-level intent detection is required.

MTEB MTOPDomainClassification (de) is a German-language domain classification subset derived from the MTOP task-oriented parsing corpus, pairing user utterances with domain labels (e.g., travel, music, shopping). It is intended for evaluating sentence-embedding and text-classification models on short, natural conversational queries in German, supporting benchmarking of embedding quality for domain identification, few-shot and supervised classification in NLU applications.

MTEB MTOPDomainClassification (es) is the Spanish domain-classification subset of the MTOP task-oriented dataset formatted for the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains Spanish user utterances labeled with coarse-grained task domains (e.g., music, alarm, navigation), enabling evaluation of sentence embeddings on domain prediction in task-oriented dialogue. The set is useful for benchmarking and comparing multilingual or Spanish embedding models on semantic classification and downstream intent/domain retrieval tasks.

MTEB MTOPDomainClassification (fr) is the French subset of the MTOP domain-classification task included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It consists of French task-oriented user utterances annotated with domain labels (e.g., calendar, messaging, navigation) for single-label domain classification. The set is intended to evaluate sentence and utterance embedding models and classifiers on domain-level intent understanding, cross-lingual transfer, and few-shot generalization for dialogue and intent classification applications in French.

MTOPIntentClassification (en) is the English intent-classification subset of the MTOP dataset as included in MTEB. It contains user utterances labeled with intent categories spanning multiple domains, providing a multi-class intent detection benchmark. The dataset is intended to evaluate sentence embeddings and downstream classifiers on their ability to capture intent semantics for task-oriented dialogue, and is useful for training and benchmarking intent classifiers, few-shot/zero-shot transfer, and embedding-based retrieval in conversational AI.

MTEB MTOPIntentClassification (de) is a German-language intent classification dataset derived from the MTOP corpus and included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It contains user utterances in German annotated with intent labels across multiple task-oriented domains, enabling training and evaluation of intent detection models. The dataset is suited for assessing sentence embedding quality, supervised classifiers, and retrieval-based intent recognition, and for benchmarking multilingual transfer and semantic representation performance on German intent understanding.

MTEB MTOPIntentClassification (es) is a Spanish intent classification dataset derived from the MTOP task-oriented parsing collection. It contains short user utterances across multiple domains annotated with intent labels, enabling supervised training and evaluation of intent classifiers and sentence-embedding models. As part of the MTEB benchmark, it assesses semantic representation quality and downstream performance for Spanish task-oriented language understanding.

MTEB MTOPIntentClassification (fr) is a French-language subset of the MTOP intent classification task included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It contains user utterances in French annotated with intent labels across multiple task-oriented dialogue domains, designed for training and evaluating intent detection and text-embedding models. The dataset supports supervised classification, embedding-based semantic retrieval, and cross-lingual transfer experiments, offering diverse, real-world formulations of user requests to benchmark model robustness in French intent understanding.

MasakhaNEWSClassification (eng) is an English subset of the MasakhaNEWS news-topic classification dataset used in the MTEB benchmark. It contains news articles labeled by topical categories and is intended for supervised training and evaluation of text classifiers and sentence embeddings. The set is suited for benchmarking topical classification accuracy, assessing embedding quality, and studying cross-lingual or domain transfer between English and African-language news domains.

MasakhaNEWSClassification (fra) is the French-language subset of the MasakhaNEWS news-topic classification dataset used in the MTEB benchmark. It contains French news texts paired with topical category labels, enabling supervised training and evaluation of text classification and embedding models. Focused on news content relevant to African contexts, the dataset provides a realistic benchmark for assessing multilingual and French-language models’ ability to capture topical semantics, robustness in low-resource domains, and generalization across news topics.

MasakhaNEWSClusteringP2P (eng) is a benchmark dataset derived from the MasakhaNEWS news corpus, formatted for pairwise clustering evaluation in English. It contains news texts (headlines and short articles) grouped by topical clusters and presented as pairs labeled whether they belong to the same cluster. The dataset is intended to measure the quality of sentence/document embeddings and clustering algorithms on news-domain semantic grouping, supporting evaluation of unsupervised clustering, pairwise similarity, and topic-level retrieval for English-language news content.

MTEB MasakhaNEWSClusteringP2P (fra) is a French-language subset of the MasakhaNEWS corpus formatted for clustering and pairwise evaluation in the MTEB benchmark. It contains French news articles about African current events organized into topical clusters and paired into positive/negative examples to assess semantic similarity. The dataset is intended to evaluate embedding models on article-level clustering, pairwise similarity, and retrieval tasks in a realistic news domain.

MasakhaNEWSClusteringS2S (eng) is the English subset of the MasakhaNEWS clustering task in MTEB, consisting of news articles annotated with topic cluster labels and provided in a sequence-to-sequence format. It is designed to evaluate embedding, sequence-to-sequence, and clustering methods on short-to-medium length news texts, measuring a model’s ability to group semantically related items. The dataset is useful for benchmarking clustering quality and for studying cross-lingual transfer and robustness on news-domain content originating from African-language collections.

MasakhaNEWSClusteringS2S (fra) is a French subset of the MasakhaNEWS clustering sequence-to-sequence task in the MTEB benchmark. It contains French news texts organized into semantic clusters with representative cluster-level targets, designed to evaluate embedding models’ ability to group similar news items and produce or select representative cluster summaries. The dataset supports benchmarking of clustering quality and cluster-aware sequence-to-sequence generation in a multilingual, news-domain setting, useful for assessing model performance in downstream tasks like topic grouping and cluster summarization.

MTEB MassiveIntentClassification (pl) is a Polish-language intent classification dataset from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains user utterances labeled with a large, diverse set of intent categories to evaluate models’ ability to map short queries to semantic intent classes. The dataset is intended for benchmarking and training sentence- and embedding-based classifiers (including few-shot and zero-shot evaluations) to assess semantic representation quality on practical intent-detection tasks in Polish.

MTEB MassiveIntentClassification (de) is a German-language dataset of short user utterances annotated with intent labels, curated for intent classification benchmarking within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It enables evaluation of sentence embeddings and downstream classifiers on intent detection, clustering, and semantic retrieval in German, providing diverse, domain-spanning queries and standardized labels to assess model discrimination of user intents and robustness to linguistic variation.

MTEB MassiveIntentClassification (es) is a Spanish intent-classification dataset of short user utterances paired with intent labels, part of the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It provides a large, diverse set of text–label pairs spanning many intent categories to evaluate and train text-embedding and classification models for intent detection in Spanish-language conversational and search applications. The dataset is suitable for supervised, few-shot, and zero-shot evaluation of embedding quality, semantic retrieval, and downstream intent classification performance.

MassiveIntentClassification (ru) is a Russian-language intent classification dataset in the MTEB benchmark containing user utterances annotated with intent labels across a large and diverse set of intent categories. It is designed to evaluate text-embedding and classification models on their ability to distinguish fine-grained user intents in Russian conversational queries, supporting multi-class classification and benchmarking downstream intent-detection performance.

MTEB MassiveIntentClassification (en) is a large-scale English intent classification dataset from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains thousands of short user utterances labeled with fine-grained intent categories across diverse domains, designed to evaluate embedding and classifier performance on many-way intent detection. The dataset emphasizes short-text semantics, class imbalance, and cross-domain generalization, and is suited for benchmarking and training embedding-based intent classifiers, few-shot evaluation, and retrieval-style intent matching.

MTEB MassiveIntentClassification (fr) is a French intent classification dataset comprising short user utterances labeled with intent categories across diverse domains. It is designed to evaluate and train sentence embedding and intent-detection models on multi-class classification and retrieval tasks in French, measuring how well representations separate and group semantically equivalent intents. The dataset is suitable for supervised, few-shot, and zero-shot evaluation of embedding quality, intent classifiers, and downstream dialogue or NLU systems.

MTEB MassiveIntentClassification (zh-CN) is a large-scale Simplified Chinese dataset of short user utterances labeled with many fine-grained intent categories. It is designed to evaluate and train text embedding and intent-classification models on real-world conversational and query data, challenging models to discriminate closely related intents. The dataset is suitable for supervised classification, few-shot evaluation, and benchmarking embedding-based retrieval and clustering for Chinese intent detection.

MTEB MassiveScenarioClassification (zh-CN) is a Chinese-language benchmark dataset for evaluating text embeddings on diverse scenario-level classification tasks. It contains short texts labeled with scenario or intent categories spanning many real-world domains, enabling assessment of embedding models’ ability to separate and generalize across varied semantic classes. The dataset is suitable for benchmarking zero-/few-shot and supervised embedding-based classifiers, and for evaluating downstream tasks such as semantic search and clustering in Mandarin Chinese.

MTEB MassiveScenarioClassification (pl) is a Polish-language classification dataset designed to evaluate text embedding models on a large, multi-scenario categorization task. It comprises short Polish texts labeled across many real-world scenarios and topics, enabling assessment of semantic representations for downstream classification. The dataset is suitable for benchmarking and fine-tuning embedding-based classifiers, measuring generalization across diverse domains, and comparing performance in supervised and few-shot settings for Polish NLP.

MTEB MassiveScenarioClassification (es) is a Spanish-language benchmark for scenario classification that pairs short texts with labeled scenario categories spanning diverse domains. It is intended to evaluate and compare text embedding and classification models on their ability to distinguish contexts and intents in Spanish content. The dataset is suited for supervised and embedding-based evaluation workflows, including few-shot and transfer settings, and helps assess model robustness across varied real-world scenarios.

MTEB MassiveScenarioClassification (de) is a German-language benchmark for multi-class scenario classification, containing short texts annotated with scenario/category labels. Included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB), it is designed to evaluate the quality of sentence and document embeddings and the performance of downstream classifiers on semantic scenario discrimination in German. The dataset supports training and evaluation of embedding models, supervised classifiers, and cross-lingual transfer approaches on realistic scenario-labeling tasks.

MassiveScenarioClassification (en) is an English-language, large-scale scenario classification dataset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It contains diverse text examples annotated with scenario/category labels across many domains, designed to evaluate the quality of text embeddings and downstream classifiers on broad, multiclass scenario recognition. The dataset emphasizes scalability, label variety, and cross-domain generalization and is suitable for training and benchmarking embedding models and classification pipelines using metrics like accuracy and F1.

MTEB MassiveScenarioClassification (fr) est un jeu de données d’évaluation pour la classification de scénarios en français, intégré au Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. Il propose des textes français annotés par scénario couvrant une grande diversité de domaines et de granularités de labels, afin de tester la qualité et la généralisation des représentations textuelles. Le corpus sert à comparer et sélectionner des modèles d’embeddings et de classificateurs en configurations supervisées, peu‑données ou de transfert, pour des tâches pratiques de catégorisation de situations et d’intentions.

MTEB MassiveScenarioClassification (ru) is a Russian-language dataset of short user utterances annotated with scenario/intention labels, curated for evaluating sentence-embedding models on scenario/classification tasks. It enables supervised training and benchmark evaluation of classifiers and embedding-based methods for intent or scenario recognition, clustering, and semantic retrieval in Russian. As part of the MTEB suite, it assesses model ability to produce representations that separate real-world scenario categories and supports research on multilingual and cross-lingual transfer for dialogue and intent understanding.

MTEB MintakaRetrieval (fr) is a French-language retrieval dataset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark designed to evaluate embedding-based semantic search and retrieval models. It provides French queries paired with candidate passages or documents and relevance labels, covering varied topics to test cross-domain generalization. The dataset is intended for benchmarking retrieval metrics (e.g., recall@k, MRR) and for training or evaluating embeddings and dense retrieval systems on French semantic search tasks.

MTEB MultilingualSentiment is a multilingual sentiment classification dataset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It contains short texts across multiple languages annotated with sentiment labels (e.g., positive, negative, neutral) to evaluate the ability of sentence and text embeddings to capture sentiment information. The dataset is intended for benchmarking multilingual embedding models on supervised and transfer/zero-shot sentiment detection, enabling comparison of cross-lingual generalization and downstream classification performance.

MTEB OnlineShopping (default) is an e-commerce short-text dataset of product titles paired with category labels, designed to evaluate text embedding models on semantic classification, clustering, and retrieval tasks. It provides concise, real-world product descriptions typical of online shopping queries, enabling benchmarking of embedding quality for category prediction, product clustering, and similarity-based search.

MTEB PAC (default) is a default task suite within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that evaluates text embeddings on pairwise comparison problems. It comprises labeled text pairs across diverse domains to assess models’ ability to capture semantic similarity, paraphrase, and relatedness. The suite is intended for benchmarking embedding quality in classification, ranking and retrieval scenarios, emphasizing robustness and cross-domain generalization.

MTEB PAWSX (default) is a multilingual paraphrase identification dataset derived from PAWS, containing sentence pairs in multiple languages (e.g., English, Spanish, German, French, Chinese, Japanese, Korean) labeled as paraphrase or non-paraphrase. It includes adversarial examples with high lexical overlap but altered word order or meaning, making it a strong test of semantic understanding beyond surface similarity. The dataset is used in MTEB to evaluate multilingual sentence embeddings and models on paraphrase detection, cross-lingual transfer, and robustness to lexical and syntactic perturbations.

PolEmo2.0-IN is a Polish-language sentiment analysis dataset comprising product reviews (the in-domain split of PolEmo2.0) annotated with sentiment polarity labels (positive, negative, neutral). It contains sentence- and review-level opinion texts collected from e-commerce sources and is used in MTEB to evaluate embedding models on sentiment classification and the ability to capture subjective, domain-specific language in Polish.

MTEB PolEmo2.0-OUT (default) is a Polish sentiment dataset drawn from the PolEmo2.0 corpus containing product and service reviews annotated with sentiment polarity (positive, negative, neutral). As the OUT subset (non-restaurant domain), it covers diverse product categories and is used in MTEB to evaluate sentence and document embeddings on sentiment classification and retrieval tasks, measuring models’ ability to capture opinion semantics and generalize across domains.

MTEB RUParaPhraserSTS (default) is a Russian-language semantic textual similarity and paraphrase dataset used within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains pairs of Russian sentences annotated with similarity/paraphrase labels or continuous similarity scores, enabling quantitative evaluation of embedding models on paraphrase detection and STS tasks. Designed for assessing semantic alignment, it is commonly used to benchmark sentence and multilingual embeddings via cosine similarity, retrieval, clustering, and correlation metrics, helping compare model performance on Russian paraphrase understanding and semantic matching.

MTEB RuReviewsClassification (default) is a Russian-language review classification dataset from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains user reviews of products and services in Russian paired with sentiment labels (typically positive, negative, and neutral) for supervised classification. The split labeled “default” provides a standard train/validation/test partition for benchmarking. It is intended to evaluate text embeddings and sentence-level classifiers for sentiment detection and semantic representation quality in Russian.

RuSTSBenchmarkSTS is a Russian semantic textual similarity (STS) dataset included in the MTEB suite. It provides Russian sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores to evaluate how well sentence embeddings capture semantic closeness. The split and annotations support benchmarking and comparison of embedding models on Russian-language STS using standard correlation metrics.

MTEB RuSciBenchGRNTIClassification (default) is a benchmark dataset for classifying Russian scientific texts into GRNTI (state rubricator) subject categories. It pairs Russian scientific documents (titles/abstracts) with GRNTI labels, enabling evaluation of text embeddings and classifiers on domain-specific topic categorization and hierarchical label mapping. The dataset is intended for assessing model performance on Russian scientific NLP tasks such as topic classification, label prediction, and semantic representation quality.

MTEB RuSciBenchOECDClassification (default) is a labeled dataset of Russian scientific texts annotated with OECD Fields of Science and Technology categories. It is designed to train and evaluate text-embedding models and classifiers on domain-specific, multilingual (Russian) subject classification tasks, supporting multiclass discipline labeling, metadata enrichment, and assessment of embedding quality for scientific-document retrieval and categorization.

SICK-R (default in MTEB) is the semantic relatedness split of the SICK dataset: English sentence pairs annotated with graded relatedness scores that quantify how semantically similar or related the sentences are. Designed for regression, it evaluates sentence and text embeddings on their ability to capture fine-grained semantic similarity and compositional meaning; models are typically judged by correlation (Pearson/Spearman) between predicted and human scores. The dataset’s lexical and structural variation makes it a compact, challenging benchmark for semantic textual similarity and embedding generalization.

SICK-R-PL is the Polish-language variant of the SICK semantic relatedness dataset used in MTEB. It contains Polish sentence pairs annotated with continuous human relatedness scores (typically 1–5) and is intended for semantic textual similarity/regression evaluation. In MTEB it is used to assess sentence embeddings by correlating embedding-based similarities (e.g., cosine) with human judgments (Spearman/Pearson), measuring how well embeddings capture fine-grained semantic relatedness.

MTEB SICKFr (default) is the French adaptation of the SICK sentence-pair dataset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains French sentence pairs annotated with semantic relatedness scores and entailment labels, enabling evaluation of sentence embeddings on semantic textual similarity (STS) and natural language inference (NLI) tasks. It is suited for benchmarking multilingual and cross-lingual embedding models, measuring their ability to capture fine-grained semantic similarity and inference relations.

MTEB STS12 (default) is a semantic textual similarity benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores, used to evaluate how well embeddings capture fine-grained semantic relatedness. Covering diverse domains (e.g., news, forums, headlines), it is typically evaluated with correlation metrics (Spearman/Pearson) against human judgments to compare and benchmark embedding models.

MTEB STS13 (default) is the SemEval 2013 Semantic Textual Similarity subset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It consists of sentence pairs annotated with continuous similarity scores reflecting human judgments of semantic equivalence. The split and evaluation follow MTEB defaults, making it suitable for assessing embedding quality via correlation metrics (e.g., Spearman/Pearson) and for benchmarking models on fine-grained semantic similarity, retrieval, and clustering tasks.

MTEB STS14 (default) is the STS-2014 subset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, consisting of sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores across diverse domains (news, headlines, captions, forums). It is used to evaluate sentence and text-pair embedding models by measuring how well embedding-based similarity (e.g., cosine) correlates with human judgments (Spearman/Pearson). The task provides a standardized, multi-domain benchmark for semantic textual similarity performance.

MTEB STS15 (default) is the SemEval 2015 Semantic Textual Similarity subset incorporated into the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains sentence pairs annotated with graded human similarity scores and is used to evaluate sentence- and sentence-pair embedding models. Under the default MTEB setup it uses the standard STS15 splits and scores models by correlation (Pearson/Spearman) between predicted similarities and human judgments, providing a fine-grained measure of semantic representation quality across diverse domains.

MTEB STS16 (default) is the Semantic Textual Similarity 2016 subset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains English sentence pairs with continuous human-annotated similarity scores (typically 0–5) and is used to evaluate sentence embedding quality by measuring how well embedding-based similarity correlates with human judgments (e.g., Pearson/Spearman). It serves as a standard benchmark for sentence-level semantic similarity tasks in MTEB.

MTEB QBQTC (default) is a subset of the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that evaluates how well sentence embeddings capture topical similarity for short questions and queries. It comprises user questions paired with topic labels (and optionally query pairs), using a default train/validation/test split to support supervised, few-shot, and zero-shot evaluation. Common uses include topic classification, nearest-neighbor retrieval, and clustering to measure embedding quality on question-level topical coherence and retrieval accuracy.

MTEB STSB (default) is the Semantic Textual Similarity Benchmark task from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains human-annotated sentence pairs with graded similarity scores (originally 0–5) drawn from multiple domains, and provides standard train/validation/test splits. It is used to evaluate sentence- and sentence-pair embedding models by comparing embedding-based similarity (e.g., cosine) to human judgments using correlation metrics (Spearman/Pearson), serving as a core benchmark for semantic alignment and regression/ranking performance.

MTEB STSBenchmark (default) is the Semantic Textual Similarity (STS) Benchmark included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It contains English sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores and is used to evaluate the quality of sentence/text embeddings by measuring correlation (e.g., Pearson/Spearman) between model-computed similarity and human judgments. The task provides a standard, language-focused benchmark for assessing embedding models on semantic similarity and related retrieval or clustering applications.

MTEB STSBenchmarkMultilingualSTS (de) is a German semantic textual similarity (STS) benchmark combining STSBenchmark and MultilingualSTS data. It contains German sentence pairs labeled with human similarity scores, enabling evaluation of sentence- and text-embedding models on semantic similarity, retrieval, and clustering tasks. The dataset covers varied domains and paraphrase/translation scenarios, making it useful for assessing embedding quality and cross-model comparability on German STS tasks.

STSBenchmarkMultilingualSTS (zh) is the Chinese subset of the STS Benchmark within MTEB, comprising Chinese sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores (typically on a 0–5 scale). It is designed to evaluate sentence and text embedding models on semantic textual similarity, measuring how well embeddings capture graded semantic relatedness across diverse domains. Common evaluation metrics are Pearson/Spearman correlation between predicted and gold scores, making the dataset suitable for benchmarking and fine-tuning multilingual or Chinese-specific embedding models.

MTEB STSBenchmarkMultilingualSTS (pl) is the Polish subset of the Semantic Textual Similarity benchmarks used in the MTEB suite. It consists of Polish sentence pairs with human-annotated similarity scores (typically on a 0–5 scale) and is designed to evaluate multilingual sentence and text embeddings on semantic relatedness. Commonly used evaluation metrics are Pearson/Spearman correlation and ranking measures, making the dataset suitable for benchmarking and comparing embedding models’ ability to capture fine-grained semantic similarity in Polish.

MTEB STSBenchmarkMultilingualSTS (es) is the Spanish subset of the STS (Semantic Textual Similarity) collection within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains Spanish sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores (typically on a 0–5 scale) and is intended for evaluating sentence/text embeddings on semantic similarity. The dataset is used to benchmark embedding quality for tasks such as correlation-based STS evaluation, retrieval, clustering, and cross-lingual transfer in Spanish.

MTEB STSBenchmarkMultilingualSTS (ru) is the Russian subset of the Multilingual STS Benchmark within the MTEB suite. It consists of Russian sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores for evaluating semantic textual similarity and sentence embedding quality. The set is intended to benchmark multilingual and monolingual embedding models on their ability to capture fine-grained semantic relatedness, supporting evaluation with correlation metrics (Pearson/Spearman), ranking, and downstream retrieval or clustering tasks.

MTEB SummEval (default) is a summarization evaluation subset within the Massive Text Embeddings Benchmark containing source articles, system-generated and reference summaries, and human quality judgments (coherence, consistency, fluency, relevance). Ratings are provided on a fine-grained scale, enabling evaluation of embedding models and automatic metrics against human assessments. It is intended for benchmarking embedding-based summary comparison, quality estimation, and semantic similarity methods in summarization tasks.

MTEB SummEvalFr (default) is a French summarization evaluation dataset derived from SummEval, containing document–summary pairs with human quality annotations (e.g., coherence, consistency, fluency, relevance). It is designed for evaluating summarization systems and embedding-based metrics in French, enabling comparison of model-generated summaries to human judgments and supporting development of automatic evaluation and quality-prediction methods.

MTEB TNews (default) is a short-form Chinese news dataset used within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark to evaluate text embeddings on topic discrimination, retrieval, and clustering. It contains brief news headlines or short articles paired with topical labels, making it suitable for assessing semantic representation quality on concise, domain-specific texts. TNews is commonly used to benchmark models' ability to capture fine-grained topic signals and support classification and semantic-search tasks in Chinese.

MTEB ToxicConversationsClassification (default) is a conversational toxicity classification dataset in the Massive Text Embeddings Benchmark. It contains short multi-turn dialogues annotated for toxic or abusive content and is designed to evaluate and train text-embedding and classification models that detect harmful language in conversational context. The dataset is useful for benchmarking embedding quality and downstream tasks such as content moderation, safety filtering, and building more robust conversational agents.

MTEB TweetSentimentExtractionClassification (default) is a benchmark dataset of tweets annotated with sentiment labels (positive, negative, neutral) and corresponding sentiment-bearing spans (selected_text). It supports both sentiment classification and span extraction tasks, enabling evaluation of models that predict overall tweet sentiment and identify the exact text segment expressing that sentiment. The dataset is targeted at embedding-based and sequence-labeling approaches for social media sentiment analysis, offering noisy, short-text examples representative of real-world Twitter language.

MTEB Waimai (default) is a Chinese-domain benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) comprising short, user-generated texts from the food-delivery (waimai) domain—such as menu items, product titles, and brief reviews. It is designed to evaluate text embedding models on tasks like semantic search, clustering, and classification in a domain with colloquial language, abbreviations, and domain-specific vocabulary. The dataset stresses models’ ability to capture fine-grained semantic distinctions in short, noisy Chinese texts, making it useful for benchmarking embeddings for retrieval, recommendation, and downstream tasks in local-language service platforms.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (fr) is a French-language retrieval benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark designed to evaluate sentence- and passage-embedding models on question-answer retrieval. It provides French queries (questions) and a collection of candidate passages or QA pairs with ground-truth relevance labels for supervised evaluation. The task measures semantic search and ranking quality (e.g., Recall@k, MRR, nDCG), assessing an embedding model’s ability to retrieve correct answers or relevant passages in French and to support downstream QA and information-retrieval applications.

AmazonPolarityClassification is a large-scale binary sentiment classification dataset derived from Amazon product reviews. Each example pairs review text (title and/or body) with a positive or negative polarity label across diverse product categories. It is used to train and evaluate text-embedding and classification models on sentiment detection and cross-domain generalization.

ArguAna is a dataset of short arguments and claims extracted from online debate forums, annotated with topic and stance information and linked to semantically similar or paraphrased claims. Included in MTEB to evaluate embeddings on argument retrieval, semantic similarity, and clustering, it tests a model’s ability to group semantically equivalent claims and discriminate opposing stances in opinionated text. ArguAna is useful for benchmarking embedding quality in argumentative and opinion mining applications such as semantic search and claim clustering.

ArxivClusteringP2P is a benchmark dataset of arXiv paper texts curated for evaluating embedding models on pairwise clustering and similarity tasks. It contains paper titles and abstracts (paper-to-paper pairs) labeled by whether the two papers share the same arXiv subject category, enabling evaluation of embeddings for semantic clustering, nearest-neighbor retrieval, and pairwise similarity classification. Designed for the MTEB suite, the dataset measures an embedding model’s ability to group related scientific documents and separate distinct research topics in an unsupervised or weakly supervised setting.

ArxivClusteringS2S is a clustering benchmark from the MTEB suite built from arXiv scientific texts, using short textual units (titles and/or abstracts) grouped by subject categories. It evaluates embedding models’ ability to recover topical clusters and separate scientific disciplines in an unsupervised setting. The dataset is used to assess semantic quality of sentence/document embeddings for topic discovery and clustering metrics (e.g., NMI, ARI).

MTEB AskUbuntuDupQuestions is a duplicate-question detection dataset drawn from the Ask Ubuntu Stack Exchange, containing pairs of user questions labeled as duplicates or non-duplicates. It targets semantic similarity and near-duplicate retrieval tasks in a technical Q&A domain, enabling evaluation of sentence and passage embeddings for duplicate detection, clustering, and semantic search. The dataset is useful for benchmarking embedding models on domain-specific paraphrase/duplication detection and improving retrieval or reranking systems for technical help forums.

MTEB Banking77Classification is a fine-grained intent classification dataset of ~13k English customer-service queries labeled with 77 banking-related intents. It provides diverse, realistic user phrasings for evaluating sentence embeddings and classifiers on domain-specific intent detection tasks, measuring embedding quality and downstream classification accuracy in a challenging, fine-grained setting.

MTEB BiorxivClusteringP2P is a biomedical clustering dataset built from bioRxiv preprints, providing paper text (titles/abstracts) with pairwise labels indicating whether two papers belong to the same topical cluster. It is designed to evaluate embedding models on paper-to-paper semantic similarity, clustering and retrieval in a specialized scientific domain. The dataset tests models’ ability to capture fine-grained topical structure in biomedical literature and is useful for benchmarking embeddings for literature organization, semantic search, and topic discovery.

MTEB BiorxivClusteringS2S is a benchmark of bioRxiv preprints organized into topical clusters for evaluating representation and clustering quality in a sequence-to-sequence (S2S) context. Items consist of document-level texts (title and/or abstract) with cluster labels, enabling assessment of embedding methods, S2S encoders, and generative models on scientific-language grouping tasks. It targets evaluation of semantic clustering, topic coherence, and downstream retrieval or classification in the biomedical preprint domain.

MTEB CQADupStackAndroidRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark drawn from the CQADupStack Android forum, containing Android-related questions and labeled duplicate relationships. It is intended for evaluating dense retrieval and embedding models on semantic question matching and duplicate detection: given a query question, systems must rank semantically equivalent or duplicate posts higher than non-duplicates. The split supports evaluation of embedding quality for information retrieval, semantic search, and community question-answering applications within the Android domain.

MTEB CQADupStackEnglishRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark derived from the CQADupStack collection of English StackExchange question threads, focused on duplicate-question detection and semantic search. It provides queries paired with candidate question posts across multiple StackExchange communities (e.g., programming, server administration, web development), enabling evaluation of embedding models on recall/ranking metrics for cross-domain, technical and conversational Q&A content. The dataset is designed to test semantic retrieval quality, duplicate identification, and generalization of text representations in real-world forum-style language.

MTEB CQADupstackGamingRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark drawn from the CQADupStack Gaming subset (StackExchange). It contains gaming-related question posts with labeled duplicate or near-duplicate relationships, enabling evaluation of semantic search, dense retrieval, and embedding models. The dataset tests model ability to match user queries to semantically equivalent community QA posts in a domain-specific setting with gaming terminology and colloquial language.

MTEB CQADupstackGisRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark derived from the CQADupStack collection for the GIS StackExchange community. It provides user questions (titles and bodies) as queries and a corpus of candidate questions annotated for duplicate relationships, enabling evaluation of embedding models on semantic retrieval and duplicate-question detection. The set tests an embedding model’s ability to retrieve semantically equivalent QA items despite lexical and stylistic variation in real community QA data.

MTEB CQADupstackMathematicaRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark derived from the CQADupStack Mathematica subset of Stack Exchange. It contains user questions as queries and a corpus of prior questions with annotated duplicate/relevant links, enabling evaluation of semantic search and duplicate-question retrieval. Designed for embedding and retrieval models, it tests the ability to capture technical, math-focused Q&A semantics and rank semantically equivalent or duplicate questions.

CQADupStackPhysicsRetrieval is a retrieval-style subset of the CQADupStack corpus (from Physics Stack Exchange) used in the MTEB benchmark. It contains real user questions (titles and bodies) with annotations identifying duplicate or related question pairs, enabling evaluation of semantic search and duplicate-detection via embeddings. The dataset is suited for benchmarking retrieval, semantic similarity, and clustering performance in a technical, domain-specific QA setting.

MTEB CQADupstackProgrammersRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark built from the CQADupStack "Programmers" (Software Engineering) forum, containing real Stack Exchange questions and labeled duplicate relationships. It provides query questions with candidate pools and relevance labels for duplicate detection, enabling evaluation of semantic search and dense embedding retrieval models. The data emphasizes short, technical, and paraphrased programming-related language, making it useful for measuring embedding quality on domain-specific question matching and ranking tasks.

MTEB CQADupStackRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark derived from the CQADupStack collection of Stack Exchange question threads. It contains user questions from multiple technical and community forums with labeled duplicate relationships, organized as queries and candidate pools for evaluating semantic search and duplicate detection. The dataset is used within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) to assess embedding models’ ability to retrieve semantically equivalent questions across diverse domains and to measure performance on real-world question-answering and duplicate-finding retrieval tasks.

MTEB CQADupstackStatsRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark derived from the CQADupStack corpus, focusing on the Statistics (Stats) StackExchange community. It contains real user questions as queries and a pool of candidate questions with relevance annotations indicating duplicate or semantically equivalent posts. The dataset is intended to evaluate embedding- and retrieval-based models on semantic similarity and duplicate detection in a technical Q&A domain, measuring how well representations retrieve relevant, semantically matching questions. It is useful for benchmarking dense and sparse retrieval, reranking, and retrieval-oriented embedding methods in a specialized, domain-specific context.

MTEB CQADupStackTexRetrieval is a text-retrieval benchmark derived from the CQADupStack collection of Stack Exchange forums. It contains question posts (titles and optional bodies) from multiple community Q&A domains, with annotated duplicate/related pairs that serve as relevance labels. The dataset is designed to evaluate embedding and retrieval models on semantically matching or duplicate-question retrieval, measuring how well models rank relevant question instances for a given query in real-world QA forums.

MTEB CQADupstackUnixRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark built from Unix Stack Exchange question threads (titles and bodies) with labeled duplicate relationships. It evaluates semantic search and duplicate-question retrieval by testing how well embeddings retrieve known duplicates (metrics like recall@k and MRR). The dataset emphasizes domain-specific technical language and paraphrasing, making it useful for benchmarking and improving sentence- and document-level embedding models for forum question retrieval and duplicate detection.

MTEB CQADupStackWebmastersRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark drawn from the CQADupStack collection for the Webmasters Stack Exchange community. It provides real user questions as queries and a corpus of Webmasters posts with relevance labels indicating duplicate or related questions. The set is intended to evaluate embedding-based semantic retrieval and duplicate-question detection in the web administration/SEO domain, testing models’ ability to match semantically equivalent or closely related forum posts.

MTEB CQADupStackWordpressRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark drawn from the CQADupStack WordPress forum, containing real-world Q&A threads with annotated duplicate relationships. Each item includes question titles and bodies (and associated thread metadata) with links to duplicate or related threads, enabling construction of query–relevant document pairs. It is intended to evaluate semantic retrieval and duplicate-detection performance of embedding and ranking models on conversational, technical forum content and to assess generalization of retrieval systems to real user question–answer forums.

ClimateFEVER is a climate-focused fact verification dataset containing real-world climate and environmental claims paired with candidate evidence sentences and veracity labels (e.g., supported, refuted, or not enough information). It is included in MTEB to benchmark embedding models on retrieval and semantic matching tasks in a domain where precise factual grounding matters. The dataset is useful for evaluating semantic search, dense retrieval, clustering, and downstream fact-checking robustness against climate misinformation.

MTEB DBPedia is a labeled text dataset derived from the DBpedia ontology, consisting of short Wikipedia article summaries mapped to topical classes. Included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, it is used to evaluate embedding models on multiclass classification, retrieval, and clustering tasks by testing how well representations separate knowledge-rich, topic-driven texts. The dataset provides a realistic benchmark for assessing semantic discrimination and topic-level generalization of text encoders.

MTEB EmotionClassification is a labeled dataset of short texts annotated with emotion categories, designed to evaluate the ability of text embeddings to capture affective content. It contains diverse, real-world utterances (e.g., social media posts, comments) labeled with discrete emotions (such as joy, sadness, anger, fear) and is used to benchmark embedding models on downstream emotion classification tasks. The dataset supports supervised classification and embedding-based evaluation, helping assess representation quality for emotion detection, sentiment analysis, and affect-aware NLP applications.

MTEB FEVER is the FEVER fact verification dataset adapted for the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains claims paired with candidate evidence sentences drawn from Wikipedia and annotations indicating whether the evidence Supports, Refutes, or provides NotEnoughInfo for each claim. The task evaluates embedding models on evidence retrieval, similarity-based ranking, and claim verification, measuring how well representations capture factual consistency and semantic matching between claims and supporting or contradicting text. It is suited for benchmarking retrieval, reranking, and supervised verification pipelines that require robust factual and contextual understanding.

FiQA2018 is a finance-domain sentiment benchmark from the FiQA 2018 shared task containing short financial texts (e.g., headlines, microtexts) annotated with fine‑grained continuous sentiment scores and aspect labels. In MTEB it is used as a regression-style evaluation to measure how well text embeddings capture nuanced, domain-specific sentiment and aspect polarity, supporting development of models for financial sentiment analysis and downstream finance applications.

MTEB HotpotQA is a retrieval-focused subset of the HotpotQA challenge formatted for the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It consists of multi-hop questions paired with supporting paragraphs (positives) amid many distractor passages, requiring models to retrieve and aggregate evidence across documents. The dataset evaluates embedding and retrieval models on passage ranking, multi-document reasoning, and robustness to distractors, making it useful for developing dense retrieval, reranking, and QA pipelines that must handle cross-document inference.

MTEB ImdbClassification is a binary sentiment classification dataset of movie reviews used in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark to evaluate text embeddings on downstream classification. It contains long-form user reviews labeled positive or negative (commonly 50k examples split into train and test) and tests how well fixed embeddings support simple classifiers (e.g., logistic regression) for sentiment detection in a movie-review domain.

MTEB MSMARCO is the MS MARCO passage retrieval subset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It pairs real anonymized user queries with web passages and human relevance judgments to create a large-scale, realistic retrieval and ranking task. The split is used to evaluate embedding models on dense retrieval and semantic search, typically measured with metrics like MRR, recall, and nDCG, making it a standard benchmark for assessing embedding quality and generalization in information retrieval.

MedrxivClusteringP2P is an MTEB clustering dataset built from medRxiv preprints to evaluate embedding models on biomedical scientific text. Each instance is a paper (title and/or abstract) and items are grouped into clusters of related papers (paper-to-paper relationships), providing a realistic domain-specific clustering benchmark. It tests an embedding model’s ability to capture fine-grained topical and semantic similarity in biomedical literature, useful for assessing clustering quality (e.g., NMI/ARI) and downstream tasks like literature discovery and grouping.

MedrxivClusteringS2S is a biomedical clustering dataset from the MTEB suite, built from MedRxiv preprints to evaluate sentence- and document-level embedding models on clustering and similarity tasks. It groups abstracts or text segments into topical clusters with ground-truth cluster labels, enabling assessment of representation quality for medical-topic separation, unsupervised organization, and retrieval in the biomedical domain. The dataset is useful for benchmarking embedding models’ ability to capture domain-specific semantics and discriminate closely related medical concepts.

MTEB MindSmallReranking is a small-scale reranking benchmark derived from the MIND news dataset, designed to evaluate embedding-based ranking models. Each example contains a query (typically a user-news interaction or short text) and a set of candidate news articles with relevance annotations (positive and negative labels or graded relevance). The dataset is intended for training and testing reranking and learning-to-rank approaches, supporting evaluation with standard ranking metrics (e.g., MRR, nDCG) and tasks such as pairwise/triplet supervision and supervised reranking of retrieval results.

NFCorpus is a textual dataset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) for evaluating semantic embeddings on retrieval and relevance tasks. It comprises a collection of documents paired with relevance annotations (queries or labels) that enable assessment of nearest-neighbor retrieval, ranking, and semantic matching performance. NFCorpus is intended to benchmark embedding models on real-world retrieval scenarios, supporting comparisons of representation quality, search effectiveness, and generalization across semantic similarity and information retrieval tasks.

MTEB NQ is the Natural Questions subset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, containing real user questions paired with relevant Wikipedia passages. It is used to evaluate embedding and retrieval models by measuring how well vector representations rank passages that contain correct answers. The dataset is suited for benchmarking dense retrieval, open-domain QA, and embedding-based search performance.

MTEB QuoraRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark derived from the Quora question-pairs dataset. Each example gives a query question and a corpus of candidate questions with labeled duplicates (semantically equivalent questions), enabling evaluation of embedding models on semantic search and duplicate detection. It measures how well representations retrieve equivalent questions from a candidate set and is useful for benchmarking embeddings for question deduplication, semantic retrieval, and QA‑retrieval pipelines.

RedditClustering (MTEB) is a benchmark dataset of Reddit posts/comments grouped into cluster labels derived from discussion threads or topical groupings. It contains short, informal social-media texts paired with cluster IDs to evaluate the quality of text embeddings for unsupervised clustering and topic grouping. Designed to test embedding models and clustering pipelines using metrics like ARI or NMI, the dataset challenges models with colloquial language, abbreviations, and diverse, real-world topics common on Reddit.

MTEB RedditClusteringP2P is a clustering and pairwise-similarity benchmark drawn from Reddit posts, providing post-to-post examples with cluster assignments. It is designed to evaluate embedding models’ ability to group informal social-media text by topic and to discriminate same-cluster vs. different-cluster pairs. The dataset is used for clustering metrics (e.g., ARI/NMI) and pairwise classification tasks, stressing robustness to noisy, conversational language.

MTEB SCIDOCS is a scientific-document retrieval dataset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It comprises queries and corresponding relevant academic documents drawn from scientific literature, with relevance signals derived from citation or topical relationships. The dataset is designed to evaluate embedding-based semantic search, dense retrieval, and re-ranking methods on domain-specific, technical text. It is useful for benchmarking document- and passage-level embeddings, measuring retrieval metrics such as recall, MRR, and nDCG in scientific IR scenarios.

MTEB SciDocsRR is a benchmark dataset for evaluating semantic retrieval and relevance-ranking of scientific documents. It comprises query–document pairs drawn from scientific literature, each annotated with relevance labels (binary or graded) to indicate how well candidate documents satisfy the query. The set is designed to test embedding models, retrieval pipelines, and rerankers on domain-specific language and topical reasoning, enabling assessment with ranking metrics such as NDCG and MAP. It is useful for developing and comparing models that must capture fine-grained scientific semantics and generalize across research domains.

MTEB SciFact is a benchmark subset derived from the SciFact corpus for evaluating text embeddings on scientific claim verification and evidence retrieval. It pairs concise scientific claims with candidate abstracts and sentence-level evidence annotations labeled SUPPORTS, REFUTES, or NOT ENOUGH INFO, enabling retrieval, reranking, and claim–evidence matching evaluations. The dataset tests semantic search and verification performance in the scientific domain, emphasizing precise cross-document matching and fine-grained sentence-level relevance.

MTEB StackExchangeClustering is a short-text clustering benchmark drawn from StackExchange question posts (titles and short excerpts) with ground-truth clusters derived from their originating communities or topical tags. It is designed to evaluate embedding methods on unsupervised topic grouping and semantic clustering of concise, real-world Q&A texts, enabling comparison of cluster quality, coherence, and retrieval performance for downstream applications.

StackExchangeClusteringP2P is a clustering benchmark drawn from Stack Exchange content, consisting of question and answer posts paired with ground-truth groupings that indicate semantic equivalence or topic-level clusters. It is designed to evaluate embedding and clustering methods on short technical and conversational text, measuring how well models group semantically related posts and distinguish distinct topics. The dataset supports tasks such as unsupervised clustering, nearest-neighbor retrieval, and cluster-quality evaluation for text embeddings in QA and forum domains.

MTEB StackOverflowDupQuestions is a dataset of Stack Overflow question pairs derived from community-marked duplicate links, used to evaluate embeddings on duplicate detection and semantic retrieval in the technical Q&A domain. Each example pairs two questions (typically titles and/or short bodies) with a label or relation indicating whether they are duplicates, enabling benchmarking of pairwise similarity, ranking, and retrieval performance for models handling technical language and question-answering scenarios.

MTEB TRECCOVID is an information-retrieval benchmark in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) derived from the TREC-COVID challenge. It contains real-world COVID-19 queries paired with relevance judgments over scientific literature (e.g., CORD-19), enabling evaluation of embedding models on semantic search and ranking in a biomedical domain. The dataset tests models’ ability to handle domain-specific terminology and short, real-user queries, making it useful for assessing retrieval quality, domain adaptation, and embedding-driven search over scientific documents.

MTEB Touche2020 is an information-retrieval benchmark derived from the TOUCHÉ 2020 shared task. It provides query–document pairs with human relevance judgments for ad‑hoc ranking, enabling evaluation of semantic search and dense embedding models. The dataset is used to measure retrieval performance (e.g., recall@k, nDCG) and to test robustness to real-world query formulations and topical variation, making it suitable for benchmarking embedding-based retrieval and re‑ranking systems.

MTEB ToxicConversationsClassification is a dataset for detecting toxic content in multi-turn conversational contexts. It contains dialog turns or short conversations paired with toxicity labels (binary or categorical) to train and evaluate classifiers and embedding models on context-aware toxicity detection. The dataset is designed to benchmark model performance on moderation and safety tasks, emphasizing understanding of conversational context, implicit abuse, and robustness to varied phrasing. It is useful for developing content-moderation systems, safety filters, and research on contextualized hate/toxicity classification.

MTEB TweetSentimentExtractionClassification is a Twitter sentiment dataset combining sentiment classification and sentiment-span extraction annotations. Each example contains a tweet labeled with a sentiment (e.g., positive, negative, neutral) alongside the text span that expresses that sentiment, enabling both label prediction and targeted extraction tasks. The dataset is tailored for evaluating embedding-based models on short, informal social media text, challenging methods with noisy language, emojis, hashtags, and domain-specific phrasing. It is useful for benchmarking and developing models for tweet-level sentiment analysis, span detection, and representation learning in conversational or social-media contexts.

TwentyNewsgroupsClustering is a clustering benchmark derived from the 20 Newsgroups corpus, containing newsgroup posts spanning 20 topical categories. It provides raw documents with ground-truth topic labels for external evaluation, enabling assessment of text embedding quality and unsupervised clustering algorithms using metrics like ARI or NMI. The dataset challenges models with topical overlap and intra-class diversity, making it useful for benchmarking representation learning and clustering performance on real-world short-text data.

AmazonCounterfactualClassification (en-ext) is an English dataset of Amazon product texts paired with minimally edited counterfactual variants and binary labels indicating whether the original class (e.g., sentiment or rating category) changes under the counterfactual. It is designed to evaluate embedding models and classifiers on sensitivity to fine-grained semantic edits, counterfactual robustness, and contrastive discrimination between near-identical inputs. The "en-ext" split provides extended coverage for diverse products and writing styles, making it useful for benchmarking representation quality in tasks requiring causal/contrastive reasoning and robustness to small textual perturbations.

MTEB AmazonCounterfactualClassification (ja) is a Japanese-language classification dataset from the MTEB suite containing Amazon product text examples paired with counterfactual variants and labels indicating whether the counterfactual changes the target class. It is designed to evaluate embedding and classification models’ ability to detect class changes under minimal, realistic edits, measuring robustness and generalization of representations on Japanese product-review/product-title data.

MTEB AmazonReviewsClassification (ja) is a Japanese-language subset of the Amazon Reviews classification collection used in the MTEB benchmark. It contains Japanese Amazon product review texts paired with categorical labels (such as star ratings or product categories) for supervised text classification. The dataset is intended to evaluate sentence-embedding models and classifiers on tasks like sentiment and product-category prediction in Japanese e-commerce reviews.

MTEB BUCC (de-en) is a German–English bitext mining dataset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark to evaluate cross-lingual sentence retrieval and parallel-sentence identification. It comprises German and English sentences extracted from comparable corpora (Wikipedia) with gold labels indicating translation equivalents, enabling benchmarking of multilingual sentence embeddings for bilingual alignment, bitext mining, and cross-lingual semantic similarity. Typical evaluation uses precision/recall/F1 for retrieved parallel pairs, making it useful for developing and comparing retrieval, alignment, and multilingual embedding models.

MTEB BUCC (fr-en) is a French–English bitext-mining benchmark drawn from the BUCC shared task, containing sentence pairs labeled as translation/non-translation. It is used within MTEB to evaluate cross-lingual sentence embeddings on translation retrieval and parallel sentence mining, measuring retrieval precision, recall and F1 for identifying true bilingual matches in comparable corpora. The dataset supports development and comparison of multilingual embedding models and cross-lingual retrieval systems.

MTEB BUCC (ru-en) is the Russian–English subset of the BUCC parallel-sentence mining dataset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It provides comparable corpora with sentence-level annotations that mark true translation pairs across Russian and English, enabling evaluation of bilingual sentence embeddings and bitext-mining systems. The set is commonly used to benchmark cross-lingual retrieval, parallel sentence extraction, and precision/recall/F1 performance of multilingual or aligned embedding models in bitext mining and retrieval tasks.

MTEB BUCC (zh-en) is a Chinese–English bitext mining dataset drawn from the BUCC shared task and included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It contains comparable corpora with annotated parallel sentence pairs for evaluating cross-lingual sentence retrieval and parallel-sentence identification. The dataset is commonly used to benchmark multilingual sentence embeddings and retrieval models on translation retrieval, mining precision/recall/F1, and cross-lingual semantic alignment.

MTEB MTOPDomainClassification (hi) is a Hindi-language domain classification dataset drawn from the MTOP task-oriented parsing corpus and packaged for the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It contains user utterances in Hindi annotated with domain labels (e.g., calendar, messaging, navigation), enabling evaluation of embedding and classification models on short, conversational queries. The set is intended to benchmark semantic representations for supervised, zero-shot, and cross-lingual domain classification, as well as related tasks like clustering and retrieval in multilingual dialog and task-oriented NLP.

MTEB MTOPDomainClassification (th) is a Thai-language domain classification dataset derived from the MTOP task-oriented parsing corpus and included in the MTEB benchmark. It contains user utterances labeled with domain categories (e.g., calendar, music, reminders, etc.) to evaluate models on coarse-grained domain discrimination in conversational or task-oriented settings. The set is intended for assessing and training sentence-embedding and classification models on Thai, including multilingual and cross-lingual transfer scenarios, and serves as a benchmark for semantic understanding in low-resource language contexts.

MTEB MTOPIntentClassification (hi) is the Hindi subset of the MTOP intent-classification task used in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains Hindi user utterances from task-oriented dialogues paired with intent labels, enabling evaluation and training of embedding models and classifiers for intent recognition in a multilingual conversational setting. The dataset is suitable for benchmarking embedding quality, cross-lingual transfer, retrieval, and clustering of conversational intents.

MTEB MTOPIntentClassification (th) is a Thai-language intent classification subset derived from the MTOP task-oriented parsing corpus, included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It contains Thai user utterances labeled with intent categories from task-oriented dialogue scenarios and is intended to evaluate sentence-embedding models on intent detection. The dataset is used to benchmark semantic representation quality, multilingual and cross-lingual transfer, and downstream intent-classification performance for Thai.

MTEB MassiveIntentClassification (af) is the Afrikaans subset of the Massive Intent Classification task in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It comprises short Afrikaans user utterances labeled with intent categories for supervised intent classification and sentence-embedding evaluation. The dataset is intended to assess multilingual embedding and classification models on fine-grained conversational intents in a low-resource language setting.

MTEB MassiveIntentClassification (am) is an Amharic intent-classification dataset within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, containing short user queries annotated with intent labels. It is designed to evaluate embedding models and classifiers on intent detection, semantic clustering, and retrieval for Amharic conversational text, supporting benchmarking of multilingual and cross-lingual semantic understanding in a low-resource language.

MTEB MassiveIntentClassification (ar) is an Arabic intent-classification benchmark drawn from the MassiveIntentClassification task in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains Arabic user utterances labeled with a large, fine-grained set of intent categories to evaluate sentence-embedding and classification methods under many-class conditions. The dataset is intended for assessing embedding quality and downstream performance in zero-shot, few-shot, or supervised intent classification, multilingual transfer, and large-scale retrieval or clustering scenarios.

MTEB MassiveIntentClassification (az) is the Azerbaijani subset of the Massive Intent Classification collection in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains short user utterances labeled with intent classes, providing supervised examples for multiclass intent detection and embedding-based retrieval. Designed to evaluate and train multilingual sentence-embedding and NLU models, it supports benchmarking of embedding quality, few-shot/transfer experiments, and downstream conversational intent classification in Azerbaijani.

MTEB MassiveIntentClassification (bn) is a Bengali-language intent classification dataset from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It contains user utterances in Bangla labeled with intent categories to evaluate and train sentence embedding models and intent classifiers. The dataset is designed for benchmarking multi-class intent detection, supporting supervised classification, embedding-based retrieval, and few-shot evaluation for conversational AI and virtual assistant use cases in Bengali.

MassiveIntentClassification (cy) is the Welsh subset of the MTEB MassiveIntentClassification dataset: a collection of Welsh user utterances paired with intent labels for intent classification. It is designed to train and evaluate multilingual and cross-lingual semantic representations and classifiers, particularly for intent detection and few-shot transfer. The dataset supports benchmarking embedding quality and classification performance on real-world conversational intents, aiding research in multilingual NLU and dialogue systems.

MTEB MassiveIntentClassification (da) is a Danish-language intent classification dataset from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains short user utterances paired with fine-grained intent labels, enabling evaluation of text embeddings and classifiers on intent detection in Danish. Designed for single-label classification across many intent categories, it is useful for benchmarking semantic representation quality, few-shot/zero-shot transfer, and practical conversational understanding tasks.

MTEB MassiveIntentClassification (el) is a Greek-language intent classification dataset within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains user utterances annotated with intent labels, designed to evaluate embedding models on intent recognition, clustering, and retrieval tasks in Greek. The dataset is useful for benchmarking embedding quality for downstream intent classification, zero-shot or few-shot transfer, and semantic search in a low-resource language setting.

MTEB MassiveIntentClassification (fa) is a Persian-language intent classification dataset containing user utterances paired with intent labels. Designed for evaluating sentence embeddings and supervised classifiers, it covers many intent categories typical of conversational assistants and task-oriented dialogs. The dataset is suitable for training and benchmarking multi-class intent detection models in Persian, enabling assessment of embedding quality, classification accuracy, and model generalization in real-world conversational scenarios.

MassiveIntentClassification (fi) is a Finnish-language intent classification subset of the MTEB benchmark. It contains short user utterances labeled with intent categories across diverse domains, designed to evaluate text-embedding and classification models on intent discrimination in Finnish. The dataset is suited for benchmarking supervised and few-shot intent classification, clustering, and retrieval tasks, and for assessing multilingual embedding generalization to real-world conversational intents.

MTEB MassiveIntentClassification (he) is a Hebrew intent-classification dataset from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, containing Hebrew user utterances annotated with intent labels across a broad set of categories. It is designed to evaluate and benchmark sentence-embedding and classification models on multi-class intent recognition in Hebrew conversational and NLU settings. The dataset is useful for training and testing intent classifiers, comparing representation quality for downstream intent prediction, and assessing multilingual generalization of embedding models.

MTEB MassiveIntentClassification (hi) is a Hindi-language intent classification dataset within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains Hindi user utterances annotated with a large, fine-grained set of intent labels to support training and evaluation of intent detection systems and semantic representations. The dataset is intended for benchmarking supervised intent classification, assessing text-embedding quality for clustering and retrieval, and measuring few-shot or cross-lingual transfer performance for multilingual conversational understanding.

MTEB MassiveIntentClassification (hu) is a Hungarian intent-classification dataset of short user utterances labeled with a large set of fine-grained intent classes. It is designed to evaluate embedding-based and supervised models on intent detection in Hungarian, posing challenges like many labels, class imbalance and terse conversational text. Used within the MTEB benchmark, it measures semantic representation quality and classification/retrieval performance on real-world intent understanding.

MTEB MassiveIntentClassification (hy) is an Armenian-language intent classification dataset from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It pairs short user utterances with intent labels to evaluate embedding and classification models on intent discrimination, clustering, and retrieval in Armenian. The dataset is designed to benchmark multilingual and cross-lingual embedding quality for conversational AI, intent detection, and downstream search or routing tasks.

MassiveIntentClassification (id) is an Indonesian many-way intent classification dataset from the MTEB suite containing user utterances paired with fine-grained intent labels. It is designed to evaluate and train sentence-embedding and classification models on large-vocabulary intent detection tasks in Indonesian, testing models’ ability to separate semantically similar intents for few-shot classification, nearest-neighbor retrieval, and conversational understanding benchmarks.

MTEB MassiveIntentClassification (is) is the Icelandic subset of the Massive Intent Classification task in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains Icelandic user utterances paired with intent labels, designed to evaluate sentence embeddings and classifiers on intent-detection performance. The dataset is used to benchmark model accuracy and generalization for multilingual and cross-lingual intent classification.

MTEB MassiveIntentClassification (it) is an Italian-language intent classification dataset from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It pairs short user utterances in Italian with a large, diverse set of intent labels, enabling supervised training and evaluation of multi-class intent classifiers and text-embedding models. Designed to test semantic discrimination and robustness across conversational domains, it is useful for benchmarking and fine-tuning multilingual and Italian-specific NLP systems for intent detection.

MTEB MassiveIntentClassification (ja) is a Japanese-language intent classification dataset from the MTEB benchmark containing user utterances paired with intent labels across multiple domains. It provides supervised, single-label examples for training and evaluating models on intent detection and classification, making it suitable for benchmarking embedding-based and classifier-based approaches in Japanese conversational understanding. Use cases include fine-tuning intent classifiers, evaluating nearest-neighbor or retrieval-based intent mapping, and measuring generalization across diverse intent categories.

MTEB MassiveIntentClassification (jv) is the Javanese subset of the Massive Intent Classification task from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains short Javanese user utterances paired with intent labels to evaluate text-embedding models and downstream classifiers on fine-grained intent discrimination. MTEB Tatoeba (dtp-eng) is a subset of the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark built from the Tatoeba sentence collection for the dtp↔eng language pair. It provides short parallel sentences designed to evaluate multilingual sentence embeddings on cross-lingual retrieval and semantic similarity tasks. The dataset is useful for benchmarking embedding models’ ability to match semantically equivalent sentences across languages, particularly for short, conversational-style text. It serves as a compact, language-pair-specific test for cross-lingual generalization and retrieval performance.

MTEB Tatoeba (kat-eng) is a sentence-level parallel dataset of Georgian–English sentence pairs drawn from the Tatoeba corpus and included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It provides short, everyday sentences with direct translations for evaluating cross-lingual retrieval, bitext mining, and multilingual sentence embedding quality. The dataset is useful for benchmarking model ability to align semantic representations across Georgian and English and for testing zero-shot cross-lingual transfer in retrieval and similarity tasks.

MTEB Tatoeba (jpn-eng) is a subset of the Tatoeba parallel sentence collection used in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains short Japanese–English sentence pairs with crowd-sourced translations and is designed to evaluate multilingual sentence embeddings on cross-lingual retrieval and semantic similarity tasks. The dataset provides a compact, diverse set of everyday sentences for benchmarking how well embeddings align semantically across Japanese and English.

MTEB Tatoeba (csb-eng) is a sentence-level Kashubian–English parallel dataset from the Tatoeba collection, included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark to evaluate multilingual sentence embeddings. It provides paired translations for cross-lingual retrieval and semantic similarity tasks, enabling assessment of embedding alignment and retrieval accuracy on a low-resource language pair.

MTEB Tatoeba (xho-eng) is a bilingual sentence-pair dataset drawn from the Tatoeba corpus containing aligned Xhosa–English sentences used in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It provides short, real-world parallel sentences for evaluating cross-lingual sentence embeddings, semantic similarity, and retrieval performance, enabling assessment of a model’s ability to match translations and represent meaning across Xhosa and English—particularly useful for benchmarking multilingual and low-resource language models.

MTEB Tatoeba (orv-eng) is a bilingual sentence retrieval dataset extracted from Tatoeba, containing short parallel sentence pairs in orv and English. It is used within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark to evaluate multilingual sentence embeddings on cross-lingual retrieval and semantic similarity tasks. The dataset’s aligned translations and compact, low-resource nature make it suitable for assessing embedding alignment, zero-shot transfer, and cross-lingual retrieval performance between orv and English.

MTEB Tatoeba (ind-eng) is a sentence-level parallel dataset of Indonesian–English translation pairs drawn from the Tatoeba corpus, used within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark to evaluate multilingual sentence embeddings.
