It provides short, diverse sentences with direct cross-lingual alignments for tasks such as bitext retrieval, semantic search, and cross-lingual similarity. The dataset enables assessment of embedding quality for retrieval metrics (e.g., recall@k) and generalization across languages, making it useful for benchmarking and improving multilingual representation models.

MTEB Tatoeba (tuk–eng) is a Turkmen–English sentence-pair dataset drawn from the Tatoeba project and included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It provides aligned, crowd-sourced sentences for evaluating cross-lingual sentence embeddings on tasks like bitext retrieval and semantic similarity, enabling assessment of multilingual and zero-shot transfer performance between Turkmen and English.

MTEB Tatoeba (max-eng) is a multilingual sentence retrieval benchmark derived from the Tatoeba corpus, containing short sentences in dozens to hundreds of languages paired with English translations. It is designed to evaluate cross-lingual and multilingual sentence embedding models by measuring retrieval and alignment between non‑English sentences and their English counterparts. The "max‑eng" variant maximizes English coverage per language, offering a consistent English‑centric evaluation for assessing zero‑shot cross‑lingual transfer, retrieval accuracy, and embedding quality on short conversational sentences.

MTEB Tatoeba (swh-eng) is a Swahili–English subset of the Tatoeba sentence-pair benchmark included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains parallel short, crowd-sourced sentences intended to evaluate multilingual sentence embeddings on cross-lingual retrieval and similarity tasks. Commonly used for bitext retrieval, translation candidate ranking, and assessing cross-lingual transfer for a lower-resource language pair, it tests how well embeddings align Swahili and English semantics.

MTEB Tatoeba (hin-eng) is a sentence-level parallel collection of Hindi–English translation pairs drawn from the community-sourced Tatoeba corpus and included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It provides short, diverse, real-world sentences with ground-truth translations for evaluating cross-lingual sentence embeddings and retrieval models. The dataset is used to measure semantic alignment and retrieval accuracy between Hindi and English representations, making it useful for benchmarking multilingual embedding performance on a lower-resource language pair.

MTEB Tatoeba (dsb-eng) is a bilingual sentence-pair dataset of Lower Sorbian (dsb) and English drawn from the Tatoeba corpus, provided within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It contains short, user-contributed everyday sentences aligned across the two languages and is intended for evaluating cross-lingual sentence embeddings on tasks such as bilingual retrieval, bitext mining, and semantic similarity. The dataset is useful for benchmarking model performance on low-resource cross-lingual transfer and multilingual retrieval scenarios.

MTEB Tatoeba (ber-eng) is a bilingual sentence-pair dataset drawn from the Tatoeba project, containing parallel Berber (ber) and English sentences used within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It is designed to evaluate multilingual and cross-lingual sentence embeddings on tasks such as sentence retrieval, semantic similarity, and translation alignment. The dataset supports benchmarking models’ ability to capture semantic equivalence across a low-resource language (Berber) and English, making it useful for assessing cross-lingual generalization and retrieval performance.

MTEB Tatoeba (tam-eng) is a bilingual collection of aligned short sentences in Tamil and English, drawn from the Tatoeba corpus and included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It is designed to evaluate multilingual sentence embedding models on cross-lingual retrieval and semantic similarity tasks by measuring whether semantically equivalent Tamil and English sentences are mapped to nearby vector representations. The dataset is useful for benchmarking and developing models for cross-lingual retrieval, semantic search, and translation-oriented embedding applications.

MTEB Tatoeba (slk-eng) is a Slovak–English subset of the Tatoeba parallel-sentence corpus included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It provides short, user-contributed sentence pairs across diverse everyday topics for evaluating cross-lingual sentence representations. The data is commonly used to benchmark multilingual embeddings on tasks such as cross-lingual retrieval, semantic similarity, nearest-neighbor translation mining, and zero-shot transfer for semantic search.

MTEB Tatoeba (tgl-eng) is a parallel sentence-pair dataset of Tagalog–English examples derived from the Tatoeba corpus, included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark to evaluate cross-lingual sentence embeddings. It provides aligned short sentences for tasks such as bilingual retrieval and semantic similarity, enabling assessment of embedding models’ ability to match and rank semantically equivalent sentences across Tagalog and English. The dataset is useful for benchmarking cross-lingual transfer, semantic alignment, and retrieval performance, particularly for lower-resource language scenarios.

MTEB Tatoeba (ast-eng) is a bilingual subset of the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark consisting of short parallel sentences in Asturian and English from the Tatoeba corpus. It is used to evaluate multilingual and cross-lingual sentence embeddings on retrieval and similarity tasks, assessing models’ ability to match semantically equivalent sentences across Asturian and English. The dataset’s varied, casual-language sentences provide a lightweight, real-world benchmark for zero-shot transfer and cross-lingual retrieval performance.

MTEB Tatoeba (mkd-eng) is a bilingual test set derived from the Tatoeba corpus containing aligned Macedonian–English sentence pairs. It is designed to evaluate cross-lingual sentence embeddings and retrieval—measuring how well models match semantically equivalent short, user-contributed sentences across Macedonian and English. Common uses include translation retrieval, cross-lingual semantic similarity, and assessing multilingual representation and zero-shot transfer performance.

MTEB Tatoeba (khm-eng) is a bilingual Khmer–English sentence-pair dataset from the Tatoeba collection included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark to evaluate multilingual sentence embeddings on cross-lingual retrieval and semantic similarity. It provides community-sourced parallel sentences for testing models’ ability to retrieve translations and preserve semantic similarity across a low-resource language pair.

MTEB Tatoeba (ces-eng) is a Czech–English parallel sentence dataset drawn from the Tatoeba collection, provided for evaluating cross-lingual sentence embeddings and retrieval. It consists of short, diverse bilingual sentence pairs with gold-standard translations, enabling assessment of bilingual alignment, cross-lingual semantic similarity, and bitext retrieval performance. The set is commonly used in benchmark suites to measure embedding generalization and zero-shot cross-language transfer for downstream retrieval and matching tasks.

MTEB Tatoeba (tzl-eng) is a bilingual sentence-pair subset from the Tatoeba collection included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, containing Talossan–English parallel sentences. It is designed to evaluate multilingual sentence embeddings on cross-lingual retrieval and semantic similarity tasks, enabling assessment of embedding alignment, zero-shot transfer, and retrieval performance for a low-resource language paired with English.

MTEB Tatoeba (urd-eng) is a sentence-level parallel subset from the Tatoeba collection used in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark to evaluate multilingual sentence embeddings for Urdu–English. It provides short aligned Urdu and English sentences for cross-lingual retrieval and semantic similarity tasks, enabling measurement of embedding alignment, retrieval accuracy, and zero-shot transfer between a low-resource and a high-resource language. The set is commonly used to benchmark and compare embedding models’ cross-lingual transfer and retrieval performance.

MTEB Tatoeba (ara-eng) is a subset of the Tatoeba parallel-sentence collection included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark to evaluate cross-lingual sentence embeddings between Arabic and English. It contains aligned short, diverse user-contributed sentences and their translations, enabling assessment of semantic similarity and bilingual retrieval. The split is intended for embedding evaluation tasks such as bitext retrieval, cross-lingual semantic search, and analysis of transferability of sentence-level representations.

MTEB Tatoeba (kor-eng) is a sentence-level Korean–English parallel corpus from the Tatoeba collection, included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) to evaluate multilingual sentence embeddings. It contains short, human-translated sentence pairs of everyday content and is used to assess cross-lingual retrieval, semantic similarity, and embedding alignment between Korean and English, making it useful for benchmarking and fine-tuning models for multilingual semantic search and cross-lingual transfer.

MTEB Tatoeba (yid-eng) is a bilingual sentence-pair dataset derived from the Tatoeba collection, containing short, crowd-sourced Yiddish–English sentence alignments across diverse, conversational topics. Designed for evaluation within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB), it is used to assess cross-lingual sentence embeddings on tasks such as retrieval, translation ranking, and semantic similarity. The data is informal and varied, making it a practical benchmark for testing robustness and cross-lingual generalization of embedding models.

MTEB Tatoeba (fin-eng) is a Finnish–English sentence-pair subset of the Tatoeba corpus prepared for the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It provides short, human-aligned translations for evaluating cross-lingual sentence embeddings on retrieval and semantic similarity tasks. The dataset is commonly used to benchmark multilingual embedding quality in bitext retrieval, semantic search, and cross-lingual nearest-neighbor retrieval.

MTEB Tatoeba (tha-eng) is a bilingual sentence-pair dataset of Thai–English parallel sentences, drawn from the crowd-sourced Tatoeba collection and packaged for the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains short, diverse user-contributed sentences aligned across Thai and English, and is used to evaluate cross-lingual sentence embeddings and retrieval performance (e.g., parallel sentence retrieval, semantic similarity) on a low-resource, typologically distant language pair.

MTEB Tatoeba (wuu-eng) is a sentence-level bilingual retrieval benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, containing parallel Wu Chinese (wuu) and English sentence pairs. It is designed to evaluate cross-lingual sentence embeddings on semantic retrieval and similarity tasks, measuring how well models align meanings across a low-resource Sinitic variety and English. The set is useful for assessing multilingual embedding quality, zero-shot retrieval performance, and generalization to less-represented language pairs.

AllegroReviews is a Polish-language dataset of user-generated product reviews collected from the Allegro e-commerce platform. Reviews include text (and often titles) with associated metadata such as star ratings, enabling supervised tasks like sentiment/rating prediction and unsupervised tasks like semantic search, clustering, and retrieval. Included in the MTEB benchmark to evaluate embedding models on e-commerce and opinion-text domains, it tests models’ ability to capture fine-grained sentiment and product-related semantics in Polish.

AlloProfClusteringP2P is a clustering-focused subset of the MTEB benchmark built from AlloProf educational content. It contains student questions and related text units paired with binary labels indicating whether two items belong to the same semantic cluster, enabling pairwise evaluation of semantic similarity and cluster membership. The dataset is intended to benchmark embedding models on clustering, duplicate-question detection, and pairwise retrieval tasks, emphasizing performance on educational, domain-specific language.

AlloProfClusteringS2S is a dataset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) for evaluating embedding and sequence-to-sequence models on text clustering. It contains text items represented as source–target (sequence-to-sequence) pairs along with cluster labels that group semantically related items. The benchmark is intended to measure how well learned representations capture group structure using clustering metrics (e.g., NMI, F1) and to support development of models for semantic grouping, topic discovery, and downstream tasks that rely on cluster-aware embeddings.

AlloprofReranking is a reranking benchmark in the MTEB suite derived from Alloprof educational QA data. It provides student queries paired with candidate passages and graded relevance labels, enabling evaluation of embedding-based rerankers and dense retrieval models on domain-specific educational content (primarily French). The dataset is intended for training and benchmarking reranking and re-ranking stages, with common metrics such as MRR and NDCG used to assess ranking quality and model generalization on educational question–answer retrieval.

MTEB AlloprofRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark drawn from the Alloprof educational platform, consisting of real user queries paired with candidate educational passages and relevance annotations. It is designed to evaluate semantic search and embedding-based retrieval models in the educational domain, focusing on matching natural language questions to the most relevant explanatory resources. The dataset supports development and assessment of dense and sparse retrieval methods, ranking models, and applications like question answering and study-assistant systems.

ArguAna-PL is a Polish argumentation/stance dataset containing sentences from argumentative online discussions annotated for stance (pro, con, or neutral) with respect to specific topics. It is intended to evaluate sentence-embedding models on stance detection, argument mining, and related classification or retrieval tasks in Polish, enabling assessment of semantic representations for detecting argumentative orientation and topic-related sentiment.

MTEB BSARDRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) that supplies query–document pairs with relevance labels for evaluating embedding-based semantic search. It provides a corpus of candidate documents and annotated queries to test dense retrieval, candidate generation, and ranking models. The dataset is used to measure retrieval effectiveness with metrics such as recall, MRR, and nDCG, helping compare and validate vector embedding approaches on real-world information‑seeking tasks.

MTEB CBD is a curated subset of the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark focused on Customer–Business Dialogue (CBD) data. It contains short conversational utterances and paired examples annotated for semantic similarity, retrieval, and clustering, enabling evaluation of embedding models on dialogue-style, domain-specific language. The dataset is intended to benchmark embedding quality for downstream tasks like FAQ retrieval, intent clustering, and semantic search in customer support contexts.

MTEB CLSClusteringP2P is a clustering task in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that evaluates text embeddings by grouping labeled texts into clusters and comparing cluster assignments to ground-truth labels using pairwise (point-to-point) metrics. It contains collections of texts with class labels and is designed to test an embedding model’s ability to separate semantically similar items, guiding development and tuning of embeddings and clustering pipelines for unsupervised grouping and downstream classification.

MTEB CLSClusteringS2S is a benchmark task in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that evaluates models on joint classification and clustering of short texts framed as a sequence-to-sequence problem. The data consist of textual instances paired with class labels (clusters), enabling evaluation of embedding quality both by supervised label prediction (sequence-to-sequence label generation) and by unsupervised clustering consistency. It is used to assess how well embeddings separate semantic classes and support downstream tasks such as classification accuracy and clustering metrics (e.g., NMI, ARI).

CmedqaRetrieval is a medical question–answer retrieval dataset in the MTEB suite that pairs clinical questions with candidate passages or answer snippets annotated for relevance. It is designed to evaluate embedding-based semantic search and dense retrieval models on domain-specific language, challenging them with clinical terminology, paraphrasing, and implicit relevance. The dataset is useful for benchmarking and fine-tuning retrieval and ranking models for medical QA and clinical information access.

MTEB CovidRetrieval is a COVID-19–focused information retrieval dataset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It pairs a corpus of COVID-19 scientific documents (titles and abstracts) with user queries and curated relevance labels to evaluate semantic search and retrieval systems in the biomedical domain. Designed for benchmarking dense and sparse retrieval, reranking, and embedding models, it supports standard IR metrics (MRR, nDCG, recall) to measure models’ ability to retrieve relevant pandemic-related literature.

MTEB DBPedia-PL is a Polish-language variant of the DBpedia ontology classification dataset used in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains short Polish Wikipedia-derived texts paired with DBpedia ontology class labels, providing a multi-class classification task. The set is intended to evaluate and train multilingual sentence/document embedding models and classifiers on semantic categorization of Polish text.

MTEB DuRetrieval is a retrieval dataset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB), derived from the Baidu DuReader collection. It contains Chinese information-seeking queries paired with candidate passages/documents and relevance labels, designed to evaluate embedding-based semantic search and document retrieval models on real-world QA-style retrieval tasks.

MTEB EcomRetrieval is an e-commerce retrieval benchmark containing product queries paired with candidate product titles/descriptions and relevance labels. It is designed to evaluate text-embedding and semantic-search models on realistic product search tasks such as query–product matching, product ranking, and duplicate detection across diverse categories. The dataset supports measuring retrieval quality (e.g., recall@k, nDCG) and helps assess model performance and generalization in commercial search and recommendation scenarios.

FiQA-PL is a Polish-language financial dataset in the MTEB suite containing short financial texts annotated with fine-grained sentiment/relevance labels. It is intended to evaluate sentence and document embeddings on domain-specific semantic tasks—particularly sentiment intensity (regression), similarity, and ranking—helping assess model performance on Polish financial-language understanding for applications like sentiment analysis and information retrieval.

MTEB HALClusteringS2S is a sentence-to-sentence clustering dataset within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark designed to evaluate embedding models' ability to group semantically similar sentences. It provides collections of short texts with ground-truth cluster assignments, supporting evaluation of clustering algorithms (k-means, hierarchical, etc.) and metrics such as ARI and NMI. The dataset targets semantic grouping and boundary detection tasks, making it useful for benchmarking embedding quality for unsupervised grouping, topic discovery, and downstream clustering-sensitive applications.

MTEB HotpotQA-PL is a passage-level adaptation of the HotpotQA multi-hop question-answering dataset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It pairs questions with candidate passages (gold supporting paragraphs plus distractors) to evaluate embedding models on passage retrieval and reranking for multi-step reasoning. The dataset stresses retrieval of multiple supporting documents and measures how well embeddings enable finding and ranking evidence needed for compositional QA.

MTEB IFlyTek is a Chinese short-text classification dataset of user queries and domain-specific labels used within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark to evaluate sentence embeddings. It contains fine-grained, multi-class intent/label annotations across many categories, making it useful for testing embedding quality on classification, clustering and retrieval tasks that require distinguishing nuanced semantic differences in short, domain-focused texts.

MTEB JDReview is a Chinese-language product review dataset sourced from JD.com, composed of user review text paired with associated labels (e.g., ratings or sentiment/product category). Included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB), it is used to evaluate embeddings on tasks such as sentiment/product classification, semantic retrieval, and clustering in e-commerce review settings. The dataset is suitable for training and benchmarking models that must capture fine-grained consumer opinion and product-related semantics.

MTEB MLSUMClusteringP2P is a multilingual news clustering dataset derived from the MLSUM summarization corpus. It provides real-world news articles grouped by topic and formatted in a point-to-point clustering setup (document pairs with cluster membership) to evaluate document-embedding quality for topic grouping and clustering. The dataset spans multiple languages and domains, making it suitable for benchmarking multilingual embedding models on clustering metrics and cross-lingual topic discovery.

MTEB MLSUMClusteringS2S is a multilingual clustering dataset derived from the MLSUM news corpus, formatted for sequence-to-sequence evaluation. It pairs news articles in multiple languages with cluster identifiers (topic/group labels) and presents inputs and targets as text sequences to assess models that perform clustering or label generation in a generative S2S setup. The dataset is intended to benchmark multilingual embedding and sequence models on their ability to produce cluster-consistent representations and to generate cluster labels across diverse languages and news domains.

MTEB MMarcoReranking is a reranking benchmark in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark built from the MS MARCO passage collection. It provides real user queries paired with pre-retrieved candidate passages and binary relevance labels, simulating the second-stage reranking task where an initial result set must be reordered by relevance. The dataset is designed to evaluate embedding-based rerankers, cross-encoders, and learning-to-rank models on top-of-list metrics (e.g., MRR, NDCG), supporting development and comparison of methods for improving search precision on realistic web-search queries.

MTEB MMarcoRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark derived from the MS MARCO retrieval task and packaged for the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It pairs real anonymized web search queries with a large corpus of passages/documents and relevance labels to evaluate embedding models’ ability to perform semantic retrieval and ranking. Intended for large-scale, real-world search scenarios, it assesses models on ranking and retrieval metrics and supports comparison of dense and sparse retrieval approaches. The dataset is useful for benchmarking embedding quality, retrieval robustness, and end-to-end search performance.

MSMARCO-PL is a Polish-language adaptation of the MS MARCO passage ranking collection designed for passage retrieval and semantic search evaluation. It provides Polish queries paired with candidate passages and ground-truth relevance annotations, enabling benchmarking of dense and sparse retrieval models, embedding quality, and cross- or mono-lingual ranking performance on large-scale, real-world search queries.

MedicalRetrieval is the medical-domain subset of the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB), providing query–document pairs with relevance labels to evaluate text‑embedding and retrieval models on biomedical and clinical information‑access tasks. It targets semantic search, ranking, and reranking in medicine by exposing models to domain‑specific terminology, abbreviations, and high‑precision relevance needs. The collection is intended for benchmarking embedding quality and retrieval effectiveness for medical search, QA, and knowledge‑access systems.

MTEB MultiLongDocRetrieval (ru) is a Russian-language benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark for evaluating retrieval and ranking of long-form documents. It provides queries paired with a corpus of long Russian documents and relevance labels, targeting semantic search scenarios where document length and context-rich content challenge embedding models. The dataset is intended to assess embedding-based retrieval systems on metrics such as recall@k, MRR and nDCG, and to measure models’ ability to capture topical relevance across extended text for applications like semantic search, question answering and document-ranking in Russian.

MTEB MultiLongDocRetrieval (zh) is a Chinese long-document retrieval benchmark in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It provides queries paired with a large corpus of lengthy Chinese documents and relevance annotations to evaluate semantic retrieval and ranking of long-form content. The dataset is intended for testing embedding models’ ability to represent and retrieve long-context documents, supporting evaluation with standard retrieval metrics (e.g., recall, MRR). It targets research on scalable, robust retrieval for Chinese long-read information needs.

MultilingualSentiment is a sentiment classification dataset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) containing sentences and short texts labeled for sentiment across multiple languages. It enables evaluation of multilingual sentence embeddings and models on sentiment recognition, cross-lingual transfer, and robustness to language- and domain shifts. The dataset is suitable for supervised classification, zero-shot transfer, and retrieval-style tasks that probe how well embeddings preserve sentiment information across languages.

Description: NFCorpus-PL is a Polish-language corpus in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) designed for evaluating text embeddings on retrieval and semantic-search tasks. It contains Polish documents and associated queries/relevance information (or pairwise similarity signals), enabling evaluation of passage/document retrieval, semantic similarity, and clustering performance for Polish text. NFCorpus-PL is useful for benchmarking multilingual and language-specific embedding models on real-world Polish retrieval scenarios.

MTEB NQ-PL is a Polish-language adaptation of the Natural Questions dataset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It comprises real user questions in Polish paired with annotated relevant passages or answer spans, enabling evaluation of embedding models on open-domain question answering, retrieval, and ranking tasks. The dataset is intended to benchmark semantic search and dense retrieval performance for Polish-language models and to assess generalization of embedding representations in non-English contexts.

MTEB OnlineShopping is an e-commerce text dataset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark designed to evaluate embedding models on product-related language. It contains short, real-world product titles/descriptions (and associated category labels or query–product pairs) that reflect noisy, domain-specific phrasing. The dataset is suited for semantic search/retrieval, product classification, clustering, and recommendation tasks, enabling assessment of embedding quality and domain generalization for online-shopping applications.

MTEB PAC is a component of the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) that focuses on pairwise and classification (PAC) tasks for evaluating text embeddings. It contains labeled pairs and short-text classification sets spanning domains and languages to test semantic similarity, paraphrase detection, and downstream classification performance. The suite enables comparison of embedding models on practical tasks such as retrieval, clustering, and supervised text classification.

PolEmo2.0-IN is a Polish-language sentiment dataset of product reviews annotated with sentiment labels (including aspect-level annotations). Included in the MTEB suite to evaluate text embeddings on sentiment classification and semantic representation tasks, it provides real user-written consumer feedback that challenges models to capture polarity and fine-grained opinion signals in Polish.

PolEmo2.0-OUT is the out-of-domain split of the Polish PolEmo2.0 sentiment dataset, consisting of consumer review texts in Polish manually annotated with sentiment labels (e.g., positive/negative/neutral). It is used in MTEB to evaluate text embeddings and downstream classifiers on sentiment classification and to test robustness and generalization under domain shift for Polish-language NLP.

MTEB Quora-PL is a Polish-language paraphrase dataset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains pairs of Polish questions annotated as duplicate or non-duplicate, enabling evaluation of semantic textual similarity, paraphrase identification, and retrieval/ranking tasks. The dataset is intended to benchmark sentence and passage embedding models on monolingual Polish semantic understanding, clustering, and downstream applications like question deduplication and search.

SCIDOCS-PL is a Polish-language scientific document dataset in the MTEB benchmark, containing scholarly texts (articles/abstracts) paired with relevance judgments for query–document retrieval. It is designed to evaluate and compare embedding models on semantic search, document ranking and clustering in a domain-specific, non-English setting, stressing long-form content and specialized vocabulary typical of scientific literature.

MTEB SciFact-PL is a Polish-language version of the SciFact claim verification dataset adapted for the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It pairs scientific claims with candidate sentences from research abstracts labeled as SUPPORTS, REFUTES or NOT ENOUGH INFO, enabling evaluation of Polish sentence embeddings on retrieval, evidence selection and claim classification in the scientific/biomedical domain. The dataset is intended for benchmarking and training models for fact-checking, semantic search and evidence-aware NLP in Polish.

MTEB SyntecReranking is a dataset for evaluating and training retrieval reranking models within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It provides query texts paired with candidate document lists and graded relevance labels, focusing on the quality of post-retrieval ordering rather than initial retrieval. Designed as a synthetic/controlled reranking benchmark, it enables systematic comparison of embedding-based rerankers and supervised ranking models using standard metrics such as NDCG and MRR.

MTEB SyntecRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that pairs technical-domain documents or passages with synthetic queries and relevance labels. It is designed to evaluate embedding-based semantic search and dense retrieval models on technical information‑seeking tasks, emphasizing domain-specific terminology, paraphrasing, and fine-grained relevance. The dataset is useful for benchmarking embedding quality, retrieval ranking, and generalization of models in technical or industrial contexts.

MTEB T2Reranking is a reranking benchmark within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) that evaluates models’ ability to reorder candidate documents or passages given a query. Each instance contains a query, a list of retrieved candidates, and relevance labels used to supervise or evaluate reranking performance. The task measures how well embedding- or similarity-based models improve initial retrieval lists by promoting more relevant items, making it suitable for developing and comparing reranking and re-ranking stages in information retrieval pipelines.

MTEB T2Retrieval is a retrieval-focused subset of the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) for evaluating text embedding models on text-to-document retrieval tasks. It provides query–corpus pairs with relevance annotations across diverse domains (e.g., QA, news, product search) to measure how well embeddings support semantic search and ranking. The task is used to compare embedding methods with standard retrieval metrics (Recall, MRR, nDCG) and to benchmark dense and hybrid retrieval systems for real-world information retrieval scenarios.

MTEB TNews is a Chinese short-text news dataset of headline-like snippets labeled with topic categories. Included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, it evaluates embedding models on multi-class topic classification, semantic retrieval, and clustering for brief news texts. The dataset stresses models’ ability to capture fine-grained topical distinctions in short, noisy Chinese content.

TRECCOVID-PL is a passage-level subset of the TREC-COVID retrieval benchmark included in MTEB. It contains COVID-19–related queries (topics) paired with human relevance judgments over scientific articles and extracted passages, enabling evaluation of semantic retrieval, reranking, and embedding-based search models on pandemic-era biomedical literature. The dataset is intended for benchmarking embedding quality on real-world, domain-specific information needs.

MTEB ThuNewsClusteringP2P is a Chinese news clustering dataset from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that provides news documents with pairwise annotations indicating whether two items belong to the same topical cluster. It is designed to evaluate document- and sentence-level embeddings on clustering and pairwise retrieval tasks, measuring how well representations separate topical groups in the news domain. The dataset is commonly used to benchmark clustering quality (e.g., pairwise F1, ARI) and to develop/topic-aware embedding models for Chinese text.

ThuNewsClusteringS2S is an MTEB benchmark dataset for evaluating text embeddings on news clustering formulated as a sequence-to-sequence task. It draws from the THU News corpus and groups Chinese news articles into topical clusters, providing inputs paired with target cluster identifiers or representative texts. The dataset is designed to assess semantic grouping, clustering quality, and embedding suitability for short-to-medium news pieces, supporting both unsupervised clustering evaluation and supervised sequence-to-sequence approaches for topic assignment or cluster summarization.

MTEB VideoRetrieval is a benchmark task within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that evaluates cross-modal embedding quality for video retrieval. It contains collections of short video clips paired with textual queries or captions and measures how well embedding models retrieve relevant videos given text (and vice versa) using rank-based metrics (e.g., recall@K, MRR). The task is intended to assess and compare joint text–video and cross-modal encoders for applications like text-to-video search, video recommendation, and multimodal representation learning.

MTEB Waimai is a domain-specific dataset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark containing Chinese food-delivery (waimai) user-generated texts—such as short reviews, queries and order comments—with relevance and label annotations. It is designed to evaluate text embedding models on domain-adapted tasks like semantic retrieval, clustering and classification in noisy, colloquial short-text scenarios. The dataset stresses robustness and semantic discrimination for embeddings applied to e-commerce and conversational food-delivery applications.

MTEB GerDaLIR is a German-language information retrieval dataset within the Massively Multilingual/Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) designed to evaluate embedding models on document- and passage-level retrieval. It contains German queries paired with candidate documents or passages and relevance judgments across diverse domains, enabling assessment of semantic search and ranking performance. The dataset supports evaluation of dense retrieval, embedding-based similarity, and reranking methods, helping measure model quality and generalization on German IR tasks.

MTEB GermanDPR is a German-language dense retrieval benchmark in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It provides German queries paired with relevant passages and relevance annotations to evaluate semantic search and dense passage retrieval systems. The dataset is intended to assess and compare embedding models and retrieval architectures on German information-seeking tasks, supporting training and benchmarking of embedding-based retrievers and re-rankers.

MTEB MIRACL is a multilingual information retrieval dataset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark containing query–document pairs with human relevance labels across many languages. It is designed to evaluate embedding-based semantic search and retrieval models in monolingual and cross-lingual settings, measuring retrieval quality and cross-language generalization of text embeddings.

MTEB WikiCLIR is a cross-lingual information retrieval dataset derived from Wikipedia, providing query–document relevance pairs across multiple languages. It is designed to evaluate multilingual and cross-lingual embedding and retrieval models by testing their ability to match queries in one language to relevant Wikipedia passages or articles in another. WikiCLIR supports benchmarking of zero-shot and supervised retrieval, semantic search, and cross-lingual transfer, enabling comparison of embeddings’ multilingual alignment and retrieval effectiveness on realistic encyclopedic content.

MTEB XMarket is a multilingual e-commerce retrieval dataset containing aligned product titles and descriptions from multiple marketplaces and languages. It provides paired and matched product records across categories and locales to evaluate sentence and document embeddings on cross-lingual semantic search, retrieval/ranking, and product matching tasks. XMarket is intended to benchmark embedding models’ ability to generalize across languages and real-world e-commerce distributions.

MTEB NewsClassification is a benchmark dataset of news texts paired with topical labels, created to evaluate the quality of text embeddings for news topic classification. It enables assessment of embedding models using classification and retrieval-style protocols (e.g., linear probing or k-NN), measuring how well representations separate topical categories and support downstream tasks such as topic detection, clustering, and content-based routing. The dataset serves as a standardized testbed for comparing embedding methods on real-world news content and their ability to generalize across diverse news domains.

MTEB ArxivClassification (default) is a multiclass classification dataset of arXiv papers that pairs paper titles and/or abstracts with their arXiv subject category labels. It is intended to evaluate text embedding models on topical discrimination and downstream classification (e.g., k-NN or linear classifiers) and retrieval tasks. The data spans diverse scientific disciplines with domain-specific language, making it useful for assessing embedding quality and generalization on scholarly text.

MTEB CUADAffiliateLicenseLicenseeLegalBenchClassification is a legal-domain classification dataset derived from the CUAD contract corpus, with clauses and text spans labeled for whether they pertain to affiliate licensing or licensee-related obligations. It is intended to train and evaluate embedding models and classifiers on fine-grained legal clause identification and relation detection, supporting tasks such as contract review, compliance monitoring, semantic search and clustering. Provided as the default MTEB split, the dataset offers supervised examples for benchmarking model performance on legal semantic understanding.

MTEB CUADAffiliateLicenseLicensorLegalBenchClassification is a legal-domain classification dataset consisting of contract clause excerpts labeled by whether they pertain to affiliates, license provisions, or licensors. Designed for use in the MTEB benchmark, it supports supervised training and evaluation of embedding and classification models for clause identification, role detection, and semantic retrieval in contracts. The dataset is useful for contract analytics, compliance checks, due diligence automation, and benchmarking legal NLP models on fine-grained clause-level distinctions.

MTEB CUADAntiAssignmentLegalBenchClassification (default) is a binary classification dataset derived from the CUAD contract-understanding corpus that focuses on detecting anti-assignment clauses. It provides contract clause excerpts labeled as containing or not containing an anti-assignment provision, designed to evaluate text-embedding methods and downstream classifiers in the legal domain. The set is intended for benchmarking semantic representation quality, few-shot and supervised classification performance, and robustness of models on contract clause identification tasks.

MTEB CUADAuditRightsLegalBenchClassification is a legal-domain text classification dataset of contract clauses and legal passages annotated for the presence and type of audit-rights provisions. It is designed to evaluate embeddings and classifiers on fine-grained legal clause recognition and compliance-related labeling, supporting tasks such as contract review, audit-right detection, and legal information retrieval. The dataset is provided with default train/validation/test splits for standardized benchmarking within the MTEB suite.

MTEB CUADCapOnLiabilityLegalBenchClassification is a legal-domain classification dataset derived from CUAD/LegalBench that focuses on identifying "cap on liability" clauses in contracts. Each instance pairs a contractual clause with a label indicating the presence (or category) of a liability cap. The dataset is designed to train and evaluate text embedding and classification models for clause detection, contract review automation, and legal risk assessment, offering a domain-specific benchmark for model performance and generalization.

CUAD ChangeOfControl (MTEB LegalBench — classification) is a binary text-classification dataset of contract clause excerpts labeled for the presence of "change of control" provisions. Each example pairs a clause text from real-world contracts with a label indicating whether it constitutes a change-of-control clause. It is intended to benchmark embedding and classification models on legal-domain clause identification, supporting development and evaluation of automated contract review, compliance screening, and risk‑assessment systems.

MTEB CUADCompetitiveRestrictionExceptionLegalBenchClassification is a sentence-level classification dataset derived from the CUAD contract corpus and included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). Each example pairs a contract clause with a label indicating whether it represents a competitive-restriction exception. The dataset evaluates embedding and classification models on domain-specific legal language, testing their ability to identify restrictive clauses and exceptions in contracts. It is useful for benchmarking legal NLP models and for applications in contract review, compliance checking, and automated clause tagging.

MTEB CUAD CovenantNotToSue LegalBench Classification is a legal-domain text classification dataset derived from the CUAD contract-understanding collection and adapted for the MTEB benchmark. It contains contract clauses and short excerpts labeled for the presence (or absence) of a “covenant not to sue” clause, enabling binary supervised classification. The dataset is intended to evaluate embedding and classifier models’ ability to capture fine-grained legal semantics, handle domain-specific vocabulary, and generalize across varied contract phrasing for downstream legal NLP tasks.

MTEB CUADEffectiveDateLegalBenchClassification (default) is a legal-domain binary classification dataset derived from the CUAD contract-understanding corpus. It contains contract clauses and sentence-level excerpts labeled for whether they express an effective date clause, provided with default train/validation/test splits. The set is intended for evaluating and training embedding-based classifiers, semantic retrieval, and other legal NLP models on the task of detecting effective-date provisions in contracts.

MTEB CUADExclusivityLegalBenchClassification (default) is a legal-domain classification benchmark that evaluates text embeddings on the task of detecting and categorizing exclusivity-related content in contract clauses and short legal texts. It pairs clause-level text with exclusivity labels, enabling assessment of embedding quality via embedding-based classifiers (k-NN, linear probes) or downstream supervised models. The dataset is intended for benchmarking and developing models for contract clause classification, legal review automation, and retrieval/triage in contract analysis workflows.

MTEB CUADExpirationDateLegalBenchClassification (default) is a legal-domain classification benchmark derived from CUAD within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains contract clause texts labeled for the presence and type of expiration/termination date information, and is intended to evaluate embedding and classification models on their ability to detect and categorize expiration-date related clauses in contracts. The task supports development of contract analysis, clause extraction, and compliance automation tools in legal NLP.

MTEB CUADGoverningLawLegalBenchClassification is a legal clause classification dataset derived from CUAD/LegalBench that focuses on identifying "governing law" clauses in contracts. Each example is a contract sentence or passage labeled for the presence of a governing-law clause, enabling supervised training and evaluation of embedding-based classifiers and retrieval models on domain-specific legal language. It is intended for benchmarking semantic representations and downstream tasks like contract analysis, compliance checking, and legal information extraction.

Part of the MTEB suite, CUAD IP Ownership Assignment (LegalBench Classification, default) is a legal-domain clause-level classification dataset derived from the Contract Understanding Atticus Dataset (CUAD). It contains contract clauses annotated for how intellectual property ownership or assignment is handled (e.g., assignment to a party, retention, license-only, joint ownership). Designed to evaluate and train embedding models and classifiers on fine-grained semantic distinctions in contractual language, it supports benchmarking of clause-level legal understanding and contract analysis tasks.

MTEB CUADInsuranceLegalBenchClassification is a classification benchmark combining legal and insurance domain texts—including contract clauses and insurance-related excerpts—annotated with categorical labels. It is designed to evaluate text-embedding models on domain-specific classification tasks such as clause identification, policy/claim categorization, and legal topic labeling. The dataset emphasizes real-world legal language and domain terminology, enabling assessment of embedding quality for downstream supervised classifiers and similarity-based retrieval in legal and insurance applications.

MTEB CUAD IrrevocableOrPerpetualLicense LegalBench Classification is a clause-level legal classification dataset derived from the CUAD contract-annotation corpus and integrated into MTEB. Each example pairs a contract clause with a binary label indicating whether it expresses an irrevocable or perpetual license. It is intended to evaluate and train embeddings and classifiers for legal language understanding, contract clause detection, and downstream retrieval or compliance applications.

CUADJointIPOwnershipLegalBenchClassification is a clause-level legal classification dataset combining CUAD and LegalBench resources to identify intellectual property (IP) ownership provisions in contracts. It pairs contract clause text with labels indicating joint ownership, assignment, exclusive ownership, or other IP-related statuses, enabling supervised training and evaluation of models for clause detection, contract review, and automated due diligence. Designed for benchmarking legal-domain embeddings and classifiers, it supports development of tools for IP ownership recognition, risk assessment, and contract analysis.

MTEB CUADLicenseGrantLegalBenchClassification (default) is a supervised classification dataset derived from CUAD that focuses on identifying license‑grant clauses in legal contracts. Each example pairs a clause text with labels indicating the presence and type of license grant, enabling evaluation of embeddings and downstream classifiers on legal clause understanding. It is intended for benchmarking semantic representations and model performance on domain‑specific, contract‑level classification tasks.

MTEB CUADLiquidatedDamagesLegalBenchClassification is a legal clause classification dataset derived from CUAD, containing contract clause texts labeled for the presence or absence of liquidated damages provisions. It is intended for evaluating and training text embeddings and classifiers in the legal domain, supporting contract analysis, clause retrieval, and automated identification of liquidated damages language. Expert annotations make it suitable for benchmarking semantic representations and fine-tuning models for contract understanding and information extraction.

CUADMinimumCommitmentLegalBenchClassification is a legal-domain text classification benchmark derived from the CUAD contract-understanding dataset, focusing on identifying clauses that indicate "minimum commitment" obligations. It provides labeled contract clauses for supervised evaluation of embedding and classification models in legal NLP, testing models' ability to discriminate clause types and capture contract-specific semantics under the MTEB default evaluation setup.

MTEB CUADMostFavoredNationLegalBenchClassification is a legal-domain text classification dataset derived from CUAD annotations for detecting and classifying "Most Favored Nation" (MFN) clauses in contracts. It contains contract excerpts labeled for presence and type of MFN language, enabling evaluation of embedding models and classifiers on fine-grained legal clause identification, semantic understanding, and contract analysis tasks.

MTEB CUADNoSolicitOfCustomersLegalBenchClassification is a binary classification dataset derived from the CUAD contract-understanding corpus, containing contract clauses labeled for the presence or absence of "no solicitation of customers" provisions. It pairs clause text with binary labels to support training and evaluation of embedding- and classifier-based models for legal clause detection. The dataset targets challenges of legal-domain language, paraphrasing, and subtle contextual cues relevant to compliance, due diligence, and contract review tasks.

MTEB CUADNoSolicitOfEmployeesLegalBenchClassification (default) is a binary classification dataset derived from the CUAD contract corpus, labeled for clauses that prohibit solicitation of employees. It is designed to evaluate and train embedding and classification models on detecting no-solicit-of-employees provisions in contractual language, supporting legal NLP tasks such as automated contract review, clause extraction, and compliance checking. The dataset focuses on domain-specific phrasing and legal nuance to test model robustness on real-world contract text.

MTEB CUADNonCompeteLegalBenchClassification is a legal text classification dataset derived from contract clause annotations, focusing on identifying and classifying non-compete (restrictive covenant) clauses. It provides contract excerpts labeled for the presence and/or type of non-compete provisions to support supervised evaluation of embedding-based classifiers and representation models in the legal domain. The benchmark is intended for assessing model performance on domain-specific clause detection, compliance automation, and legal document analysis tasks requiring robust semantic understanding of contractual language.

A labeled English dataset of contract clauses for binary classification of non-disparagement provisions. Each example pairs a clause excerpt with a label indicating whether it constitutes a non-disparagement clause, enabling supervised training and evaluation of legal NLP models. Intended for embedding and classification benchmarks, it supports tasks like contract review, compliance checks, and semantic search in legal document pipelines.

MTEB CUADNonTransferableLicenseLegalBenchClassification (default) is a clause-level legal classification dataset derived from CUAD/LegalBench. It contains short contract clauses annotated with a binary label indicating whether the clause expresses a non-transferable license. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating text-embedding models and classifiers on legal clause detection, contract review, and compliance tasks, supporting supervised learning, benchmarking, and downstream retrieval or NLP pipelines in the legal domain.

MTEB CUADNoticePeriodToTerminateRenewalLegalBenchClassification is a supervised legal-clause classification dataset derived from the CUAD contract corpus, focused on clauses that specify notice periods to terminate or renew agreements. Each example pairs a contract clause with a label indicating whether and how it describes notice requirements for termination/renewal, enabling training and evaluation of classifiers and embedding models on fine-grained contractual language. It is intended for benchmarking legal NLP tasks such as clause detection, contract review automation, and semantic embedding quality in the domain of contracts.

MTEB CUADPostTerminationServicesLegalBenchClassification is a legal-domain clause classification dataset derived from the CUAD contract-understanding corpus. It contains contract clauses annotated for the presence and type of post‑termination services/obligations, enabling binary or multi‑class classification of clauses relating to post‑termination support, transition, and related services. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating NLP models and embedding-based classifiers on contract clause identification and legal-domain generalization.

CUADPriceRestrictionsLegalBenchClassification is a legal-domain classification dataset from MTEB that contains contract clauses annotated for the presence of price restriction provisions (e.g., price floors, ceilings, discount or pricing constraints). It is designed for supervised learning and evaluation of models that detect and classify clause types in contracts, supporting tasks such as automated contract review, clause extraction, and embedding-based retrieval or similarity benchmarking in the legal/contractual domain.

CUADRenewalTermLegalBenchClassification (default) is a legal-domain classification dataset derived from the CUAD contract-understanding corpus and included in the MTEB benchmark. It contains contract clause excerpts annotated for the presence and type of renewal/renewal-term provisions (e.g., automatic renewal, fixed-term renewal), enabling supervised training and evaluation of NLP models for clause detection and classification. The dataset supports development of embedding- and classifier-based systems for contract review, due diligence, and automated extraction of renewal-related obligations.

MTEB CUADRevenueProfitSharingLegalBenchClassification is a legal-domain classification dataset derived from the CUAD contract-understanding corpus, focused on identifying and categorizing clauses related to revenue and profit-sharing. It contains contract excerpts labeled for the presence and type of revenue/profit-sharing provisions, designed to evaluate and train models for clause classification, retrieval, and embedding-based similarity tasks. The dataset is suited for benchmarking text embedding and classification systems on fine-grained legal language understanding, contract review automation, and due-diligence workflows.

MTEB CUADRofrRofoRofnLegalBenchClassification is a legal-domain text classification subset in the MTEB benchmark that pairs contract clauses and legal passages with categorical labels for clause types or legal issues. It is designed to evaluate embedding models’ ability to capture fine-grained legal semantics for downstream supervised classification, retrieval, and clustering tasks. The dataset emphasizes domain-specific vocabulary and subtle contextual distinctions, making it useful for benchmarking representation quality and generalization of models in legal NLP applications.

MTEB CUADSourceCodeEscrowLegalBenchClassification (default) is a classification dataset derived from the CUAD contract-understanding benchmark that focuses on identifying source-code-escrow clauses in legal contracts. Each example pairs a contract paragraph or clause span with labels indicating the presence (or absence) and type of source-code-escrow provisions, enabling supervised training and evaluation of models for clause classification, contract review automation, and legal information retrieval. It is intended for benchmarking embedding and classification models on legal-domain clause detection and compliance tasks.

MTEB CUADTerminationForConvenienceLegalBenchClassification is a legal clause classification dataset drawn from the CUAD contract-annotation corpus and packaged for the MTEB benchmark. It contains contract excerpts labeled for the presence/type of “termination for convenience” provisions, enabling evaluation of embedding models and classifiers on fine-grained legal clause identification. The dataset is intended for benchmarking supervised classification, semantic search, and contract-review systems that must detect and differentiate termination-for-convenience language from other contractual clauses.

MTEB CUADThirdPartyBeneficiaryLegalBenchClassification is a legal clause classification dataset derived from the CUAD corpus, containing contract clause texts labeled for whether they establish third‑party beneficiary rights. It is intended for training and evaluating embedding models and classifiers on domain‑specific legal language, supporting clause detection, contract review automation, and benchmarking model performance on fine‑grained legal concept recognition and retrieval tasks.

MTEB CUADUncappedLiabilityLegalBenchClassification is a binary classification dataset of contract clauses drawn from the CUAD corpus, annotated for the presence of uncapped liability language (clauses that do not limit damages). It provides real-world English contract excerpts labeled positive/negative for uncapped liability to benchmark text-embedding and classification models under the MTEB framework. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating models for legal clause detection, automated contract review, risk triage, and embedding-based retrieval in the contracts domain.

MTEB CUADUnlimitedAllYouCanEatLicenseLegalBenchClassification (default) is a legal-domain text classification dataset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark derived from contract and license documents. It contains clause-level and short-text excerpts labeled by legal category or issue, intended to evaluate embedding quality and classifiers on fine-grained legal understanding. The set is useful for benchmarking representation models on legal clause classification, contract review automation, compliance checking, and other downstream legal-NLP tasks.

MTEB CUADVolumeRestrictionLegalBenchClassification is a legal-text classification dataset derived from the CUAD contract corpus and included in the MTEB suite. It contains contract excerpts labeled for the presence and type of volume-restriction clauses (e.g., minimum/maximum purchase obligations, volume caps, or related quantity limits). The dataset is intended to train and evaluate embedding-based classifiers and retrieval systems for clause detection, compliance screening, and contract analytics, serving as a benchmark for model performance on legal-domain classification tasks involving volume-related contractual constraints.

MTEB CUADWarrantyDurationLegalBenchClassification is a legal text classification dataset derived from the CUAD contract-understanding collection, annotated for warranty-duration information. It contains contract clause excerpts labeled by whether and how a warranty period is specified (e.g., fixed term, lifetime, unspecified), enabling supervised training and evaluation of classifiers and embedding models on fine-grained legal-language distinctions. The dataset is intended for benchmarking model performance in legal clause identification, extraction of contractual temporal constraints, and assessing semantic representation quality in downstream legal NLP tasks.

MTEB CanadaTaxCourtOutcomesLegalBenchClassification is a supervised classification dataset of Canada Tax Court decisions, containing court opinions and associated metadata paired with outcome labels (e.g., taxpayer vs. Crown outcome or judgment categories). It is designed to evaluate and benchmark text embeddings and classifiers on legal-domain tasks, testing models’ ability to capture outcome-relevant semantics from judicial language. The dataset supports development of legal NLP models for outcome prediction, case summarization, and domain-specific retrieval or clustering.

MTEB ContractNLIConfidentialityOfAgreementLegalBenchClassification is an NLI-style classification dataset of contract clauses annotated for their relationship to a confidentiality-of-agreement hypothesis. Each example pairs a clause with a label (entailment/contradiction/neutral) indicating whether the clause asserts, negates, or is unrelated to confidentiality obligations. It is designed to evaluate and train models on legal semantic inference, clause detection, and domain-specific understanding for contract analysis and compliance automation.

A classification dataset drawn from legal contracts for evaluating explicit identification in contract NLI tasks. It contains clauses or sentence pairs annotated with multi-class labels (e.g., entailment/neutral/contradiction or explicit/non‑explicit) that indicate whether a target attribute, obligation, or party is explicitly stated. Designed for training and benchmarking models on legal natural language inference, clause identification, and embedding-based classification or retrieval, it supports development of systems for contract analysis, compliance checking, and automated clause extraction.

MTEB ContractNLI–InclusionOfVerballyConveyedInformation is a legal-domain, NLI-style classification dataset of contract clauses annotated for whether they express or entail the inclusion of verbally conveyed information. Designed for evaluating embeddings and classification models on fine-grained contract understanding, it supports binary/NLI label supervision to test model ability to detect references to spoken communications in contractual text. It is useful for contract review, compliance screening, and benchmarking semantic understanding in legal NLP.

MTEB ContractNLILimitedUseLegalBenchClassification is a legal-domain natural language inference (NLI) classification dataset of contract clause pairs labeled for entailment, contradiction, or neutral. It is designed to benchmark embedding and classification models on semantic inference and reasoning over contractual language, supporting evaluation of domain adaptation, clause-level understanding, and robustness in legal NLP. Note: access and use are restricted under limited-use/licensing terms due to data sensitivity.

MTEB ContractNLINoLicensingLegalBenchClassification is a legal-domain NLI classification dataset of premise–hypothesis pairs derived from contract text, labeled for entailment, contradiction, or neutrality. Built as part of the MTEB LegalBench suite, it evaluates sentence-embedding models and NLI classifiers on fine-grained semantic reasoning over contractual language. The dataset is intended for benchmarking domain-adapted embeddings and downstream tasks such as clause matching, compliance checking, and contract understanding.

ContractNLINoticeOnCompelledDisclosureLegalBenchClassification is a legal-domain NLI classification dataset from the MTEB suite containing contract notices or clauses about compelled disclosure paired with hypotheses, annotated for entailment/contradiction/neutral. It is designed to evaluate text-embedding and classification models on legal reasoning and compliance-related inference, supporting benchmarking for contract interpretation, compelled-disclosure detection, and downstream legal NLP tasks such as compliance automation and legal question answering.

MTEB ContractNLIPermissibleAcquirementOfSimilarInformationLegalBenchClassification is a legal NLI-style classification dataset composed of contract clauses paired with candidate information-seeking statements and expert labels indicating whether acquiring similar information is permitted by the contract. It is intended to train and benchmark models on contractual entailment and compliance reasoning (e.g., permissible/impermissible/uncertain), using realistic contractual language and annotations to evaluate performance on legal decision-making, contract automation, and compliance-checking tasks.

MTEB ContractNLIPermissibleCopyLegalBenchClassification is a legal NLI classification dataset that pairs contract clauses with candidate copy text and labels indicating whether copying that text is permissible under the contract terms. Designed for supervised training and evaluation of models on contract compliance and clause interpretation, it supports binary or multi-class inference of permissibility (e.g., permissible, impermissible, conditional). The dataset is intended to benchmark embedding and classification models for automated contract review, compliance checking, and legal-language understanding.

MTEB ContractNLIPermissibleDevelopmentOfSimilarInformationLegalBenchClassification (default) is a legal NLI sentence-pair classification dataset derived from contract text. Each example pairs a contract clause with a hypothesis about whether the clause permits development of similar information; labels indicate permit/forbid/inconclusive (entailment/contradiction/neutral). It is designed to evaluate text embedding models and classifiers on fine-grained legal inference, contract compliance decisions, and domain adaptation for automated contract review and legal QA.

MTEB ContractNLIPermissiblePostAgreementPossessionLegalBenchClassification is a legal natural language inference classification dataset of contract clause–hypothesis pairs focused on permissible post‑agreement possession. Each example pairs a contractual provision with a hypothesis about whether post‑agreement possession is allowed, labeled (entailment/contradiction/neutral) to indicate whether the contract text supports, forbids, or leaves the hypothesis undetermined. Curated from contract language with manual annotations, it is intended for evaluating and fine‑tuning embedding models and sentence‑pair classifiers on legal contract reasoning, rights/obligations extraction, and robustness in juridical NLI tasks.

A legal NLI classification dataset of contract clauses focused on the “return of confidential information” obligation. Each example pairs a contract clause (premise) with a hypothesis about whether the clause requires return or destruction of confidential information and is labeled for entailment (entails / neutral / contradict) or equivalent binary obligation labels. Designed for training and evaluating NLI, text-embedding, and classification models in the legal domain, it supports tasks like clause identification, contract review, and automated compliance detection.

MTEB ContractNLISharingWithEmployeesLegalBenchClassification (default) is a legal-domain NLI classification dataset containing contract clauses paired with hypotheses about whether information may be shared with employees. Each example is labeled to indicate entailment, contradiction, or neutrality with respect to the hypothesis (i.e., whether the clause permits, forbids, or does not address sharing with employees). It is intended for evaluating and training embedding and classification models on contract understanding, compliance checking, and legal information extraction.

A supervised classification benchmark of contract clauses labeled for whether they permit, prohibit, or are ambiguous about sharing information with third parties. Designed to evaluate and fine-tune embedding and classification models on fine-grained legal language and contract intent, it supports tasks such as contract review, compliance detection, and legal NLI by measuring model ability to discern permissions and restrictions in contractual text.

MTEB ContractNLISurvivalOfObligationsLegalBenchClassification (default) is a legal-domain natural language inference classification dataset of contract clause–hypothesis pairs labeled to indicate whether an obligation survives contract termination (e.g., entailment/contradiction/neutral or binary survive/not). It is designed to train and evaluate sentence-embedding, NLI and classification models on fine-grained legal reasoning about obligation scope, temporal effects and clause interpretation. The benchmark targets practical contract-review and compliance automation scenarios, assessing models’ ability to capture legal entailment and post‑termination obligations.

MTEB CorporateLobbyingLegalBenchClassification is a supervised text classification dataset of corporate lobbying and legal documents labeled by topic and legal/regulatory category. It contains real-world disclosures, filings, and policy-related texts annotated for issue area, lobbying target, and compliance or legal stance, enabling evaluation of embedding and classification models on domain-specific legal language. The dataset is intended for benchmarking model performance on fine-grained legal-topic classification, domain adaptation, and robustness in regulatory and public-policy contexts.

MTEB CyrillicTurkicLangClassification (default) is a multiclass text classification dataset of short Cyrillic-script texts labeled by Turkic language (e.g., Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Tatar, Bashkir). It is designed to evaluate embedding models’ ability to discriminate closely related languages and script-specific variants, using standard classification metrics (accuracy, F1). The dataset is suited for benchmarking multilingual and cross-lingual embeddings, language identification systems, and transfer learning methods for low-resource Turkic languages.

MTEB DBpediaClassification (default) is a multi-class text classification dataset of Wikipedia article abstracts mapped to DBpedia ontology labels (commonly 14 classes such as Company, Artist, Film, etc.). It is included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark to evaluate embedding models on semantic separation and downstream classification performance using short, encyclopedic descriptions. The dataset is suited for assessing representation quality for classification, retrieval, and clustering tasks in a structured knowledge-domain setting.

MTEB DefinitionClassificationLegalBenchClassification (default) is a benchmark dataset in the legal domain for classifying definitional text. It comprises legal sentences and clauses paired with labels that indicate whether a segment is a formal definition (and/or its definitional subtype), enabling evaluation of sentence-embedding models on fine-grained semantic discrimination in legal language. The set is intended for supervised and embedding-based classification evaluations (e.g., accuracy, F1) to measure how well representations capture definitional semantics in legal texts.

MTEB Diversity1LegalBenchClassification (default) is a benchmark dataset within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) focused on legal-domain classification. It contains a diverse collection of legal texts—case summaries, statutes, and regulatory passages—paired with categorical labels spanning common legal topics and issue types. Designed to evaluate embedding models on supervised and similarity-based classification tasks, it supports binary and multi-class evaluation under the MTEB default protocol. The dataset highlights model ability to capture nuanced legal semantics and generalize across jurisdictions and document styles, making it suitable for comparing embedding quality for downstream legal NLP applications.

MTEB Diversity2LegalBenchClassification (default) is a benchmark dataset of legal texts labeled across diverse legal categories, designed to evaluate text embedding models on supervised classification tasks in the legal domain. It provides standardized train/validation/test splits and a variety of label types to test embedding quality and downstream classifier performance (e.g., accuracy, F1) on domain-specific legal classification problems. This dataset is intended for benchmarking and comparing embedding and representation methods on real-world legal document classification.

MTEB Diversity3LegalBenchClassification (default) is a benchmark subset from the MTEB suite for evaluating text embeddings and classifiers on legal-domain classification tasks. It contains diverse legal texts—such as case summaries, filings, and statutes—paired with categorical labels covering topics, outcomes, or legal categories, with variation in label granularity and document length. Designed to measure representation quality and robustness of embedding and classification models in legal NLP, it supports model comparison, selection, and fine-tuning for downstream legal classification applications.

MTEB Diversity4LegalBenchClassification (default) is a legal-domain text classification benchmark within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark suite. It comprises diverse legal documents (e.g., case summaries, statutes, contracts, queries) across jurisdictions and label granularities to evaluate how well embeddings support downstream supervised classification. The dataset emphasizes domain-specific vocabulary, long and structured texts, and fine-grained class distinctions, enabling comparison of embedding models using standard metrics such as accuracy and F1.

MTEB Diversity5LegalBenchClassification (default) is a benchmark suite within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark focused on legal-domain text classification. It aggregates five diverse legal classification tasks covering different document types and topical areas, each consisting of legal texts paired with class labels to evaluate downstream classification performance. The suite is used to compare embedding models on their ability to represent specialized legal language for supervised classification (and related retrieval/nearest-neighbor setups) under MTEB’s default evaluation protocol, typically using metrics like accuracy and F1. It is intended to assess model generalization and suitability for legal NLP applications such as document triage, issue tagging, and automated labeling.

MTEB Diversity6LegalBenchClassification (default) is a collection of six diverse legal-domain text classification tasks within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, assembled to evaluate embedding models on legal NLP challenges. It contains labeled legal documents spanning multiple jurisdictions and categories (e.g., document type, topic, or outcome), enabling evaluation of semantic representations via k-NN, linear-probe, and zero-shot classification protocols. The benchmark measures embedding quality for legal-topic detection and document-level classification, supporting development and comparison of models tailored to legal applications.

MTEB FinancialPhrasebankClassification is a sentence-level classification dataset drawn from the Financial Phrasebank, consisting of short financial news and analyst phrases labeled for sentiment (positive, negative, neutral). Included in the MTEB benchmark to evaluate and compare sentence embeddings and classification models on domain-specific financial language, it tests models’ ability to capture nuanced sentiment and terminology in concise financial text.
