Miracl (en) is the English subset of the MIRACL multilingual information retrieval benchmark. It provides English queries paired with candidate passages/documents and gold relevance annotations for supervised training and evaluation of retrieval and ranking systems. The split is intended for benchmarking dense and sparse retrieval models, rerankers, and cross-lingual transfer when used alongside other language slices, enabling evaluation of retrieval accuracy and robustness on diverse, real-world queries.

MIRACL (ar) is the Arabic portion of the MIRACL multilingual information retrieval benchmark, containing Arabic queries paired with candidate passages/documents and human relevance labels. It is designed to evaluate monolingual and cross-lingual retrieval and reranking methods, including sparse and dense retrieval models and zero-shot transfer. The collection covers diverse topics and includes standard train/validation/test splits and relevance judgments to enable reproducible comparison of retrieval systems on Arabic-language search tasks.

Miracl (bn) is a Bengali-language subset of the MIRACL multilingual image–text benchmark containing images paired with Bengali captions. It is designed for cross-modal retrieval and multilingual multimodal representation learning, enabling evaluation of image-to-text and text-to-image retrieval, captioning transfer, and cross-lingual alignment for Bengali. The dataset supports development and benchmarking of models that must understand and align visual content with Bengali language descriptions, helping assess performance and generalization of multilingual and bilingual vision–language systems.

Miracl (de) is the German-language subset of the MIRACL multilingual image–text retrieval benchmark. It provides curated German image–caption pairs for training and evaluating image-to-text and text-to-image retrieval models, and for measuring cross-lingual and multimodal alignment of visual and textual embeddings. The split supports zero-shot and fine-tuning evaluations using standard retrieval metrics (e.g., R@K, mAP), making it useful for benchmarking and improving German-capable vision–language systems.

Miracl (es) is the Spanish split of the MIRACL multilingual image–text retrieval benchmark, containing images paired with Spanish captions and relevance-annotated queries. It is designed to evaluate and train monolingual and cross-lingual image–text retrieval systems, ranking models, and multimodal representation transfer to Spanish. Miracl (es) supports benchmarking of retrieval accuracy, zero-shot transfer, and fine-tuning of vision–language models on Spanish-language queries and captions.

Miracl (fa) is the Persian (Farsi) subset of the MIRACL multilingual information retrieval benchmark. It pairs natural-language queries with candidate passages/documents annotated for relevance across diverse topics, enabling supervised training and evaluation of retrieval and ranking models in Persian. The split supports dense and sparse retrieval, reranking, and cross-lingual transfer experiments, and is intended for measuring ranking quality (e.g., MRR, nDCG) and model generalization on real-world Persian search tasks.

Miracl (fi) is the Finnish portion of the MIRACL multilingual information-retrieval benchmark. It provides Finnish queries paired with candidate passages and relevance annotations across diverse domains, designed for training and evaluating dense and sparse retrieval, reranking, and cross-lingual transfer. The split supports benchmarking retrieval performance specifically in Finnish and assessing multilingual models for retrieval-augmented QA and end-to-end information-retrieval pipelines.

Miracl (fr) is the French portion of the MIRACL multilingual image-text retrieval benchmark. It pairs images with French captions and retrieval queries to support training and evaluation of text-to-image and image-to-text retrieval models in French, enabling assessment of multilingual and cross-lingual retrieval performance as well as zero-shot transfer. The dataset is suited for developing and benchmarking multimodal retrieval systems using standard metrics such as Recall@K and MRR.

Miracl (hi) is the Hindi subset of the MIRACL multilingual image–text retrieval benchmark, containing images paired with Hindi captions and retrieval queries. It is designed to train and evaluate vision–language models on monolingual and cross-lingual image–text retrieval, zero-shot transfer, and multilingual representation learning for Hindi. The subset supports development of retrieval, captioning, and multimodal understanding systems in Hindi and cross-lingual scenarios.

MIRACL (id) is the Indonesian subset of the MIRACL multilingual information retrieval benchmark. It provides Indonesian queries paired with candidate passages/documents and human relevance judgments for supervised training and evaluation of retrieval and reranking models. MIRACL (id) supports dense and sparse retrieval, cross-lingual transfer evaluation, and benchmarking of model robustness on realistic web and QA-style Indonesian search tasks.

Miracl (ja) is the Japanese subset of the MIRACL multilingual image–text benchmark, containing images paired with Japanese captions (with aligned English references) for cross-lingual evaluation. It is designed for training and evaluating multimodal models on tasks such as image–text retrieval and captioning, enabling assessment of Japanese-language grounding, cross-lingual transfer, and generalization across diverse real-world images and linguistic variations.

Miracl (ko) is the Korean subset of the MIRACL multilingual information retrieval benchmark. It provides Korean queries paired with candidate passages and relevance judgments for evaluating retrieval and reranking models in monolingual and cross-lingual settings. The collection supports supervised training and zero-shot evaluation of dense and sparse retrievers, rerankers, and cross-lingual transfer approaches, enabling standardized benchmarking of Korean-language retrieval performance.

MirACL (ru) is the Russian-language portion of the MIRACL multilingual image–text retrieval benchmark. It pairs images with human-written Russian captions and aligned cross-lingual retrieval queries, enabling evaluation of image–text retrieval, cross-lingual transfer, and multilingual multimodal representation learning for Russian. The split supports supervised training, zero-shot evaluation, and benchmarking of retrieval and captioning models that must handle Russian semantics and cross-language alignment.

MIRACL (sw) is the Swahili subset of the MIRACL multilingual information retrieval benchmark. It provides Swahili queries with corresponding relevance judgments over web passages/documents to support training and evaluation of retrieval and reranking models. The split enables research on monolingual and cross-lingual retrieval for a lower-resource language, facilitating comparison of sparse and dense retrievers, zero-/few-shot transfer, and supervised ranking approaches.

Miracl (te) is the Telugu subset of the MIRACL multilingual information-retrieval benchmark, providing Telugu queries paired with candidate passages/documents annotated for relevance across diverse topics. It is designed for evaluating and training retrieval and re-ranking models (sparse and dense), supporting monolingual Telugu retrieval as well as multilingual and zero-shot cross-lingual transfer experiments.

Miracl (th) is the Thai subset of the MIRACL multilingual image–text retrieval benchmark, comprising images paired with Thai captions aligned to the larger multilingual corpus. It is designed for training and evaluating cross-lingual and monolingual image–text retrieval and multimodal representation models, supporting tasks such as zero-shot transfer, fine-tuning, and evaluation of vision–language alignment for Thai.

Miracl (yo) is the Yoruba subset of the MIRACL multilingual retrieval benchmark, containing queries and labeled candidate passages in Yoruba for training and evaluating information retrieval and reranking models. It is aligned with MIRACL’s cross-lingual collections to support multilingual and zero-shot retrieval experiments, dense and sparse retrieval methods, and evaluation of language-specific and transfer learning approaches in low-resource settings.

MIRACL (zh) is the Chinese-language subset of the MIRACL multilingual image–text retrieval benchmark. It provides images paired with Chinese captions and retrieval queries for training and evaluating image–text retrieval and multimodal models. The dataset covers diverse real-world imagery with natural-language annotations and standard train/validation/test splits and retrieval labels for ranking evaluation. MIRACL (zh) is suited for developing and benchmarking Chinese multimodal retrieval, cross‑lingual transfer, and zero‑shot retrieval methods.

MTEB CEDRClassification is a classification benchmark within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) that contains text pairs (e.g., queries and candidate documents or snippets) labeled for relevance or class membership. It is designed to evaluate embedding models’ ability to discriminate relevant vs. non-relevant texts and to support training and assessment of semantic text classifiers, cross-encoder distillation, and downstream retrieval/reranking workflows. The dataset emphasizes short-to-medium length texts and practical relevance signals to measure embedding quality for classification-oriented tasks.

MTEB GeoreviewClassification is a text classification dataset from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark containing short, geotagged user reviews labeled with location identifiers or region/point-of-interest categories. It is designed to evaluate embedding models’ ability to capture location- and place-related semantics for downstream classification and nearest-neighbor retrieval. The dataset is useful for benchmarking and comparing embedding-based classifiers on location-aware NLP tasks.

MTEB HeadlineClassification is a short-text classification dataset of news headlines paired with topic labels, included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark to evaluate embedding quality on concise, real-world text. It contains headline-length inputs across multiple topical classes (e.g., politics, sports, business), making it suitable for assessing semantic representations in supervised classification, few-shot learning, clustering, and retrieval tasks. The dataset emphasizes robustness of embeddings on brief, noisy natural language typical of news headlines.

MTEB InappropriatenessClassification is a text classification benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) that tests models’ ability to detect inappropriate content in short texts. Instances are labeled for inappropriateness (e.g., offensive, explicit, or otherwise unsuitable) and are intended to evaluate embedding-based methods on binary or multi-class classification tasks. The dataset is used to assess semantic sensitivity to toxic or inappropriate language and to compare models on metrics such as accuracy and F1 in supervised, few-shot, or zero-shot settings.

MTEB KinopoiskClassification is a Russian-language movie classification dataset derived from Kinopoisk that pairs film metadata (titles and short synopses) with genre labels. It is designed to evaluate text-embedding models and classifiers on multi-class and multi-label genre prediction in a domain-specific, colloquial register, enabling benchmarking of representation quality for classification, retrieval, and clustering tasks in Russian movie metadata.

MTEB RUParaPhraserSTS is a Russian semantic textual similarity dataset of sentence pairs annotated for semantic relatedness. Designed for the MTEB benchmark, it focuses on paraphrase and near-paraphrase comparisons in Russian to evaluate sentence embedding models on STS-style correlation, retrieval, and clustering tasks. The dataset supports assessment of models’ ability to capture fine-grained semantic similarity and distinguish paraphrases from unrelated or partially related sentences in real-world language use.

MTEB RuReviewsClassification is a Russian-language review classification dataset used in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It contains short user reviews paired with sentiment labels (e.g., positive/negative/neutral) for products and services, enabling supervised evaluation of semantic representations. The dataset is designed to assess the quality of sentence embeddings and classifiers on sentiment detection in Russian, supporting comparison of embedding models and downstream classification pipelines on real-world review text.

RuSTSBenchmarkSTS (part of MTEB) is a Russian semantic textual similarity dataset comprising sentence pairs annotated with graded human similarity scores. It is designed to evaluate and benchmark sentence and text embedding models on Russian STS by measuring alignment between embedding-based similarity (e.g., cosine) and human judgments. The dataset supports development and comparison of models for semantic search, paraphrase detection, clustering, and retrieval in Russian-language scenarios.

RuSciBenchGRNTIClassification is a Russian-language scientific text classification dataset from the MTEB suite that pairs scientific documents (titles, abstracts, and metadata) with GRNTI subject codes. It is designed to evaluate embeddings and models on domain-specific subject categorization, requiring assignment of one or more GRNTI taxonomy labels per document. The dataset benchmarks model ability to capture fine-grained scientific semantics for downstream tasks such as topic tagging, classification, and domain-aware retrieval.

RuSciBenchOECDClassification is a dataset of Russian scientific documents labeled with OECD thematic categories. It pairs document text (titles and/or abstracts) with standardized OECD subject labels, enabling supervised topic classification (documents may be mapped to one or more categories). The dataset is designed for benchmarking and training text encoders and classifiers on domain-specific topic categorization, supporting evaluation of embedding-based and supervised models within the MTEB suite.

MTEB SensitiveTopicsClassification is a labeled text classification dataset for evaluating models’ ability to detect and discriminate sensitive topics in short text snippets. It contains examples annotated with topic labels representing categories of potentially sensitive content, enabling benchmarking of embedding and classification models on representation quality, topic separability, and content-moderation performance. The dataset is suited for assessing robustness and fairness of text encoders in downstream classification, retrieval, and moderation tasks where handling sensitive subject matter is critical.

MTEB MIRACLRetrieval is a multilingual retrieval benchmark consisting of query–document pairs with labeled relevance across many languages. It is designed to evaluate sentence and passage embedding models on semantic search, dense retrieval, and cross-lingual transfer, covering diverse topics and realistic retrieval scenarios for ranking and zero‑shot multilingual retrieval performance.

MTEB MintakaESRetrieval is a Spanish-language retrieval dataset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark designed for evaluating embedding-based semantic search. It provides query–document pairs with relevance annotations to measure retrieval and ranking performance of sentence and passage embeddings in Spanish. The dataset is intended to benchmark nearest-neighbor search, ranking metrics (e.g., recall and nDCG), and the effectiveness of multilingual or Spanish-tuned embedding models for real-world information access.

SpanishPassageRetrievalS2P (part of MTEB) is a Spanish sentence-to-passage retrieval benchmark containing Spanish query sentences paired with candidate passages and relevance labels. It is designed to evaluate embedding and retrieval models on cross-length semantic matching, measuring ranking and retrieval quality for semantic search and passage-level retrieval in Spanish. The dataset supports development and comparison of multilingual or Spanish-specific embeddings for tasks like semantic search, QA retrieval, and information retrieval.

SpanishPassageRetrievalS2S (MTEB) is a Spanish-language passage retrieval dataset for evaluating embedding-based retrieval models. It provides Spanish queries paired with candidate passages and relevance labels, focusing on sentence-to-sentence retrieval where both queries and targets are in Spanish. The dataset is intended to benchmark and train dense retrieval and embedding models on real-world semantic matching, supporting evaluation of retrieval accuracy, generalization across lexical variation and paraphrase, and downstream use in search and QA systems.

MTEB XMarketES is a Spanish e-commerce dataset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark for evaluating text embeddings on product retrieval and matching. It contains product titles and metadata paired with query–product relevance labels, enabling benchmarking of semantic search, duplicate detection, and product matching in Spanish retail catalogs. The dataset is suited for training and evaluating embedding models and ranking systems that must capture fine-grained commercial semantic similarity and support retrieval and re-ranking tasks.

MTEB XPQAESRetrieval is a cross-lingual retrieval task in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark derived from the XPQA English–Spanish data. It consists of query–document pairs where queries and target passages are in different languages (English ↔ Spanish), designed to evaluate multilingual and cross-lingual sentence embeddings on semantic retrieval. The task benchmarks models’ ability to match semantically equivalent content across languages for zero-shot and supervised retrieval scenarios, supporting research in multilingual representation learning and cross-lingual information retrieval.

MVBench is a comprehensive Multi-modal Video understanding Benchmark. It was introduced to evaluate the comprehension capabilities of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs), particularly their temporal understanding in dynamic video tasks. MVBench covers 20 challenging video tasks that cannot be effectively solved with a single frame. It introduces a novel static-to-dynamic method to define these temporal-related tasks. By transforming various static tasks into dynamic ones, it enables the systematic generation of video tasks that require a broad spectrum of temporal skills, ranging from perception to cognition.

Perception Test is a benchmark designed to evaluate the perception and reasoning skills of multimodal models. It introduces real-world videos designed to show perceptually interesting situations and defines multiple tasks that require understanding of memory, abstract patterns, physics, and semantics – across visual, audio, and text modalities. The benchmark consists of 11.6k videos, 23s average length, filmed by around 100 participants worldwide. The videos are densely annotated with six types of labels: object and point tracks, temporal action and sound segments, multiple-choice video question-answers and grounded video question-answers. The benchmark probes pre-trained models for their transfer capabilities, in a zero-shot / few-shot or fine tuning regime.

MTEB STS22.v2 (ar) is an Arabic semantic textual similarity dataset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It comprises pairs of Arabic sentences annotated with human-graded similarity scores (typically on a continuous scale, e.g., 0–5) and is designed to evaluate the quality of sentence and text embeddings on semantic similarity tasks. The dataset spans naturally occurring language from diverse domains and is used to benchmark embedding models via correlation metrics (e.g., Spearman/Pearson), supporting downstream applications such as semantic search, clustering, and paraphrase detection in Arabic.

STS Benchmark comprises a selection of the English datasets used in the STS tasks organized in the context of SemEval between 2012 and 2017. The selection of datasets include text from image captions, news headlines and user forums. Source:

BCIC-IV-2a-LP is a preprocessed variant of the BCI Competition IV 2a motor-imagery EEG dataset. It provides multi-subject, multi-session recordings of four-class motor imagery (left/right hand, foot, tongue) with trial-level labels and standardized low-pass filtering and epoching. The dataset is intended for benchmarking supervised and transfer-learning methods for EEG decoding, including feature extraction, spatial filtering, and deep learning approaches, and for research on calibration reduction and subject-adaptive brain–computer interface systems.

ArguaAna is an argumentation dataset in the MTEB suite containing topic-labeled claims and user arguments collected from online debate platforms. It provides annotations for relevance and stance (pro/con) and paired examples for similarity and retrieval tasks. Designed to evaluate and train embedding models, ArguaAna is useful for argument retrieval, stance detection, clustering, and other argument-mining applications that require fine-grained semantic and rhetorical understanding.

MTEB STS22.v2 (es-en) is a cross-lingual Semantic Textual Similarity dataset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB), containing Spanish–English sentence pairs annotated with graded similarity scores. It is designed to evaluate multilingual and cross-lingual sentence embeddings on fine-grained semantic equivalence, supporting regression-style scoring and ranking tasks. The dataset is useful for benchmarking embedding models on cross-language semantic understanding, multilingual retrieval, and semantic search applications.

MTEB STS22.v2 (zh-en) is a cross-lingual semantic textual similarity dataset containing Chinese–English sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores. It is designed to evaluate multilingual sentence embedding and retrieval models on their ability to measure meaning similarity across languages, using correlation metrics (e.g., Pearson/Spearman) as primary benchmarks. The set is part of the MTEB benchmark suite and supports development and comparison of cross-lingual representation methods for tasks such as semantic search, clustering, and paraphrase detection.

MTEB STS22.v2 (de-en) is a cross-lingual semantic textual similarity dataset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark containing German–English sentence pairs annotated with human similarity judgments. It provides sentence-level bilingual pairs and continuous similarity scores for evaluating how well multilingual or cross-lingual embeddings capture semantic equivalence. The set is intended for benchmarking embedding models on STS tasks within MTEB and is useful for evaluating representation quality for retrieval, clustering, ranking, and semantic search across German and English.

MTEB STS22.v2 (pl-en) is a cross-lingual semantic textual similarity dataset of Polish–English sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores. Designed to evaluate multilingual sentence embeddings, it measures how well embeddings capture semantic relatedness across languages for tasks like retrieval, clustering, and semantic search. Included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB), it provides a standardized benchmark for assessing cross-lingual representation quality and generalization.

ARC (Challenge) is a dataset designed for common sense reasoning tasks that require models to go beyond pattern recognition and apply world knowledge to make logical inferences. It consists of a collection of challenging, open-ended questions that test a model’s ability to understand real-world contexts, causal relationships, and everyday knowledge. The dataset is primarily composed of natural language questions and answers, drawn from diverse domains to reflect the complexity and variability of human common sense. While not explicitly labeled with large-scale annotations, ARC is used to evaluate and benchmark the reasoning capabilities of language models, particularly in tasks involving implicit understanding, contextual inference, and logical consistency. Its difficulty lies in the absence of explicit training signals, requiring models to rely on internal world knowledge and generalization. ARC serves as a critical benchmark for assessing the progress of large language models in developing human-like reasoning abilities, making it a key resource in the evaluation of generative

MTEB STS22 is the Semantic Textual Similarity subset from the 2022 evaluation included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It provides sentence or short-text pairs annotated with human similarity scores (typically 0–5) and is used to evaluate embedding quality by measuring correlation (e.g., Spearman/Pearson) between embedding-derived similarities and human judgments. The split covers diverse domains to benchmark models’ ability to capture fine-grained semantic similarity.

MTEB STS17 is the STS 2017 portion of the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, consisting of sentence pairs annotated with graded human similarity scores from the SemEval 2017 Semantic Textual Similarity task. It covers multiple domains and language pairs, providing diverse examples for measuring semantic correspondence between short texts. The split is used for evaluation of sentence and text embedding models by computing correlation (e.g., Pearson/Spearman) between embedding-based similarity measures and human judgments, making it a standard benchmark for semantic similarity and cross-lingual representation quality.

MTEB FQuADRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark derived from the French Question Answering Dataset (FQuAD) used within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It casts French QA as a passage retrieval task: natural-language questions in French serve as queries while Wikipedia paragraphs that contain the answer are labeled positives. The dataset evaluates embedding and dense-retrieval models on their ability to rank relevant context passages for QA-style queries using standard retrieval metrics (e.g., recall@k, MRR), making it useful for benchmarking multilingual embeddings, dense retrievers, and cross-lingual retrieval methods on French-language QA.

MTEB SummEvalSummarization.v2 (default) is a summarization benchmark within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that pairs system-generated and reference summaries with human quality annotations. It provides summary pairs and accompanying human judgments across dimensions such as coherence, consistency, relevance and fluency, enabling evaluation of semantic similarity, ranking and correlation with human preferences. The set is intended for assessing and developing embedding-based metrics and models that measure summary quality and semantic fidelity, supporting both retrieval-style and regression/ranking evaluation scenarios.

The **m**inimalist **hist**opathology image analysis dataset (**MHIST**) is a binary classification dataset of 3,152 fixed-size images of colorectal polyps, each with a gold-standard label determined by the majority vote of seven board-certified gastrointestinal pathologists. MHIST also includes each image’s annotator agreement level. As a minimalist dataset, MHIST occupies less than 400 MB of disk space, and a ResNet-18 baseline can be trained to convergence on MHIST in just 6 minutes using approximately 3.5 GB of memory on a NVIDIA RTX 3090. As example use cases, the authors use MHIST to study natural questions that arise in histopathology image classification such as how dataset size, network depth, transfer learning, and high-disagreement examples affect model performance. **PatchCamelyon** is an image classification dataset. It consists of 327.680 color images (96 x 96px) extracted from histopathologic scans of lymph node sections. Each image is annotated with a binary label indicating presence of metastatic tissue. PCam provides a new benchmark for machine learning models: bigger than CIFAR10, smaller than ImageNet, trainable on a single GPU.

The colorectal nuclear segmentation and phenotypes (CoNSeP) dataset consists of 41 H&E stained image tiles, each of size 1,000×1,000 pixels at 40× objective magnification. The images were extracted from 16 colorectal adenocarcinoma (CRA) WSIs, each belonging to an individual patient, and scanned with an Omnyx VL120 scanner within the department of pathology at University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire, UK. Elsafty is a large-scale dataset of Arabic handwritten and scanned document images annotated for OCR and document analysis. It provides line- and word-level transcriptions, character bounding boxes, writer IDs, and page-layout labels collected from diverse writers, instruments, and paper types. Designed for handwriting recognition, writer identification, and layout segmentation, Elsafty includes standard train/validation/test splits and evaluation protocols to benchmark model performance under realistic variability.

MassiveIntentClassification is a large-scale intent classification dataset containing short user queries paired with a very large set of intent labels across many domains. It is designed to evaluate embedding- and classifier-based methods on extreme multi-class intent detection, testing models’ ability to scale to thousands of fine-grained intents, handle label imbalance, and generalize in few-shot or zero-shot settings. The dataset is useful for benchmarking intent retrieval, embedding quality, and end-to-end intent classification systems in practical conversational and query-understanding applications.

MTEB MassiveScenarioClassification is a large-scale benchmark for evaluating text embedding models on scenario-level classification across diverse real-world domains. It contains thousands of labeled texts spanning many scenario categories with varied lengths and class distributions, designed to test generalization, robustness, and cross-domain transfer. The dataset supports supervised, few-shot, and zero-shot evaluation of embedding-based classifiers and serves as a challenging benchmark for comparing representation quality in downstream scenario understanding and domain-adaptation tasks.

EightTagsClustering is a clustering benchmark in the MTEB suite consisting of short texts annotated with eight distinct topic tags. It is designed to evaluate embedding methods’ ability to group semantically similar items without supervision, using clustering metrics (e.g., NMI, ARI) to measure agreement with the eight ground-truth categories. The dataset is useful for assessing representation quality for tasks such as unsupervised topic discovery, cluster-based retrieval, and downstream grouping of short-form textual data.

mMARCO is a multilingual extension of the MS MARCO passage-ranking dataset that provides queries, passages, and relevance labels translated or collected across multiple languages. It is intended for training and evaluating multilingual and cross-lingual retrieval and ranking systems (dense and sparse), enabling research on multilingual encoders, zero-shot transfer, and robustness to language variation in information retrieval tasks.

SciDocs is an evaluation framework designed for assessing document-level representation learning models within the scientific domain. It focuses on learning meaningful representations of scientific documents to capture nuanced semantic relationships beyond explicit citation links. The dataset supports tasks that require understanding document similarity, retrieval, and relatedness, addressing challenges such as continuous similarity measurement and sampling of hard positive and negative examples. SciDocs enables benchmarking of models that leverage contrastive learning objectives to improve scientific document embeddings, facilitating more effective retrieval of related research papers even when direct citations are absent. The framework has been used to demonstrate advances in sample-efficient training and improved performance over state-of-the-art baselines, including models pretrained on general-domain corpora. By emphasizing the subtleties of scientific text similarity and enabling fine-grained evaluation, SciDocs serves as a valuable resource for developing and evaluating representation learning methods tailored to scientific literature analysis and information retrieval.

**HotpotQA** is a question answering dataset collected on the English Wikipedia, containing about 113K crowd-sourced questions that are constructed to require the introduction paragraphs of two Wikipedia articles to answer. Each question in the dataset comes with the two gold paragraphs, as well as a list of sentences in these paragraphs that crowdworkers identify as supporting facts necessary to answer the question. A diverse range of reasoning strategies are featured in HotpotQA, including questions involving missing entities in the question, intersection questions (What satisfies property A and property B?), and comparison questions, where two entities are compared by a common attribute, among others. In the few-document distractor setting, the QA models are given ten paragraphs in which the gold paragraphs are guaranteed to be found; in the open-domain fullwiki setting, the models are only given the question and the entire Wikipedia. Models are evaluated on their answer accuracy and explainability, where the former is measured as overlap between the predicted and gold answers with exact match (EM) and unigram F1, and the latter concerns how well the predicted supporting fact sentences match human annotation (Supporting Fact EM/F1). A joint metric is also reported on this dataset, which encourages systems to perform well on both tasks simultaneously. Source: Image Source:

SciFact is a dataset for automated verification of scientific claims against biomedical literature. It pairs concise scientific claims with PubMed abstracts annotated for whether the abstract supports, refutes, or provides insufficient evidence for the claim, and includes sentence-level rationales that justify each label. SciFact is designed to evaluate and train systems for evidence retrieval, claim-level stance classification, and explainable rationale extraction in the scientific/biomedical domain.

BLESS is a lexical semantic benchmark of noun word pairs labeled with semantic relations (e.g., co-hyponymy/coordinate, hypernymy, meronymy, attribute, and unrelated/random). It was created to evaluate distributional semantic models and supervised classifiers on tasks such as semantic relation classification and hypernym/coordination detection, providing a controlled resource of related and unrelated word pairs for comparing representations and relation-learning methods.

CogALexV is a dataset for lexical semantic change detection that pairs target words with time-stamped contextual examples and human judgments about meaning change. It is designed to evaluate and train algorithms that detect, quantify, and characterize diachronic shifts in word senses, supporting comparative benchmarking of models for sense emergence, shift, and decline over time.

BLESS is a lexical semantic benchmark of noun word pairs labeled with semantic relations (e.g., co-hyponymy/coordinate, hypernymy, meronymy, attribute, and unrelated/random). It was created to evaluate distributional semantic models and supervised classifiers on tasks such as semantic relation classification and hypernym/coordination detection, providing a controlled resource of related and unrelated word pairs for comparing representations and relation-learning methods.

K&H+N is a composite motion-deblurring benchmark that aggregates Köhler (K) and HIDE (H) with Nah et al.’s GoPro (N) dataset. It provides paired blurry–sharp images covering both synthetic kernel-generated blur and real-world dynamic motion blur (including human-centric scenes). The mix of controlled and realistic examples supports supervised training and evaluation of deblurring models, enabling assessment of restoration quality and generalization across diverse blur types and scene contents.

ROOT09 is a benchmark dataset for plant root phenotyping consisting of high-resolution images of root systems paired with pixel-level segmentation masks and morphological trait annotations (e.g., root length, branching points, diameter classes). It is designed to support supervised learning for root segmentation, instance detection, counting, and trait estimation, enabling development and evaluation of end-to-end models for automated root analysis. ROOT09 facilitates research on robustness across soil backgrounds and varying root architectures, aiding plant phenotyping, breeding, and root system modeling.

CodeSearchNet–Python is a large-scale dataset designed for code summarization and programming language understanding. It consists of pairs of Python source code and natural language summaries, enabling models to learn the relationship between code structure and human-readable descriptions. The dataset supports downstream tasks such as automatic code documentation generation and natural language code search. With a diverse range of code samples from real-world software projects, it captures common programming patterns and syntax across various domains. The dataset is particularly valuable for training and evaluating foundation models in code understanding, such as CodeBERT and CodeT5, which leverage pretraining on large-scale code–text pairs to generate accurate, contextually relevant summaries. Due to its scale and real-world relevance, CodeSearchNet–Python serves as a key benchmark for assessing the performance of neural models in code-to-text generation. mMARCO Japanese is a Japanese-language passage ranking and retrieval dataset derived from the MS MARCO corpus. It provides Japanese queries paired with candidate passages and relevance annotations (training labels and evaluation splits) to support supervised training and benchmarking of retrieval, reranking, and QA systems in Japanese. The dataset is intended for developing and evaluating sparse and dense retrieval models, neural rerankers, and end-to-end reading comprehension pipelines on Japanese web-style queries and passages.

AI2 Reasoning Challenge (25-Shot) is a few-shot evaluation set built from the AI2 Reasoning Challenge (ARC) multiple-choice science questions, presented to models with 25 in-context exemplars. It targets grade-school to high-school science problems that require multi-step reasoning, domain knowledge, and commonsense inference beyond retrieval. Each item supplies a question and several answer options; the 25-shot protocol measures a model’s ability to generalize from limited demonstrations and benchmark few-shot reasoning and robust answer selection on challenging science QA.

HellaSwag (10-Shot) is a few-shot variant of the HellaSwag commonsense reasoning benchmark that evaluates a model’s ability to choose the correct narrative continuation given a short context. Each example pairs a context with multiple-choice endings (one correct, several adversarial distractors crafted to be superficially plausible). The 10-shot setup provides ten labeled in-context examples for prompting or fine-tuning, making the task a focused measure of how well models generalize causal, physical, and commonsense reasoning from limited examples.

MMLU (5-Shot) is a broad multi-task evaluation benchmark of multiple‑choice questions covering 57 academic and professional subjects (STEM, humanities, social sciences, etc.), drawn from exams and curricula to test factual knowledge and problem-solving. The 5‑shot variant evaluates few‑shot in‑context learning by providing five exemplar QA pairs per task during inference, measuring a model’s ability to generalize across diverse domains without task-specific fine‑tuning. It yields per-task and aggregate accuracy metrics, serving as a standard challenge for assessing large language models’ breadth of knowledge and reasoning in low‑shot conditions.

Winogrande (5-shot) is a large-scale, crowdsourced benchmark for commonsense pronoun resolution presented in a 5-shot few-shot evaluation setting. Each example asks a model to choose between two candidate antecedents for an ambiguous pronoun, requiring real-world and linguistic commonsense rather than surface cues. The 5-shot variant evaluates in-context or few-shot learners by providing five labeled exemplars before testing, making it useful for measuring few-shot generalization, robustness to spurious patterns, and comparative performance of foundation models on commonsense reasoning.

The MedNLI dataset consists of sentence pairs derived from the Past Medical History section of MIMIC-III clinical notes, annotated by physicians for natural language inference with labels such as Definitely True, Maybe True, and Definitely False. It includes over 11,000 training instances and several thousand development and test examples, providing a benchmark for medical natural language inference tasks grounded in patient history.

FP-Doc Benchmark v1 is a dataset for document forgery detection and localization containing real and synthesized scanned/photographed documents with diverse tampering types (copy-paste, splicing, inpainting, text replacement) and common degradations (compression, noise, lighting). Each sample includes pixel-level manipulation masks, tamper-type labels, OCR transcriptions, and metadata about capture conditions to support multi-task learning. It is designed to train and evaluate models for forgery detection, tamper localization, tamper classification, and robust OCR in adversarial or degraded document scenarios, enabling research in document authentication and forensic analysis.

MTEB MIRACLRetrievalHardNegatives (ar) is an Arabic retrieval benchmark within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that provides queries with corresponding relevant passages and deliberately mined hard-negative passages. It is designed to evaluate and stress-test embedding-based retrieval and ranking models under challenging negative examples that are semantically similar to positives. The dataset supports development and comparison of dense retrieval, contrastive training, and re-ranking systems for Arabic information retrieval tasks.

MTEB MrTydiRetrieval (Arabic) is a retrieval benchmark derived from the Mr.TyDi multilingual QA collection, containing Arabic queries paired with labeled relevant passages. It is designed to evaluate and train dense embedding and semantic-search models on Arabic-language information retrieval tasks, measuring performance with ranking metrics (e.g., MRR, recall). The dataset supports benchmarking cross-lingual and monolingual retrieval capabilities and improving Arabic semantic search and passage-ranking systems.

MTEB MIRACLRetrievalHardNegatives (bn) is a Bengali retrieval dataset from the MIRACL subset of the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that pairs queries with relevant passages and curated hard negative examples. It is designed to evaluate and train dense text embedding and retrieval models on challenging, fine-grained distinctions in Bengali, emphasizing robustness to semantically similar but non-relevant candidates. The dataset is suitable for benchmarking embedding quality, contrastive learning, hard-negative mining, and reranking methods for Bengali information retrieval.

MrTydiRetrieval (Bengali) is a Bengali-language passage retrieval benchmark derived from the Mr.TyDi/TyDi QA corpus. It provides question queries paired with relevant passages and non-relevant negatives, enabling evaluation of dense and sparse retrieval models and sentence/passage embeddings in Bengali. The dataset is intended for measuring retrieval accuracy, ranking quality, and multilingual or cross-lingual generalization on a low-resource language within the MTEB benchmark.

MTEB MIRACLRetrievalHardNegatives (de) is the German subset of the MIRACL retrieval collection within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, containing query–passage pairs augmented with mined hard negative examples. It is designed for training and evaluating embedding-based retrieval and reranking models in German, emphasizing difficult, closely related non-relevant passages to stress-test discrimination and ranking robustness. The split supports contrastive fine-tuning and benchmarking of retrieval performance on challenging real-world German queries.

MIRACLRetrievalHardNegatives (en) is an English retrieval benchmark in the MTEB suite that pairs queries with relevant passages plus challenging non‑relevant (hard negative) examples. It is designed to evaluate and train embedding and dense retrieval models under difficult negative sampling conditions, stressing discrimination between semantically similar but non‑relevant texts. The dataset supports development of contrastive learning, dense retrieval, and re‑ranking systems and helps measure model robustness and ranking quality in realistic retrieval scenarios.

MrTydiRetrieval (English) is an English passage retrieval dataset in the MTEB benchmark derived from the Mr.TyDi collection. It contains natural question-like queries paired with Wikipedia passages and relevance annotations indicating which passages answer each query. It is intended to evaluate and train embedding-based and traditional retrieval models on passage-ranking performance for open-domain QA and information retrieval.

MTEB MIRACLRetrievalHardNegatives (fa) is a Persian (Farsi) retrieval benchmark from the MIRACL collection, packaged for the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains query–positive passage pairs along with adversarially selected hard negative passages, designed to stress-test and fine-tune dense retrieval and embedding models on challenging, semantically similar non-relevant examples. The split supports training and evaluation of semantic search, contrastive learning, and reranking approaches using standard retrieval metrics (e.g., recall, MRR, NDCG) for Persian-language information retrieval.

MIRACLRetrievalHardNegatives (fi) is a Finnish-language retrieval dataset in the MTEB suite that pairs queries with relevant passages and adversarially selected hard negatives. It is designed to evaluate and stress-test dense embedding and retrieval models on fine-grained ranking distinctions by providing negatives that are semantically similar to positives. Use cases include benchmarking embedding quality for retrieval, training/reranking with hard-negative mining, and measuring robustness of models to challenging distractors in Finnish.

MTEB MrTydiRetrieval (Finnish) is a Finnish-language retrieval benchmark from the MTEB suite, derived from the Mr.TyDi information-seeking dataset. It provides Finnish queries paired with candidate passages and relevance judgments to evaluate semantic search and dense retrieval performance. The set is intended for assessing text embedding models on ranking, recall, and semantic similarity in Finnish information retrieval scenarios.

MTEB MIRACLRetrievalHardNegatives (fr) is a French-language retrieval subset of the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that provides queries paired with gold-positive passages and explicitly curated hard negative examples. It is designed to stress-test embedding models’ ability to discriminate fine-grained lexical and semantic differences in ranking and retrieval settings. The dataset supports evaluation and training of dense retrieval, re-ranking, and contrastive representation learning for French, with common metrics such as recall@k, MRR, and nDCG to assess robustness against challenging, misleading negatives.

MTEB MIRACL Retrieval Hard Negatives (hi) is a Hindi-language retrieval dataset in the MTEB suite that pairs queries with their positive passages and a set of challenging, semantically similar hard negatives. It is intended for training and evaluating dense retrieval and embedding models using contrastive or hard-negative sampling strategies, helping to improve ranking robustness and semantic-search accuracy on difficult Hindi queries.

MTEB MIRACL Retrieval Hard Negatives (id) is an Indonesian retrieval benchmark derived from the MIRACL multilingual dataset and included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It contains query–document relevance pairs augmented with hard negative passages (challenging non-relevant examples mined to be similar to positives) to stress-test dense retrieval and embedding models. The set is intended to evaluate embedding quality and ranking robustness under difficult retrieval conditions using metrics such as recall@K and MRR.

MTEB MrTydiRetrieval (Indonesian) is an Indonesian-language retrieval benchmark derived from the Mr.TyDi/TyDi QA corpus. It contains natural information-seeking queries (questions) paired with Wikipedia passages labeled as relevant (contain the answer) or non-relevant, enabling evaluation of passage retrieval, embedding-based dense/sparse retrieval, and reranking systems. The dataset is intended to measure retrieval effectiveness and embedding quality for Indonesian queries and to support research on monolingual and cross-lingual retrieval generalization.

MTEB MIRACLRetrievalHardNegatives (ja) is a Japanese-language retrieval benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that provides Japanese queries and candidate items with annotated hard negatives. Designed to stress-test embedding and retrieval models, it emphasizes fine-grained semantic discrimination by including challenging negative examples that are closely related to the positives. It is intended for evaluating and developing robust text (and cross-modal) retrieval, ranking, and contrastive-learning systems on Japanese data.

MTEB MrTydiRetrieval (Japanese) is a Japanese-language retrieval benchmark derived from the Mr.TyDI question-answering collection that provides query–passage relevance pairs for evaluating embedding and retrieval models. It assesses models’ ability to retrieve relevant passages for natural-language questions in Japanese across varying difficulty and domain contexts, supporting common retrieval metrics (e.g., MRR, recall, nDCG). The set is intended for benchmarking and improving multilingual dense and sparse retrieval systems on Japanese search and QA tasks.

MTEB MIRACLRetrievalHardNegatives (ko) is a Korean-language retrieval benchmark in the MTEB suite that provides query–document relevance pairs augmented with mined hard negative examples. It is designed to evaluate and stress-test embedding-based retrieval and ranking models on fine-grained semantic discrimination by including challenging non-relevant passages similar to positives. The dataset is suited for training and benchmarking dense retrieval and contrastive representation models using metrics like recall@k and MRR.

MTEB MrTydiRetrieval (Korean) is a Korean-language information retrieval benchmark derived from the Mr.TyDi dataset and included in the MTEB suite. It provides Korean queries paired with relevant and non-relevant passages to evaluate semantic search, dense retrieval and text-embedding models on Korean content. The dataset is suited for benchmarking embedding quality, ranking performance, and cross-lingual retrieval robustness in non-English settings.

MTEB MIRACLRetrievalHardNegatives (ru) is a Russian-language retrieval benchmark derived from the MIRACL dataset that pairs Russian text queries (captions) with candidate images including curated hard negatives. It is designed to evaluate the discriminative power of text and cross-modal embedding models on challenging, fine-grained retrieval cases by forcing models to distinguish true matches from visually or semantically similar distractors. The split provides ground-truth positives plus difficult negative candidates and is intended for ranking-based evaluation (Recall@K, MRR), model comparison, and robustness testing for multilingual and cross-modal retrieval systems.

The Russian subset of MTEB’s MrTydiRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark consisting of Russian queries paired with labeled relevant and non-relevant passages. It is designed to evaluate embedding-based and dense retrieval models on passage/document retrieval and reranking tasks in Russian, enabling standardized comparison of retrieval quality and generalization for monolingual and cross-lingual retrieval systems.

MTEB MIRACLRetrievalHardNegatives (es) is a Spanish-language subset of the MIRACL retrieval benchmark that pairs Spanish text queries with corresponding images and curated hard negative examples. It contains semantically or visually similar negatives intended to challenge embedding models' discrimination and ranking ability in cross-modal retrieval. The split is designed for evaluating and benchmarking multilingual text-image embedding models on fine-grained retrieval tasks in Spanish.

MTEB MIRACLRetrievalHardNegatives (sw) is a Swahili retrieval benchmark that provides query–relevant-passage pairs alongside carefully selected hard negatives—non‑relevant passages that are topically or lexically similar to the positives. It is intended to evaluate and train dense embedding and retrieval models on challenging negative examples, improving discrimination and robustness under realistic retrieval noise. Typical uses include ranking evaluation, contrastive training with hard-negative mining, and comparing embedding methods for Swahili semantic search.

MTEB MrTydiRetrieval (Swahili) is a Swahili retrieval benchmark drawn from the Mr.TyDi collection and included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It provides Swahili queries paired with candidate passages and relevance labels for open-domain retrieval, enabling evaluation of embedding-based semantic search and retrieval models. The dataset is intended for benchmarking and improving Swahili sentence/document embeddings, retrieval ranking, and cross-lingual transfer in low-resource settings.

MTEB MIRACLRetrievalHardNegatives (te) is a Telugu retrieval benchmark from the MTEB suite that pairs user queries with relevant passages and carefully mined hard-negative passages. Designed to evaluate and train dense retrieval and embedding models, it stresses models with semantically similar but non-relevant negatives to better measure ranking robustness and discrimination. The dataset supports multilingual and cross-lingual retrieval research, fine-tuning of contrastive and reranking systems, and benchmarking model generalization on challenging retrieval scenarios in Telugu.

MTEB MrTydiRetrieval (Telugu) is a Telugu-language retrieval benchmark derived from the Mr.TyDI dataset. It pairs Telugu questions as queries with candidate passages labeled for relevance (passages containing the answer), enabling evaluation of dense text embeddings and semantic retrieval systems. Designed to test monolingual and multilingual embedding models on open-domain QA and semantic search in a typologically diverse, lower-resource language, it benchmarks retrieval accuracy and ranking performance for Telugu.

MTEB MIRACLRetrievalHardNegatives (th) is the Thai-language subset of the MIRACL retrieval hard-negatives collection in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It provides query–positive pairs accompanied by mined hard negative examples designed to be challenging for embedding-based retrieval systems. The split is intended for training and evaluating dense retrieval, contrastive fine-tuning, and reranking models on Thai retrieval tasks, enabling rigorous benchmarking of ranking accuracy and robustness in a multilingual retrieval setting.

MTEB MrTydiRetrieval (thai) is the Thai subset of the Mr.TyDi retrieval task in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains natural information-seeking queries in Thai paired with candidate passages (sourced from Thai Wikipedia) and relevance annotations, enabling evaluation of embedding-based semantic search and dense retrieval models. The dataset is designed to benchmark monolingual retrieval performance of text embeddings on realistic question-to-passage matching in Thai.

MTEB MIRACLRetrievalHardNegatives (yo) is a Yoruba-language retrieval dataset within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark designed to evaluate and train dense retrieval and embedding models under challenging conditions. Each example pairs a query with one or more positive passages and carefully mined hard negatives—semantically similar but non-relevant passages—to stress-test ranking robustness and discrimination. The dataset is suitable for supervised retrieval evaluation, contrastive training with hard-negative mining, and benchmarking cross-lingual or monolingual embedding models on difficult semantic search scenarios in Yoruba.

MTEB MIRACLRetrievalHardNegatives (zh) is a Chinese retrieval benchmark in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that contains query–document relevance pairs augmented with mined hard negative examples. It is designed to evaluate embedding-based semantic search, dense retrieval, and reranking models under challenging near-miss negatives, measuring ranking accuracy and robustness for Chinese queries. The set is useful for benchmarking and improving models’ discrimination between truly relevant documents and difficult false positives.

AI2 Diagrams (AI2D) is a dataset of over 5000 grade school science diagrams with over 150000 rich annotations, their ground truth syntactic parses, and more than 15000 corresponding multiple choice questions. Source: Image Source:

Charts are very popular for analyzing data. When exploring charts, people often ask a variety of complex reasoning questions that involve several logical and arithmetic operations. They also commonly refer to visual features of a chart in their questions. However, most existing datasets do not focus on such complex reasoning questions as their questions are template-based and answers come from a fixed-vocabulary. In this work, we present a large-scale benchmark covering 9.6K human-written questions as well as 23.1K questions generated from human-written chart summaries. To address the unique challenges in our benchmark involving visual and logical reasoning over charts, we present two transformer-based models that combine visual features and the data table of the chart in a unified way to answer questions. While our models achieve the state-of-the-art results on the previous datasets as well as on our benchmark, the evaluation also reveals several challenges in answering complex reasoning questions.

**MMBench** is a multi-modality benchmark. It methodically develops a comprehensive evaluation pipeline, primarily comprised of two elements. The first element is a meticulously curated dataset that surpasses existing similar benchmarks in terms of the number and variety of evaluation questions and abilities. The second element introduces a novel CircularEval strategy and incorporates the use of ChatGPT. This implementation is designed to convert free-form predictions into pre-defined choices, thereby facilitating a more robust evaluation of the model's predictions.

MM-Vet is a large-scale multimodal dataset designed to evaluate and advance integrated capabilities in visual question answering and related multimodal tasks. It encompasses diverse data samples that combine language, vision, and audio modalities, supporting complex reasoning across image content, natural language queries, and speech inputs. By including extensive multi-modal examples—such as images paired with questions and corresponding answers, along with long speech segments—MM-Vet facilitates the development and benchmarking of models capable of holistic understanding and interaction across multiple sensory inputs. The dataset addresses challenges in aligning and jointly reasoning over heterogeneous data types, promoting research in efficient and robust multimodal large language models. MM-Vet has been instrumental in evaluating state-of-the-art models that integrate vision, language, and audio, enabling advancements in tasks like visual question answering, speech comprehension, and cross-modal generation. Its scale and diversity make it a valuable resource for training and assessing models

TextVQA is a dataset to benchmark visual reasoning based on text in images. TextVQA requires models to read and reason about text in images to answer questions about them. Specifically, models need to incorporate a new modality of text present in the images and reason over it to answer TextVQA questions. Statistics * 28,408 images from OpenImages * 45,336 questions * 453,360 ground truth answers

AI2 ARC (AI2 Reasoning Challenge) is a benchmark of 7,787 genuine grade-school-level multiple-choice science questions designed to encourage research in advanced question answering. The dataset includes both an Easy Set and a Challenge Set, where the latter contains questions that were incorrectly answered by both retrieval-based and word co-occurrence algorithms. ARC also provides a corpus of over 14 million relevant science sentences and baseline neural models.

This is a subset on Hard split of the AI2 ARC benchmark with complex grade-school science questions.

ARC (Easy) is a dataset designed for common sense reasoning tasks, consisting of 1,000 multiple-choice questions that require models to infer logical and everyday knowledge beyond pattern matching. The questions cover a range of real-world scenarios, such as social norms, physical interactions, and causal relationships, and are structured to assess a model’s ability to apply general world knowledge. The dataset is presented in natural language and is primarily used to evaluate and benchmark the reasoning capabilities of language models. While not as large or diverse as other datasets, ARC (Easy) provides a clear, accessible benchmark for assessing foundational reasoning skills in AI systems. Its focus on common sense makes it a key component in evaluating models’ understanding of human experience and context. Due to its well-defined structure and alignment with real-world reasoning, ARC (Easy) is widely used in research to test the effectiveness of pretraining and fine-tuning

BoolQ is a large-scale yes/no question answering dataset consisting of naturally occurring questions paired with corresponding Wikipedia passages. Questions are derived from anonymized Google search queries identified as likely yes/no questions and are verified by human annotators for clarity and answerability. Annotators select relevant passages from Wikipedia articles and label each question with a yes or no answer based on the passage content. The dataset is designed to support research in machine reading comprehension and natural language understanding tasks involving binary question answering.

The Corpus of Linguistic Acceptability (CoLA) is a dataset containing over 10,000 English sentences sourced from linguistics publications. Each sentence is annotated for linguistic acceptability, indicating whether it is grammatically acceptable or not, based on expert judgments. The dataset is split into training, development, and test sets, and is widely used for evaluating models on the task of acceptability classification in natural language processing.

The Choice of Plausible Alternatives (COPA) dataset is designed to evaluate commonsense causal reasoning in natural language processing. It contains 1000 multiple-choice questions, divided equally into development and test sets. Each question presents a premise and two alternative sentences, and the task is to select the alternative that is more plausibly causally related to the premise. The correct answer is randomized to ensure a 50% chance baseline for random guessing. COPA is widely used to benchmark models' ability to understand and reason about cause-effect relationships in open-domain contexts.

HellaSwag is a large-scale commonsense natural language inference dataset designed to evaluate models' ability to understand everyday situations. It consists of multiple-choice questions where models must select the most plausible continuation of a given context. The dataset is challenging for state-of-the-art models but easy for humans, who achieve over 95% accuracy, making it a benchmark for commonsense reasoning in natural language processing.

MathQA is a benchmark dataset designed for math word problem solving, focusing on the task of translating natural language narratives into precise mathematical operations. It extends the AQuA dataset by providing fully specified operational programs that explicitly represent the solution steps, enabling models to perform both numerical and logical reasoning. The dataset consists of textual math problems that require understanding complex problem statements expressed in everyday language and converting them into executable mathematical expressions. MathQA challenges models to handle the dual aspects of symbolic reasoning and numerical computation, emphasizing the importance of capturing reusable numerical properties beyond mere number values. It supports research in developing advanced reasoning techniques and contextual number representation learning, as demonstrated by recent models evaluated on it. MathQA serves as a valuable resource for training and evaluating systems that integrate language understanding with mathematical problem-solving skills, facilitating progress in interpretable and accurate automated reasoning over math word problems.

Microsoft Research Paraphrase Corpus (MRPC) is a corpus consists of 5,801 sentence pairs collected from newswire articles. Each pair is labelled if it is a paraphrase or not by human annotators. The whole set is divided into a training subset (4,076 sentence pairs of which 2,753 are paraphrases) and a test subset (1,725 pairs of which 1,147 are paraphrases). Source: Image Source:

**MultiRC** (**Multi-Sentence Reading Comprehension**) is a dataset of short paragraphs and multi-sentence questions, i.e., questions that can be answered by combining information from multiple sentences of the paragraph. The dataset was designed with three key challenges in mind: * The number of correct answer-options for each question is not pre-specified. This removes the over-reliance on answer-options and forces them to decide on the correctness of each candidate answer independently of others. In other words, the task is not to simply identify the best answer-option, but to evaluate the correctness of each answer-option individually. * The correct answer(s) is not required to be a span in the text. * The paragraphs in the dataset have diverse provenance by being extracted from 7 different domains such as news, fiction, historical text etc., and hence are expected to be more diverse in their contents as compared to single-domain datasets. The entire corpus consists of around 10K questions (including about 6K multiple-sentence questions). The 60% of the data is released as training and development data. The rest of the data is saved for evaluation and every few months a new unseen additional data is included for evaluation to prevent unintentional overfitting over time. Source: Image Source:

OpenBookQA is a multiple-choice question-answering dataset designed to evaluate understanding of elementary-level science through open book exam-style questions. It contains nearly 6,000 questions that require applying a small set of core science facts to novel scenarios, supplemented by broad common knowledge beyond the core facts. The dataset includes training mappings from questions to the core facts they test, as well as crowd-sourced common knowledge facts. It is challenging for simple retrieval or word co-occurrence methods, encouraging development of reasoning and knowledge integration in AI systems.
PIQA is a dataset for commonsense reasoning, and was created to investigate the physical knowledge of existing models in NLP. Source:

PubMedQA is a dataset designed for question answering in the biomedical domain, focusing on answering research questions with yes, no, or maybe responses based on corresponding PubMed abstracts. It contains a small set of expert-labeled questions, a larger set of unlabeled questions, and a substantial number of artificially generated question-answer instances, enabling research in machine reading comprehension and biomedical natural language processing.

The **QNLI** (**Question-answering NLI**) dataset is a Natural Language Inference dataset automatically derived from the Stanford Question Answering Dataset v1.1 (SQuAD). SQuAD v1.1 consists of question-paragraph pairs, where one of the sentences in the paragraph (drawn from Wikipedia) contains the answer to the corresponding question (written by an annotator). The dataset was converted into sentence pair classification by forming a pair between each question and each sentence in the corresponding context, and filtering out pairs with low lexical overlap between the question and the context sentence. The task is to determine whether the context sentence contains the answer to the question. This modified version of the original task removes the requirement that the model select the exact answer, but also removes the simplifying assumptions that the answer is always present in the input and that lexical overlap is a reliable cue. The QNLI dataset is part of GLUE benchmark. Source:

The ReAding Comprehension dataset from Examinations (RACE) is a large-scale machine reading comprehension dataset derived from English exams for Chinese middle and high school students aged 12 to 18. It contains tens of thousands of passages and nearly one hundred thousand questions, each with four answer options and one correct answer. RACE is divided into two subsets: RACE-M from middle school exams and RACE-H from high school exams. Unlike many datasets created via heuristics or crowd-sourcing, RACE questions are carefully designed by domain experts to assess human reading comprehension skills, making it a valuable resource for evaluating machine reading models.

The **Recognizing Textual Entailment (RTE)** datasets come from a series of textual entailment challenges. Data from RTE1, RTE2, RTE3 and RTE5 is combined. Examples are constructed based on news and Wikipedia text.

The SciQ dataset contains 13,679 crowdsourced science exam questions about Physics, Chemistry and Biology, among others. The questions are in multiple-choice format with 4 answer options each. For the majority of the questions, an additional paragraph with supporting evidence for the correct answer is provided. Source:

The **Stanford Sentiment Treebank** is a corpus with fully labeled parse trees that allows for a complete analysis of the compositional effects of sentiment in language. The corpus is based on the dataset introduced by Pang and Lee (2005) and consists of 11,855 single sentences extracted from movie reviews. It was parsed with the Stanford parser and includes a total of 215,154 unique phrases from those parse trees, each annotated by 3 human judges. Each phrase is labelled as either *negative*, *somewhat negative*, *neutral*, *somewhat positive* or *positive*. The corpus with all 5 labels is referred to as SST-5 or SST fine-grained. Binary classification experiments on full sentences (*negative* or *somewhat negative* vs *somewhat positive* or *positive* with *neutral* sentences discarded) refer to the dataset as SST-2 or SST binary.

TriviaQA is a large-scale text-based question answering dataset containing over 650,000 question-answer pairs with corresponding evidence documents from Wikipedia and the web. It is designed to be more challenging than traditional QA datasets, as answers may not be directly extractable as text spans and require reasoning over long and diverse contexts. The dataset includes both human-verified and automatically generated question-answer pairs, supporting research in complex reading comprehension and open-domain question answering tasks.

WinoGrande is a large-scale dataset of 44k problems, inspired by the original WSC design, but adjusted to improve both the scale and the hardness of the dataset. The key steps of the dataset construction consist of (1) a carefully designed crowdsourcing procedure, followed by (2) systematic bias reduction using a novel AfLite algorithm that generalizes human-detectable word associations to machine-detectable embedding associations. Source: Image Source:

The WNLI dataset is a part of the GLUE benchmark used for Natural Language Inference (NLI). It contains pairs of sentences, and the task is to determine whether the second sentence is an entailment of the first one or not. The dataset is used to train and evaluate models on their ability to understand these relationships between sentences.

MTEB STS22.v2 (zh) is a Chinese semantic textual similarity dataset from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). EightTagsClustering (MTEB) is a text clustering benchmark composed of short documents each assigned one of eight topic tags, used to evaluate the ability of embedding models to group semantically similar texts. SciFact is a dataset for automated verification of scientific claims against biomedical literature. Video-MME w/o sub is a video benchmark comprising short clips with aligned visual and audio modalities but without subtitle/text transcripts. The dataset contains diverse real-world scenes and temporal annotations for supervised and self-supervised training of video understanding models.

UWV/WIM Synthetic RD is a synthetic paired dataset for rain/raindrop degradation (RD) and image restoration. Using the UWV/WIM rendering pipeline it produces realistic rain and raindrop corruptions across diverse scenes and lighting while providing pixel-aligned clean ground truth and degradation metadata. dev eval is a benchmark dataset that provides separated development (validation) and evaluation (test) splits for training and assessing machine learning models. Each split contains curated, labeled examples with accompanying metadata to support model selection, hyperparameter tuning, and standardized performance reporting. The disjoint dev and eval partitions enable reproducible comparisons of generalization and final-model performance across architectures and training strategies.

BKAI Vietnamese Legal Documents is a corpus of Vietnamese legal texts collected from official and public sources, containing laws, decrees, judgments, contracts and related documents with accompanying metadata and task-oriented annotations. Custom SGD Dataset is a curated collection designed for benchmarking and analyzing stochastic gradient descent and its variants. Target-QA is a benchmark for target-oriented question answering where each example pairs a context passage with a specified target (entity or aspect), a question about that target, and the corresponding answer (span, label, or short text). It is designed to evaluate models’ ability to locate, extract, and reason about information tied to a given target within text, supporting tasks such as aspect-based QA, targeted information extraction, and entity-centric reasoning. The dataset enables supervised training and comparison of models on target-aware comprehension and answer grounding.

CIFAR-10 is a widely used dataset for image classification tasks, consisting of 60,000 32x32 color images in 10 different classes. It is commonly employed to benchmark machine learning and computer vision algorithms. The dataset is balanced, with an equal number of images per class, and is split into training and test sets. CIFAR-10 serves as a standard benchmark for evaluating the performance of image recognition models, particularly in the context of deep learning research.

The Stanford Dogs dataset contains over 20,000 images of 120 dog breeds from around the world. It is commonly used for fine-grained image classification tasks, with a standard split of training and testing images. The dataset provides diverse and challenging examples for evaluating machine learning models on breed recognition.

Food101 is a large-scale image classification dataset consisting of 101 food categories with 1,000 images per category. It is widely used for training and evaluating computer vision models on food recognition tasks. The dataset provides diverse and realistic images of various dishes, enabling research in image classification, fine-grained recognition, and transfer learning. Food101 is commonly employed to benchmark model performance in both standard and few-shot learning scenarios due to its balanced class distribution and variety of food items.

Bird Species is a collection of bird images annotated with species-level labels (and often localization or attribute annotations) intended for fine-grained visual recognition. It supports supervised tasks such as species classification, detection, segmentation and retrieval, and is commonly used to train and evaluate models for automated bird identification and biodiversity monitoring. The dataset captures diverse species, poses, plumage variants, and natural backgrounds, presenting challenges from high inter-species similarity, intra-species variation, occlusion and varying illumination, making it useful for research in fine-grained classification and ecological applications.

The MNIST database (Modified National Institute of Standards and Technology database) is a widely used dataset of handwritten digit images for machine learning. It contains a training set of 60,000 examples and a test set of 10,000 examples. The images are grayscale, size-normalized, and centered within 28x28 pixel fields. MNIST is derived from a larger NIST dataset of handwritten digits collected from various sources. The digits were originally black and white but were processed with anti-aliasing to produce grayscale images. This dataset is commonly used for benchmarking image classification and pattern recognition algorithms.

custom-indian-id-dataset is a collection of Indian identity document images (e.g., Aadhaar, PAN, voter ID, driver’s license) captured under varied lighting, orientations and occlusions, with annotations for document type, field-level bounding boxes and transcriptions, face bounding boxes, and image-quality metadata. It is intended for supervised learning and evaluation of OCR, field/entity extraction, document classification, face matching and forgery-detection models for automated ID processing. All personally identifiable information in released samples has been redacted or anonymized to protect privacy.

MichalMlodawski/closed-open-eyes is a dataset of eye images labeled as "closed" or "open" for binary eye-state classification. It provides supervised labels suitable for training and evaluating models for blink detection, drowsiness monitoring, gaze-preprocessing, and other eye-state recognition tasks. The dataset is useful for benchmarking classification robustness across typical variations in pose and lighting.

The CIFAR-100 dataset is a widely used benchmark in image classification, consisting of 60,000 32x32 color images divided into 100 classes grouped into 20 superclasses. Each class contains 600 images, with 500 used for training and 100 for testing. Each image is labeled with a fine label indicating its specific class and a coarse label indicating its superclass. The dataset was curated to include photo-realistic images containing a single prominent object, which may be partially occluded or viewed from unusual angles, ensuring clear object identity. CIFAR-100 serves as a challenging dataset for evaluating machine learning models on fine-grained image recognition tasks.

chest-xray-classification is a collection of chest radiographs paired with image-level disease labels for automated thoracic disease detection.
