Labels are typically derived from radiology reports or expert annotation, making the dataset suitable for supervised learning, transfer learning, and model calibration studies; common uses include AUC-based benchmarking, localization with bounding boxes or heatmaps, and investigations of label noise and dataset bias.

While small in scale compared to large-scale datasets, it provides a clear and accessible benchmark for evaluating model performance in a controlled setting. Due to its simplicity and well-defined task, it is frequently used in academic tutorials, model development pipelines, and as a baseline for comparing new algorithms. lewtun/dog_food is an image dataset of dog food items (packaging and loose kibble) paired with metadata labels such as product name, brand, and category. It is designed for supervised tasks including fine-grained product classification, visual product retrieval, and object detection in retail or inventory settings. The dataset supports training and evaluating models that need to distinguish brands, formulations, and packaging variations, and is useful for research in product recognition, automated shelving, and e-commerce visual search.

image_folder is a generic dataset format consisting of images stored in a directory, optionally organized into class-specific subfolders. It yields image samples (and inferred labels when subfolder names represent classes) for use in supervised classification or as unlabeled collections for unsupervised and transfer-learning tasks. Lightweight and framework-agnostic, image_folder is commonly used for quick prototyping, data loading, augmentation, and benchmarking.

Stanford 40 Actions is a still-image benchmark for human action recognition containing images labeled with 40 distinct action categories. Each image depicts a person performing an action in diverse poses and backgrounds and includes person-level annotations (bounding boxes) to support classification and localization tasks. The dataset is widely used to train and evaluate single-image action classifiers, fine-grained action understanding, and context-aware models for human-centric scene analysis.

GeoGuessr is a geolocation dataset derived from geotagged Street View panoramas used to benchmark image-based location prediction. Each sample pairs a street-level image (often panoramic or multi-view crops) with precise GPS coordinates and region labels, enabling supervised tasks such as global or city-scale geolocalization, country/continent classification, and retrieval-based place recognition. The dataset exposes real-world variability in architecture, signage, vegetation, weather, and occlusions, making it suitable for evaluating robustness and spatial reasoning in models that infer geographic location from visual cues.

Street View House Numbers (SVHN) is a large-scale dataset for digit classification consisting of over 600,000 32x32 RGB images of digits (0-9) cropped from real-world house number photos. The images are centered on the digit of interest but may include neighboring digits and background clutter, making the task challenging. The dataset is divided into training, testing, and an additional extra set containing images that are generally easier and intended to support training. SVHN is widely used for benchmarking machine learning models on digit recognition in natural scenes.

fashion_mnist_quality_drift is a benchmark dataset built from Fashion-MNIST that simulates image-quality drift by applying common degradations (JPEG compression, noise, blur, and downsampling) at multiple severity levels and across sequential partitions. Images retain their original labels but are organized into domains representing progressively changing quality, enabling evaluation of classification robustness, drift detection, domain adaptation, and continual learning methods. The dataset is lightweight and reproducible, providing a controlled setting for studying model performance and calibration under systematic quality degradation.

CIFAR-10 is a widely used dataset for image classification tasks, consisting of 60,000 32x32 color images in 10 different classes. CIFAR-10 serves as a standard benchmark for evaluating the performance of image recognition models, particularly in the context of deep learning research.

The CIFAR-100 dataset is a widely used benchmark in image classification, consisting of 60,000 32x32 color images divided into 100 classes grouped into 20 superclasses. Each class contains 600 images, with 500 used for training and 100 for testing. Each image is labeled with a fine label indicating its specific class and a coarse label indicating its superclass. The dataset was curated to include photo-realistic images containing a single prominent object, which may be partially occluded or viewed from unusual angles, ensuring clear object identity. CIFAR-100 serves as a challenging dataset for evaluating machine learning models on fine-grained image recognition tasks.

Food101 is a large-scale image classification dataset consisting of 101 food categories with 1,000 images per category. It is widely used for training and evaluating computer vision models on food recognition tasks. The dataset provides diverse and realistic images of various dishes, enabling research in image classification, fine-grained recognition, and transfer learning. Food101 is commonly employed to benchmark model performance in both standard and few-shot learning scenarios due to its balanced class distribution and variety of food items.

The Describable Textures Dataset (DTD) contains 5640 texture images collected from natural scenes. Each image is annotated with human-centric attributes that describe perceptual properties of textures, such as directionality, regularity, and roughness. The dataset is designed for texture recognition and attribute prediction tasks in computer vision, providing a challenging benchmark for models to understand and classify textures based on descriptive attributes.

Its focus on animal breeds provides a structured domain for studying challenges such as class imbalance and intra-class variation. OxfordPets serves as a valuable resource for developing and evaluating models that require robust visual representations and effective learning from few labeled samples per class.

The Stanford Cars dataset contains 16,185 images of cars categorized into 196 classes based on make, model, and year. The images are divided nearly equally into training and testing sets, with approximately 8,144 training images and 8,041 testing images. Each image has a resolution of 360 by 240 pixels. The dataset is commonly used for fine-grained image classification tasks in computer vision.

The dataset is provided in a standardized preprocessed format suitable for supervised learning, enabling development and evaluation of segmentation networks, tumor growth analysis, and downstream tasks such as survival prediction and treatment planning.

Perception Test is a benchmark designed to evaluate the perception and reasoning skills of multimodal models. The videos are densely annotated with six types of labels: object and point tracks, temporal action and sound segments, multiple-choice video question-answers and grounded video question-answers. The benchmark probes pre-trained models for their transfer capabilities, in a zero-shot / few-shot or fine tuning regime.

Its inclusion of extended audio sequences makes it particularly valuable for assessing models’ ability to comprehend and reason over long-form speech. MVBench is a comprehensive Multi-modal Video understanding Benchmark. It was introduced to evaluate the comprehension capabilities of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs), particularly their temporal understanding in dynamic video tasks. MVBench covers 20 challenging video tasks that cannot be effectively solved with a single frame. It introduces a novel static-to-dynamic method to define these temporal-related tasks. By transforming various static tasks into dynamic ones, it enables the systematic generation of video tasks that require a broad spectrum of temporal skills, ranging from perception to cognition.

CV-Bench is a unified benchmark suite for evaluating computer vision models across multiple tasks, including image classification, object detection, semantic/instance segmentation, keypoint detection, and tracking. It aggregates diverse real-world images and videos with standardized splits and evaluation metrics to enable fair, reproducible comparisons. Designed to test robustness and generalization, CV-Bench includes varied scenes, occlusions, and imaging conditions and supports research on multi-task learning, transfer learning, and practical deployment of vision systems.

SWAG (Situations With Adversarial Generations) is a large-scale dataset designed for grounded commonsense inference, combining natural language inference with physically grounded reasoning. It contains over 100,000 multiple-choice questions derived from video captions, where each question presents a partial description of a situation and four possible continuations. The correct continuation is the actual next event caption from the video, while the three incorrect options are adversarially generated and human-verified to challenge machine understanding without confusing humans. SWAG serves as a benchmark for evaluating models' ability to anticipate plausible future events in grounded scenarios and to learn robust commonsense representations.

It contains over 100,000 multiple-choice questions derived from video captions, where each question presents a partial description of a situation and four possible continuations. The correct continuation is the actual next event caption from the video, while the three incorrect options are adversarially generated and human-verified to challenge machine understanding without confusing humans. SWAG serves as a benchmark for evaluating models' ability to anticipate plausible future events in grounded scenarios and to learn robust commonsense representations.

The ReAding Comprehension dataset from Examinations (RACE) is a large-scale machine reading comprehension dataset derived from English exams for Chinese middle and high school students aged 12 to 18. It contains tens of thousands of passages and nearly one hundred thousand questions, each with four answer options and one correct answer. RACE is divided into two subsets: RACE-M from middle school exams and RACE-H from high school exams. Unlike many datasets created via heuristics or crowd-sourcing, RACE questions are carefully designed by domain experts to assess human reading comprehension skills, making it a valuable resource for evaluating machine reading models.

desc: nielsr/funsd-layoutlmv3 is a version of the FUNSD form-understanding dataset preprocessed for LayoutLMv3. It contains scanned form images paired with word-level OCR text, token bounding boxes, semantic entity labels (e.g., question/answer/header/other) and annotated entity relations, all packaged to match LayoutLMv3’s multimodal input format. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating layout-aware document understanding models on tasks like semantic entity recognition and key–value/relation extraction from noisy scanned forms.

IP102 is a large-scale benchmark dataset for insect pest recognition containing images of 102 pest categories collected in real-world agricultural scenes. It provides category labels and object-level annotations to support classification and detection tasks. The dataset exhibits wide intra-class variation, inter-class similarity, occlusion, and background clutter, making it suitable for developing and evaluating deep learning models for automated pest monitoring and precision agriculture.

PDT Dataset is a curated benchmark dataset designed to support development and evaluation of machine learning models. It provides diverse, high-quality samples with standardized training/validation/test splits and rich annotations and metadata to enable reproducible comparisons. PDT is intended for supervised learning and benchmarking in tasks relevant to its modality (e.g., classification, detection, segmentation, or restoration), helping researchers assess model accuracy, robustness, and generalization on realistic data.

Custom Dataset (Friends) is a small, in-the-wild collection of images and short video clips of a consistent group of people captured across varied lighting, poses, expressions, and occlusions. Each sample includes identity labels and common visual annotations (face bounding boxes and optional landmarks), enabling tasks such as face recognition/verification, landmark detection, expression classification, and multi-person tracking. The dataset is intended for prototyping and benchmarking face-related models in personal or small-scale scenarios and for evaluating robustness to natural appearance variation.

custom-cargo-package-dataset is a curated dataset of images captured in warehouse and conveyor-belt environments for logistics and automation research. Each sample includes high-resolution RGB (optionally depth) views annotated with bounding boxes, instance segmentation masks, package class labels (e.g., box, envelope, pallet), barcode/label regions, and damage/no-damage indicators; some entries include metadata such as dimensions, weight, and tracking IDs. The collection exhibits varied lighting, occlusion, stacking, and viewpoints to support robust model training. It is intended for benchmarking and developing object detection, instance segmentation, OCR/barcode reading, anomaly/damage detection, and automated sorting/tracking systems.

Safety Equipment is a dataset for detecting and recognizing personal protective equipment (PPE) in images and video frames. It contains annotated scenes showing people in workplace and public environments with labels and bounding boxes (and optionally segmentation masks) for common items such as helmets, high-visibility vests, safety goggles, and gloves. Designed for supervised learning, it supports object detection, multi-label classification, and instance segmentation to enable automated compliance monitoring, safety analytics, and downstream tasks like alerting and robotics. The dataset includes diverse viewpoints, occlusions, and lighting conditions to benchmark model robustness in real-world safety scenarios.

Custom Rubber Duck Dataset is a curated collection of RGB images showing rubber ducks across diverse indoor and outdoor scenes with variations in scale, pose, lighting, background clutter, occlusion, and material appearance. Each image is annotated with bounding boxes and instance segmentation masks (with consistent instance IDs) to support supervised training and evaluation. The dataset is intended for object detection, instance segmentation, and small-object recognition research, and is well suited for studies in domain adaptation, synthetic-to-real transfer, data augmentation, and robotic manipulation of simple objects.

BISINDO Dataset is a video dataset of Indonesian Sign Language (BISINDO) designed for sign recognition and translation research. It contains multi-signer recordings of signed utterances with accompanying gloss annotations and signer metadata, enabling supervised training and evaluation for tasks such as isolated sign classification, temporal segmentation/localization, and sequence-to-text translation. The dataset supports development of models robust to signer variation, appearance and background changes, and is intended to advance automated recognition and accessibility tools for Indonesian sign language users.

PASCAL VOC 2012 is a large-scale multi-label image dataset designed for object detection, segmentation, and multi-label classification tasks in computer vision. It contains approximately 10,582 images across 20 object categories, with each image annotated with multiple labels reflecting real-world object presence. The dataset is widely used to evaluate the performance of deep learning models in visual recognition, particularly in scenarios involving label ambiguity and class overlap. Its annotations support both single and multi-label classification, making it a foundational benchmark for training and testing models in object recognition. The dataset is characterized by diverse scenes, complex object interactions, and varying levels of occlusion and clutter, which introduce significant challenges in accurate label prediction. Due to its rich annotation structure and broad applicability, PASCAL VOC 2012 has been instrumental in advancing methods such as deep label distribution learning, explainable

desc: SQuAD v2 is a reading-comprehension dataset built from Wikipedia passages that combines answerable questions with a large set of crowd‑written unanswerable but plausible questions. It requires models to both extract answer spans when present and detect/abstain on unanswerable questions, making it a standard benchmark for training and evaluating robust extractive QA systems and confidence/calibration strategies.

The Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD) is a large-scale reading comprehension dataset consisting of question-answer pairs based on Wikipedia articles. Answers are spans of text extracted directly from the corresponding passages. SQuAD 1.1 contains over 100,000 question-answer pairs across several hundred articles, created through crowdsourcing to ensure diversity and naturalness. SQuAD 2.0 extends this by adding unanswerable questions designed to challenge models to determine when no answer is supported by the text, making it a benchmark for both answer extraction and answerability detection in machine reading comprehension.

AdversarialQA consists of three reading comprehension datasets created using an adversarial human annotation process involving three different models: BiDAF, BERTLarge, and RoBERTaLarge. Each dataset contains approximately 10,000 training examples, 1,000 validation examples, and 1,000 test examples. The adversarial annotation approach ensures that the questions are challenging for state-of-the-art models, providing a valuable resource for training and evaluating robust question answering systems.

squad_adversarial is an adversarially modified version of the SQuAD reading-comprehension benchmark designed to test QA robustness. Context paragraphs are augmented with human-crafted distracting sentences or perturbations that introduce plausible but incorrect answer spans, while questions remain the same. The set is used to evaluate and stress-test models’ reliance on superficial cues and to benchmark improvements in robustness and generalization for machine reading comprehension.

squadshifts amazon is a domain-shift reading-comprehension benchmark consisting of SQuAD-style question–answer pairs where contexts are drawn from Amazon product content (descriptions, specifications and reviews). Answers are provided as text spans in the original contexts. The split is intended to evaluate robustness and generalization of models trained on standard SQuAD to e‑commerce language and realistic distribution shifts, and to support fine-tuning and stress-testing of QA systems on product-focused queries.

squadshifts new_wiki is an extractive question-answering benchmark that tests model robustness to temporal and distributional shifts in knowledge sources. It reuses SQuAD-style questions but pairs them with passages drawn from a newer snapshot of Wikipedia, so contexts, phrasing, and answer presence can differ from the original dataset. The split is intended for evaluating generalization, domain adaptation, calibration, and out-of-distribution behavior of span-extraction models when faced with updated or changed source text. It is useful for research on model updating, continual learning, and deployment robustness under real-world content drift.

squadshifts nyt is an out-of-domain SQuAD-style extractive question answering benchmark created from New York Times article passages. It provides context–question–answer triplets in the SQuAD format to evaluate robustness and generalization of QA models under domain shift from typical training domains (e.g., Wikipedia) to newswire text. The set is used to assess transfer, domain adaptation, and calibration of reading-comprehension systems on real-world news content.

SQuADShifts Reddit is an extractive question-answering benchmark that adapts SQuAD-style QA to the Reddit domain by pairing Reddit post passages with corresponding question–answer span annotations. It is designed to evaluate out-of-distribution generalization and robustness of models trained on SQuAD (Wikipedia) when applied to conversational, informal, and noisy web text. The split is useful for benchmarking domain transfer, calibration, and failure modes of extractive QA systems in real-world social-media contexts.

dataset_node: Custom Medical QA Dataset␟Medical Question Answering
desc: Custom Medical QA Dataset is a curated, de-identified collection of medical question–answer pairs and associated contexts designed for training and evaluating clinical QA models. It covers multiple specialties and formats (case-based vignettes, short-answer, multiple-choice), with each item annotated and verified by medical experts and accompanied by metadata such as specialty, difficulty, evidence citations, and rationale. Intended for use in QA, answer generation, retrieval-augmented reasoning, and model evaluation for clinical language tasks, the dataset emphasizes traceability and safe usage and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.

SQuAD_it is an Italian machine reading comprehension dataset of context passages paired with questions and span-based answers in Italian. It provides extractive QA annotations (context, question, answer span) for supervised training and evaluation of Italian-language question answering models. The dataset is useful for benchmarking reading-comprehension performance, transfer learning from multilingual models, and development of end-to-end extractive QA systems in Italian.

CatalanQA is a Catalan-language question answering dataset of context–question–answer triplets designed for machine reading comprehension. It provides annotated passages with corresponding questions and extractive answer spans to enable supervised training and evaluation of QA models in Catalan. The dataset supports research on monolingual QA, cross-lingual transfer, and adaptation of pretrained multilingual or Catalan-specific language models to downstream comprehension tasks.

Quoref is a reading-comprehension benchmark of paragraph–question–answer triples specifically designed to test coreference resolution in QA. Each example pairs a passage (commonly from Wikipedia) with questions whose correct answers require resolving pronouns or entity mentions across sentences; answers are provided as short text spans. Quoref serves as a focused diagnostic for evaluating and improving models’ ability to track entities and perform context-dependent reference resolution in reading comprehension.

Kenyacorpus is a multilingual Kenyan text corpus compiled from diverse Kenyan sources (news, blogs, forums and social media) capturing English, Swahili and common local-language and code-switched varieties. It is intended for training and evaluating NLP models on tasks such as language modeling, machine translation, code-switching, POS tagging, NER and sentiment analysis, providing realistic lexical, orthographic and dialectal variation representative of Kenyan usage and domains.

squad_bn is a Bangla (Bengali) extractive question-answering dataset adapted from the SQuAD format, containing context paragraphs paired with questions and exact answer spans. It is intended for training and evaluating QA models in Bangla, supporting research on monolingual and cross-lingual transfer, language-specific understanding, and robustness of reading-comprehension systems in low-resource languages.

The Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD) is a large-scale reading comprehension dataset consisting of question-answer pairs based on Wikipedia articles. Answers are spans of text extracted directly from the corresponding passages. SQuAD 1.1 contains over 100,000 question-answer pairs across several hundred articles, created through crowdsourcing to ensure diversity and naturalness. SQuAD 2.0 extends this by adding unanswerable questions designed to challenge models to determine when no answer is supported by the text, making it a benchmark for both answer extraction and answerability detection in machine reading comprehension.

squad_es v2.0.0 is a Spanish-language extractive question-answering dataset mirroring SQuAD v2.0. It pairs Spanish context paragraphs with questions and span-based answers, and includes unanswerable questions requiring models to predict no-answer. Provided in the standard SQuAD format (context, question, answers with text and character offsets), it is intended for training and evaluating Spanish reading-comprehension and QA systems, including fine-tuning transformer-based models and benchmarking no-answer detection.

ArgricultureQA is a curated question-answer dataset focused on agricultural knowledge, containing diverse factoid, procedural, diagnostic, and troubleshooting QA pairs covering crops, soil management, pest and disease control, fertilization, irrigation, and livestock. Designed for training and evaluating domain-specific QA, dialogue, and retrieval models, it supports development of farmer-facing chatbots, decision-support tools, and information-extraction systems. Entries are sourced and validated from expert literature, extension services, and practitioner forums to ensure practical relevance, and include contextual metadata (e.g., crop type, region, season) to enable conditioned and contextualized responses. ArgricultureQA benchmarks model understanding of domain terminology, causal reasoning, and stepwise recommendations in real-world farming scenarios.

SubjQA is a dataset for subjective question answering that focuses on opinion- and preference-oriented queries rather than factual questions. It pairs questions with related context passages and crowd-sourced answers or labels that capture variability in human judgments (e.g., differing opinions, answerability, and degree of subjectivity). The dataset is intended to support development and evaluation of models that must detect subjectivity, handle ambiguous or opinion-based queries, predict answerability, and aggregate diverse human responses for more robust, user-aligned QA systems.

NovelQSI is a multi-view benchmark for novel-view synthesis and scene representation learning. It contains collections of calibrated images of diverse objects and scenes with held-out target views for evaluation, and where available accompanying geometry or depth annotations. The dataset is designed to train and evaluate neural rendering, view interpolation, few-shot generalization and multi-view reconstruction methods, and includes standard splits and metrics (e.g., PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS) to compare model fidelity and perceptual quality.

SQuAD v1.1 (Stanford Question Answering Dataset) is a large-scale extractive reading-comprehension dataset containing roughly 100k crowd‑sourced question–answer pairs over ~500+ Wikipedia articles. Each example pairs a context paragraph with a question whose answer is a contiguous text span in the passage, enabling supervised training and evaluation of extractive QA models. Standard evaluation uses Exact Match and F1 metrics to measure answer accuracy.

dataset_node: BioASQ Phase B Yes/No Dataset␟Yes/No Question Classification
root_b: bioasq phase b yes no dataset
desc: BioASQ Phase B Yes/No Dataset is a biomedical question-answering benchmark of yes/no (binary) questions curated from the BioASQ challenge. Each instance contains a domain-specific question paired with an expert-provided yes or no answer and accompanying supporting material (relevant snippets/documents and annotations). The dataset is designed for supervised learning and evaluation of binary QA, textual entailment, and evidence retrieval systems in the biomedical domain, enabling models to learn factual verification and claim validation from biomedical literature.

Shakespeare Q&A Dataset is a question–answer dataset built from the works of William Shakespeare, pairing questions about plots, characters, lines, and themes with answers grounded in the original texts. Each example links the question and answer to a supporting passage (play, act, scene, line span) and is labeled for answer type (extractive vs. abstractive) and reasoning category (literal comprehension, inference about motivation, rhetorical/device interpretation, historical/contextual). It is designed to benchmark and train reading-comprehension and QA systems on Early Modern English, implicit reasoning, and literary analysis, supporting extractive QA, generative QA, multiple-choice evaluation, and domain-adaptation research.

Natural Questions (Simplified) is a machine reading comprehension and open-domain QA dataset derived from Google search queries paired with relevant Wikipedia pages. It provides anonymized real-user questions with human-annotated short answer spans and long answer passages, presented in a cleaned/simplified format for easier training and evaluation. The dataset is used to train and benchmark retrieval, extractive, and generative QA models on diverse, realistic queries across broad knowledge domains.

SQuAD1.1 is a widely used benchmark dataset for machine reading comprehension and question answering tasks. It consists of over 100,000 question-answer pairs derived from Wikipedia articles, where each question is associated with a specific answer span within the passage. The dataset is designed to evaluate models' ability to understand context, locate relevant information, and extract precise answers. Questions and answers are in English, and the dataset is commonly used to assess performance on metrics such as exact match (EM) and F1 score. Its scale and real-world relevance make it a standard for training and evaluating models in natural language understanding, including architectures like BERT and T5. The dataset has been instrumental in advancing end-to-end reading comprehension systems, enabling the development of models that can perform contextual reasoning and span prediction. A subsequent version, SQuAD 2.0, introduces more challenging and

Country-Capital Mixed QA is a benchmark of question–answer pairs about countries and their capitals using mixed formats (country→capital, capital→country, multiple-choice, cloze, and distractor-based prompts). It is designed to train and evaluate factual-recall and knowledge-retrieval models, testing direct lookup, inverse mapping, handling of distractors, and robustness across varying difficulty. The dataset supports assessment of accuracy, calibration, and few-/zero-shot generalization for geopolitically grounded factual knowledge.

Custom Indonesian QA Dataset is a curated collection of Indonesian-language question–answer pairs, optionally paired with supporting context passages, designed for training and evaluating question-answering models. It covers diverse topics and realistic user queries to support extractive and generative QA, reading comprehension, and conversational QA benchmarks. The dataset is intended for fine-tuning and measuring model accuracy, robustness, and language understanding in Indonesian.

root_b: nasa impact nasa smd qa benchmark
desc: nasa-impact/nasa-smd-qa-benchmark is a domain-specific question-answering benchmark built from NASA Science Mission Directorate (SMD) materials. It contains question–answer pairs paired with supporting passages extracted from SMD web pages and documents to evaluate retrieval-augmented and reading-comprehension QA systems on NASA-related scientific and programmatic content. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating domain-adapted QA models, information retrieval pipelines, and fact-checking or knowledge-grounding approaches in a scientific/government-context.

LIBERO-90 is a subset of the LIBERO-100 benchmark suite, comprising 90 diverse tasks designed to evaluate imitation learning algorithms in robotic manipulation. The dataset encompasses a wide range of complex control challenges that require learning from demonstrations to generate multimodal and discontinuous behaviors. It serves as a comprehensive testbed for assessing policy learning methods, particularly those leveraging advanced architectures such as diffusion-based models and Transformer variants. LIBERO-90 emphasizes scalability and efficiency in policy learning by providing tasks that demand generalization across varied robotic scenarios. Performance metrics typically focus on task success rates and computational efficiency, reflecting the dataset’s role in driving innovations in parameter-efficient and scalable imitation learning models. By enabling evaluation across numerous manipulation tasks, LIBERO-90 supports research aimed at improving both the robustness and resource efficiency of learned robotic policies.

AIME24 is a dataset designed for mathematical reasoning, consisting of problems from the American Invitational Mathematics Examination (AIME) held in 2024. It contains a curated collection of challenging, multi-step problems requiring deep mathematical insight, algebraic manipulation, number theory, combinatorics, and geometry. The problems are presented in natural language and demand precise, step-by-step solutions, making it a strong benchmark for evaluating models’ ability to perform complex reasoning. With a focus on problem-solving rather than factual recall, AIME24 emphasizes the model’s capacity to understand abstract mathematical concepts and apply logical inference. The dataset is typically used to assess and improve the reasoning capabilities of large language models in STEM domains. Due to its high difficulty and rigorous structure, AIME24 serves as a critical benchmark for testing the robustness and generalization of mathematical reasoning in AI systems.

Graduate-Level Google-Proof Q&A (GPQA) consists of PhD-level multiple-choice questions in science domains, including chemistry, biology, and physics, to evaluate expert-level reasoning and factual knowledge without relying on web retrieval.

This is a subset on The most challenging GPQA tier requiring advanced scientific reasoning.

ALFRED is a large-scale simulated benchmark for embodied instruction following and interactive task execution in household environments. It pairs natural-language high-level goals and step-by-step human-written instructions with egocentric RGB-D demonstration trajectories and low-level action sequences recorded in the AI2-THOR simulator. The dataset includes object annotations, goal/subgoal labels, and diverse everyday tasks (e.g., pick-and-place, heat/cool, clean, toggle, slice), supporting research on language grounding, visual navigation, long-horizon planning, and hierarchical policy learning for agents that must translate instructions into perception-action sequences.

The MNIST database (Modified National Institute of Standards and Technology database) is a widely used dataset of handwritten digit images for machine learning. It contains a training set of 60,000 examples and a test set of 10,000 examples. The images are grayscale, size-normalized, and centered within 28x28 pixel fields. MNIST is derived from a larger NIST dataset of handwritten digits collected from various sources. The digits were originally black and white but were processed with anti-aliasing to produce grayscale images. This dataset is commonly used for benchmarking image classification and pattern recognition algorithms.

The IMDb dataset is a large-scale graph-based dataset commonly used for link prediction and network analysis tasks. It represents a heterogeneous information network consisting of entities such as users, movies, and reviews, with edges capturing interactions like user ratings and reviews. This dataset supports various tasks including link prediction, node classification, and network reconstruction, making it valuable for evaluating network representation learning methods. IMDb is frequently employed as a benchmark to assess the performance of graph-based learning models, particularly those designed to handle complex relational structures and dynamic interactions within heterogeneous networks.

MTEB BUCC.v2 (ru-en) is a bilingual bitext-mining benchmark for Russian–English that provides candidate sentence pairs annotated for whether they are translations. Sourced from comparable corpora (e.g., Wikipedia), it is used to evaluate cross-lingual sentence embeddings and retrieval systems on parallel sentence identification and mining tasks. The dataset supports standard metrics such as precision, recall, and F1, enabling assessment of embedding alignment, bilingual retrieval accuracy, and robustness of models in extracting parallel sentences from noisy comparable data.

MTEB BibleNLPBitextMining (eng_Latn-rus_Cyrl) is a parallel verse-level dataset of aligned Bible translations in English (Latin script) and Russian (Cyrillic) intended for bitext mining and cross-lingual retrieval evaluation. It provides high-quality, tightly aligned sentence/verse pairs suited for benchmarking embedding-based bilingual retrieval, parallel sentence extraction, and alignment algorithms. The domain-specific religious text offers a controlled setting to assess multilingual sentence embedding quality, cross-script robustness, and bitext mining performance.

A bitext mining dataset from the MTEB collection containing aligned Bible sentences/verses in Russian (Cyrillic) and English (Latin) scripts. It is designed for training and evaluating cross-lingual sentence embeddings and retrieval models, supporting tasks such as parallel sentence extraction, bilingual retrieval, and multilingual semantic similarity. The dataset facilitates benchmarking of embedding-based bitext mining and cross-lingual transfer between Russian and English.

MTEB FloresBitextMining (ace_Arab-rus_Cyrl) is a bilingual bitext-mining benchmark pairing Acehnese in Arabic script (ace_Arab) with Russian in Cyrillic (rus_Cyrl). Built within the FLORES bitext-mining setup, it supplies candidate sentence pairs and mined/gold alignments to evaluate cross-lingual sentence embeddings and parallel-sentence retrieval systems. The dataset targets evaluation of models’ ability to discover and align parallel text across typologically and script-diverse languages, supporting research in multilingual retrieval and machine translation mining.

MTEB FloresBitextMining (bam_Latn-rus_Cyrl) is a bitext mining benchmark providing sentence-level bilingual data between Bambara (bam, Latin script) and Russian (ru, Cyrillic), assembled from FLORES-derived and web-mined sources. It is intended to evaluate cross-lingual sentence embedding and retrieval models on parallel sentence identification, mining precision/recall, and alignment quality for a low-resource — high-resource language pair, supporting research in multilingual embeddings, bitext mining, and downstream translation tasks.

MTEB FloresBitextMining (dzo_Tibt-rus_Cyrl) is a bitext-mining benchmark pairing Dzongkha (Tibetan script) and Russian (Cyrillic) sentences derived from the FLORES collection. It supplies parallel and non-parallel sentence pairs for evaluating cross-lingual sentence embeddings and retrieval models on a low-resource, different-script language pair. The set is intended to test bitext mining, bilingual retrieval precision, and embedding generalization across typologically distant languages and scripts.

MTEB FloresBitextMining (hin_Deva-rus_Cyrl) is a bilingual bitext-mining dataset derived from the FLORES collection that pairs Hindi (Devanagari script) and Russian (Cyrillic script) sentences. It provides candidate sentence pairs with gold or silver alignments for training and evaluating cross-lingual sentence embeddings, parallel sentence extraction, and bitext retrieval systems. The dataset is intended to benchmark embedding quality and mining performance across two typologically distant languages and scripts, supporting tasks such as bilingual retrieval, alignment precision/recall, and evaluation of cross-lingual semantic matching.

MTEB FloresBitextMining (khm_Khmr-rus_Cyrl) is a bilingual bitext-mining benchmark derived from the FLORES multilingual translation data, targeting Khmer (Khmr) ↔ Russian (Cyril) parallel sentence retrieval and alignment. It provides authentic translation pairs with challenging negatives to evaluate multilingual sentence embedding models on cross-lingual retrieval, precision@k, and parallel-corpus mining. Designed to stress low-resource and typologically distant language pairs, it supports development and evaluation of cross-lingual retrieval, bitext mining, and multilingual embedding methods.

MTEB FloresBitextMining (mag_Deva-rus_Cyrl) is a bitext-mining benchmark dataset for cross-lingual sentence embedding evaluation, containing mined parallel and non-parallel sentence pairs between Magahi (Devanagari script) and Russian (Cyrillic script). Designed for the MTEB suite, it tests the ability of multilingual embedding models to retrieve and align parallel sentences in a low-resource language pair, supporting tasks such as parallel sentence retrieval, cross-lingual semantic similarity, and data mining for machine translation. The dataset highlights script and lexical differences to challenge model robustness across diverse orthographies and scarce-data settings.

MTEB FloresBitextMining (pap_Latn-rus_Cyrl) is a bilingual bitext-mining benchmark derived from the FLORES corpus for Papiamento (pap_Latn) and Russian (rus_Cyrl). It provides sentence-level candidate pairs labeled as parallel or non-parallel to evaluate cross-lingual embedding models and retrieval algorithms. The dataset is intended for benchmarking parallel sentence mining, cross-lingual similarity, and bitext retrieval performance, enabling assessment of multilingual encoders’ ability to identify accurate translations across Latin and Cyrillic scripts.

MTEB FloresBitextMining (sot_Latn-rus_Cyrl) is a bitext-mining evaluation set pairing Sesotho (sot, Latin script) and Russian (rus, Cyrillic) sentences derived from the FLORES collection. It is designed to benchmark cross-lingual sentence embeddings and parallel-sentence retrieval systems by providing aligned and non-aligned sentence pairs across a low-resource, cross-script language pair. The set is useful for evaluating precision/recall of mining algorithms, robustness of embeddings to script and linguistic divergence, and performance on downstream tasks that require accurate parallel-sentence identification.

MTEB FloresBitextMining (tur_Latn-rus_Cyrl) is a benchmark dataset for bitext mining and cross-lingual retrieval between Turkish (Latin script) and Russian (Cyrillic script). It provides comparable corpora with reference parallel alignments to evaluate models’ ability to identify or retrieve parallel sentence pairs across these languages. The dataset is designed to benchmark and improve multilingual sentence embeddings, parallel-corpus mining, and downstream translation and cross-lingual retrieval systems.

MTEB FloresBitextMining (ace_Latn-rus_Cyrl) is a bitext mining benchmark built from FLORES for the Acehnese (ace_Latn)–Russian (rus_Cyrl) pair. It provides candidate sentence pairs labeled as parallel or non-parallel to evaluate cross-lingual sentence embeddings and mining algorithms across different scripts and low-resource settings. The dataset stresses the ability to detect true translations for corpus alignment, parallel data creation, bilingual retrieval, and downstream machine translation tasks.

MTEB FloresBitextMining (ban_Latn-rus_Cyrl) is a bilingual bitext-mining dataset pairing Bengali (Latin script) with Russian (Cyrillic) sentences. Provided as part of the MTEB benchmark, it contains parallel and non-parallel sentence examples for evaluating cross-lingual retrieval, parallel sentence extraction, and sentence-embedding alignment across different scripts. The dataset is intended to test and compare multilingual embedding models’ ability to identify translation equivalents and discriminate non-translations between Bengali (Latn) and Russian (Cyrl).

MTEB FloresBitextMining (ell_Grek-rus_Cyrl) is a bilingual bitext mining dataset of aligned sentence pairs between Modern Greek and Russian (Cyrillic), derived from the FLORES resources for the MTEB benchmark. It is intended to evaluate cross-lingual sentence-embedding models on tasks such as bitext mining, parallel sentence identification, and bilingual retrieval, testing models’ ability to match semantically equivalent sentences across different languages and scripts.

MTEB FloresBitextMining (hne_Deva-rus_Cyrl) is a bitext-mining benchmark derived from the FLORES multilingual corpora, containing mined parallel sentence pairs between hne (Devanagari script) and Russian (Cyrillic). It is designed to evaluate multilingual sentence embeddings and cross-lingual retrieval systems on a script- and resource-challenged language pair. The dataset supports benchmarking of bitext mining, parallel sentence extraction, and cross-lingual semantic search, helping compare and improve embedding models for translation retrieval and alignment.

MTEB FloresBitextMining (kik_Latn-rus_Cyrl) is a bitext-mining benchmark in the MTEB suite derived from the FLORES multilingual dataset for the Kikongo (kik, Latin script) ↔ Russian (rus, Cyrillic script) language pair. It evaluates cross-lingual sentence retrieval and parallel-sentence extraction by presenting source sentences with candidate pools containing true translations mixed with distractors. The benchmark measures embedding models’ ability to identify parallelism across distant languages and scripts, supporting development of cross-lingual retrieval, alignment, and parallel-corpus construction methods.

MTEB FloresBitextMining (mai_Deva-rus_Cyrl) is a bitext-mining benchmark drawn from the FLORES resources, containing candidate sentence pairs between Maithili (Devanagari script) and Russian (Cyrillic script). MTEB NTREXBitextMining (rus_Cyrl-jpn_Jpan) is a bitext mining benchmark focusing on Russian (Cyrillic)–Japanese (Japanese script) sentence pairs. MTEB NTREXBitextMining (rus_Cyrl-kor_Hang) is a bitext-mining benchmark in the MTEB suite pairing Russian (Cyrillic) and Korean (Hangul) sentences. MTEB NTREXBitextMining (rus_Cyrl-lit_Latn) is a bilingual bitext mining subset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark designed to evaluate cross-lingual sentence embeddings for Russian (Cyrillic) ↔ Lithuanian (Latin). MTEB NTREXBitextMining (rus_Cyrl-mkd_Cyrl) is a bitext-mining subset of the MTEB benchmark containing Russian (Cyrillic) and Macedonian (Cyrillic) sentence pairs and alignment labels. MTEB NTREXBitextMining (rus_Cyrl-nld_Latn) is a bilingual bitext-mining benchmark within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB), targeting Russian (Cyrillic)–Dutch (Latin) cross-lingual alignment. MTEB NTREXBitextMining (rus_Cyrl–pol_Latn) is a bitext-mining benchmark for Russian (Cyrillic) ↔ Polish (Latin) that provides aligned sentence pairs with non-parallel distractors to evaluate embedding-based cross-lingual retrieval and parallel-sentence extraction. MTEB NTREXBitextMining (rus_Cyrl-por_Latn) is a sentence-level bitext mining dataset pairing Russian (Cyrillic) and Portuguese (Latin) text to evaluate cross-lingual embedding and retrieval models. It contains candidate sentence pairs mined from web-scale corpora with gold labels for parallel vs. non-parallel alignments, enabling benchmarking of bilingual sentence retrieval, parallel sentence extraction, and embedding quality on noisy real-world data. The set is useful for developing and assessing methods for data mining for machine translation and cross-lingual retrieval.

MTEB NTREXBitextMining (rus_Cyrl-slk_Latn) is a bitext mining benchmark within the MTEB suite that evaluates models’ ability to detect and retrieve parallel sentence pairs between Russian (Cyrillic) and Slovak (Latin). MTEB NTREXBitextMining (rus_Cyrl–slv_Latn) is a bitext mining benchmark pair from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, containing Russian (Cyrillic) and Slovene (Latin) sentence pairs for evaluating cross-lingual retrieval and parallel sentence extraction. MTEB NTREXBitextMining (rus_Cyrl-spa_Latn) is a benchmark for cross-lingual bitext mining between Russian (Cyrillic) and Spanish (Latin). MTEB NTREXBitextMining (rus_Cyrl-srp_Cyrl) is a bitext-mining benchmark in the MTEB suite focused on Russian–Serbian (both Cyrillic) sentence pairs. The dataset is intended for assessing embedding quality in mining parallel corpora, bilingual retrieval, and downstream tasks like machine translation data creation.

MTEB NTREXBitextMining (rus_Cyrl-srp_Latn) is a bitext-mining benchmark for evaluating cross-lingual alignment between Russian (Cyrillic) and Serbian (Latin). The dataset is designed to assess embedding quality and mining robustness for closely related languages with different scripts, supporting tasks like cross-lingual retrieval, parallel data extraction for MT, and evaluation of representation alignment.

MTEB NTREXBitextMining (rus_Cyrl-swa_Latn) is a bilingual bitext-mining evaluation set in the MTEB suite for Russian (Cyrillic) and Swahili (Latin). NTREXBitextMining (rus_Cyrl-swe_Latn) is a cross-lingual bitext mining subset from MTEB designed to evaluate extraction of parallel sentence pairs between Russian (Cyrillic) and Swedish (Latin). MTEB NTREXBitextMining (rus_Cyrl-tur_Latn) is a benchmark subset for cross-lingual bitext mining between Russian (Cyrillic) and Turkish (Latin). MTEB NTREXBitextMining (rus_Cyrl-ukr_Cyrl) is a bilingual bitext-mining benchmark containing comparable corpora in Russian and Ukrainian (Cyrillic) with labeled parallel and non-parallel sentence pairs. It evaluates multilingual sentence embedding models on cross-lingual retrieval and parallel sentence extraction between two closely related languages, stressing lexical similarity, subtle syntactic differences, and named-entity variation. The set is intended for measuring embedding quality via mining precision/recall/F1 and for developing systems for parallel corpus creation, sentence alignment, and cross-lingual retrieval.

MTEB NTREXBitextMining (rus_Cyrl-vie_Latn) is a bitext-mining benchmark in the MTEB suite designed to evaluate cross-lingual sentence embeddings on Russian (Cyrillic) ↔ Vietnamese (Latin) data. It provides comparable corpora with annotated parallel/non-parallel sentence pairs to test retrieval-based alignment and mining of translation candidates across distinct scripts and distant languages. The benchmark targets metrics like precision/recall and retrieval ranking (e.g., MRR) and is useful for assessing and improving multilingual embedding models for downstream tasks such as bitext extraction and machine translation data mining.

MTEB NTREXBitextMining (rus_Cyrl-zho_Hant) is a benchmark for cross-lingual bitext mining between Russian (Cyrillic) and Traditional Chinese. It provides bilingual examples for evaluating sentence-embedding models’ ability to retrieve and align parallel sentences across these languages, supporting standard retrieval metrics (precision/recall, P@k). The set is intended to assess and compare multilingual embedding quality for parallel-sentence extraction, cross-lingual retrieval, and downstream translation-related tasks.

MTEB NTREXBitextMining (rus_Cyrl-zul_Latn) is a bitext mining dataset for evaluating multilingual sentence embeddings on cross-lingual parallel-sentence extraction between Russian (Cyrillic) and Zulu (Latin). It provides candidate sentence pairs labeled as parallel or non-parallel, enabling assessment of models on retrieval, ranking, and binary mining accuracy across a typologically and script-diverse language pair. The set is part of the MTEB benchmark suite and is intended to test embedding generalization for low-resource and distant-language bitext discovery.

MTEB NTREXBitextMining (slk_Latn-rus_Cyrl) is a bitext mining benchmark within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) targeting the Slovak (Latin) ↔ Russian (Cyrillic) language pair. The set is intended to measure embedding quality for mining parallel data, supporting metrics like precision/recall and retrieval-based evaluation for downstream machine translation and cross-lingual transfer applications.

MTEB NTREXBitextMining (slv_Latn-rus_Cyrl) is a bitext mining subset used in the Massive Text Embeddings Benchmark to evaluate cross-lingual sentence embedding performance between Slovenian (Latin script) and Russian (Cyrillic script). It provides aligned and non-aligned sentence pairs for retrieval-style evaluation, enabling assessment of models’ ability to identify parallel sentences across languages with different scripts. The dataset targets cross-lingual retrieval, bitext extraction, and multilingual embedding robustness, posing challenges from orthographic, lexical, and low-resource characteristics of the language pair.

MTEB NTREXBitextMining (spa_Latn-rus_Cyrl) is a bitext-mining subset of the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark for the Spanish (Latin) ↔ Russian (Cyrillic) language pair. It provides paired and non-paired text examples for evaluating multilingual sentence/document embeddings on cross-lingual retrieval and parallel-sentence extraction tasks. The set is intended to measure embedding quality for bitext discovery, supporting experiments on precision/recall, retrieval ranking, and downstream tasks such as parallel data mining and cross-lingual information retrieval.

MTEB NTREXBitextMining (srp_Cyrl-rus_Cyrl) is a sentence-level bitext mining benchmark for Serbian (Cyrillic) ↔ Russian (Cyrillic). It provides candidate sentence pairs with ground-truth labels for parallel vs. non-parallel, enabling evaluation of multilingual sentence embeddings and retrieval models on cross-lingual sentence alignment and parallel sentence extraction. The dataset is intended to assess embedding quality for mining parallel corpora in closely related Cyrillic languages and to measure retrieval metrics such as precision, recall, and F1 in a realistic bitext-mining setting.

MTEB NTREXBitextMining (srp_Latn-rus_Cyrl) is a sentence-level bitext mining benchmark for Serbian (Latin script) ↔ Russian (Cyrillic script). It supplies candidate sentence pairs with relevance labels (derived from NTREX web-mined corpora) to evaluate cross-lingual sentence embeddings and retrieval models on parallel sentence extraction and cross-lingual retrieval tasks. The set stresses script and language differences to assess embedding alignment, precision/recall, and robustness of mining methods in a real-world noisy setting.

MTEB NTREXBitextMining (swa_Latn-rus_Cyrl) is a benchmark dataset for cross-lingual bitext mining between Swahili (Latin script) and Russian (Cyrillic script). It provides labeled candidate sentence pairs (positive parallel pairs and negatives) to evaluate models on parallel sentence retrieval, alignment, and cross-lingual semantic similarity. The set is designed to test multilingual sentence embeddings and bitext extraction methods on a challenging, typographically and linguistically diverse language pair.

MTEB NTREXBitextMining (swe_Latn-rus_Cyrl) is a bilingual bitext-mining benchmark containing Swedish (Latin script) and Russian (Cyrillic script) corpora with annotated parallel sentence pairs. It is designed to evaluate multilingual sentence embedding and retrieval models on cross-lingual parallel sentence identification and mining tasks using retrieval metrics. The dataset supports development and comparison of embedding-based approaches for mining parallel data, cross-lingual search, and downstream machine translation or transfer learning.

MTEB NTREXBitextMining (tam_Taml-rus_Cyrl) is a bitext-mining benchmark for Tamil (Tamil script) ↔ Russian (Cyrillic). It provides candidate sentence pairs labeled as parallel or non-parallel to evaluate multilingual sentence embeddings and retrieval models on cross-lingual sentence retrieval and parallel-sentence extraction. The set is intended to test model robustness across script and language differences and to support development and comparison of bitext mining, cross-lingual search, and multilingual representation learning methods.

MTEB NTREXBitextMining (tur_Latn-rus_Cyrl) is a bitext-mining benchmark for Turkish (Latin script) ↔ Russian (Cyrillic script). It contains bilingual sentence pairs and non-parallel examples for evaluating and training embedding-based cross-lingual retrieval and parallel-sentence extraction systems. Included in the MTEB suite, the dataset measures models’ ability to detect translation equivalents across different scripts and supports evaluation of multilingual embeddings, cross-lingual retrieval, and machine-translation data mining.

MTEB NTREXBitextMining (ukr_Cyrl-rus_Cyrl) is a benchmark dataset for cross-lingual bitext mining between Ukrainian and Russian in Cyrillic script. It provides comparable sentence collections with gold-standard alignment labels to evaluate embedding-based retrieval and parallel-sentence extraction methods. Designed for assessing bilingual sentence embeddings and mining pipelines, the dataset supports evaluation with retrieval metrics (precision/recall/F1) and helps measure a model’s ability to discover parallel sentences for machine translation and cross-lingual NLP tasks.

MTEB NTREXBitextMining (vie_Latn-rus_Cyrl) is a bitext-mining benchmark offering sentence-level parallel and comparable data between Vietnamese (Latin script) and Russian (Cyrillic). It supplies positive parallel pairs and non-parallel candidates to evaluate embedding-based cross-lingual retrieval, parallel sentence extraction, and bitext mining systems. The set is designed to test models’ ability to detect and rank translations across different scripts and to support evaluation with standard retrieval and precision/recall metrics for MT and cross-lingual NLP tasks.

MTEB NTREXBitextMining (zho_Hant-rus_Cyrl) is a benchmark for cross-lingual bitext mining between Traditional Chinese (zho_Hant) and Russian in Cyrillic script (rus_Cyrl). It provides candidate sentence/document pairs from comparable corpora with labels indicating true translation pairs, enabling evaluation of multilingual sentence embeddings and retrieval models. The dataset targets cross-script, distant-language alignment challenges and is intended for assessing and developing methods for parallel sentence mining, cross-lingual retrieval, and downstream translation tasks.

MTEB NTREXBitextMining (zul_Latn-rus_Cyrl) is a bitext-mining benchmark from the MTEB/NTREX suite for evaluating cross-lingual sentence-embedding models on mining parallel sentences between Zulu (Latin script) and Russian (Cyrillic). It provides labeled parallel and non-parallel sentence/document pairs to test retrieval and alignment performance (e.g., recall@k, precision) on a low-resource, cross‑script language pair. The dataset is intended for benchmarking multilingual embeddings and bitext extraction systems in challenging cross-script scenarios.

MTEB SIB200Classification (rus_Cyrl) is a Russian (Cyrillic) multi-class text classification benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains short documents labeled across 200 fine-grained topical categories and is designed to evaluate embedding models’ ability to separate semantic classes using downstream probes such as linear classifiers, k-NN, or clustering. The dataset is suited for testing embedding quality, topic discrimination, and cross-lingual transfer on Cyrillic Russian text.

MTEB STS22.v2 (ru) is the Russian subset of the Semantic Textual Similarity 2022 (v2) task within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains pairs of Russian sentences annotated with human similarity scores across diverse domains and registers. The dataset is designed to evaluate sentence embedding models by comparing model-derived similarity (e.g., cosine) with human judgments (typically via Spearman correlation), enabling benchmarking of monolingual and cross-lingual semantic representation quality for Russian.

mMARCO-ar is the Arabic subset of the multilingual MS MARCO retrieval benchmark, providing Arabic queries paired with candidate passages and associated relevance annotations derived from the original MS MARCO data. It enables supervised training and evaluation of passage ranking, reranking, and dense retrieval models in Arabic, supporting research on monolingual and cross-lingual information retrieval, transfer learning, and benchmarking Arabic retrieval system performance.

mMARCO-de is a German-language subset of the multilingual MS MARCO (mMARCO) benchmark providing real user queries paired with candidate passages and relevance labels. It is designed to train and evaluate German information retrieval, passage ranking, and question-answering models, supporting both sparse and dense retrieval as well as neural reranking. Derived from MS MARCO content and adapted or translated into German, mMARCO-de enables research on monolingual and cross-lingual retrieval, domain adaptation, and end-to-end ranking performance in German-language settings.

mMARCO-en is an English retrieval dataset derived from the MS MARCO passage collection, containing real user queries paired with candidate passages and relevance labels. It is designed for training and evaluating passage retrieval, ranking, and re-ranking models (sparse and dense), enabling supervised learning of relevance scoring and end-to-end retrieval pipelines. The dataset supports benchmarking of retrieval effectiveness and generalization to web-search style question answering and information-seeking tasks.

mMARCO-es is a Spanish-language passage ranking dataset derived from the MS MARCO collection, providing Spanish queries paired with candidate passages and relevance labels for supervised training and evaluation of information retrieval and ranking models. It supports development and benchmarking of dense and sparse retrievers, neural rerankers, and cross-lingual retrieval or translation workflows, enabling evaluation with standard ranking metrics (MRR, NDCG) on realistic, web-derived question–passage pairs in Spanish.

mMARCO-hi is the Hindi subset of the multilingual MS MARCO passage retrieval benchmark, containing Hindi queries paired with candidate passages and relevance annotations derived from MS MARCO. It is designed for training and evaluating passage retrieval, reranking, and open-domain question answering systems in Hindi, supporting both sparse and dense retrieval approaches. The dataset enables benchmarking retrieval effectiveness (e.g., MRR, Recall) and research on multilingual and low-resource retrieval, cross-lingual transfer, and Hindi-language QA models.

mMARCO-id is an Indonesian-language variant of the MS MARCO passage-ranking dataset, providing real user queries paired with candidate passages and relevance labels in Indonesian. It is designed for training and evaluating retrieval, reranking, and passage-level QA models in Indonesian, and for research on multilingual and cross-lingual retrieval, dense vector encoders, and transfer learning from high-resource languages.

mMARCO-it is an Italian-language retrieval benchmark derived from the MS MARCO corpus, providing queries paired with candidate passages and relevance labels translated or mapped into Italian. It is intended for training and evaluating Italian passage-ranking, reranking, and dense retrieval models, enabling research on cross-lingual transfer and language-specific ranking techniques. The dataset supports supervised learning of retrieval systems and standardized evaluation of ranking effectiveness in Italian information retrieval tasks.

mMARCO-ja is a Japanese-language adaptation of the MS MARCO benchmark, produced by translating queries and passages into Japanese while retaining original relevance labels and answer spans. It provides real-world search queries paired with candidate passages and relevance judgments (and extracted answer spans for QA), enabling supervised training and evaluation of Japanese retrieval, ranking, and reading-comprehension models. The dataset is suited for benchmarking multilingual transfer, cross-lingual retrieval, and Japanese IR/QA research.

mMARCO-nl is a Dutch-language retrieval and question-answering benchmark derived from the MS MARCO corpus, providing Dutch queries paired with candidate web passages and relevance labels. It is intended for training and evaluating passage retrieval, ranking (sparse and dense), and reading-comprehension models in Dutch, and for studying cross-lingual transfer and domain adaptation. The dataset supports supervised learning and standardized IR evaluation (e.g., MRR, recall, nDCG) for Dutch-language search and QA tasks.

mMARCO-pt is a Portuguese-language passage retrieval dataset derived from the MS MARCO collection, providing Portuguese queries and candidate passages with associated relevance judgments. It is designed for training and evaluating information retrieval and ranking models (sparse and dense retrievers, rerankers) in Portuguese, and for studying cross-lingual transfer and multilingual retrieval performance. The dataset enables development of passage-level ranking systems and benchmarking of retrieval effectiveness on realistic, search-oriented query–document pairs in Portuguese.

mMARCO-ru is a Russian-language passage retrieval dataset derived from the MS MARCO corpus by translating queries and passages into Russian while preserving the original relevance labels. It provides query–passage pairs for supervised training and evaluation of ranking and retrieval models in Russian, enabling development and benchmarking of lexical and dense retrieval, cross-lingual transfer, and multilingual information retrieval systems on realistic web-search style queries.

mMARCO-vi is a Vietnamese passage-ranking dataset derived from the MS MARCO corpus, containing Vietnamese-translated queries and passages with associated relevance labels. It is designed for training and evaluating Vietnamese information retrieval and ranking models (sparse and dense retrieval, reranking, and passage-level QA), enabling benchmarking of retrieval effectiveness and research on cross-lingual transfer and Vietnamese-language IR. The dataset may include translation artifacts from the original English source.

mMARCO-zh is the Chinese subset of the multilingual MS MARCO collection, comprising Chinese queries paired with candidate passages and relevance labels for passage ranking and retrieval. It is intended for training and evaluating Chinese-language ad-hoc retrieval, passage-ranking, and open-domain QA systems, enabling supervised learning of neural rankers and benchmarks for retrieval performance. By adapting MS MARCO annotations and web-sourced passages to Chinese, mMARCO-zh supports large-scale evaluation and cross-lingual transfer research in information retrieval and retrieval-augmented NLP.

MTEB AngryTweetsClassification is a Twitter-based emotion classification dataset in the MTEB suite that contains short tweets labeled for the presence of anger. It is designed to evaluate and benchmark text embedding models and classifiers on emotion/affect detection tasks, measuring how well embeddings capture anger-related semantics for downstream classification, retrieval, and clustering.

MTEB BornholmBitextMining is a benchmark dataset for bitext mining included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It contains candidate sentence pairs labeled as translations or non‑translations to evaluate the ability of multilingual sentence embeddings to identify parallel sentences across languages. The dataset is intended for assessing retrieval and ranking performance of embedding models in parallel sentence extraction tasks, supporting development of cross‑lingual retrieval, machine translation data mining, and multilingual representation learning.

DanishPoliticalCommentsClassification is a Danish-language dataset of online political comments annotated with classification labels (e.g., supportive, critical, neutral or topic-specific categories). Sourced from social-media and news comment threads, it is intended to train and evaluate models for political stance/sentiment classification and to benchmark text-embedding methods on downstream classification and retrieval tasks. The dataset exposes models to informal language, idioms and domain-specific references common in Danish political discourse, making it useful for research in stance detection, sentiment analysis and robust embedding evaluation.

MTEB LccSentimentClassification is a sentence-level sentiment classification dataset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It contains short texts labeled with sentiment classes (e.g., positive/negative/neutral) and is intended to evaluate and compare sentence embedding models and downstream classifiers on sentiment detection. The dataset is suited for benchmarking embedding quality and classifier performance on short-form sentiment texts using metrics such as accuracy and F1.

MTEB NordicLangClassification is a language classification dataset within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark focused on Nordic languages. It contains short texts labeled by their language (e.g., Danish, Norwegian, Swedish, Icelandic, Finnish, and related varieties) drawn from diverse domains and registers to test language discrimination and robustness. The dataset is intended for evaluating and training multilingual embeddings and classifiers on fine-grained Nordic language identification and cross-lingual representations, providing a benchmark for model performance on closely related languages and dialects.

MTEB ScalaDaClassification is a supervised text classification subset of the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It provides labeled text samples paired with categorical labels and standard train/test splits to evaluate sentence and document embeddings on classification tasks. The dataset is intended for benchmarking embedding quality via downstream classifiers (accuracy, F1, etc.), supporting model comparison, selection, and assessment of transferability to real-world classification problems.

Latin Intertextuality Dataset is a curated corpus of Latin texts annotated with intertextual links (quotations, allusions, echoes, and reworkings) between passages and their sources. Each record pairs target and source passages with span-level offsets, normalized references (author/work/book/line), relation-type labels, and provenance metadata to support supervised learning. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating models for intertextual detection, text reuse retrieval, paraphrase/semantic similarity, and citation/link prediction in historical corpora; typical evaluation protocols use precision/recall/F1 and retrieval metrics (mAP, recall@k).

QQP (Quora Question Pairs) is a dataset of question pairs labeled as duplicate or non-duplicate, created to support paraphrase detection and semantic similarity research. It contains hundreds of thousands of question pairs collected from Quora with binary annotations, enabling supervised training and evaluation of classifiers, sentence embeddings, and retrieval models. QQP is commonly used as a benchmark for duplicate question detection, paraphrase identification, and related downstream NLP tasks.

PAWS (Paraphrase Adversaries from Word Scrambling) is a benchmark for paraphrase identification composed of sentence pairs with high lexical overlap but differing semantics, produced via word swapping and controlled generation (and extended via back-translation). It contains both automatically constructed high-overlap pairs and human-annotated paraphrase/non-paraphrase labels (with variants such as PAWS-Wiki and multilingual PAWS-X). PAWS is designed to evaluate model robustness to word order and adversarial perturbations, providing a challenging testbed for sentence encoding, paraphrase detection, and general natural language understanding.

Microsoft Research Paraphrase Corpus (MRPC) is a corpus consists of 5,801 sentence pairs collected from newswire articles. Each pair is labelled if it is a paraphrase or not by human annotators. The whole set is divided into a training subset (4,076 sentence pairs of which 2,753 are paraphrases) and a test subset (1,725 pairs of which 1,147 are paraphrases). Source: Image Source:

The **Multi-Genre Natural Language Inference** (**MultiNLI**) dataset has 433K sentence pairs. Its size and mode of collection are modeled closely like . MultiNLI offers ten distinct genres (Face-to-face, Telephone, 9/11, Travel, Letters, Oxford University Press, Slate, Verbatim, Goverment and Fiction) of written and spoken English data. There are matched dev/test sets which are derived from the same sources as those in the training set, and mismatched sets which do not closely resemble any seen at training time. Source:

The **SNLI** dataset (**Stanford Natural Language Inference**) consists of 570k sentence-pairs manually labeled as entailment, contradiction, and neutral. Premises are image captions from Flickr30k, while hypotheses were generated by crowd-sourced annotators who were shown a premise and asked to generate entailing, contradicting, and neutral sentences. Annotators were instructed to judge the relation between sentences given that they describe the same event. Each pair is labeled as “entailment”, “neutral”, “contradiction” or “-”, where “-” indicates that an agreement could not be reached. Source:

The Extreme Summarization (**XSum**) dataset is a dataset for evaluation of abstractive single-document summarization systems. The goal is to create a short, one-sentence new summary answering the question “What is the article about?”. The dataset consists of 226,711 news articles accompanied with a one-sentence summary. The articles are collected from BBC articles (2010 to 2017) and cover a wide variety of domains (e.g., News, Politics, Sports, Weather, Business, Technology, Science, Health, Family, Education, Entertainment and Arts). The official random split contains 204,045 (90%), 11,332 (5%) and 11,334 (5) documents in training, validation and test sets, respectively.

It is designed for training and evaluating abstractive and extractive summarization models on news-domain content and for research in multilingual and cross-lingual transfer for Spanish-language summarization.

XLSum (csebuetnlp/xlsum) is a large-scale multilingual abstractive summarization dataset of news articles paired with concise (single-sentence) summaries across 44 languages. It provides single-document article-summary pairs suitable for training and evaluating multilingual and cross-lingual summarization models, benchmarking generation quality, and studying transfer and generalization across diverse languages and scripts.

scientific_papers is a paired corpus of full-text scientific articles and their abstracts (commonly split into arXiv and PubMed subsets). It supplies article bodies, abstracts, titles and basic metadata, enabling supervised training and evaluation of abstractive summarization and long-document understanding models. The dataset is suited for benchmarking long-form summarization, information extraction, scientific QA, and related tasks across diverse research domains.

The CNN/Daily Mail dataset is a large-scale, text-based question answering dataset composed of news articles from the CNN and Daily Mail outlets, paired with corresponding questions and answers. It is widely used to evaluate machine reading comprehension and natural language understanding systems, particularly in tasks requiring the ability to extract and reason over information from unstructured text. The dataset contains hundreds of thousands of document-question-answer triples, reflecting real-world journalistic content in English, and is characterized by complex, open-domain questions that require contextual understanding. Due to its scale and diversity, it serves as a benchmark for training and evaluating models in reading comprehension, such as attention-based neural networks and transformer architectures. Billsum is useful for research on domain adaptation, content extraction, controlled generation, and improving automated summarization for policy and legal documents.

SAMSum is a dataset designed for abstractive dialogue summarization, a subtask of natural language processing focused on generating concise summaries that capture the essential information from conversational text. The dataset consists of dialogues paired with human-written summaries, enabling models to learn how to produce coherent and informative condensations of multi-turn conversations. SAMSum is particularly valuable for developing and evaluating abstractive summarization models, which generate novel summary text rather than extracting sentences verbatim. It presents challenges such as understanding conversational context, managing informal language, and preserving key dialogue elements. The dataset is widely used to benchmark the performance of large language models and summarization systems, facilitating advancements in dialogue understanding and generation. Its focus on dialogue rather than monologic text distinguishes it from traditional summarization datasets, making it an important resource for research on conversational AI and summarization techniques.

BigPatent is a large-scale text summarization dataset comprising approximately 1.3 million U.S. patent documents paired with human-written abstractive summaries. Due to the technical and formal nature of patent documents, BigPatent presents challenges including long input sequences and domain-specific language, making it a valuable benchmark for evaluating the ability of models to handle extended contexts and specialized vocabulary. It is widely used to develop and assess advanced natural language processing models, particularly those employing transformer architectures. The dataset’s scale and complexity have motivated innovations in model design, such as sparse attention mechanisms that enable efficient processing of long sequences, thereby improving summarization performance. BigPatent serves as a critical resource for advancing abstractive summarization methods in real-world, technical domains requiring both precision and conciseness

desc: TNSMC (Turkish News Summarization Master Corpus) is a corpus of Turkish news articles paired with human-written summaries for training and evaluating single-document summarization systems. It contains article–summary pairs across diverse news topics, supporting both extractive and abstractive approaches and standard automatic evaluation (e.g., ROUGE). TNSMC serves as a benchmark for developing Turkish-language summarization, headline generation, and related downstream NLP tasks.

Spider (Korean) is a Korean-language adaptation of the Spider text-to-SQL benchmark, providing natural-language questions in Korean paired with corresponding SQL queries and database schemas across diverse domains. It preserves Spider’s cross-domain, multi-table and compositional query complexity (joins, nested queries, aggregations), enabling evaluation of generalization to unseen databases.
