Census-Income (Adult) is a tabular supervised classification dataset derived from the 1994 U.S. Census used to predict whether an individual’s annual income exceeds $50K. It contains roughly 48,000 records with a mix of continuous and categorical attributes (age, workclass, education, occupation, hours-per-week, race, sex, native-country, etc.), and a binary target. The dataset is commonly used for benchmarking classification algorithms and for research on feature encoding, handling missing values and categorical variables, class imbalance, interpretability, and fairness/privacy in income prediction tasks.

Diabetes 130-US Hospitals is a de-identified electronic health record dataset of 101,766 hospital admissions for diabetic patients collected from 130 U.S. hospitals (1999–2008). It contains ~50 demographic, administrative and clinical features per admission, including age, race, diagnoses (ICD-9 codes), admission/discharge types, lab/test counts, medications, and length of stay, with a multi-class readmission label (<30 days, >30 days, or no readmission). The dataset is widely used for supervised tasks such as readmission prediction, risk stratification, and medication or diagnosis modeling, and supports investigations into class imbalance, feature engineering, and fairness in clinical ML.

pokemon.csv is a tabular dataset of Pokémon species with per-monster attributes such as ID and name, primary/secondary types, base stats (HP, Attack, Defense, Sp. Atk, Sp. Def, Speed, Total), generation, and a legendary flag; some versions also include height, weight, base experience and abilities. It is suitable for supervised tasks (type or legendary-status classification, stat regression), clustering and similarity / recommendation experiments, and for demonstrating feature engineering and multi-label learning on small-to-medium sized structured data.

train.csv is the primary training split for the benchmark: a tabular CSV where each row is an example and columns include an identifier, input feature fields (numeric and categorical) and a target label for supervised learning. World Happiness is a country-level socio-economic dataset compiling annual happiness scores and explanatory indicators (e.g., GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom, generosity, perceptions of corruption) drawn from the World Happiness Report and related sources. It is structured for supervised regression and exploratory analysis to study drivers of subjective well-being, temporal trends, and cross-country comparisons. Common uses include predictive modeling of happiness scores, causal/feature-importance studies, fairness and policy analysis, and benchmarking interpretable models on real-world social indicators.

diabetes_detection is a supervised tabular dataset for binary classification of diabetes status, containing patient-level clinical and demographic features (e.g., age, BMI, blood glucose measures, blood pressure, and related lab results) paired with diagnostic labels indicating diabetic vs. non-diabetic outcomes. It is designed to support development and evaluation of machine learning models for early detection, risk stratification, and screening, including feature selection, calibration, and fairness analyses. The dataset is suitable for benchmarking preprocessing pipelines, imbalanced-class handling, and performance metrics such as AUC, sensitivity, and specificity in healthcare prediction tasks.

iris_classification is a small supervised multiclass dataset of 150 Iris flower samples, each with four numeric features (sepal length, sepal width, petal length, petal width) and a label for one of three species (setosa, versicolor, virginica). It is widely used for benchmarking and teaching classification algorithms, feature selection, and visualization techniques, providing a low-dimensional, well-understood testbed for evaluating model training, validation, and basic multiclass performance metrics.

UNSW_NB15 training set is a labeled network traffic CSV used for supervised intrusion detection research. It contains flow-level records extracted from synthetic mixed benign and malicious traffic, with a rich set of features (numeric and categorical) describing packet/flow statistics, protocol and service attributes, and engineered content/time-based metrics. Each record includes a binary label (normal/attack) and a categorized attack type (e.g., DoS, Exploit, Reconnaissance, Worms), making the file suitable for binary and multi-class classification, anomaly detection, feature selection, and benchmarking of IDS models.

trips_nonempty_bl1m.csv is a tabular CSV of non-empty mobility trip records intended for transportation and mobility ML tasks. Each row represents a completed trip with anonymized identifiers and typically includes start/end timestamps, origin and destination (coordinates or zone IDs), travel distance and duration, and optional attributes such as mode or fare. The file is prefiltered to remove empty or incomplete trips and is sized for scalable experiments (on the order of one million records), making it suitable for travel-time estimation, destination prediction, demand forecasting, trajectory clustering, and anomaly detection.

mdelcristo/NQ-F_1min_OHLCV_Parquet is a columnar Parquet dataset of 1‑minute OHLCV (open, high, low, close, volume) bars for the NQ‑F instrument (Nasdaq‑100 futures). skill_level_dataset_1998 is a synthetic, class-balanced dataset for predicting skill levels. It provides simulated feature vectors (performance metrics, behavioral signals, and contextual attributes) paired with discrete skill-level labels across multiple classes. Designed for controlled benchmarking of classification, ranking, and calibration methods, it enables reproducible evaluation of model accuracy, fairness, and feature-importance without class imbalance confounds, and is suitable for experiments in supervised learning, domain adaptation, and curriculum learning.

risk_tolerance_dataset_v1 is a synthetic tabular dataset of 2,000 rows for modeling individual financial risk tolerance. Each record contains simulated demographic and financial covariates (e.g., age, income, net worth), behavioral/psychometric features (e.g., investment_experience, time_horizon, survey-style responses), and a target risk_tolerance label provided both as a continuous score and as categorical bands (low/medium/high). Generated with controlled distributions and configurable noise, the dataset is intended for supervised regression and classification, calibration and fairness testing, robustness and interpretability experiments, and rapid prototyping of risk-prediction pipelines without using real personal data.

confidence_dataset_v1_3000 is a synthetic, class- and confidence-balanced dataset of 3,000 samples designed for training and evaluating model confidence, calibration, and uncertainty estimation. Each example pairs an input (feature vector or simulated observation) with a ground-truth class label and an associated target confidence score or correctness indicator, generated under controlled noise and distributional settings. Balanced across classes and confidence strata, the dataset supports development and benchmarking of calibration methods, selective prediction/thresholding strategies, and meta-models for reliability-aware decision making.

idea_difficulty_dataset_2000 is a synthetic, balanced benchmark of 2,000 short idea prompts annotated with multi-level difficulty labels (e.g., easy / medium / hard) and scalar difficulty scores. Samples were procedurally generated and augmented to cover diverse domains and complexity cues (required skills, estimated time, resource intensity), with labels evenly distributed to avoid class imbalance. The dataset is intended for supervised classification, regression, and ranking tasks—evaluating models that predict task complexity, calibrate generation systems, or support curriculum planning—and includes standard train/validation/test splits and metadata per example for controlled experiments.

LEGO-Sizes is a dataset of images of LEGO pieces annotated with piece identity and physical size information (e.g., dimensions or stud counts). Images capture varied poses, backgrounds, lighting and partial occlusion to support realistic size inference. It is intended for training and evaluating models for size estimation (regression), piece classification, scale-aware detection and segmentation, and applications such as inventory automation, robotic manipulation, and AR that require inferring physical dimensions from images.

Chess Positions with Concepts is a dataset of chess positions (FENs) annotated with human-interpretable tactical and positional concept labels. Each example includes the FEN, side to move, legal moves, material counts and optional engine evaluation, plus multi-hot concept labels covering patterns such as check, mate threat, fork, skewer, pin, discovered attack, passed/isolated/doubled pawns, open file, king safety, outpost, space advantage, and similar motifs. Labels are produced by a combination of rule-based detection, engine heuristics and expert verification. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating concept-based and interpretable models, concept bottleneck approaches, and research on aligning learned representations with human chess reasoning.

Wellness Tourism Dataset is a multimodal benchmark for machine learning on wellness-focused travel experiences, combining venue images, descriptive text, user reviews and ratings, amenity tags (spa, yoga, thermal baths, retreats), pricing and star-level metadata, and geolocation/time information. It supports tasks such as destination classification, personalized recommendation, sentiment and review analysis, multimodal retrieval, and demand/seasonality forecasting. Binary classification experiments on full sentences (negative or somewhat negative vs somewhat positive or positive with neutral sentences discarded) refer to the dataset as SST-2 or SST binary.

Financial PhraseBank is a domain-specific sentiment analysis dataset focused on financial texts, designed to evaluate models' ability to classify the sentiment of financial phrases. The dataset addresses the challenge of limited labeled data and domain-specific terminology, which makes general-purpose language models ineffective. Due to its domain focus, it serves as a critical benchmark for evaluating financial sentiment analysis models, particularly those fine-tuned on domain-specific pre-trained architectures like FinBERT. The dataset supports tasks such as sentiment classification and opinion mining, and is often used to assess model performance using standard metrics like accuracy, F1-score, and precision. IndoNLU is a benchmark suite for Indonesian natural language understanding that aggregates multiple annotated datasets across tasks such as sentiment and topic classification, hate-speech detection, named entity recognition, POS tagging, paraphrase/pairwise classification, and machine reading comprehension. It provides standardized splits and evaluation protocols to train, fine-tune, and compare pretrained language models and downstream systems in Indonesian. The benchmark enables consistent assessment of model performance and advances in Indonesian NLP applications.

ANLI (Adversarial Natural Language Inference) is a large-scale NLI benchmark of sentence pairs labeled entailment, contradiction, or neutral, created via an iterative human-and-model-in-the-loop process. Crowdworkers were asked to write examples that fooled contemporary models across three rounds (R1–R3), producing challenging, adversarial instances that expose model weaknesses. ANLI is used to evaluate robustness, adversarial generalization, and out-of-distribution performance of NLI systems.

NCI Binary Classification is a molecular graph dataset of chemical compounds labeled by anticancer activity (active vs. inactive). It is commonly used to train and benchmark graph-based models and molecular machine learning methods for activity prediction, virtual screening, and representation learning on chemical structures.

NSFW-Safe-Dataset is a curated image dataset for training and evaluating automated content-moderation and NSFW-detection models. The IMDb dataset is a large-scale graph-based dataset commonly used for link prediction and network analysis tasks. This dataset supports various tasks including link prediction, node classification, and network reconstruction, making it valuable for evaluating network representation learning methods. IMDb is frequently employed as a benchmark to assess the performance of graph-based learning models, particularly those designed to handle complex relational structures and dynamic interactions within heterogeneous networks.

GLUE MNLI is the Multi-Genre Natural Language Inference subset in the GLUE benchmark: a large-scale NLI corpus (~433k premise–hypothesis pairs) annotated with three-class labels (entailment, contradiction, neutral) across diverse genres. It provides matched (in-domain) and mismatched (cross-genre) dev/test splits to evaluate model performance and generalization, making it a standard benchmark for training and assessing natural language understanding and transfer learning systems.

CoLA (Corpus of Linguistic Acceptability) in GLUE is a binary sentence-level acceptability dataset for English: each example is a naturalistic sentence labeled as grammatically acceptable or unacceptable. CoLA is commonly used to train and evaluate models on syntactic/grammatical knowledge, with performance typically reported using Matthews correlation coefficient.

The dataset is intended for supervised sentiment classification, tone analysis, and domain-adaptive language models to detect risk signals, shifts in auditor stance, or unusual language in financial reporting. It supports research in financial NLP, audit analytics, and downstream tasks such as forecasting restatements, credit risk, or regulatory compliance.

It covers diverse scenes, poses, occlusions, clothing, and motion patterns to support robust supervised learning and evaluation of video segmentation, tracking, and human parsing models. ViHSD is designed to benchmark spatial accuracy and temporal consistency of algorithms in realistic, dynamic conditions.

Custom Indonesian Dataset is a curated collection of Indonesian-language data designed for training and benchmarking machine learning models for natural language tasks. It aggregates diverse text sources (e.g., news, social media, conversational transcripts) with annotations for common tasks such as classification, named-entity recognition, sentiment analysis, and language/dialect labeling, provided with standard train/validation/test splits and metadata. The dataset supports development and evaluation of Indonesian NLP models, enabling research in domain adaptation, robustness across genres and regional variants, and downstream applications like translation, information extraction, and conversational agents.

dataset_node: German Custom Dataset␟Emotion Classification in German
desc: German Custom Dataset is a curated collection of German-language text samples with high-quality annotations for supervised NLP tasks. It spans diverse domains (news, social media, legal, conversational) and includes labels for classification (sentiment/intent), named entities, part-of-speech tags, and parallel English translations for machine translation. Designed for training and evaluation, the dataset supports benchmarking, domain adaptation, and robustness testing of German NLP models, emphasizing balanced class distributions and realistic language variation to improve generalization to practical applications.

Rommanian Sentiment Dataset is a Romanian-language corpus of texts annotated for sentiment polarity (positive, negative, neutral) at sentence and document granularity. Collected from sources such as product reviews, social media posts, and comments, it provides paired text–label examples for supervised sentiment classification and model evaluation. The dataset supports benchmarking Romanian NLP models, transfer learning and cross-lingual sentiment research, and is typically distributed as plain text with associated labels and source metadata.

dataset_node: A Large Romanian Sentiment Data Set␟Text Classification
dataset: A Large Romanian Sentiment Data Set
root_a: A Large Romanian Sentiment Data Set
root_b: a large romanian sentiment data set
desc: A Large Romanian Sentiment Data Set is a corpus of Romanian-language texts annotated for sentiment, providing a large collection of labeled examples for polarity classification. It supports supervised training and evaluation of sentiment-analysis models (sentence- and/or document-level) and is suitable for tasks such as polarity detection, lexicon induction, domain adaptation, and multilingual transfer learning. The dataset enables development and benchmarking of NLP systems that understand opinion and affect in Romanian-language content.

TREC is a question classification dataset of open-domain, fact-based questions labeled with semantic categories. It contains several thousand short questions (commonly 5,500 train / 500 test) annotated with coarse labels (6 classes such as ABBR, DESC, ENTY, HUM, LOC, NUM) and finer-grained subcategories (up to 50). TREC is widely used for supervised training and evaluation of NLP models for question classification, intent detection, semantic understanding, and as a preprocessing component in question-answering systems.

clinc_oos is a benchmark dataset for intent classification and out-of-scope (OOS) detection in conversational language understanding. It contains natural language user utterances covering 150 intent classes across multiple domains plus a set of explicit OOS examples that do not match any in-scope intent. The dataset is used to train and evaluate supervised intent classifiers and open-set/OOS detection methods, enabling assessment of accuracy, robustness to unseen queries, and generalization across domains.

Arabic Semantic Relevance is a labeled dataset of Arabic text pairs (queries, sentences, or short passages) annotated for semantic relevance and similarity. It provides human-annotated binary or graded relevance labels to support supervised training and evaluation of tasks such as semantic search, sentence-pair classification, retrieval reranking, paraphrase identification, and embedding-based similarity. The dataset covers multiple domains and language varieties to benchmark Arabic NLU models, enabling comparison of classification, ranking, and representation-learning approaches for Arabic semantic understanding.

Custom Depression Tweets Dataset is a collection of Twitter posts annotated for indicators of depression. Each entry includes tweet text and human-provided labels indicating likely depressive content or symptom severity, with optional metadata such as timestamps and anonymized user identifiers. The dataset is intended for supervised training and evaluation of NLP models for depression detection, symptom monitoring, and risk assessment, and is designed to support research into clinically relevant and privacy-preserving mental-health interventions. Use requires careful ethical review and adherence to privacy and consent guidelines.

dataset_node: Arabic Levantine Hate Speech Detection␟Hate Speech Detection
desc: Arabic Levantine Hate Speech Detection is a dataset of Levantine Arabic social media posts annotated for hate and offensive language. Collected from regional platforms and annotated by native speakers, entries are labeled for presence/absence of hate speech and include contextual metadata such as target group (e.g., religion, ethnicity, nationality, gender) and regional dialect tag (Syrian, Lebanese, Jordanian, Palestinian). It is intended for supervised training and evaluation of content-moderation and hate-detection models, as well as research on dialect-specific lexical and pragmatic cues, fairness, and cross-dialect transfer.

dataset_node: Merged Emotion Datasets (GoEmotions + ISEAR + Emotion)␟Emotion Classification
desc: Merged Emotion Datasets (GoEmotions + ISEAR + Emotion) is an English-language emotion classification corpus created by combining three complementary resources: GoEmotions (Reddit comments with fine-grained, often multi-label annotations), ISEAR (self-reported emotion episodes), and the Emotion (crowd-labeled short text) dataset. The merged set provides diverse short-text examples spanning everyday conversational, self-report, and crowd-sourced domains, with annotations harmonized to a common emotion taxonomy. It supports single- and multi-label emotion recognition, transfer learning, and cross-domain evaluation, making it useful for benchmarking model robustness, fine-grained affect classification, and applied affective-NLP tasks.

StaQC is a large-scale corpus of real-world Stack Overflow question texts paired with their corresponding code snippets, automatically mined and curated to produce high-quality natural language–code pairs. It covers multiple programming languages and includes question titles/bodies linked to solution snippets, making it suitable for supervised training and evaluation of code search/retrieval, NL-to-code generation, code summarization, and program understanding models using realistic, diverse, and noisy developer data.

WikiCAT_esv2 is a Spanish-language Wikipedia-derived dataset that pairs article texts and titles with structured category annotations and taxonomy metadata. It is designed for multi-label and hierarchical classification, taxonomy-aware representation learning, and retrieval tasks in Spanish, supporting supervised, zero‑shot and few‑shot evaluation. Each instance contains the article content, its assigned categories (with hierarchical relations), and identifiers for reproducible splits.

cardiffnlp/tweet_topic_single is a curated single-label topic classification dataset of English tweets where each short social-media message is paired with one topical category. It provides labeled examples and standard splits for training and evaluation, enabling supervised learning and benchmarking of topic and text-classification models on noisy, informal Twitter language. The dataset is useful for research into transfer learning, domain adaptation, label imbalance, and robustness to social-media artifacts such as hashtags, mentions, and abbreviations.

dataset_node: Polish Custom Dataset␟Emotion Classification in Polish
desc: Polish Custom Dataset is a curated collection of Polish-language data paired with manual annotations for common NLP tasks (e.g., sentiment, named-entity recognition, POS tagging, and intent classification). It covers diverse domains and registers to capture colloquial and formal usage, enabling supervised training and evaluation of Polish-language models. Designed to support benchmarking, domain adaptation, and robustness testing, the dataset facilitates development of tokenization, morphological analysis, and downstream applications such as information extraction and dialogue systems for Polish.

LusakaLang Language Data is a multilingual corpus collected in Lusaka, Zambia, capturing urban speech and written text with frequent code-switching between English and local language varieties. The dataset contains audio recordings with aligned transcripts, text documents, speaker and recording metadata, and task-oriented annotations such as language tags, sentence-level translations, and basic NER/sentiment labels. It is intended for benchmarking and training models for ASR, machine translation, language identification, code-switching modeling, and other low-resource NLP tasks sensitive to dialectal and sociolinguistic variation.

sms_spam is a labeled SMS message dataset for binary spam/ham classification. It provides raw short-text messages paired with ground-truth labels, enabling supervised learning and evaluation of spam-detection models. Common uses include text preprocessing and tokenization experiments, feature engineering (n-grams, TF-IDF, embeddings), baseline model benchmarking, and studying class-imbalance handling and robustness in lightweight NLP systems.

dataset_node: CheckThat! Lab Task 1 Subjectivity Detection at CLEF 2025 - English␟Subjectivity Detection
dataset: CheckThat! Lab Task 1 Subjectivity Detection at CLEF 2025 - English
root_a: CheckThat! Lab Task 1 Subjectivity Detection at CLEF 2025 - English
root_b: checkthat lab task 1 subjectivity detection at clef 2025 english
desc: CheckThat! Lab Task 1 Subjectivity Detection at CLEF 2025 — English is a supervised classification dataset of English-language texts annotated for subjectivity (subjective vs. objective). It contains short-form content drawn from social media, news and/or user-generated sources, paired with gold labels to support training and evaluation of models that detect subjective language. The dataset is provided with standard splits for training, development and testing and is intended to benchmark classifiers and preprocessing modules used in fact-checking, sentiment analysis and misinformation detection pipelines.

Arabic-Sentiment-50K is a benchmark dataset of 50,000 Arabic-language text samples annotated for sentiment. It provides supervised labels (e.g., positive/negative/neutral) for short texts drawn from online sources (tweets, reviews, posts), supporting training and evaluation of sentiment classification models. The dataset is suitable for benchmarking Arabic NLP systems, transfer learning, domain and dialect robustness studies, and error analysis; typical releases include standard train/validation/test splits and basic metadata to facilitate reproducible experiments.

SafeGuard (clean test set) is a curated evaluation split of the SafeGuard benchmark containing unperturbed, real-world inputs with ground-truth labels across safety-relevant categories. It is intended to measure baseline model performance, calibration, and error rates under nominal (non-adversarial) conditions, providing a reliable reference for accuracy, false positives/negatives, and generalization before applying adversarial or robustness evaluations. The set supports comparative assessment of detection, classification, and risk-mitigation approaches in safety-sensitive applications.

DailyDialog is a high-quality, human-written multi-turn English conversation dataset of everyday dialogues annotated with dialog acts and emotion labels. It is designed for training and evaluating open-domain conversational models, response generation, intent/act classification, and emotion recognition, providing realistic turn-taking and topical variety for modeling natural conversational behavior.

Microsoft Research Paraphrase Corpus (MRPC) is a corpus consists of 5,801 sentence pairs collected from newswire articles. Each pair is labelled if it is a paraphrase or not by human annotators. The whole set is divided into a training subset (4,076 sentence pairs of which 2,753 are paraphrases) and a test subset (1,725 pairs of which 1,147 are paraphrases). Source: Image Source:

rotten_tomatoes_movie_review is a text classification dataset of short movie review snippets from Rotten Tomatoes annotated with binary sentiment labels (positive/negative). It is designed for supervised sentiment-analysis and polarity-detection tasks on compact, colloquial review text, serving as a benchmark for training and evaluating classification and transfer-learning models on short-form opinionated language.

XNLI (Cross-lingual Natural Language Inference) is a multilingual benchmark of premise–hypothesis sentence pairs labeled with entailment, contradiction, or neutral. It extends the English MultiNLI corpus via professional translations into multiple languages to enable evaluation of cross-lingual transfer, multilingual encoders, and zero-shot/fine-tuned NLI performance across languages.

OffensEval-2020-TR is a Turkish-language dataset of Twitter posts annotated for offensive language detection, created for the SemEval-2020 OffensEval shared task. It provides supervised labels for three hierarchical subtasks: A — offensive vs. not offensive (OFF/NOT), B — targeted vs. untargeted offense (TIN/UNT), and C — target type for targeted insults (individual/group/other; IND/GRP/OTH). The corpus supports development and evaluation of classifiers for binary and fine-grained offensive content detection, target identification, and cross-lingual or multilingual transfer studies on social-media text in Turkish.

GLUE MNLI is the Multi-Genre Natural Language Inference subset in the GLUE benchmark: a large-scale NLI corpus (~433k premise–hypothesis pairs) annotated with three-class labels (entailment, contradiction, neutral) across diverse genres. It provides matched (in-domain) and mismatched (cross-genre) dev/test splits to evaluate model performance and generalization, making it a standard benchmark for training and assessing natural language understanding and transfer learning systems.

Allocine is a French-language dataset of movie reviews collected from the Allociné website, with each review annotated by the reviewer’s star-rating. It is commonly used as a benchmark for sentiment and text-classification tasks in French, supporting supervised training and evaluation of language models and transfer learning approaches.

dataset_fakeNews_Es is a Spanish-language dataset for automated misinformation detection and fact-checking. It contains news articles, headlines and social-media posts in Spanish annotated with veracity labels (e.g., true/false/unverified) and accompanied by provenance metadata such as source, publication date, URL and fact-check references. Entries include text content (title and body), and when available social engagement or author metadata. The dataset is intended for supervised classification, credibility assessment, stance detection and fact-checking research and evaluation of Spanish-language misinformation models.

Vietnamese Social Comments is a dataset of Vietnamese-language comments collected from social platforms, annotated for content-analysis tasks such as sentiment classification, toxicity/hate-speech detection, and spam/intent labeling. It captures informal, conversational text with slang, abbreviations, emojis and code-mixing, making it suitable for training and evaluating classifiers, content-moderation systems, and robustness/domain-adaptation research in Vietnamese NLP.

PRDECT-ID is a dataset for product defect detection and instance identification in industrial inspection. It contains high-resolution RGB images of manufactured items annotated with bounding boxes, defect-type labels, segmentation masks, and persistent instance IDs across multiple views or frames. Designed to support supervised learning for defect detection, classification, segmentation and cross-view re-identification/tracking under varied lighting, viewpoints and background conditions, it provides a benchmark for evaluating detection mAP, classification accuracy, segmentation IoU and ID association performance.

The **Recognizing Textual Entailment (RTE)** datasets come from a series of textual entailment challenges. Data from RTE1, RTE2, RTE3 and RTE5 is combined. Examples are constructed based on news and Wikipedia text.

Project Sentinel is a HotpotQA-derived benchmark for multi-hop question answering and evidence grounding. It contains question–answer pairs that require cross-document reasoning, annotated supporting facts, and distractor paragraphs to evaluate retrieval, reasoning chains, and verification. Designed to measure models’ multi-hop inference, evidence retrieval, and explainability, it supports span and yes/no answers and exposes reasoning paths for robustness and fact-checking research.

GoEmotions is a crowd-annotated dataset of ~58k Reddit comments labeled with 27 fine-grained emotion categories plus neutral. Annotations are multi-label (comments can express multiple emotions), enabling research and benchmarking in fine-grained emotion recognition, multi-label classification, sentiment analysis, and content moderation for NLP models. The dataset is suited for training and evaluating classifiers, transfer learning, and analyses of emotional nuance and ambiguity in online text.

Turkish News is a corpus of Turkish-language news articles collected from multiple publishers, containing titles, full article text and accompanying metadata (publication date, source, and category/tags when available). It is intended as a benchmark for Turkish NLP tasks such as topic classification, language modeling, summarization, information retrieval and named-entity recognition, supporting supervised and unsupervised experiments on real-world journalistic text and domain adaptation to newswire content.

test cls is a benchmark dataset for supervised classification, consisting of labeled examples intended as a held-out test split for evaluating model performance and generalization. It provides ground-truth class annotations across multiple categories and supports standard evaluation metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1. The dataset is designed for benchmarking and comparing classification architectures, training procedures, and post-training calibration in controlled evaluation scenarios.

NanoQuoraRetrieval R25 is a compact question-to-question retrieval benchmark derived from the Quora Question Pairs corpus. It supplies query questions paired with labeled positive (duplicate) and negative candidates under an R25 protocol (25 candidate passages per query) to evaluate semantic retrieval and reranking systems. Designed for fast experimentation and reproducible comparisons, it targets metrics such as Recall@k, MRR, and nDCG and is useful for developing and benchmarking lightweight retrieval models and embedding-based ranking in low-resource settings.

NanoMSMARCO R25 is a compact passage-ranking benchmark derived from the MS MARCO corpus. It provides a small set of real user queries, candidate passages, and relevance judgments produced by pooling to depth 25 (R25), enabling fast, reproducible evaluation of retrieval and ranking models. By preserving MS MARCO’s query diversity and relevance patterns while drastically reducing dataset size, NanoMSMARCO R25 is suited for rapid prototyping, ablation studies, and educational use with standard IR metrics (e.g., MRR, NDCG).

NanoNQ R25 is a compact retrieval benchmark derived from the Natural Questions corpus, consisting of a small set of real user questions paired with gold‑annotated relevant passages. It is tailored for evaluating passage retrieval and reranking models with emphasis on recall-at-25 and related ranking metrics. Designed for fast iteration and low-resource experiments, NanoNQ R25 enables rapid prototyping, debugging, and lightweight performance checks of retrieval pipelines.

dataset_node: NanoBEIR R25 mean␟Cross Encoder Nano BEIR
desc: NanoBEIR R25 mean is a compact information retrieval benchmark derived from the BEIR suite that reports the mean Recall@25 across a curated subset of retrieval tasks. It provides a lightweight, diverse evaluation set for quick comparison of retrieval models (sparse, dense, and rerankers) across multiple domains and query types. Designed for fast benchmarking and model selection, NanoBEIR R25 mean enables reproducible assessment of retrieval effectiveness at a moderate cutoff depth while preserving BEIR’s cross-domain challenge.

combined is an aggregated benchmark that merges multiple related datasets into a single standardized collection, unifying formats, labels, and train/validation/test splits. By combining diverse scenes, sensors, and degradation types (e.g., blur, noise, resolution changes), it provides broader coverage of real-world variability to improve model robustness and generalization. The dataset is suitable for training and evaluating supervised and transfer-learning models across tasks such as restoration, enhancement, and domain-adaptation, and serves as a challenging cross-domain benchmark for comparative evaluation.

indonesian-financial-sentiment is a labeled dataset of Indonesian-language financial texts annotated for sentiment (e.g., positive, negative, neutral). It aggregates finance-specific short texts—such as news snippets, analyst commentary, company disclosures, and social media posts—and provides human annotations to support supervised sentiment classification in the financial domain. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating models for market sentiment analysis, investor opinion mining, risk monitoring, and related downstream tasks (e.g., event-driven forecasting), and is useful for fine-tuning Indonesian NLP models and benchmarking domain-adapted sentiment classifiers.

Custom Test Set is a curated held-out dataset for final evaluation of trained models. It contains unseen samples representative of the target distribution and includes ground-truth annotations (labels, masks, or target values as appropriate) to enable standardized performance measurement. The set is intended to assess generalization and robustness across realistic and challenging conditions and is reserved for testing only (no training or hyperparameter tuning).

japanese-toxic-dataset is a corpus of Japanese-language user-generated text annotated for toxic content to support automated moderation and toxicity detection research. It contains comments and posts collected from online platforms, each labeled for toxicity (binary and/or multi-label categories such as hate, insult, harassment, sexual content, etc.) to enable supervised training and evaluation of classification models. The dataset is intended as a benchmark for building and comparing Japanese toxicity classifiers, improving content-moderation pipelines, and studying robustness, bias, and generalization in toxic-language detection for Japanese.

SemEval-2010 Task 8 dataset is designed for multi-way classification of semantic relations between pairs of nominals. It contains annotated examples where each pair is labeled with one of several mutually exclusive semantic relation types. The dataset is widely used for relation classification tasks in natural language processing, providing a benchmark for evaluating models that identify and categorize semantic relationships between noun pairs in sentences.

EXIST Dataset is a curated benchmark for evaluating machine learning models on real-world, challenging data distributions. It provides diverse, expertly annotated samples with standardized train/validation/test splits and evaluation protocols to support supervised training and reproducible comparison across methods. Designed to stress robustness and generalization, EXIST facilitates research on tasks such as classification, detection, and retrieval and enables assessment of model performance in practical deployment scenarios.

generator is a synthetic benchmark dataset of samples produced by one or more generative models, containing generated outputs paired with their latent codes, conditioning inputs, and model metadata. It is designed to evaluate and train generative modeling tasks—such as image/audio/text synthesis, controllability, inversion, and quality/diversity metrics—and supports research on model comparison, robustness, and detection of synthetic content.

Newspaper corpus (JSONL, doc-level split) is a collection of newspaper articles stored as one JSON record per document (commonly including fields such as id, date, title, body, and section/metadata). It is suited for NLP tasks at the document level—topic/classification, summarization, information extraction, event detection, retrieval, and language modeling—while the provided train/validation/test split is done by whole documents to prevent cross-sample leakage. The JSONL format and rich metadata make it convenient for preprocessing, temporal analyses, and domain-adaptation experiments on real-world news text.

IndoNLI is a natural language inference dataset for Indonesian containing premise–hypothesis sentence pairs annotated with the standard three-way labels (entailment, contradiction, neutral). It serves as a benchmark for training and evaluating Indonesian NLU models, enabling research on semantic reasoning, entailment recognition, cross-lingual transfer, and robustness across diverse genres and registers.

dataset_node: Arabic AI vs Human Text Dataset␟Arabic AI Text Detection
dataset: Arabic AI vs Human Text Dataset

desc: Arabic AI vs Human Text Dataset is a labeled corpus of Arabic text samples annotated as human-written or AI-generated. It covers multiple genres and registers (news, social media, essays, Q&A) and includes Modern Standard Arabic and common dialects, with metadata for source, generation model or author, prompt context, and topic. The dataset is intended for supervised detection and classification of AI-generated Arabic text, robustness and adversarial evaluation, calibration studies, and stylistic or forensic analyses, enabling benchmarking of detectors and generalization across domains and generation methods.

feedback-detector-dataset is a labeled collection of user-generated text (e.g., reviews, support tickets, forum posts, in-app feedback) annotated for the presence and type of product feedback. Labels indicate whether a message contains actionable feedback and often include subcategories such as bug report, feature request, complaint, praise, or usability issue, enabling binary, multiclass, and multilabel training. It is intended to train and benchmark classifiers and routing systems for automated feedback detection, prioritization, and downstream analysis (e.g., issue triage, sentiment-aware summarization), supporting research in customer analytics, moderation, and product-quality automation.

Balanced Fallacy Dataset is a labeled corpus for detecting and classifying logical and rhetorical fallacies in natural language. It contains text examples drawn from diverse sources (debates, editorials, online discussions) annotated with a standardized taxonomy of fallacy types and balanced per class to reduce label skew. Designed for supervised learning and evaluation, the dataset supports single- and multi-label classification, span-level fallacy location, and explanation-generation tasks, enabling development of robust argument-mining, misinformation-detection, and explainable NLP models.

myanmar-written-spoken-text-pairs is a parallel corpus of Myanmar (Burmese) written text aligned with its corresponding spoken-form renderings. It provides sentence- and phrase-level pairs that capture orthographic vs. colloquial/pronounced variants, including contractions, disfluencies, and register differences. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating text normalization, grapheme-to-phoneme conversion, speech synthesis (TTS), and ASR post-processing or pronunciation modeling, enabling models to map between formal written Burmese and natural spoken realizations across conversational and broadcast-style domains.

E-commerce Reviews is a dataset of user-generated product reviews from online marketplaces, pairing review text with associated metadata such as star ratings, product and user IDs, timestamps, product categories, and helpfulness votes. It captures real-world language and rating distributions, including informal phrasing, domain-specific terminology, and class imbalance across products. The dataset is suitable for supervised and unsupervised NLP and recommender tasks—sentiment and rating prediction, aspect-based sentiment analysis, review summarization, fake-review detection, and personalized recommendation—making it useful for training and evaluating models on practical e-commerce scenarios.

Civil Comments is a corpus of online news-site comments annotated by crowdworkers for toxicity and related phenomena. Each comment carries multi-label annotations (e.g., toxic/very toxic, insult, obscene, threat, identity attack) and flags for referenced identity groups (race, gender, religion, sexual orientation, etc.), together with comment text and metadata. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating toxicity/abuse detection models, bias and fairness analyses, subgroup robustness, and multi-label classification. Contains abusive and hateful language — handle with appropriate precautions.

lenu is a dataset for image restoration and enhancement consisting of paired degraded and high-quality reference images collected across diverse real-world scenes. It is designed to support supervised training and benchmarking of denoising, deblurring, low-light enhancement, and super-resolution models, providing varied degradation types (noise, motion blur, exposure issues), multiple resolutions, and standardized train/validation/test splits with common fidelity and perceptual evaluation metrics.

Amazon Polarity is a large-scale binary sentiment classification dataset of Amazon product reviews. Each example contains a review title and body paired with a polarity label (positive or negative). Covering many product categories and realistic, noisy user text, it is commonly used to train and benchmark sentiment analysis and text-classification models, and to evaluate transfer learning and robustness on real-world review data.

Suicide Detection Dataset is a curated collection of human-generated content (commonly social media posts, comments, or clinical notes) annotated for suicidal ideation and risk level to support supervised learning and evaluation of automated detection and triage models. Records include labels such as non-suicidal, ideation, and high-risk/attempt indicators, and may provide auxiliary annotations (severity, temporal cues, intent, and limited metadata) to enable binary and multi-class classification, risk scoring, and temporal detection tasks. The dataset is intended for research into early detection and intervention systems and comes with strict privacy, ethical-use guidelines, and recommendations for human-in-the-loop validation and responsible deployment.

HealthFact is a supervised benchmark for automated verification of health-related claims. It contains short medical claims paired with evidence passages from authoritative sources and human annotations of veracity (e.g., supported, refuted, or insufficient/unknown). The dataset is intended for training and evaluating pipelines that combine evidence retrieval and claim verification, and it emphasizes domain-specific language, medical terminology, and the safety-critical nature of health information. HealthFact supports research in fact-checking, evidence selection, explainable verification, and robust NLP models for healthcare misinformation.

Pharmaconer is a Spanish-language dataset for pharmaceutical named-entity recognition consisting of clinical and biomedical texts manually annotated with drug-related entities (e.g., active ingredients, brand names, formulations and drug groups). Annotations follow standard token-level labeling (BIO-style) and are produced by domain-expert annotators to support reliable supervised training and evaluation. The dataset is intended for developing and benchmarking NER, entity linking and pharmacovigilance information-extraction systems in Spanish clinical and biomedical domains.

dataset_node: Product Classification and Categorization␟Product Category Classification

desc: SuperGlue is a benchmark dataset for learning-based local feature matching that provides image pairs with annotated keypoint correspondences and ground-truth geometric transforms (e.g., homographies or relative poses). It covers diverse scenes and appearance changes (viewpoint, illumination, texture) to evaluate robustness of correspondence, outlier rejection, and matching repeatability. The dataset supports training and benchmarking end-to-end matching networks and downstream tasks such as pose estimation, visual localization, and structure-from-motion.

MASSIVE is a parallel dataset of > 1M utterances across 51 languages with annotations for the Natural Language Understanding tasks of intent prediction and slot annotation. Utterances span 60 intents and include 55 slot types. MASSIVE was created by localizing the SLURP dataset, composed of general Intelligent Voice Assistant single-shot interactions.

The Corpus of Linguistic Acceptability (CoLA) is a dataset containing over 10,000 English sentences sourced from linguistics publications. Each sentence is annotated for linguistic acceptability, indicating whether it is grammatically acceptable or not, based on expert judgments. The dataset is split into training, development, and test sets, and is widely used for evaluating models on the task of acceptability classification in natural language processing.

dataset_node: Multilingual Custom Dataset (Hungarian, Slovak, Polish, Czech)␟Multilingual Emotion Classification
dataset: Multilingual Custom Dataset (Hungarian, Slovak, Polish, Czech)
root_a: Multilingual Custom Dataset (Hungarian, Slovak, Polish, Czech)
desc: Multilingual Custom Dataset (Hungarian, Slovak, Polish, Czech) is a curated corpus of text in four Central European languages designed for training and evaluating multilingual and cross-lingual NLP models. It contains monolingual and parallel texts with task-specific annotations (e.g., classification, NER, POS tagging, and translation) to support benchmarking, transfer learning, and domain adaptation across typologically related low- to mid-resource languages. The dataset enables experiments in representation learning, cross-lingual transfer, and language-specific model optimization.

KLUE (Korean Language Understanding Evaluation) is a multi-task benchmark suite for Korean natural language processing that provides human-annotated datasets across core tasks such as classification, inference, named-entity recognition, semantic similarity, and question answering. It standardizes training and evaluation splits and metrics to enable fair comparison of Korean language models and encourage development of architectures and pretraining strategies tailored to Korean. KLUE is widely used for benchmarking model performance, error analysis, and advancing research in Korean NLP.

val is the validation split of the benchmark containing held-out examples drawn from the same distribution as the training data. It is used to monitor training, tune hyperparameters, perform early stopping, and select models without using the test set. The partition is disjoint from training and test data and is intended to provide an unbiased estimate of model performance for model selection using the benchmark’s target metrics (e.g., accuracy, F1, mAP).

NASA Aviation Incident Reports is a collection of anonymized aviation safety reports gathered by NASA’s Aviation Safety Reporting System (ASRS). It includes structured fields (flight phase, aircraft type, reporter role, date, severity/category) alongside free‑text narratives describing incidents, near‑misses, and safety hazards. The dataset is suitable for NLP and safety‑analytics tasks such as incident classification, event and entity extraction, root‑cause analysis, trend detection, and risk modeling for human factors and operational safety research.

Arabic Sentiment Dataset is a corpus of Arabic-language texts annotated for sentiment (e.g., positive, negative, neutral). Collected from sources such as social media posts, reviews, and comments, it includes Modern Standard Arabic and regional dialects to capture real-world linguistic variation. Designed for supervised training and evaluation, it supports binary and multi-class sentiment classification, domain adaptation, and robustness studies. Useful for benchmarking Arabic NLP models and building applications in opinion mining, customer feedback analysis, and social media monitoring.

Stanford Sentiment Treebank (SST) is a benchmark dataset of movie-review sentences from Rotten Tomatoes annotated with sentiment labels at both the sentence and phrase level. It provides fine-grained (5-way) and binary (2-way) sentiment labels mapped to nodes of syntactic parse trees, enabling evaluation of compositional and sentence-representation models. SST includes standard train/validation/test splits and is widely used for supervised sentiment classification and research on compositional semantics.

UIT-VSFC is a curated video dataset for face- and saliency-centered visual analysis. It provides real-world video sequences with frame-level annotations such as face bounding boxes, facial landmarks, and saliency/motion labels to support training and evaluation of face detection, tracking, landmark localization, and saliency correspondence models. The dataset emphasizes diverse poses, expressions, lighting, and occlusions to benchmark robustness of video-based face and saliency algorithms in dynamic scenes.

Fitness-Intent is a labeled dataset of fitness-related user utterances annotated with intent categories for training and evaluating intent classification models. It contains natural-language queries and commands about workouts, nutrition, scheduling, progress tracking, and related topics, each mapped to a ground-truth intent label. Designed for building conversational agents and virtual assistants in the fitness domain, the dataset supports supervised learning, evaluation, and domain adaptation for intent detection and related downstream dialogue tasks.

Fitness-Intent is a labeled dataset of fitness-related user utterances annotated with intent categories for training and evaluating intent classification models. It contains natural-language queries and commands about workouts, nutrition, scheduling, progress tracking, and related topics, each mapped to a ground-truth intent label. Designed for building conversational agents and virtual assistants in the fitness domain, the dataset supports supervised learning, evaluation, and domain adaptation for intent detection and related downstream dialogue tasks.

ucirvine/sms_spam (test split) is a labeled set of short English SMS messages for binary spam detection. Each example pairs raw message text with a label ("ham" or "spam"), reflecting real-world informal language and class imbalance. The split is intended for evaluating trained classifiers on message-level spam filtering using metrics such as accuracy, precision/recall, and F1.

CrowS-Pairs has 1508 examples that cover stereotypes dealing with nine types of bias, like race, religion, and age. In CrowS-Pairs a model is presented with two sentences: one that is more stereotyping and another that is less stereotyping. The data focuses on stereotypes about historically disadvantaged groups and contrasts them with advantaged groups. Source:

unpublished is a benchmark dataset designed to evaluate model generalization and robustness to withheld or deployment-like data distributions. It contains a curated collection of real-world examples with associated ground-truth annotations and standardized train/validation/test splits, intended to simulate domain shift from public training corpora to unreleased content. The dataset supports tasks such as classification, detection, and conditional generation, enabling research in domain adaptation, transfer learning, and robustness under realistic distributional changes.

vietnamese_students_feedback is a corpus of anonymized Vietnamese-language student feedback collected from course evaluations and surveys. Each entry contains a free-text comment and associated metadata (e.g., course, rating, and/or labels such as sentiment or topic), making the dataset suitable for supervised tasks like sentiment classification, aspect-based opinion mining, topic classification, and feedback summarization. It supports development and evaluation of Vietnamese NLU models and tools for automated survey analysis and educational quality improvement.

dataset_node: Czech Custom Dataset␟Emotion Classification in Czech
desc: Czech Custom Dataset is a curated collection of Czech-language data with manual annotations for supervised machine learning. Designed to support tasks such as classification, sequence labeling, and document-level evaluation, it aggregates diverse Czech text sources and includes standardized train/validation/test splits and metadata for reproducible experiments. The dataset targets Czech-specific linguistic phenomena and domain adaptation, enabling development and benchmarking of models tailored to the Czech language and local content.

Sentiment140 is a large-scale text dataset designed for sentiment classification, specifically capturing public opinion expressed on Twitter. It consists of tweets labeled with sentiment polarity, typically positive or negative, enabling models to learn to predict the emotional tone of short, informal social media messages. The dataset is widely used to develop and evaluate natural language processing models for sentiment analysis, a task critical for understanding brand perception, product feedback, and public attitudes in real time. Sentiment140 presents challenges such as noisy, informal language, abbreviations, and the brevity of tweets, which require robust feature extraction and modeling techniques. Models trained on this dataset are commonly assessed using classification metrics like accuracy, precision, and recall. Due to its domain-specific nature and large volume of labeled examples, Sentiment140 serves as a benchmark for advancing sentiment classification methods, including recent approaches in federated and personalized learning that address data heterogeneity across users

The Reuters-21578 dataset is a widely used collection of newswire articles for text categorization and information retrieval research. It contains over 10,000 documents from the Reuters newswire in 1987, covering multiple topics and categories. The dataset includes a large vocabulary and is commonly used for benchmarking text classification algorithms.

isa-ras/frustration_dataset is a labeled multimodal dataset for automatic detection and analysis of human frustration in interactive tasks. It contains participant recordings (e.g., facial video, audio, interaction logs and physiological signals) with time-aligned annotations of frustration levels and event labels, suitable for supervised learning and temporal modeling. The dataset targets affective computing and human–robot/human–computer interaction research, enabling development and evaluation of models for frustration recognition, temporal segmentation, and intervention strategies.

Parafraseja is a Portuguese paraphrase dataset of sentence pairs with human annotations indicating whether pairs are paraphrases. It covers diverse everyday and formal domains to capture lexical and syntactic variation, supporting both binary paraphrase classification and graded semantic similarity tasks. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating paraphrase identification, textual entailment, and paraphrase generation models, and for augmenting downstream NLU systems in Portuguese.

**SciCite** is a dataset of citation intents that addresses multiple scientific domains and is more than five times larger than ACL-ARC.

sem_eval_2024_task_2 is the official dataset released for SemEval 2024 Task 2, providing curated and human-annotated text examples split into training, validation, and test sets. Each example is labeled according to the task’s prediction target and accompanied by metadata and annotation notes to support reproducible evaluation. The dataset is intended to benchmark and compare supervised models on the shared task’s challenge across languages and domains, and is distributed with annotation guidelines and baseline evaluation scripts.

The **IMDb Movie Reviews** dataset is a binary sentiment analysis dataset consisting of 50,000 reviews from the Internet Movie Database (IMDb) labeled as positive or negative. The dataset contains an even number of positive and negative reviews. Only highly polarizing reviews are considered. A negative review has a score ≤ 4 out of 10, and a positive review has a score ≥ 7 out of 10. No more than 30 reviews are included per movie. The dataset contains additional unlabeled data. Stanford Sentiment Treebank (SST) is a benchmark dataset of movie-review sentences from Rotten Tomatoes annotated with sentiment labels at both the sentence and phrase level. It provides fine-grained (5-way) and binary (2-way) sentiment labels mapped to nodes of syntactic parse trees, enabling evaluation of compositional and sentence-representation models. SST includes standard train/validation/test splits and is widely used for supervised sentiment classification and research on compositional semantics.

AG News is a widely used text classification dataset consisting of news articles categorized into four classes: World, Sports, Business, and Science/Technology. It includes a large number of samples, with tens of thousands of training examples and a smaller test set, derived from the titles and descriptions of news articles. The dataset is commonly used for benchmarking text classification models in natural language processing tasks.

dair-ai/emotion is a labeled text dataset for emotion recognition, containing short utterances annotated with discrete emotion labels (e.g., joy, sadness, anger, fear). It is intended for training and evaluating supervised NLP models for emotion classification and affective computing, enabling benchmarking of classifiers, transfer learning, and robustness on conversational or social-media-style text.

TweetEval is a benchmark evaluation framework designed for natural language processing tasks on Twitter data, focusing on seven diverse classification problems including sentiment analysis. The dataset comprises text from tweets, reflecting the unique linguistic characteristics and informal style of social media language. It serves as a standardized platform to assess and compare models tailored to Twitter-specific challenges such as sentiment polarity detection, irony recognition, and emoji prediction. By consolidating multiple related tasks, TweetEval addresses the fragmentation in social media NLP research and facilitates the development of robust, domain-adapted models. The dataset supports the evaluation of various classification approaches, including recent transformer-based architectures pretrained on generic corpora and further adapted to Twitter data. Performance is typically measured using standard classification metrics such as F1 score, precision, and recall. TweetEval’s comprehensive and heterogeneous nature makes it a valuable resource for advancing sentiment analysis and other text classification tasks in the social media context.

dataset_node: Internal MS-Autoimmune Corpus␟Binary Text Classification (Autoimmune Neurology)
desc: Internal MS-Autoimmune Corpus is a de-identified, multimodal clinical dataset of patients with multiple sclerosis and related autoimmune markers. It combines structured EHR elements (demographics, diagnoses, medications, lab results, immunologic assay data) with unstructured clinical text (neurology notes, MRI and pathology reports) and curated labels (disease subtype, relapse events, treatment response). The corpus is intended for ML development and benchmarking on tasks such as clinical NLP (entity extraction, coding), phenotype and subgroup identification, prognosis and trajectory modeling, biomarker discovery, and treatment-response prediction.

agentlans/refusal-classifier-data is a labeled text dataset of user prompts and assistant responses annotated for refusal behavior. It provides examples marked with binary accept/refuse labels and fine-grained refusal categories or reasons (e.g., safety, privacy, illegal requests, policy), plus optional rationale and metadata. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating classifiers and filters that predict when a conversational agent should decline or safely redirect a request, supporting work in alignment, safety, and content-moderation for dialog systems.

LusakaLang Test Set is a standardized evaluation corpus drawn from urban multilingual use in Lusaka, Zambia, designed to benchmark speech and language models on low-resource and code-switched scenarios. The set includes manually verified audio recordings with time-aligned transcriptions, orthographic text, reference translations, and speaker/recording metadata, covering common local varieties (e.g., English, Nyanja/Chewa, Bemba) and natural code‑switching and noise conditions. LusakaLang is intended for evaluating ASR, machine translation, language identification, and robust NLU systems, emphasizing real-world conversational speech, acoustic variability, and cross-lingual generalization.

Clickbait Detection Dataset is a labeled corpus of online headlines and social media posts annotated for clickbaitiness, typically paired with corresponding article text and metadata (publisher, timestamps, URLs, often images). It supports supervised learning of classifiers and regressors to detect or score clickbait, providing human judgments for training and evaluation. The dataset enables research on feature representations (textual, contextual, visual), robustness to platform variation, and application areas such as content moderation, feed ranking, and combating deceptive or sensationalized headlines.

epi_classify4_gard is a 4-way supervised classification benchmark built from EPI-derived samples curated in the GARD collection. Each instance includes preprocessed features and a ground-truth class label, enabling training and evaluation of multi-class classifiers. The dataset is intended for benchmarking model accuracy, calibration, and robustness, and for studies of feature selection and generalization across the GARD cohort.

Dutch Social is a corpus of Dutch-language social media posts with accompanying metadata and human annotations for tasks such as sentiment analysis, topic classification, and abusive-language detection. It captures informal language, slang, emoji, and code-switching typical of online conversations, making it useful for training and evaluating NLP models for social-media understanding, content moderation, and domain-adaptive language processing in Dutch.

ecommerce_reviews_with_language_drift is a dataset of e-commerce product reviews collected across multiple time periods and regions, each review paired with metadata such as timestamp, product category, and numeric ratings or sentiment labels. The corpus exhibits realistic language drift—shifts in vocabulary, slang, product-specific terms, spelling variations, and code-switching—across temporal and regional splits. It is designed for evaluating and training NLP models on sentiment classification, robustness to distribution shift, domain adaptation, continual learning, and drift-detection tasks by providing chronological and cross-domain evaluation splits that mimic real-world deployment changes.

emotone_ar is an Arabic emotional speech dataset containing spoken utterances labeled with emotional annotations for use in speech emotion recognition. It provides raw audio recordings (with accompanying transcripts and speaker metadata) annotated with categorical and/or dimensional emotion labels, enabling supervised training and evaluation of classification and regression models for affective state estimation. The dataset supports research on Arabic-language emotion detection, model generalization across speakers and recording conditions, and downstream tasks such as emotion-aware dialogue and multimodal affective analysis.

Custom Dataset is a user-defined collection of curated samples assembled for a specific machine learning task. It pairs inputs (images, text, audio, or tabular records) with task-relevant annotations and standard train/validation/test splits to support supervised training and evaluation. Designed for flexibility and reproducibility, it facilitates benchmarking, model development, and transfer learning in domain-specific scenarios.

LusakaLang Training Data is a de-identified, ethically collected corpus of conversational and written language samples representative of Lusaka, Zambia, designed for training NLP and speech models for low-resource and code-switched settings. It contains parallel and monolingual text and speech recordings in English and dominant local languages (commonly spoken varieties), with time-aligned transcripts, speaker and domain metadata, and annotations for intent, named entities, and code-switch boundaries. The dataset supports tasks such as ASR, language identification, code-switch modeling, intent classification, and conversational agent development, with an emphasis on real-world urban register and multilingual phenomena.

hate_speech18 is a labeled dataset of social media posts for training and evaluating hate-speech and abusive-language detection models. It provides raw text (typically tweets) annotated for harmful content (e.g., hate, abusive/offensive, or neutral), often with accompanying metadata such as user identifiers and timestamps when available. The dataset is intended for supervised text classification benchmarking, model evaluation, and research into moderation, robustness, and fairness in automated hate-speech detection.

OffensEval-2020 is a dataset for offensive language detection in social media, containing tweets annotated with hierarchical labels for three tasks: A) offensive vs. not offensive, B) targeted vs. untargeted offense, and C) type of target (individual, group, or other). It provides supervised training and evaluation data for binary and multi-class classification of abusive, profane, or hateful content, and is used to benchmark and develop moderation, content-filtering, and robustness methods for noisy, informal text.

Mental_Health_Condition_Classification is a labeled text dataset for supervised classification of mental health conditions. It contains textual samples paired with annotations indicating one or more mental health labels (e.g., depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder, PTSD), enabling binary, multi-class, or multi-label modeling. The dataset is intended for developing and evaluating NLP systems for screening, detection, and research into automatic identification of mental-health-related language. Because entries may contain sensitive personal content, users should follow privacy, consent, and ethical guidelines when using the data.

dataset_node: Indonesian Spam Detection Dataset v2␟Text Classification
desc: Indonesian Spam Detection Dataset v2 is a labeled corpus of Indonesian-language messages annotated as spam or non-spam (ham). It contains real-world examples exhibiting colloquial language, slang, abbreviations, obfuscation and occasional code-mixing, and provides message text together with binary labels and optional metadata (e.g., timestamps or sender IDs) when available. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating supervised text-classification and spam-filtering models, supporting work on tokenization, feature engineering, class-imbalance handling, and robustness to adversarial or noisy inputs in Indonesian NLP.

rlogh/superhero-texts (augmented test) is an augmented test split of superhero-themed short texts with systematic perturbations—paraphrases, typos, token-level noise, entity swaps, and punctuation/capitalization changes. It retains original labels/annotations and includes metadata about applied augmentations to enable controlled evaluation. Designed to benchmark robustness and generalization of NLP models on classification, intent detection, NER, and generation within a domain-specific narrative/dialogue setting, it is useful for stress-testing model performance under realistic lexical and syntactic variation.

AnnoMI is a curated dataset of images with high-quality human annotations (pixel-level masks, bounding boxes, and class labels) designed for supervised learning and benchmarking. It provides consistent manual labels and accompanying metadata across diverse imaging conditions to support tasks such as segmentation, object detection, and classification. AnnoMI enables development and evaluation of models focused on accurate object delineation, label consistency, and generalization to real-world variations.

MASSIVE (en-US) is the English subset of the MASSIVE multilingual spoken language understanding benchmark. It contains diverse user utterances across multiple domains, each annotated with intent labels and slot-level span annotations for intent classification and slot filling. Designed for training and evaluating SLU/NLU models and for studying cross-lingual and transfer learning, it provides realistic conversational queries covering many intent types and entity categories in en-US.

A dataset of social media posts and news articles related to the Catalan independence movement, curated for political-NLP tasks. Entries include raw text (Catalan, Spanish, English), timestamps, anonymized user/source metadata, and event labels tied to key moments (e.g., the 2017 referendum and subsequent demonstrations). A portion of items is annotated for stance (pro/anti/neutral), sentiment, and topical labels, making the collection suitable for stance detection, sentiment analysis, misinformation/propaganda studies, topic modeling, and timeline or event extraction. The dataset supports research on multilingual political discourse, argument mining, and social dynamics around regional independence movements.

consumer-finance-complaints is a public dataset of consumer-submitted complaints about financial products and services (credit cards, mortgages, loans, debt collection, credit reporting, bank accounts, student loans, etc.). Records typically include a short narrative or description, product and issue labels, company name, date, location metadata, complaint ID and company response/status. It is suitable for NLP tasks such as classification, topic modeling, summarization, intent/entity extraction, trend analysis and automated triage, and for studies on regulatory compliance, consumer protection and fairness in financial services.

Politics is a curated dataset of political text—news articles, social media posts, and speeches—annotated with labels such as topic, stance, sentiment, and partisan bias, along with metadata like source and date. It is intended for training and evaluating NLP models on tasks including topic classification, stance and sentiment detection, bias and factuality assessment, summarization, and named-entity-targeted analysis. The dataset supports research in political discourse, opinion mining, misinformation detection, and domain adaptation for models handling real-world political content.

XGLUE is a comprehensive cross-lingual benchmark consisting of 11 tasks across 19 languages, designed to evaluate models' zero-shot transfer capabilities. Training data is available only in English, requiring models to generalize learned knowledge to other languages. Unlike similar benchmarks, XGLUE includes both natural language understanding and generation tasks. It incorporates five established cross-lingual tasks such as named entity recognition and question answering, along with six new tasks derived from real-world scenarios, including news classification, query-ad matching, and question generation. This diversity of languages and tasks makes XGLUE a valuable resource for assessing the performance of multilingual pre-trained models in cross-lingual natural language processing.

Rotten Tomatoes is a sentence-level sentiment dataset of short movie review snippets from the Rotten Tomatoes website, each labeled for binary sentiment (positive vs. negative). It is commonly used to train and evaluate supervised text-classification models, benchmark sentiment-analysis performance, and study transfer learning and domain adaptation for NLP systems.

desc: The **QNLI** (**Question-answering NLI**) dataset is a Natural Language Inference dataset automatically derived from the Stanford Question Answering Dataset v1.1 (SQuAD). SQuAD v1.1 consists of question-paragraph pairs, where one of the sentences in the paragraph (drawn from Wikipedia) contains the answer to the corresponding question (written by an annotator). The dataset was converted into sentence pair classification by forming a pair between each question and each sentence in the corresponding context, and filtering out pairs with low lexical overlap between the question and the context sentence. The task is to determine whether the context sentence contains the answer to the question. This modified version of the original task removes the requirement that the model select the exact answer, but also removes the simplifying assumptions that the answer is always present in the input and that lexical overlap is a reliable cue. The QNLI dataset is part of GLUE benchmark. Source:

dataset_node: Slovak Custom Dataset␟Emotion Classification in Slovak
desc: Slovak Custom Dataset is a curated corpus of Slovak-language texts assembled for supervised ML and NLP research. It comprises documents from news, web, and social media sources, with sentence- and token-level annotations (POS tags, lemmas, named entities) and document-level labels for tasks such as topic and sentiment classification where available. Data is provided in standardized train/validation/test splits and includes basic metadata (source, timestamp, genre). The dataset is intended for benchmarking and developing Slovak language models and downstream systems for POS tagging, NER, sentiment analysis, topic classification, and related tasks.

FakeTrue.Br is a dataset for misinformation detection in Brazilian Portuguese, containing news articles and short claims labeled as fake or true with corresponding fact-check annotations and source metadata (publisher, date, URLs). It aggregates verified rulings from Brazilian fact-checking organizations and pairs claims with supporting or debunking evidence, enabling supervised training for binary classification, claim verification, and evidence retrieval. The dataset supports development and evaluation of NLP models focused on fact-checking, misinformation mitigation, cross-lingual transfer, and robustness to stylistic and domain shifts in Portuguese-language content.

WikiCAT_ca is a Catalan Wikipedia-derived dataset consisting of articles paired with their Wikipedia category annotations. It is designed for supervised tasks such as multi-label topic classification, hierarchical category prediction, and cross-lingual transfer for Catalan NLP. By providing natural-language documents with real-category labels, WikiCAT_ca supports development and evaluation of document classification, topic modeling, taxonomy-aware models, and other downstream language understanding tasks in Catalan.

datasetX is a curated benchmark dataset for supervised machine learning, containing diverse real-world samples paired with high-quality ground-truth annotations. It provides standardized training, validation, and test splits plus descriptive metadata to support reproducible experiments. datasetX is designed to evaluate model accuracy, robustness, and generalization across varied conditions and is suitable for tasks such as classification, detection, and segmentation.
