desc: 2024-mcm-everitt-ryan/job-bias-synthetic-human-benchmark-v2 is a benchmark dataset for evaluating and mitigating demographic bias in automated hiring systems. It pairs synthetically generated candidate records (resumes, bios, cover letters) with human annotations of job suitability and labeled demographic attributes, and includes controlled counterfactual perturbations (e.g., name/pronoun swaps, attribute edits) to expose spurious correlations. The dataset is organized for classification and ranking tasks and provides evaluation protocols and splits for common fairness metrics (demographic parity, equal opportunity, calibration) and stress tests. It is intended for model auditing, fairness research, and development of bias-detection and mitigation methods in recruitment pipelines.

TVL-game-layer-dataset is a collection of rendered game scenes with separated image layers and corresponding alpha masks designed for training and evaluating layer decomposition and compositing models. Each sample pairs composite frames with per-layer RGBA images (e.g., foreground, background, effects) and masks to support tasks such as layer segmentation, alpha matting, occlusion handling, and image reconstruction. The dataset provides realistic game-engine content for supervised learning of layer-aware restoration, object removal, and interactive scene editing.

Textual Entailment Recognition has been proposed recently as a generic task that captures major semantic inference needs across many NLP applications, such as Question Answering, Information Retrieval, Information Extraction, and Text Summarization. This task requires to recognize, given two text fragments, whether the meaning of one text is entailed (can be inferred) from the other text. ### Task Type RTE (Recognizing Textual Entailment) Sentence Pair Classification - Entailment - Not Entailment ### Example ``` { "premise": "Автор поста написал в комментарии, что прорвалась канализация.", "hypothesis": "Автор поста написал про канализацию.", "label": "entailment", "idx": "6062" } ``` ### How did we collect data? All text examples were collected from open news sources and literary magazines, then manually reviewed and supplemented by a human assessment on Yandex.Toloka

Custom Literary Dataset (Deduplicated) is a curated collection of literary texts—novels, short stories, poems, and essays—cleaned, normalized, and deduplicated to remove exact and near-duplicate passages while preserving author- and work-level diversity. Each document includes basic metadata (author, title, year, genre) and is provided in plain-text and tokenized-ready formats with recommended train/validation/test splits for reproducible experiments. The dataset is intended for language modeling, text generation, authorship and stylistic analysis, genre classification, and other NLP tasks where reducing duplication bias and preserving literary variety are important.

Do Not Code is a safety-focused dataset of user prompts that request executable code for harmful, illegal, or otherwise disallowed actions, paired with human annotations and example safe refusals. It covers diverse phrasing and intent levels (e.g., malware, bypassing security, illicit automation) and includes labels for violation type, severity, and recommended safe alternatives or explanations. Designed to train and evaluate models on detecting unsafe coding requests, producing policy-compliant refusals, and suggesting non-actionable or educational alternatives, it supports research in model safety, alignment, and content filtering.

MNLI (Multi-Genre Natural Language Inference) is a large-scale dataset for natural language inference containing approximately 433k sentence pairs (premise, hypothesis) annotated with three-way labels: entailment, contradiction, or neutral. Collected across multiple written and spoken genres, it enables training and evaluation of models that must generalize across diverse domains. MNLI includes matched and mismatched development/test sets to measure in-domain and cross-genre performance, making it a standard benchmark for sentence-level semantic understanding, transfer learning, and NLU model evaluation.

sst2-es-mt is a Spanish, machine-translated version of the SST-2 binary sentiment dataset. It contains SST-2 sentences translated from English into Spanish using automatic translation while preserving the original positive/negative labels. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating Spanish sentiment classifiers, studying cross-lingual transfer, and measuring the effects of machine-translation noise on model performance.

go_emotions-es-mt is a Spanish machine-translated version of the GoEmotions dataset, containing Reddit-derived comments paired with the original multi-label annotations over 27 emotion categories plus neutral. It provides Spanish text and corresponding emotion labels for training and evaluating emotion recognition models, enabling cross-lingual transfer experiments and analysis of machine-translation effects on emotion classification performance.

FrenchMedMCQA is a French-language medical multiple-choice question-answering dataset containing clinical and biomedical MCQs with question stems, multiple answer options (typically four), and gold labels. Questions are translated or adapted from medical exam–style sources to cover diagnosis, treatment, physiology, pharmacology, and clinical reasoning. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating French medical QA and reasoning models, benchmarking domain knowledge, multilingual transfer, and clinical NLP performance.

sort_v2 is a multi-object tracking dataset and benchmark that provides annotated video sequences with per-frame bounding boxes and persistent object IDs for supervised training and evaluation of online and offline trackers. It includes diverse scenarios (static and moving cameras, varying densities and occlusions) and metadata such as visibility/occlusion flags and frame timestamps. Designed for reproducible evaluation, sort_v2 supports common MOT metrics (MOTA, MOTP, ID switches) and standard train/validation/test splits to facilitate development and comparison of tracking algorithms.

deprem_private_dataset_v13 is a private seismic dataset for earthquake detection and characterization, containing multi-station waveform recordings paired with curated event catalogs. It provides preprocessed continuous and triggered seismogram segments (standardized sampling), spectrograms, station metadata, and annotations such as origin time, hypocenter (latitude/longitude/depth), magnitude, and P/S picks with quality flags. The dataset includes train/validation/test splits and is intended for supervised tasks including event detection, phase picking, magnitude estimation, localization, and earthquake/non‑earthquake classification or early‑warning model development. v13 denotes harmonized preprocessing, cleaned labels, and metadata normalization to support robust model training and evaluation in realistic noise and coverage conditions.

autextification2023 is a multimodal dataset for training and evaluating models that automatically generate natural-language text from structured or semi-structured inputs. It provides aligned pairs of source artifacts (tables, key–value records, JSON-like objects, form screenshots) and human-authored textualizations (summaries, descriptions, captions), supporting data-to-text, table-to-text, and form-captioning tasks. The collection is intended for supervised learning and benchmarking of fluency, faithfulness, and concision in textification systems across diverse domains.

The **SNLI** dataset (**Stanford Natural Language Inference**) consists of 570k sentence-pairs manually labeled as entailment, contradiction, and neutral. Premises are image captions from Flickr30k, while hypotheses were generated by crowd-sourced annotators who were shown a premise and asked to generate entailing, contradicting, and neutral sentences. Annotators were instructed to judge the relation between sentences given that they describe the same event. Each pair is labeled as “entailment”, “neutral”, “contradiction” or “-”, where “-” indicates that an agreement could not be reached. Source:

Custom Dataset is a user-defined collection of curated samples assembled for a specific machine learning task. It pairs inputs (images, text, audio, or tabular records) with task-relevant annotations and standard train/validation/test splits to support supervised training and evaluation. Designed for flexibility and reproducibility, it facilitates benchmarking, model development, and transfer learning in domain-specific scenarios.

ViSpamReviews is a Vietnamese-language dataset of online reviews annotated for spam detection. Each record includes the review text in Vietnamese and associated metadata (e.g., rating, timestamp, user/product IDs) with binary spam/genuine labels (and in some versions fine-grained spam categories). It is designed for supervised training and evaluation of spam/fraud detection, content-moderation, and text-classification models, and supports robustness, domain adaptation, and multilingual transfer experiments in Vietnamese NLP.

Yelp Polarity is a large-scale binary sentiment classification dataset of Yelp business reviews, where each review is labeled positive or negative (derived from star ratings). It provides real-world, user-generated text of varying lengths and noise, suitable for training and evaluating supervised sentiment and text-classification models. The dataset is commonly used as a benchmark for model performance and robustness on informal, domain-specific review language.

Stance is a labeled text dataset for stance classification, containing documents (e.g., tweets, headlines, or short articles) paired with explicit targets and annotated for their stance (commonly favor/against/neutral or similar). It is designed to train and evaluate supervised models that determine an author's position toward a given claim or entity, supporting research in opinion mining, rumor and misinformation detection, argumentation analysis, and cross-target generalization.

deprem_private_dataset_v1_2 is a private multimodal earthquake damage dataset containing high-resolution aerial and street-level imagery collected after seismic events, paired with expert annotations including building-level damage severity labels, bounding boxes and segmentation polygons, and metadata (GPS coordinates, timestamps, sensor/platform). It is designed for supervised tasks such as damage classification, object detection, semantic segmentation and rapid damage-mapping to support post-disaster assessment and resource prioritization. Version v1.2 expands geographic coverage and annotation consistency, and includes quality-checked metadata for reproducible training and evaluation.

nubes is a curated dataset of annotated cloud imagery for computer vision and remote sensing tasks. It contains RGB sky and satellite images paired with pixel-level cloud segmentation masks, categorical cloud-type labels, and auxiliary metadata (timestamp, location, sensor parameters). Designed for supervised learning of cloud detection, semantic segmentation, cloud-cover estimation and classification, nubes captures diverse illumination, seasonal and atmospheric conditions to challenge generalization and robustness. The dataset supports development and evaluation of models for weather analysis, solar forecasting, and scene understanding in meteorological and earth-observation applications.

NSMC (Naver Sentiment Movie Corpus) is a Korean-language sentiment classification dataset of roughly 200,000 movie reviews sourced from Naver. Each example contains review text paired with a binary sentiment label (positive/negative), typically provided as balanced train/test splits. NSMC is widely used to train and evaluate Korean text-classification and sentiment-analysis models, and for benchmarking transfer learning and fine-tuning approaches in Korean NLP.

iSarcasm is a dataset of tweets, each labelled as either sarcastic or non_sarcastic. Each sarcastic tweet is further labelled for one of the following types of ironic speech: - sarcasm: tweets that contradict the state of affairs and are critical towards an addressee; - irony: tweets that contradict the state of affairs but are not obviously critical towards an addressee; - satire: tweets that appear to support an addressee, but contain underlying disagreement and mocking; - understatement: tweets that undermine the importance of the state of affairs they refer to; - overstatement: tweets that describe the state of affairs in obviously exaggerated terms; - rhetorical question: tweets that include a question whose invited inference (implicature) is obviously contradicting the state of affairs. For each sarastic tweet, there's also: - an explanation, in English sentences, as to why it is sarcastic, and - a rephrase that conveys the same meaning non-sarcastically. Both have been provided by the author of the tweet. iSarcasm contains 4,484 tweets, out of which 777 are labelled as sarcastic and 3,707 as non-sarcastic. You'll find two files, isarcasm_train.csv and isarcasm_test.csv, each containing 80% and 20% of the examples chosen at random, respectively. Each line in a file has the format tweet_id,sarcasm_label,sarcasm_type, where sarcasm_type are only defined for sarcastic tweets, as specified above. Source:

desc: BABE (test) is the held-out evaluation split of the BABE benchmark for image deblurring and blur-kernel analysis. It comprises a diverse set of real and synthetic blurry images, paired with ground-truth sharp references and, when available, corresponding blur kernels, to assess restoration accuracy and kernel estimation robustness. The dataset is intended as a standardized, challenging test set for comparing supervised and blind deblurring models and measuring generalization to varied motion, defocus, and noise conditions.

BASIL (all sentences) is a sentence-level text dataset composed of complete sentences extracted from diverse written sources and provided as individual samples for NLP research. It is designed for tasks that require fine-grained sentence representations—such as sentence classification, semantic similarity, retrieval, and sentence-level generation—by supplying clean, standalone sentence units (often with available metadata like source and position). BASIL (all sentences) enables training and evaluation of sentence encoders, summarizers, and retrieval systems, facilitating benchmarking of models’ sentence understanding and context-aware selection capabilities.

Internal test set is a private, held-out dataset used for final evaluation of models. It contains labeled examples representative of production or target-domain data but is excluded from training and validation to provide unbiased estimates of generalization and robustness. The set is intended for performance benchmarking, model selection, and readiness assessment under realistic distributional conditions; it is not publicly released.

Northell/ros-classifiers-materials-flat is a labeled image dataset of flat material swatches intended for material classification and recognition tasks. It contains top-down photographs of uniform, flat samples annotated by material type (e.g., wood, metal, fabric, plastic, glass, stone), captured under consistent lighting and framing to emphasize texture and color cues. The dataset is suitable for training and evaluating image classifiers, feature extractors, and domain-transfer methods for applications like product search, robotic perception, and augmented-reality material identification.

WebOrganizer/TopicAnnotations-Llama-3.1-8B is a corpus of web pages and page metadata annotated with topic labels automatically generated by the Llama 3.1 8B model. Each entry pairs page text and metadata with one or more predicted topic tags, model confidence scores, and the prompt/template used for annotation; labels are optionally aligned to a target topic taxonomy. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating topic classification, content organization, weak supervision, and analysis of LLM-based annotation quality in web-scale indexing and retrieval pipelines.

IconicAI/DDD (custom subset manually labeled) is a curated subset of the IconicAI collection with human-verified annotations intended for supervised computer-vision research. The subset pairs high-quality images with manually assigned class labels and structured metadata (and where available, bounding-box or mask annotations), enabling training and evaluation of classification, detection, and retrieval models on iconographic/product imagery. It emphasizes fine-grained, consistent labels and real-world variability, making it useful for benchmarking model accuracy, transfer learning, and annotation-quality studies.

Child Protection Dataset is a curated, ethically managed benchmark for developing and evaluating automated systems that detect and classify content posing risks to children. It contains legally sourced, de-identified multimedia (images, video, text) with expert annotations for harmful-content categories, age/consent indicators, severity labels, and contextual metadata. Designed for supervised learning, triage, retrieval, and forensic analysis, the dataset supports moderation and safety tools under strict access controls and compliance requirements to minimize harm and protect subjects.

Educational Stories is a dataset of short narrative texts crafted for educational NLP tasks. Each story is paired with metadata (age/grade level, topic, reading-difficulty), pedagogical annotations (learning objectives, target vocabulary), and evaluation items such as multiple-choice and free-response comprehension questions with answers, concise summaries, and key-fact extractions. It is intended for training and evaluating models for reading comprehension, question answering and generation, summarization, text simplification, curriculum-aware content selection, and assessing age-appropriate language understanding.

dataset_node: Fiction Genre Validation Set (52 Stories)␟Narrative Genre Classification

desc: MALT (filtered) is a curated, quality-filtered subset of the MALT corpus that provides cleaned, deduplicated, and label-verified examples for supervised NLP tasks. By removing noisy, low-quality, and ambiguous instances and mitigating class imbalance, it enables more reliable training and evaluation for tasks such as text classification, sequence labeling, and dependency/structure prediction. MALT (filtered) serves as a cleaner benchmark to assess model robustness, generalization, and downstream performance in language-understanding applications.

LusakaLang Topic Dataset is a multilingual, code-switched text corpus collected from public social media, community forums, and local news in Lusaka, Zambia, annotated with topic labels (e.g., politics, health, education, transport, commerce). It includes posts and short messages in English and major local languages (Nyanja, Bemba, Tonga) with metadata such as source, timestamp, and language tags, and balanced train/validation/test splits. Designed for supervised topic classification and multi-label tagging, the dataset targets research on code-switching, low-resource NLP, domain adaptation, and robust topic models for African urban text.

eoir_privacy is a dataset for developing and evaluating privacy-preserving computer vision methods. It contains images and video frames annotated with sensitive regions (faces, license plates, text and other personal identifiers) alongside anonymized/redacted ground truth, enabling training and benchmarking of detection, segmentation and anonymization models. The collection covers varied real-world scenes and capture conditions to support assessment of privacy–utility trade-offs and robustness of anonymization techniques.

Description: joelito/brazilian_court_decisions is a corpus of Brazilian judicial decisions (legal opinions) in Portuguese, accompanied by document-level metadata (e.g., court, date, case identifiers). It provides real-world legal text suitable for NLP tasks such as text classification, summarization, information extraction, and retrieval in the Brazilian legal domain. The dataset supports development and evaluation of models for legal analytics, automated case outcome prediction, and downstream applications requiring domain-specific language understanding and document-level reasoning.

Online Lecture Sentiment Dataset is a multimodal corpus of recorded online lectures (video, audio, aligned transcripts and timestamped slide/segment metadata) segmented and human-annotated for affect and engagement. Annotations include discrete sentiment labels (e.g., positive/neutral/negative), continuous valence/arousal and engagement scores, and segment-level timestamps, enabling training and evaluation of sentiment classification, multimodal affect recognition, engagement estimation, lecture quality assessment, and adaptive educational analytics.

emo is a dataset for emotion and affect recognition containing human facial images (and/or short video clips) annotated with categorical emotion labels (e.g., anger, disgust, fear, happiness, sadness, surprise, neutral) and, where provided, continuous affect measures such as valence and arousal. It is designed for supervised learning and benchmarking of emotion classification and affect-estimation models, supporting tasks like facial expression recognition, valence–arousal regression, and cross-dataset generalization. emo facilitates research in affective computing and human–computer interaction by providing diverse, real-world expressions across varied poses, lighting, and demographics.

SemEval-2018 Task 1 (Affect in Tweets) is a tweet-level dataset for emotion and sentiment analysis, containing tweets annotated with both categorical labels and continuous intensity scores. Annotations cover multiple affect dimensions (notably anger, fear, joy, sadness and general valence) and support subtasks including emotion/sentiment classification, emotion intensity regression, and ordinal classification. The dataset is provided with standard train/dev/test splits and is intended to benchmark models that predict presence and strength of emotions in short social-media text, enabling evaluation of regression, classification, and multi-label approaches for affective computing on Twitter.

The WNLI dataset is a part of the GLUE benchmark used for Natural Language Inference (NLI). It contains pairs of sentences, and the task is to determine whether the second sentence is an entailment of the first one or not. The dataset is used to train and evaluate models on their ability to understand these relationships between sentences.

multilingual_parental_occupations is a survey-derived dataset from the IEA ICILS study that contains parental occupation responses in multiple languages together with mapped standardized occupation codes and basic survey metadata (e.g., student/school identifiers, country). It provides free-text occupation entries and their corresponding harmonized labels (e.g., ISCO or study-specific categories), enabling supervised learning for multilingual text classification, cross-lingual occupation coding, entity normalization, and domain adaptation research. The dataset is suited for developing and evaluating models that must normalize heterogeneous, multilingual occupational descriptions into consistent taxonomies for demographic analysis and downstream educational studies.

dataset_node: Hungarian Custom Dataset␟Emotion Classification in Hungarian
desc: Hungarian Custom Dataset is a curated, annotated dataset for Hungarian language processing. It contains diverse-domain text (news, web, social media, Wikipedia) annotated with tokenization, lemmas, morphological features, POS tags, syntactic parses and named-entity labels, provided in standard train/validation/test splits. The dataset supports tasks such as POS tagging, morphological analysis, dependency parsing, NER and text classification, facilitating development and evaluation of Hungarian NLP models and cross-lingual transfer.

desc: GLUE MRPC is the Microsoft Research Paraphrase Corpus task in the GLUE benchmark for sentence-pair paraphrase identification. It contains roughly 3.6k sentence pairs drawn from news sources, each annotated with a binary label indicating whether the two sentences are semantically equivalent. MRPC is used to train and evaluate models on paraphrase detection and sentence-level semantic similarity, commonly measured with accuracy and F1, and serves as a compact benchmark for fine-tuning and assessing pretrained language models on sentence-pair classification.

dataset_node: Custom Fiction/Non-Fiction Dataset (85k samples)␟Fiction vs Non-Fiction Classification
desc: Custom Fiction/Non-Fiction Dataset (85k samples) is a labeled corpus of 85,000 text samples annotated as fiction or non-fiction. Samples are drawn from diverse published and web sources and include document-level metadata when available (title, author, publication, date). The dataset is intended for supervised binary classification, genre and stylistic analysis, domain adaptation, and training or evaluating language models on narrative versus expository text. Standard train/validation/test splits are provided for benchmarking.

Custom Fashion Reviews (ko) is a Korean-language dataset of user-written reviews for fashion products, paired with product metadata such as product ID, category, timestamp, and star ratings. It captures real customer feedback on clothing, shoes, and accessories and is suitable for sentiment classification, aspect-based sentiment analysis, review summarization, recommendation and domain-specific language modeling. The dataset enables development and evaluation of Korean NLP models for e-commerce scenarios, supporting supervised learning, transfer learning, and benchmarking of performance on fashion review understanding and downstream recommendation tasks.

marker-associations-snp-binary-base is a genomic benchmark dataset of binary-encoded single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) markers paired with binary outcome/association labels. Each sample is represented by a high-dimensional 0/1 genotype vector (allele absence/presence) and a corresponding binary phenotype or marker-significance label; optional covariates for population structure or technical confounders are provided. It is intended for supervised learning and feature-selection tasks in genomic prediction, GWAS-style association discovery, and benchmarking classifiers or sparse interpretable models on high-dimensional, potentially imbalanced binary data.

reviews_with_drift is a benchmark dataset of text reviews annotated for sentiment (or other categorical labels) with explicit temporal or simulated distributional drift. Each example includes review text, label, and temporal metadata to enable streaming and time-aware experiments. It is designed to evaluate concept-drift detection, online/adaptive classifiers, and continual learning methods under gradual, abrupt, or recurring label/text shifts. The dataset supports tasks like sentiment classification, domain adaptation, and robustness benchmarking for models exposed to changing data distributions.

filter_v2 is a paired-image dataset for learning and evaluating image filtering operations. It contains original images and corresponding filtered outputs across a variety of filter types (color grading, contrast/saturation adjustments, blur, sharpen, denoise, etc.) and intensities, with metadata labeling filter type and parameters. Designed for supervised training and benchmarking of filter approximation, image-to-image translation, style adjustment, and real-time enhancement models, it emphasizes diverse scenes and device conditions to measure fidelity and generalization.

StereoSet is a large-scale English-language dataset designed to evaluate stereotypical biases in language models across four domains: gender, profession, race, and religion. It consists of naturally occurring text samples that reflect common societal stereotypes, enabling the measurement of a model’s tendency to produce biased or discriminatory content. By focusing on bias detection, StereoSet provides a benchmark to assess and quantify the presence of harmful stereotypes in model outputs, which is critical for developing fair and ethical natural language processing systems. The dataset challenges models to distinguish between stereotypical and anti-stereotypical associations, facilitating research into bias mitigation techniques. Its broad coverage of multiple social dimensions and naturalistic text makes it a valuable resource for bias evaluation in language understanding and generation tasks. StereoSet has been employed to benchmark large language models, helping to highlight and reduce the propagation of social biases in AI systems.

deprem_private_dataset_v1_3 is a private, annotated image dataset for post-earthquake damage assessment and rapid-response research. It contains aerial/drone and ground-level RGB imagery with GPS and timestamp metadata, paired with building- and infrastructure-level annotations including bounding boxes, pixel-wise damage segmentation masks, categorical damage-severity labels, and pre-/post-event change pairs. The dataset is intended to train and evaluate supervised models for damage detection, segmentation, and change detection to support automated mapping, triage, and resource prioritization; v1_3 includes refined annotations and expanded spatial coverage.

ASSIN2 is a Portuguese-language benchmark for semantic textual similarity and textual entailment containing sentence pairs annotated with graded similarity scores and categorical entailment labels. It covers both Brazilian and European Portuguese and provides standard splits for training and evaluation, enabling supervised learning and benchmarking of STS, paraphrase detection, and natural language inference (NLI) models in Portuguese.

politic-it is an Italian-language political text dataset comprising news articles and social media posts about Italian politics, paired with metadata (timestamp, source, author) and task-oriented annotations. It is designed for NLP research on political discourse and supports supervised tasks such as stance detection, sentiment analysis, topic classification, misinformation/ veracity assessment, and timeline or network analyses. The dataset is suitable for training and evaluating models on Italian political language, cross-lingual transfer, and robustness/fairness studies.

Yelp Polarity is a large-scale binary sentiment classification dataset of Yelp business reviews, where each review is labeled positive or negative (derived from star ratings). It provides real-world, user-generated text of varying lengths and noise, suitable for training and evaluating supervised sentiment and text-classification models. The dataset is commonly used as a benchmark for model performance and robustness on informal, domain-specific review language.

bgglue is a Bulgarian language understanding benchmark modeled after GLUE, providing a suite of diverse NLP tasks (e.g., text classification, natural language inference, paraphrase detection, named entity recognition, and reading comprehension) with standardized train/dev/test splits and evaluation metrics. It enables consistent evaluation and comparison of Bulgarian and multilingual language models on core semantic and sequence-labeling problems, supporting research on fine-tuning, transfer learning, robustness, and cross-domain generalization for Bulgarian.

TeenSenti Slang Dataset is a labeled corpus of teenage social-media text containing colloquial slang, abbreviations, emojis and nonstandard spelling annotated for sentiment. It is designed to train and evaluate models that must handle informal youth language—supporting tasks such as sentiment classification, slang detection, and lexical normalization. The dataset helps develop robust NLP systems for social monitoring, content moderation, and downstream applications that require understanding of adolescent vernacular and contextual sentiment.

TweetEval is a benchmark evaluation framework designed for natural language processing tasks on Twitter data, focusing on seven diverse classification problems including sentiment analysis. The dataset comprises text from tweets, reflecting the unique linguistic characteristics and informal style of social media language. It serves as a standardized platform to assess and compare models tailored to Twitter-specific challenges such as sentiment polarity detection, irony recognition, and emoji prediction. By consolidating multiple related tasks, TweetEval addresses the fragmentation in social media NLP research and facilitates the development of robust, domain-adapted models. The dataset supports the evaluation of various classification approaches, including recent transformer-based architectures pretrained on generic corpora and further adapted to Twitter data. Performance is typically measured using standard classification metrics such as F1 score, precision, and recall. TweetEval’s comprehensive and heterogeneous nature makes it a valuable resource for advancing sentiment analysis and other text classification tasks in the social media context.

This is an **entity-level** Twitter Sentiment Analysis dataset. For each message, the task is to judge the sentiment of the entire sentence towards a given entity. For example, A outperforms B is **positive** for entity **A** but **negative** for entity **B**. The dataset contains ~70K labeled training messages and 1K labeled validation messages. It is available online for free on Kaggle.

wikd/customer_data is an anonymized synthetic customer-behavior dataset for benchmarking supervised and unsupervised ML on tabular and temporal customer records. Each sample contains demographics and account metadata (region, tenure, signup date), aggregated behavioral features and transaction counts by time window (sessions, purchases, product categories), optional free-text support/feedback fields, and targets such as churn label and lifetime-value (CLTV). It is intended for churn prediction, CLTV/regression, customer segmentation, next-purchase/recommendation and time-series forecasting tasks, and includes standard train/validation/test splits and common evaluation metrics.

The **Beyond the Imitation Game Benchmark** (BIG-bench) is a collaborative benchmark intended to probe large language models and extrapolate their future capabilities. Big-bench include more than 200 tasks. Image source:

azaheadhealth is a de-identified longitudinal clinical dataset for forecasting patient outcomes from electronic health records. It contains time-stamped features such as demographics, diagnoses, medications, laboratory results, and vital signs, with labels for common prediction tasks (short- and medium-term readmission, mortality, disease onset, and treatment response). The dataset is curated for benchmarking temporal and cross-sectional models in risk stratification, temporal representation learning, and clinical decision support, and includes standard train/validation/test splits and evaluation metrics for reproducible comparison. Data use requires adherence to applicable privacy and data-use agreements.

The **Sentences Involving Compositional Knowledge** (**SICK**) dataset is a dataset for compositional distributional semantics. It includes a large number of sentence pairs that are rich in the lexical, syntactic and semantic phenomena. Each pair of sentences is annotated in two dimensions: relatedness and entailment. The relatedness score ranges from 1 to 5, and Pearson’s r is used for evaluation; the entailment relation is categorical, consisting of entailment, contradiction, and neutral. There are 4439 pairs in the train split, 495 in the trial split used for development and 4906 in the test split. The sentence pairs are generated from image and video caption datasets before being paired up using some algorithm. Source: Image Source:

GreekReddit is a corpus of Greek-language Reddit posts and comments collected from Reddit, containing informal social-media text and associated metadata (timestamps, subreddit, score, anonymized author identifier). It captures colloquial spelling, slang, emoji use and frequent code‑switching with English, making it well suited for training and evaluating Greek NLP models for language modeling, tokenization, sentiment and topic classification, hate/toxicity detection, dialect and sociolinguistic analysis, and domain adaptation for social-media text.

Tweets Hate Speech Detection is a labeled dataset of Twitter posts annotated for hate speech and related offensive content. Each record pairs tweet text (original or preprocessed) with annotations indicating presence/absence of hate speech and, where available, subtype labels such as abusive/offensive, severity, and target category (e.g., race, gender, religion). It is intended for supervised training and evaluation of NLP classifiers, multi-label detection, and research on fairness, robustness, and automated content moderation. Data are typically provided in CSV/JSON format with identifying information removed or anonymized.

SetFit/SentEval-CR is a binary sentiment classification dataset derived from the SentEval CR (customer review) task and formatted for few‑shot training and evaluation with SetFit. It contains short product/customer review sentences labeled positive or negative, enabling evaluation of sentence embeddings and lightweight classification heads under limited labeled data. The dataset is commonly used to benchmark transfer learning, domain adaptation, and few‑shot text classification methods.

The **Russian Corpus of Linguistic Acceptability (RuCoLA)** is built from the ground up under the well-established binary LA approach. RuCoLA consists of 9.8k in-domain sentences from linguistic publications and 3.6k out-of-domain sentence produced by generative models. Source: Image Source:

KMHAS Korean Hate Speech is a dataset of Korean-language social media posts and comments annotated for hate and abusive content. It provides binary and fine-grained labels identifying the presence, target (e.g., gender, ethnicity, disability), and type or severity of hateful language, enabling both single-label and multi-label supervised tasks. The dataset is intended for training and benchmarking hate-speech detection and content-moderation models in Korean, and for research into linguistic patterns, bias, and mitigation strategies in non-English online contexts.

BanglaSenti is a Bengali sentiment analysis dataset containing Bangla-language text samples paired with sentiment labels (e.g., positive, negative, neutral). Collected from online sources (social media and reviews), it provides annotated examples for supervised training and evaluation of sentiment classification models. The dataset facilitates development of NLP systems for emotion and opinion detection in Bengali, supports transfer learning and lexicon construction, and serves as a benchmark for comparing model performance on low-resource, non-English sentiment tasks.

dataset_node: Mail Data Indonesian Spam Detection␟Text Classification
desc: Mail Data Indonesian Spam Detection is a labeled corpus of Indonesian-language email/messages annotated as spam or non-spam (ham). It provides raw message text and often accompanying metadata (e.g., subject, sender, timestamp) to support supervised text-classification and spam-filtering tasks. The dataset is suitable for training and evaluating classifiers, development of language-specific preprocessing (tokenization, normalization), and research on challenges like informal language, obfuscation and code-switching in Indonesian text.

Email Dataset is a collection of email messages with associated metadata (sender, recipient, timestamp, subject) and optional annotations such as thread structure, labels (spam/ham, folder/category, intent), and summary or reply targets. It is designed to support supervised and unsupervised NLP tasks—spam detection, email classification and routing, thread reconstruction, summarization, reply suggestion, and information extraction—providing realistic conversational and long-form text for model training and evaluation. The dataset serves as a benchmark for robustness on noisy, domain-specific language and practical email-processing systems; users should account for privacy and de-identification requirements when applying it.

Custom Labeled Aduan Dataset is a curated collection of complaint reports ("aduan") annotated for supervised ML tasks. Each entry pairs complaint text with human-provided labels such as category/topic, severity/priority, and resolution status, and may include metadata like timestamp, source, and location. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating classification, intent detection, prioritization, and information-extraction models for automated complaint triage, routing, and analytics in customer-service, civic-tech, or public-sector workflows.

MISO-BR is a benchmark dataset for blind image restoration that provides multiple degraded observations of each scene paired with a single high-quality ground-truth image. It covers diverse real-world degradations (motion blur, noise, compression, low-light artifacts) across varied indoor and outdoor scenes and includes standardized train/validation/test splits and evaluation protocols. MISO-BR is designed to support development and comparison of multi-input single-output restoration models (e.g., burst denoising, multi-frame deblurring, exposure fusion) using common metrics such as PSNR, SSIM and perceptual scores.

MAIB Incident Reports is a corpus of maritime safety investigation reports published by the UK Marine Accident Investigation Branch. Each entry pairs long-form incident narratives with structured metadata such as date, location, vessel type, casualties, causal factors and safety recommendations. The dataset is suited for NLP tasks including classification, information extraction (entities, causal chains, recommendations), summarization, event and trend analysis, and risk modeling in a safety-critical domain. It enables development and evaluation of models that extract actionable insights from domain-specific, long-form technical reports.

MASSIVE (ja-JP) is the Japanese portion of the MASSIVE multilingual dataset for task-oriented spoken language understanding. It contains Japanese text utterances localized from English templates and annotated with intent labels and slot/value spans to support intent classification and slot filling. Designed for supervised training and evaluation, this subset enables development and benchmarking of Japanese SLU systems and cross-lingual transfer experiments for dialog and voice-assistant applications.

safe-guard-prompt-injection (test split) is a test set for evaluating language-model safety and robustness against prompt-injection attacks. It contains adversarial prompts and conversational contexts that attempt to override policies, exfiltrate information, or elicit unsafe actions, paired with expected safe handling (e.g., reject, sanitize, or provide a policy-compliant response) or labels. The split is intended to benchmark detection accuracy, safe-response generation, and the generalization of guarding mechanisms and instruction filters under realistic, novel injection patterns.

dataset_node: deepset/prompt-injections (test split, tuned threshold)␟Prompt injection detection
desc: deepset/prompt-injections (test split, tuned threshold) is a benchmark dataset of user prompts annotated for prompt-injection attacks, provided as a held-out test split with a recommended decision threshold tuned on development data. It contains prompt texts paired with binary attack labels and supporting metadata, enabling standardized evaluation of detectors that flag malicious or task-manipulating inputs. The dataset is intended for assessing classifier performance under a calibrated threshold (precision/recall/F1) and for comparing prompt-injection mitigation methods in real-world conversational and instruction-following settings.

Spanish SMS Spam Detection is a labeled corpus of Spanish-language SMS messages annotated as spam or ham for supervised binary text classification. It is intended to train and evaluate spam-filtering and NLP models that handle colloquial, abbreviated text in Spanish, supporting work on language-specific embeddings, feature engineering, class-imbalance strategies, and robustness of deployed spam detection systems.

FLICC is a curated multimodal benchmark of real-world photographs paired with human-written captions and supporting metadata. Designed for vision–language research, it provides diverse scenes, object and attribute coverage, and standardized train/validation/test splits to enable reproducible evaluation. FLICC is suitable for training and benchmarking image captioning, image–text retrieval, multimodal representation learning, and related tasks that require robust grounding between visual content and natural-language descriptions.

MNLI (Multi-Genre Natural Language Inference) is a large-scale dataset for natural language inference containing approximately 433k sentence pairs (premise, hypothesis) annotated with three-way labels: entailment, contradiction, or neutral. Collected across multiple written and spoken genres, it enables training and evaluation of models that must generalize across diverse domains. MNLI includes matched and mismatched development/test sets to measure in-domain and cross-genre performance, making it a standard benchmark for sentence-level semantic understanding, transfer learning, and NLU model evaluation.

Amazon US Reviews is a large-scale corpus of user-generated product reviews from the Amazon US marketplace, containing review text alongside metadata such as star ratings, product and category IDs, reviewer IDs, timestamps, and helpfulness votes (and often product metadata like title and price). It supports supervised and unsupervised tasks including sentiment analysis, rating prediction, recommendation and collaborative filtering, review summarization, aspect extraction, and temporal or domain-adaptive studies across diverse product categories. The dataset is useful for building and evaluating NLP and recommender-system models on realistic, long-tailed, and noisy consumer-review data.

filter_sort is a synthetic benchmark for learning and evaluating filter-and-sort operations on variable-length sequences. Each example pairs an input sequence (numeric or categorical) and a filter predicate with the corresponding filtered-and-sorted output; variations include different predicates, sort orders, sequence lengths, and noise levels. The dataset is designed to test sequence-to-sequence models, neural algorithmic reasoning, and program synthesis approaches on compositional, algorithmic generalization and robustness.

hate_speech_offensive is a text classification dataset of social media posts annotated into three categories: hate speech, offensive language, and neither. It contains human-labeled examples suitable for supervised training and benchmarking of abusive-language detection models on short, informal text. The dataset is commonly used to develop and evaluate content-moderation systems, study model fairness and bias, and assess robustness to nuanced or ambiguous abusive expressions.

The **Multi-Genre Natural Language Inference** (**MultiNLI**) dataset has 433K sentence pairs. Its size and mode of collection are modeled closely like . MultiNLI offers ten distinct genres (Face-to-face, Telephone, 9/11, Travel, Letters, Oxford University Press, Slate, Verbatim, Goverment and Fiction) of written and spoken English data. There are matched dev/test sets which are derived from the same sources as those in the training set, and mismatched sets which do not closely resemble any seen at training time. Source:

tweets_hate_speech_detection is a corpus of Twitter posts annotated for hate speech and related categories (e.g., hate/offensive/neutral or binary hate vs. non-hate). It provides raw tweet text and class labels for supervised training and evaluation of text classification models aimed at hate/toxicity detection, content moderation, and robustness/fairness analysis. The dataset is useful for benchmarking NLP models, exploring class imbalance and annotator uncertainty, and studying model bias, and it contains abusive content—use and share it in accordance with ethical, legal, and platform privacy guidelines.

desc: afg1/pombe-canto-data is a collection of curated annotation records exported from the Canto curation platform for the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe. The dataset contains structured gene-centric entries linking gene identifiers to phenotypes, molecular functions, processes, evidence codes and literature references. It is suitable for tasks in biological text mining, ontology mapping, gene–phenotype association modeling, and tools development for biocuration and knowledge-base integration.

desc: abullard1/steam-reviews-constructiveness-binary-label-annotations-1.5k is a dataset of ~1,500 Steam user reviews labeled for constructiveness (binary: constructive vs. non-constructive). Each record pairs review text with a gold label and optional metadata (e.g., review id, timestamp). The collection is intended for supervised learning and evaluation of NLP models for constructive-feedback detection, content moderation, comment-quality ranking, and related binary classification tasks. Its modest size makes it suitable for fine-tuning, prototyping, annotation studies, and benchmarking model robustness on real-world user-generated game reviews.

Cancel Culture Stance Classification is a dataset of social media posts and short-form text snippets annotated for stance toward "cancel culture." Each example is labeled by human annotators with stance categories (e.g., support, oppose, neutral/ambivalent) and includes contextual metadata when available (platform, timestamp, target/entity). The dataset is intended for supervised training and evaluation of stance detection and opinion mining models, and for downstream work on bias, fairness, domain adaptation, and interpretability in automated moderation and social discourse analysis.

quora duplicates dev is the development/validation split of the Quora Question Pairs dataset, containing paired user-submitted questions annotated as duplicate or non-duplicate. It is used to train and evaluate models for paraphrase detection, semantic similarity, duplicate question retrieval, and question-answering deduplication. The dataset reflects real-world, informal user language (including typos and varied phrasing), making it useful for assessing model robustness, calibration, and generalization in downstream tasks like ranking, retrieval, and transfer learning.

Quora Duplicates Test is the evaluation split of the Quora Question Pairs dataset for duplicate question detection and semantic similarity. It consists of paired user-generated English questions (with IDs and optional metadata) drawn from Quora, intended for binary classification of whether two questions express the same intent or meaning. The set reflects diverse, informal language and topical variety, making it useful for benchmarking paraphrase detection, question deduplication, retrieval, and related NLP models; public test labels are often withheld for leaderboard evaluation.

stsb validation is the validation split of the Semantic Textual Similarity Benchmark (STS-B), containing sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores (typically 0–5). It is used for model selection and hyperparameter tuning in tasks that measure semantic equivalence, such as sentence-level regression, embedding evaluation, and downstream NLU systems, with common evaluation metrics including Pearson and Spearman correlation.

stsb test is the test split of the Semantic Textual Similarity Benchmark (STS-B), containing sentence pairs with human-annotated similarity scores (typically on a 0–5 scale). It is used to evaluate models’ ability to measure semantic similarity and produce sentence embeddings, with performance commonly reported using Pearson/Spearman correlation against the human judgments. The split serves as a held-out benchmark for comparing semantic similarity, paraphrase detection, and related downstream models.

Combined Financial Filings (Labelbox + EDGAR) pairs raw SEC filings from EDGAR with human-curated annotations created via Labelbox. It includes document-level labels and structured annotations such as entity spans, labeled sections, key–value pairs, and table mappings to support supervised training for information extraction, document classification, table parsing, and summarization. The dataset is intended for developing and evaluating models for financial-document understanding, compliance screening, automated data extraction, and downstream analytics on real-world regulatory text with complex layouts.

NER-RE-for-Software-Mentions is a paired named entity recognition and relation extraction dataset focused on software-related text. It contains sentences from software engineering sources (e.g., documentation, release notes, issue trackers, Q&A) annotated with token-level entity spans for software mentions (products, libraries, tools, versions, platforms, authors) and typed relations between those spans (e.g., dependency, integration, produced_by, version_of, runs_on). Designed for training and evaluating joint NER+RE models, the dataset supports tasks such as software-mention detection, relation classification, entity linking, and automated extraction of software ecosystems and dependency graphs. Annotations use span-level labels (BIO-style for NER) and relation triples between annotated spans to enable supervised learning and benchmarking.

jigsaw_toxicity_pred is a text-classification dataset of user comments annotated for abusive and harmful language to support development and evaluation of automatic content-moderation models. Each example pairs an English-language comment with toxicity annotations—commonly provided as multi-label flags (e.g., toxic, severe_toxic, obscene, threat, insult, identity_hate) or as continuous toxicity scores—enabling binary, multi-label, or regression tasks. The dataset is intended for supervised learning and benchmarking of toxicity detection, calibration, and robustness, and is frequently used for research on fairness and bias mitigation in automated moderation systems.

Malaysian Social Media Posts is a corpus of public social media messages from users in Malaysia, containing short-form text in Malay, English, and code‑switched varieties together with timestamps and basic metadata. It is designed to support NLP and social-computing tasks such as language identification, sentiment and topic classification, hate/misinformation detection, and sociolinguistic or temporal analyses in Southeast Asian contexts. The dataset emphasizes informal, colloquial language and regional dialects, enabling development and evaluation of robust, multilingual models for real-world social media content.

Turkish Conspiracy Detection Dataset is a labeled corpus of Turkish-language texts collected from online sources (social media posts, comments, news articles and forums) and annotated for the presence of conspiracy-related content. Intended for supervised binary (conspiracy vs. non-conspiracy) classification and related tasks (multi-class conspiracy types, stance detection), it includes annotations, source metadata (timestamps, platform), and standard train/validation/test splits. The dataset enables development and evaluation of NLP models for misinformation detection, moderation, cross-lingual transfer, and robustness analysis in Turkish.

Services Publics Plus (data.gouv.fr) is a structured, nationwide directory of French public service points and administrative services. Each record provides descriptive metadata such as service name, category/type, postal address, contact details, opening hours and geolocation, enabling linkage between services and geographic regions. The dataset is useful for tasks like geospatial analysis, service discovery and recommendation, record linkage and entity resolution, accessibility studies, and training NLP models for information extraction and question answering about public administration.

custom_text_dataset is a curated collection of textual samples assembled for training and evaluating natural language processing models. It contains diverse content from multiple domains and genres, with optional task-specific annotations (e.g., labels, entity spans, or summaries) and standard train/validation/test splits. The dataset is formatted for easy ingestion and includes metadata for source and style, enabling experiments in classification, sequence labeling, summarization, language modeling, and domain adaptation. It supports development and benchmarking of robust, generalizable NLP systems.

Financial News Headlines (Balanced) is a curated corpus of short-form financial news headlines annotated for supervised NLP tasks. The dataset provides balanced class distributions across sentiment/market-impact labels (e.g., positive, negative, neutral) and is stratified by industry sectors and time periods to reduce label and topical bias. Each example includes the headline text with metadata such as timestamp and optional ticker/sector mapping, enabling tasks like sentiment classification, event detection, topic/topic-shift analysis, and short-horizon market-movement prediction. It is designed for training and benchmarking models that require robust, debiased evaluation on financial language.

LEDGAR (LexGLUE) is a dataset of contract provisions extracted from SEC EDGAR filings and annotated with fine‑grained clause types for multi‑label classification. It provides thousands of real-world contract clauses mapped to standardized legal clause categories, enabling supervised training and evaluation of models for clause identification, contract analytics, information extraction, compliance checking, and related legal-NLP tasks. LEDGAR benchmarks model performance on domain-specific, fine‑grained clause classification in the contract analysis setting.

ADE Corpus V2 is a manually annotated corpus for adverse drug event (ADE) extraction, containing English texts labeled with drug mentions, adverse event mentions, and their relations. It is designed for training and evaluating NLP models for ADE detection, entity recognition, and relation extraction in pharmacovigilance and clinical text mining. The LeT-Mi & ArMI Consolidated Corpus is a multimodal speech dataset that merges the LeT-Mi and ArMI collections into a single resource with synchronized high-quality audio, articulatory motion capture (e.g., EMA or optical tracking) and time-aligned transcripts and phonetic labels. marker-associations-binary-base is a dataset of marker–target pairs labeled with binary association indicators (associated vs. not associated). Each example contains identifiers for a marker and a target along with optional numeric or categorical features and a ground-truth 0/1 label. It is tailored for supervised binary classification and link-prediction tasks, enabling benchmarking of models for association detection, recommendation, and graph-based inference. The dataset is suitable for training and evaluating classifiers, ranking systems, and embedding methods that learn pairwise relationships.

Emotion is a dataset for facial expression recognition consisting of face images labeled with discrete emotion categories (e.g., anger, disgust, fear, happiness, sadness, surprise, neutral). It is intended for supervised learning and benchmarking of emotion-classification models, enabling development and evaluation of deep networks for affect recognition from facial appearance. The dataset includes variability in subjects, pose and illumination to promote robustness and generalization, making it useful for research in affective computing, human–computer interaction, and downstream tasks that require reliable emotion inference.

movie_rationales is a dataset of movie review texts annotated with classification labels (e.g., sentiment) and human-annotated rationale spans that justify each label. It provides review-level inputs paired with span- or token-level annotations indicating the text segments humans consider most relevant for the decision. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating explainable NLP models that must both predict labels and produce faithful, compact rationales, and for benchmarking rationale extraction, interpretability, and faithfulness metrics (sufficiency, comprehensiveness, plausibility). It supports research on supervised rationale learning, joint label–rationale prediction, and improving model transparency in opinion mining and related downstream tasks.

ckandemir/bitcoin_tweets_sentiment_kaggle is a labeled collection of Bitcoin-related tweets from Kaggle annotated for sentiment (e.g., positive, negative, neutral). The dataset is suitable for training and evaluating NLP models (classifiers, embeddings, transformer fine-tuning) and for research on sentiment-driven market signals and trend analysis.

iSarcasm is a dataset of tweets, each labelled as either sarcastic or non_sarcastic. Each sarcastic tweet is further labelled for one of the following types of ironic speech: - sarcasm: tweets that contradict the state of affairs and are critical towards an addressee; - irony: tweets that contradict the state of affairs but are not obviously critical towards an addressee; - satire: tweets that appear to support an addressee, but contain underlying disagreement and mocking; - understatement: tweets that undermine the importance of the state of affairs they refer to; - overstatement: tweets that describe the state of affairs in obviously exaggerated terms; - rhetorical question: tweets that include a question whose invited inference (implicature) is obviously contradicting the state of affairs. For each sarastic tweet, there's also: - an explanation, in English sentences, as to why it is sarcastic, and - a rephrase that conveys the same meaning non-sarcastically. Both have been provided by the author of the tweet. iSarcasm contains 4,484 tweets, out of which 777 are labelled as sarcastic and 3,707 as non-sarcastic. You'll find two files, isarcasm_train.csv and isarcasm_test.csv, each containing 80% and 20% of the examples chosen at random, respectively. Each line in a file has the format tweet_id,sarcasm_label,sarcasm_type, where sarcasm_type are only defined for sarcastic tweets, as specified above. Source:

swiss_law_area_prediction is a dataset of Swiss legal texts (statute articles, provisions, or case excerpts) annotated with one or more legal-area labels (e.g., civil, criminal, administrative, tax). It includes multilingual content (German, French, Italian) and document metadata, and is designed for supervised classification and multi‑label prediction tasks. The dataset supports development and evaluation of legal NLP models for area/domain classification, cross‑lingual transfer, and handling imbalanced or hierarchical label taxonomies in the Swiss legal context.

konsman/setfit-messages-optimized is a curated corpus of short conversational messages paired with classification labels, formatted and cleaned for few‑shot fine‑tuning with the SetFit workflow. The dataset emphasizes compact, representative examples and balanced label distributions to enable efficient training of sentence‑embedding–based classifiers with minimal labeled data. It is suitable for benchmarking and developing lightweight intent detection, message classification, and conversational tagging models under low‑resource conditions.

arxiv_dataset is a collection of scientific articles harvested from the arXiv preprint server, typically including titles, abstracts, authors, categories, submission dates and often full-text or extracted body text. It is designed for NLP and information-retrieval tasks such as topic classification, abstractive and extractive summarization, citation and recommendation modeling, trend analysis, and scientific language modeling. The dataset enables evaluation of models on large-scale academic text and supports research on domain adaptation, author and citation networks, and temporal shifts in research content.

CarEvaluationDataset is a multiclass classification dataset derived from the classic UCI Car Evaluation data. It contains 1,728 instances with six categorical input attributes (buying, maintenance, doors, persons, luggage boot, safety) and a four-way target label describing car acceptability (unacc, acc, good, vgood). The dataset is suited for supervised learning experiments on categorical data, benchmarking classifiers, studying feature encoding and interpretability, and rapid prototyping of decision-tree, ensemble, and rule-based models.

uc-2040-en is an English-language short-text classification dataset containing 2,040 user-contributed utterances paired with single categorical labels denoting intent or semantic class. It is curated for training and evaluating intent detection and short-text categorization models, with an emphasis on compact, balanced splits suitable for low-data and few-shot experiments. The dataset supports benchmarking supervised classifiers, transfer learning, and robustness to noisy or colloquial user input in conversational and feedback-driven applications.

Annotations were produced by native speakers with quality-control procedures to ensure consistency. LaRoSeDa is a large-scale dataset for road and lane segmentation from aerial and street-level imagery, providing high-resolution images paired with pixel-wise annotations for roads, lanes, and related scene elements. MOROCO is a Romanian-language news corpus designed for dialect identification and text classification. The dataset supports research in domain adaptation, multi-task learning, and evaluation of models that must handle real-world noisy user-generated text and class imbalance across categories.

train eval is a dataset that provides standardized, task-agnostic training and evaluation splits for supervised machine learning. It contains labeled examples organized into separate "train" and "eval" subsets with consistent formatting and metadata to enable reproducible model development, hyperparameter tuning, and fair benchmarking. The dataset’s structure supports common evaluation protocols and metrics, reducing variability from ad-hoc splitting and simplifying comparisons across models and experiments.

NanoMSMARCO R100 is a compact, reproducible subset of the MS MARCO passage ranking benchmark designed for rapid prototyping and evaluation of retrieval and reranking models. It contains query–passage pairs with relevance labels and precomputed candidate pools limited to 100 passages per query (the "R100" setting), allowing fast training and inference on constrained compute. The dataset supports supervised ranking, dense retrieval, and contrastive learning experiments, and is commonly used to compare ranking quality using metrics like MRR and nDCG while enabling quick iteration and reproducible benchmarking.

NanoNFCorpus R100 is a compact, annotated natural-language benchmark designed to evaluate low-resource and few‑shot NLP models. The R100 variant provides standardized splits with 100 labeled examples per class, covering short documents and sentences from multiple domains. Annotations include document/class labels and token-level spans suitable for tasks such as text classification, named‑entity recognition, and sequence labeling. The corpus is intended for measuring sample efficiency, transfer learning, robustness, and performance of lightweight or on‑device models under constrained supervision.

NanoNQ R100 is a compact benchmark derived from the Natural Questions (NQ) dataset for rapid evaluation of dense retrieval and reranking systems under a top-100 candidate protocol. Each query has associated ground-truth passages and a fixed 100-candidate evaluation set to measure retrieval and ranking metrics efficiently. Designed for fast prototyping and reproducible comparisons, it facilitates tuning and evaluation of lightweight retrievers, negative-sampling strategies, and rerankers in question-answering pipelines.

dataset_node: NanoBEIR R100 mean␟Cross Encoder Nano BEIR
desc: NanoBEIR R100 mean is an aggregate retrieval metric reporting the average Recall@100 across the NanoBEIR benchmark — a compact, resource‑efficient subset of the BEIR cross‑domain information retrieval suite. The metric is intended for fast model selection and evaluation of cross‑domain generalization and retrieval effectiveness under constrained compute and dataset size.

arrow is a dataset of arrow symbols collected across diverse scenes and styles, annotated for tasks such as detection, segmentation and orientation estimation. It includes varied arrow shapes, sizes, rotations, occlusions and backgrounds to encourage robustness to visual variability. Designed for training and evaluating models on directional symbol recognition, pose/orientation recovery and scene understanding, arrow is useful for applications in sign interpretation, HCI, robotics and navigation.

dataset_node: Huancavelica Late Blight Benchmark (Balanced)␟Potato Late Blight Risk Classification

The dataset’s balanced class distribution reduces label skew, making it well suited for training and evaluating supervised models for disease classification, lesion localization, and deployment-focused research on robust, in-field plant-disease detection.

amazon_reviews_multi (español) is the Spanish-language subset of the Amazon Reviews Multi corpus, containing Spanish product reviews paired with metadata such as star ratings, review titles and bodies, product category, product/customer identifiers, and timestamps. It is designed for supervised tasks like sentiment classification, rating prediction, opinion mining, and training or evaluating Spanish and multilingual language models and cross-lingual transfer methods, offering real-world e-commerce text across product categories for benchmarking classification, regression, and representation-learning approaches.

Healthcare Lifestyle Dataset is a multimodal, longitudinal collection of anonymized lifestyle signals and basic health outcomes, combining self-reported behaviors (diet, sleep, substance use), wearable sensor time series (activity, heart rate), and routine clinical measurements. It is designed to support supervised and temporal modeling of health risk prediction, chronic disease progression, behavioral phenotyping, and personalized intervention recommendation. The dataset enables development and evaluation of models for forecasting, clustering, causal analysis, and population-level health analytics relevant to preventive care and real-world deployment.

desc: Scraped Social Media Profiles (Bluesky & Twitter) is a multimodal dataset of public user profiles and associated metadata collected from Bluesky and Twitter, including usernames, profile text/bios, profile images, recent posts/tweets, timestamps, follower/following counts, and basic social graph edges. It is intended for research on user modeling, social network analysis, content moderation, misinformation detection, language and multimodal representation learning, and recommendation systems. The dataset reflects real-world platform behavior but may contain personal and sensitive information; users should apply privacy-preserving practices, respect platform terms of service and legal restrictions, and consider sampling biases and annotation limitations when using it for benchmarking or model development.

Business Proposals is a corpus of anonymized proposal documents paired with structured metadata and annotations to support enterprise document understanding. Each item includes the full proposal text plus section labels (e.g., executive summary, scope, pricing), concise human or model-generated summaries, categorical tags (industry, service type), and optional outcome or scoring labels (accepted/rejected, value). The dataset is intended for tasks such as summarization, section segmentation, information extraction, classification, outcome prediction, template generation, and retrieval in commercial document workflows.

Mental Health Crisis Detection is a labeled dataset of anonymized user-generated text (and where available, short transcripts) drawn from social media and support forums, annotated for presence of acute mental-health crisis indicators. Each instance includes timestamps and limited metadata plus expert annotations for binary crisis vs. non-crisis labels, severity/triage categories, and risk markers (e.g., suicidal ideation, self-harm, intent). The dataset is intended for supervised learning and evaluation of crisis-detection, classification, and early-warning/triage models, prioritizing real-world robustness and calibration. Because the content is highly sensitive, access and use require ethical review, strict privacy protections, and adherence to data-use agreements.

The IMDb dataset is a large-scale graph-based dataset commonly used for link prediction and network analysis tasks. It represents a heterogeneous information network consisting of entities such as users, movies, and reviews, with edges capturing interactions like user ratings and reviews. This dataset supports various tasks including link prediction, node classification, and network reconstruction, making it valuable for evaluating network representation learning methods. IMDb is frequently employed as a benchmark to assess the performance of graph-based learning models, particularly those designed to handle complex relational structures and dynamic interactions within heterogeneous networks.

Chti Synthetic Dataset is a collection of synthetically rendered images and precise ground-truth annotations designed for training and evaluating computer-vision models. It contains diverse, configurable scenes with controlled variations in lighting, weather, motion, and object appearance, and provides dense labels such as segmentation masks, depth, surface normals, and optical flow (depending on task). The dataset enables large-scale supervised learning, systematic benchmarking, ablation studies, and domain-adaptation research by offering high-quality, repeatable annotations not readily available in real-world captures.

Cleaned Toxic Comments (Kaggle) is a preprocessed version of the Kaggle Toxic Comment Classification dataset containing user comments annotated with multiple toxicity labels (toxic, severe_toxic, obscene, threat, insult, identity_hate). The cleaned set applies text normalization and noise removal (e.g., HTML/URL stripping, encoding fixes, lowercasing, deduplication) to make the data ready for training. It is intended for multi-label toxicity detection, benchmarking classification models, and research on robustness and fairness in toxic-language moderation.

YouTube Music Genre Comments (custom) is a collection of user comments from YouTube music videos linked to the videos' music-genre labels. Each record contains the comment text and basic metadata (video ID, timestamp, anonymized author tag, like count) together with the associated genre(s), enabling supervised and self-supervised learning. The dataset is suitable for tasks such as genre-conditioned language modeling, sentiment and topic analysis, comment moderation, and improving recommendation or retrieval systems by exploiting genre–comment correlations in noisy, user-generated text.

Kaggle Emotions Dataset is a labeled corpus of short texts (commonly tweets or social media posts) annotated with discrete emotion labels (e.g., anger, fear, joy, love, sadness, surprise). It is designed for supervised emotion classification and related NLP tasks such as multi-class sentiment analysis, representation learning, and transfer learning evaluation. The dataset’s concise, conversational items and class imbalance make it useful for benchmarking text classifiers, feature extraction methods, and robustness to noisy, real-world language.

GoEmotions is a dataset of 58,009 English Reddit comments manually annotated for 27 fine‑grained emotion categories plus neutral.
