Quora dev is the development split of the Quora Question Pairs dataset, consisting of user-generated question pairs labeled as duplicate or non-duplicate. It provides realistic paraphrase and non-paraphrase examples for training, validation, and benchmarking of models for duplicate question detection, paraphrase identification, and semantic similarity scoring, commonly used for hyperparameter tuning and evaluation.

eval is a standardized evaluation dataset containing a held-out, diverse set of labeled examples for benchmarking model performance. Designed for robust, repeatable assessment, it offers realistic, representative samples and ground-truth annotations across relevant classes or tasks. eval is intended for final model comparison and reporting of metrics (accuracy, F1, IoU, etc.), emphasizing generalization to unseen data and enabling fair, reproducible evaluation of algorithms.

val is the validation split of the benchmark containing held-out examples drawn from the same distribution as the training data. It is used to monitor training, tune hyperparameters, perform early stopping, and select models without using the test set. The partition is disjoint from training and test data and is intended to provide an unbiased estimate of model performance for model selection using the benchmark’s target metrics (e.g., accuracy, F1, mAP).

onet validation is the validation split of the ONET benchmark used for development-time evaluation and model selection. It contains representative labeled examples from the same distribution as the training set, enabling hyperparameter tuning, early stopping, and comparison of model variants. The split provides a standardized, held-out set to assess generalization and guide improvements before final testing.

STS dev is the development split of a Semantic Textual Similarity dataset containing sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores (continuous scale, commonly 0–5). It is intended for model validation and hyperparameter tuning for tasks such as similarity regression, sentence embedding evaluation, paraphrase detection, and semantic retrieval, providing diverse, real-world sentence pairs to benchmark and guide model generalization.

claims evidence dev is the development split of a claim–evidence dataset for automated fact verification. Each example pairs a natural-language claim with one or more candidate evidence sentences (or passages) and annotations that indicate whether the provided evidence supports, refutes, or is insufficient to verify the claim. The set is intended for training and validating models for claim classification, evidence retrieval/ranking, and explainable fact-checking, serving as a benchmark for measuring verification accuracy and evidence-selection quality.

s2orc dev is the development split of the S2ORC (Semantic Scholar Open Research Corpus), containing a representative subset of parsed scientific documents with metadata, abstracts, full-text content, and citation links. It is intended for validation and benchmarking of scientific NLP models across tasks such as information extraction, citation and reference prediction, summarization, entity linking, and metadata parsing. The split provides a diverse, multi-domain sample of scholarly content to evaluate model generalization and guide hyperparameter tuning before testing on held-out S2ORC data.

AllNLI norm dev is the normalized development split derived from AllNLI (the combined SNLI and MultiNLI corpora) for natural language inference. It contains premise–hypothesis sentence pairs labeled with entailment, contradiction, or neutral, with text normalization applied (e.g., lowercasing, punctuation/whitespace normalization, token-level normalization) to reduce surface variation. The set is intended for validation and hyperparameter tuning and for benchmarking model generalization across genres in supervised NLI and sentence-pair representation tasks.

The sts validation set is the validation split of the Semantic Textual Similarity Benchmark (STS-B). It contains pairs of sentences annotated with human similarity scores (typically on a 0–5 scale) and is used to tune and evaluate models that predict semantic similarity, produce sentence embeddings, or detect paraphrases. Common evaluation metrics are Pearson and Spearman correlation, making this split useful for model selection and benchmarking transfer learning in sentence-level semantic tasks.

dataset_node: BERnaT base contrastive all 8 3ep␟Cross Encoder Reranking
desc: BERnaT base contrastive all 8 3ep is a pretraining dataset variant created for contrastive representation learning with the BERnaT base encoder. It aggregates data from eight source partitions and supplies paired positive and negative samples (augmented or mined) formatted for contrastive loss, prepared to be consumed in experiments run for three epochs. The collection is intended to train and evaluate dense embedding quality for retrieval, clustering, and downstream classification tasks.

dataset_node: BERnaT base contrastive all 4 3ep bueno␟Cross Encoder Reranking
desc: BERnaT base contrastive all 4 3ep bueno is a curated dataset for contrastive pretraining of the BERnaT base model. It aggregates balanced samples across four domains/classes and supplies precomputed augmented positive pairs and sampled negatives, along with standard train/validation/test splits and metadata. The package includes a recommended 3-epoch (“3ep bueno”) training protocol used for baseline evaluation. Designed for self-supervised contrastive learning and downstream tasks (linear evaluation, retrieval, clustering, transfer), it enables reproducible comparisons and fast experimentation of representation-learning approaches.

dataset_node: BERnaT base contrastive parl 4 1ep mle5␟Cross Encoder Reranking
desc: BERnaT base contrastive parl 4 1ep mle5 is a paraphrase-driven contrastive dataset derived from the BERnaT base corpus. Each example pairs a source sentence with up to four parallel paraphrases (parl 4); positives are drawn from the same paraphrase group and negatives are sampled across the batch. Candidate paraphrases were filtered by maximum‑likelihood ranking, keeping the top‑5 (mle5). The dataset is split into train/validation/test and formatted for quick one‑epoch fine‑tuning (1ep). It is intended for contrastive sentence representation learning, semantic retrieval, and paraphrase identification with BERT‑style encoders.

The collection emphasizes pose, scale and lighting variation across real and synthetic captures, making it suitable for training contrastive encoders for downstream tasks such as classification, retrieval and pose estimation. It is curated for fast prototyping workflows and commonly used with short pretraining runs.

The dataset is intended for learning robust sentence representations and evaluating contrastive objectives and efficient, low-epoch pretraining strategies for Basque-language downstream tasks.

desc: Jina Reranker v3 (contrastive parl 4, 1ep) is a training snapshot and data configuration for fine-tuning neural rerankers using contrastive learning on parallel query–passage groups. Each example groups a query with a labeled positive passage and multiple negatives (4-way parallel sampling), enabling contrastive loss-based learning of discriminative embeddings. The "1ep" denotes a single-epoch training snapshot, making this dataset useful for evaluating short-run fine-tuning behavior, ranking metrics (NDCG/MRR/prec@k), and the effectiveness of contrastive reranking in retrieval pipelines.

desc: jina reranker v3 contrastive berria 4 1ep is a contrastive training dataset for fine-tuning the Jina Reranker v3 on relevance ranking. The set represents a lightweight, single-epoch fine-tuning snapshot intended to evaluate and improve reranking performance on retrieval tasks in the Berria domain.

dataset_node: jina reranker v3 contrastive bopv 4 8b 1ep␟Cross Encoder Reranking
desc: Jina Reranker v3 Contrastive BOPV 4 8B 1ep is a curated training set for supervised contrastive reranking. It is organized as query–positive–negative triplets (and in-batch groups) with negatives sampled using the BOPV-4 strategy, and is optimized for training large-scale reranker models at the ~8B parameter scale under a single-epoch training regime. The dataset is tailored for contrastive losses and hard-negative evaluation, supporting development and benchmarking of neural rerankers, sampling-strategy ablations, and retrieval-oriented fine-tuning.

Custom BEIR is a tailored variant of the BEIR information-retrieval benchmark that combines selected corpora, queries, and relevance annotations to evaluate retrieval models across multiple domains. It provides standardized query-document pairs and relevance judgments for benchmarking both sparse and dense retrieval methods under zero-shot and fine-tuned settings, with common IR metrics (nDCG, MAP, recall). The dataset is intended to measure cross-domain generalization, robustness, and ranking effectiveness of retrieval and reranking models.

eval reranking is a benchmark dataset for evaluating and training re-ranking algorithms in information retrieval and recommendation. It contains queries (or sessions), candidate item lists produced by a first-stage ranker, per-item relevance labels or graded judgments, and optional auxiliary features (item/document features, query features, and click/interaction logs). The dataset supports pointwise, pairwise, and listwise learning-to-rank tasks as well as offline simulation of online metrics, enabling comparison of neural and classical re-rankers on ranking quality (NDCG, MAP, MRR) and click-aware objectives. It is intended for developing and benchmarking re-ranking models that refine initial candidate lists to improve relevance and user satisfaction.

mMARCO pt dev is the Portuguese development split of the multilingual MS MARCO passage-ranking dataset. It provides Portuguese queries paired with candidate passages and corresponding relevance judgments (derived from translated MS MARCO content), enabling supervised training and evaluation of passage retrieval, ranking, and re-ranking models in Portuguese. The set is intended for benchmarking retrieval effectiveness, tuning validation, and studying cross-lingual or language-specific IR model performance on realistic search tasks.

Reranker is a dataset for training and evaluating reranking models in information retrieval and NLP. It provides queries paired with candidate documents or passages, initial retrieval scores or ranked lists, and human relevance labels (binary or graded), often with auxiliary features or text pairs for model input. The dataset is intended to support supervised learning of pointwise/pairwise/listwise rerankers and benchmarking with ranking metrics such as nDCG, MRR, and MAP.

**CoNLL-2003** is a named entity recognition dataset released as a part of CoNLL-2003 shared task: language-independent named entity recognition. The data consists of eight files covering two languages: English and German. For each of the languages there is a training file, a development file, a test file and a large file with unannotated data. The English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus. This corpus consists of Reuters news stories between August 1996 and August 1997. For the training and development set, ten days worth of data were taken from the files representing the end of August 1996. For the test set, the texts were from December 1996. The preprocessed raw data covers the month of September 1996. The text for the German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus. This corpus consists of texts in many languages. The portion of data that was used for this task, was extracted from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundshau. All three of the training, development and test sets were taken from articles written in one week at the end of August 1992. IndoNLU is a benchmark suite for Indonesian natural language understanding that aggregates multiple annotated datasets across tasks such as sentiment and topic classification, hate-speech detection, named entity recognition, POS tagging, paraphrase/pairwise classification, and machine reading comprehension. It provides standardized splits and evaluation protocols to train, fine-tune, and compare pretrained language models and downstream systems in Indonesian. The benchmark enables consistent assessment of model performance and advances in Indonesian NLP applications.

Acronym Identification is a labeled corpus for detecting acronyms in text and linking them to their long-form expansions. Each example contains contextual sentences or document passages with annotated acronym spans and corresponding full forms (when available), enabling supervised learning for span detection, expansion extraction, and disambiguation. The dataset captures ambiguous acronyms across varied domains and contexts, supporting evaluation of models for abbreviation resolution, named-entity-style identification, and downstream information-extraction tasks in scientific, biomedical, and technical texts.

LeNER-Br is a specialized dataset designed for Named Entity Recognition (NER) in Brazilian legal texts. It focuses on extracting and classifying entities within the legal domain, including common categories such as persons, locations, organizations, and temporal expressions, as well as domain-specific entities like laws and legal cases. The dataset is composed entirely of Portuguese-language legal documents, which distinguishes it from other general Portuguese NER datasets by providing a targeted resource for legal information extraction. LeNER-Br supports the development and evaluation of NER models tailored to the complexities of legal language, which often involves specialized terminology and entity types. Baseline experiments using models such as LSTM-CRF have demonstrated strong performance, achieving high F1 scores particularly for legislation and legal case entities, indicating the dataset’s suitability for advancing automated legal document analysis. By enabling accurate identification of legal entities, LeNER-Br facilitates improved information retrieval, decision-making

WikiANN is a large-scale multilingual named entity recognition dataset created via distant supervision from Wikipedia/Wikidata. It provides token-level BIO annotations for three coarse entity types (PER, LOC, ORG) across hundreds of languages (commonly used with 282 languages). WikiANN is widely used to train and evaluate multilingual and cross-lingual NER models and zero-shot transfer, with the caveat that annotations are automatically generated and therefore noisy.

OntoNotes 5.0 (tner/ontonotes5) is a large, manually annotated corpus commonly used for token-level named entity recognition. It provides entity labels (e.g., PERSON, ORG, GPE, LOCATION, DATE, etc.) aligned with rich linguistic annotations (syntax, propositions, coreference), and spans multiple genres such as newswire, broadcast, web, and conversational text. The dataset is a standard supervised benchmark for NER, domain- and genre-generalization studies, and for research that leverages multi-layer annotations to improve entity recognition.

dataset_node: FewNERD, CoNLL2003, and OntoNotes v5␟Named Entity Recognition
desc: FewNERD, CoNLL2003, and OntoNotes v5 are standard named-entity recognition (NER) benchmarks spanning few-shot, benchmark, and large-scale multi-genre settings. FewNERD is a few-shot NER dataset with fine-grained entity types and episode-style splits designed to evaluate low-resource and meta-learning approaches. CoNLL2003 is a widely used newswire NER benchmark (PER, LOC, ORG, MISC) in IOB format for supervised sequence labeling and model comparison. OntoNotes v5 is a large, multi-genre corpus annotated with a broader set of entity types (used in NER, coreference, and related tasks), supporting high-resource training and cross-domain evaluation.

JNLPBA is a biomedical named entity recognition dataset derived from the GENIA corpus. It consists of annotated MEDLINE abstracts focusing on five entity types relevant to biomedical text mining, including proteins, DNA, RNA, cell types, and cell lines. The dataset is widely used for evaluating machine learning models in biomedical named entity recognition tasks.

generator is a synthetic benchmark dataset of samples produced by one or more generative models, containing generated outputs paired with their latent codes, conditioning inputs, and model metadata. It is designed to evaluate and train generative modeling tasks—such as image/audio/text synthesis, controllability, inversion, and quality/diversity metrics—and supports research on model comparison, robustness, and detection of synthetic content.

lextreme is a multilingual benchmark for lexical complexity and simplification tasks. It provides sentences with highlighted target words annotated with complexity judgments and human-proposed simpler substitutes across multiple languages and domains. The dataset is intended to evaluate and train models for word-level difficulty prediction, lexical simplification (substitution/generation), and cross-lingual readability improvements.

FewNERD is a large-scale few-shot named entity recognition benchmark containing sentences annotated with fine-grained, hierarchically organized entity types. It is designed for N-way K-shot evaluation and meta-learning research, providing episode-based train/validation/test splits that test models’ ability to generalize to unseen entity categories from few examples. FewNERD supports investigation of few-shot transfer, hierarchical type modeling, and robustness of NER systems in low-resource regimes.

FewNERD (fine-grained, supervised) is a few-shot named entity recognition benchmark that provides token-level, human-annotated sentences labeled with a hierarchical, fine-grained ontology of entity types. Organized into supervised train/validation/test splits and few-shot evaluation episodes, it is designed to train and evaluate meta-learning and few-shot NER models on entity detection and fine-grained classification with limited examples per class. The dataset stresses generalization to rare and closely related entity categories, supporting research on transfer learning, label granularity, and robust NER under low-resource conditions.

root_b: grit id id nergrit corpus ner
desc: id_nergrit_corpus ner is an Indonesian named-entity recognition (NER) dataset from the GRIT collection, consisting of Indonesian sentences annotated at the token level for entity recognition. Annotations use a common sequence-labeling scheme (e.g., BIO) and cover standard entity types such as person, location, organization, and miscellaneous. The corpus is designed for training and evaluating supervised NER models and benchmarking sequence-labeling performance in Indonesian, with tokenized/labelled data and standard splits to support reproducible experiments.

dataset_node: Open PII Masking 500K␟PII Masking and Classification
desc: Open PII Masking 500K is a large-scale dataset of 500,000 text examples annotated for personally identifiable information (PII) detection and redaction. Each example contains labeled PII spans (e.g., names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, IDs, dates) alongside corresponding masked or redacted versions, making it suitable for training and evaluating span-detection, named-entity recognition, and automated de-identification models. The collection spans diverse domains (emails, chat logs, forms, clinical and customer-support text) with both real-world and synthetic samples to improve robustness. It is designed to benchmark PII masking performance and support development of privacy-preserving NLP systems.

OCR is inevitably linked to NLP since its final output is in text. Advances in document intelligence are driving the need for a unified technology that integrates OCR with various NLP tasks, especially semantic parsing. Since OCR and semantic parsing have been studied as separate tasks so far, the datasets for each task on their own are rich, while those for the integrated post-OCR parsing tasks are relatively insufficient. In this study, we publish a consolidated dataset for receipt parsing as the first step towards post-OCR parsing tasks. The dataset consists of thousands of Indonesian receipts, which contains images and box/text annotations for OCR, and multi-level semantic labels for parsing. The proposed dataset can be used to address various OCR and parsing tasks.

Corpus-Carolina is a curated Portuguese-language text corpus released by C4AI, aggregating diverse written content (news, web pages, books and public-domain texts) that has been cleaned and deduplicated for NLP use. It provides raw text and basic metadata to support language-model pretraining, tokenizer training, and downstream tasks such as classification, generation and retrieval, serving as a benchmark and resource for Portuguese-language model development and evaluation.

Invoice is a dataset of scanned and photographed invoices paired with structured annotations to support document understanding and information extraction. It includes diverse layouts, languages and imaging artifacts, with token-level transcriptions, bounding boxes, table structure labels, and key–value annotations for fields such as invoice number, dates, vendor, line items and totals. Designed for training and evaluating OCR, key‑value extraction, table parsing and layout analysis models, it facilitates development of robust end-to-end systems for automated data entry, accounts-payable automation and financial document analysis.

CoNLL03 is a widely used benchmark dataset in named entity recognition (NER) for natural language processing. It consists of annotated text corpora in English, primarily derived from news articles, with entities labeled into categories such as person names (PER), organizations (ORG), and locations (LOC), using the BIO tagging scheme. The dataset provides structured annotations that enable evaluation of sequence labeling models, particularly in identifying the beginning (B) and continuation (I) of named entities, with "O" denoting non-entity tokens. With a moderate scale and diverse domain coverage, CoNLL03 is designed to assess the performance of NER models in real-world text scenarios. Its well-established annotation standards and availability in both training and test splits make it a foundational resource for developing and benchmarking supervised NER systems. Due to its clarity and consistency, CoNLL03 has been extensively used

OntoNotes v5.0 is a large-scale, manually annotated multilingual corpus (English, Chinese, Arabic) covering ~1.6M words across multiple genres (newswire, broadcast, conversational, weblogs, etc.). It provides layered annotations including tokenization/POS, syntactic constituency trees, PropBank-style predicate-argument (semantic role) labels, word-sense annotations, named-entity tags, and coreference chains. Commonly used as a standard benchmark with predefined train/dev/test splits for training and evaluating NER, coreference resolution, semantic role labeling, parsing, and word-sense disambiguation.

id_nergrit_corpus is an Indonesian named‑entity recognition corpus containing manually annotated text with span-level entity labels (e.g., PER, LOC, ORG, MISC). It provides token- and phrase-level annotations in standard sequence-labeling formats (BIO/BILOU), enabling supervised training and evaluation of NER models. The corpus covers diverse Indonesian text sources and is intended as a benchmark for entity extraction, model comparison, and downstream tasks that require reliable named-entity identification in Indonesian.

CoNLL 2003 (English) is a widely used benchmark dataset for Named Entity Recognition (NER) in natural language processing. It consists of annotated text corpora in English, with entities labeled into categories such as persons, organizations, and locations using the BIO tagging scheme. The dataset provides structured annotations that enable models to learn entity boundaries and context-aware classification. With a moderate scale and diverse domain coverage, it serves as a standard for evaluating sequence labeling models in NLP. The annotations are derived from real-world text, including news articles, and reflect the challenges of real-world entity identification, such as overlapping entities and ambiguous context. Due to its well-established format and widespread use in research, CoNLL 2003 has been instrumental in advancing semi-supervised and multitask learning approaches for sequence labeling. It is particularly valuable for training and benchmarking models that leverage contextual information

CoNLL 2002 (Spanish) is a named entity recognition (NER) dataset focused on identifying and classifying entities such as persons, organizations, and locations in Spanish text. It consists of annotated sentences from diverse domains, structured using the BIO tagging scheme to denote the beginning (B) and interior (I) of entities, with O indicating non-entity tokens. The dataset is part of a broader benchmark for NER tasks and is commonly used to evaluate models’ ability to recognize entities in real-world text. While originally designed for single-sentence input, recent studies have explored its use in cross-sentence contexts, where additional sentences are incorporated to capture long-range dependencies, leading to improved performance. The Spanish version presents linguistic challenges due to its morphological complexity and contextual ambiguity, making it a valuable resource for evaluating multilingual NER models. This dataset has been widely used in research on

GermEval 2014 is a German-language benchmark dataset from the GermEval 2014 shared task for named entity recognition and classification. It contains manually annotated sentences with entity spans labeled into coarse categories (person, location, organization, other) using token-level IOB-style annotations and published train/dev/test splits. The dataset is used to train and evaluate sequence-labeling and information-extraction models for German-language NER and to compare model performance on real-world German texts.

gyr66/privacy_detection is a labeled image dataset for detecting privacy-sensitive content in everyday scenes. It provides bounding-box and class annotations (e.g., faces, license plates, phone/tablet screens, printed documents) across diverse indoor and outdoor images to support supervised object-detection and redaction tasks. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating privacy-preservation pipelines such as automatic face/license-plate blurring, screen/document masking, and on-device sensitive-region detection to enable compliant data-sharing and anonymization.

FUNSD-LayoutLMv3 is a preprocessed version of the FUNSD form-understanding dataset formatted for LayoutLMv3-style multimodal training. It pairs scanned form images with OCR-extracted tokens, token-level bounding boxes, semantic entity labels (e.g., question, answer, header, other) and relation/grouping annotations, enabling supervised learning and evaluation of document understanding tasks. The dataset supports semantic entity recognition, key–value/relation extraction, and layout-aware multimodal models that combine visual, textual and spatial features for form parsing and information extraction.

KLUE (Korean Language Understanding Evaluation) is a multi-task benchmark suite for Korean natural language processing that provides human-annotated datasets across core tasks such as classification, inference, named-entity recognition, semantic similarity, and question answering. It standardizes training and evaluation splits and metrics to enable fair comparison of Korean language models and encourage development of architectures and pretraining strategies tailored to Korean. KLUE is widely used for benchmarking model performance, error analysis, and advancing research in Korean NLP.

doc_lay_net-small is a compact subset of the DocLayNet benchmark for document layout analysis. It comprises scanned and digital page images annotated with semantic layout elements (e.g., headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, figures, captions) provided as bounding boxes and segmentation masks. Designed for quick prototyping and lightweight training/evaluation, this small split preserves layout diversity of the full dataset while reducing scale for faster experiments and ablation studies.

DaNE is a dataset for Danish named-entity recognition consisting of manually annotated Danish text with token-level entity labels. It provides span annotations for common entity types (e.g., PERSON, LOCATION, ORGANIZATION, MISC) in a BIO-style format, enabling supervised training and evaluation of NER models in Danish. DaNE supports research on language-specific NER, cross-lingual transfer, and downstream tasks such as entity linking and information extraction, serving as a standard benchmark for Danish NER systems.

CNEC is a labeled corpus for Chinese named-entity recognition and classification, consisting of sentences from news and web sources annotated with entity spans and fine-grained type labels. It provides standard train/validation/test splits to support supervised learning and evaluation of sequence-labeling models, and is useful for training NER, entity linking, relation extraction, and other information-extraction systems that require robust handling of domain and annotation variability.

MedNERF is a medical imaging benchmark for neural radiance field and view-synthesis research. It provides paired multi-view 2D clinical images (e.g., radiographs) with registered 3D volumetric scans (CT/MRI) and camera pose/registration metadata to enable supervised learning of 3D reconstruction and novel-view synthesis from sparse projections. The dataset supports training and evaluation of NeRF-style models for volumetric reconstruction, novel-view rendering, medical visualization, and downstream tasks such as segmentation and diagnostic image enhancement.

contratos_tceal is a corpus of public administrative and procurement contracts published by the Tribunal de Contas do Estado de Alagoas (TCE-AL), provided in Portuguese with document text and associated metadata (e.g., contracting parties, dates, contract values, object descriptions, identifiers). It is designed for legal and administrative NLP tasks such as document classification, named-entity and key‑value extraction (parties, amounts, dates), clause detection, OCR post‑processing, and anomaly/fraud detection in public procurement. The dataset enables development and benchmarking of models for Portuguese contract understanding, information retrieval, and transparency/audit analyses.

BC5CDR is a biomedical named entity recognition (NER) dataset comprising 1,500 PubMed articles annotated with 4,409 chemical entities, 5,818 disease entities, and 3,116 chemical-disease interactions. The dataset is designed to support the extraction and classification of domain-specific entities within unstructured biomedical text, facilitating structured information retrieval in the biomedical domain. Annotations follow standard NER conventions, typically using BIO notation to distinguish entity boundaries. Due to its focus on chemicals, diseases, and their interactions, BC5CDR presents challenges related to entity diversity, domain-specific terminology, and imbalanced class distributions. It has been widely used to evaluate and develop NER models, particularly those leveraging deep learning and pre-trained language models, as well as active learning strategies to reduce annotation costs. BC5CDR serves as a benchmark for advancing biomedical information extraction, enabling improved automated

Open PII Masking 500K is a large-scale dataset of 500,000 text examples annotated for personally identifiable information (PII) detection and redaction. Each example contains labeled PII spans (e.g., names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, IDs, dates) alongside corresponding masked or redacted versions, making it suitable for training and evaluating span-detection, named-entity recognition, and automated de-identification models. The collection spans diverse domains (emails, chat logs, forms, clinical and customer-support text) with both real-world and synthetic samples to improve robustness. It is designed to benchmark PII masking performance and support development of privacy-preserving NLP systems.

lst20 is a compact benchmark dataset of 20 carefully annotated samples/sequences with corresponding ground-truth labels. It is designed for supervised training and evaluation of models in tasks that require per-sample annotations (e.g., segmentation, tracking, or restoration), emphasizing realistic variability and limited-data generalization. lst20 enables reproducible comparison of accuracy, robustness and data-efficiency for methods targeting constrained-data scenarios.

coarsegrained, supervised FewNERD is a supervised few-shot NER benchmark derived from the FewNERD corpus using its coarse-grained label set. It consists of sentences annotated with entity mentions labeled into a small number of coarse categories (e.g., person, location, organization, etc.), with predefined train/validation/test splits and an episode-based k-shot N-way evaluation protocol. The dataset is intended to evaluate and train models on generalization to novel entity types with limited labeled examples, supporting both episodic meta-learning and conventional supervised fine-tuning for few-shot named entity recognition.

GermEval 2014 is a German-language Twitter sentiment analysis dataset released for the GermEval shared task. It comprises German tweets annotated for sentiment polarity (e.g., positive, negative, neutral/ambiguous) with standard train/dev/test splits. The dataset is intended for supervised learning and evaluation of sentiment classification and opinion-mining models on noisy, informal social-media text, testing robustness to colloquial language, hashtags, emojis and domain-specific expressions.

source_data_nlp is a large-scale, cleaned and anonymized text corpus compiled from diverse public sources (news, web pages, forums, social media, books, and Wikipedia). It provides raw and preprocessed variants (sentence-split, tokenized, deduplicated) with document-level metadata and standard train/validation/test splits. Designed for pretraining and downstream evaluation of NLP models, it supports language modeling, text classification, named-entity recognition, question answering, summarization, and retrieval tasks. Data has been filtered for quality and PII, and source attributions or licensing info are preserved when available.

DocLayNet-large is a large-scale dataset for document layout analysis that provides scanned and digital document images annotated with pixel-level masks and polygonal regions for multiple layout element classes (e.g., text blocks, titles, lists, tables, figures, headers/footers). It is designed to train and evaluate supervised models for semantic segmentation, layout detection, and OCR preprocessing across diverse document genres and complex page structures, enabling development of robust layout understanding and downstream information-extraction systems.

NCBI-disease is a named entity recognition (NER) dataset focused on identifying and classifying disease-related entities in biomedical text. It consists of annotated clinical and scientific documents, with entities labeled in categories such as diseases, symptoms, and conditions using the BIO tagging scheme. The dataset is derived from the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) and reflects the domain-specific terminology and complexity of medical language. Designed for training and evaluating NER models in biomedical NLP, it supports downstream applications like clinical information extraction and knowledge graph construction. Its rich entity diversity and domain-specific language make it particularly valuable for developing robust, context-aware NER systems. Recent work has leveraged large language models (LLMs) to generate high-quality annotations, enabling efficient pretraining of task-specific models like NuNER, which achieves strong performance in few-shot settings. The dataset highlights the importance of both scale and entity-type

ls-generated4 is a synthetic dataset of paired inputs and ground-truth targets produced by a programmable generator to support supervised learning for image restoration and image-to-image translation tasks. It contains diverse, automatically rendered scenes with controlled variations in lighting, noise, blur, and semantic content, along with per-sample metadata and train/validation/test splits. The dataset is intended to accelerate model development and benchmarking by providing large-scale, perfectly aligned pairs that enable reproducible training, evaluation, and domain-adaptation studies from synthetic to real data.

merged is a consolidated benchmark that unifies samples and annotations from multiple public datasets into a single, standardized collection. By increasing scale and diversity across domains, classes, and capture conditions, it supports training and evaluation of supervised models and facilitates transfer learning, domain generalization, and robustness studies. The dataset provides consistent formats and predefined splits to simplify benchmarking and comparison across methods.

merged is a consolidated benchmark that unifies samples and annotations from multiple public datasets into a single, standardized collection. By increasing scale and diversity across domains, classes, and capture conditions, it supports training and evaluation of supervised models and facilitates transfer learning, domain generalization, and robustness studies. The dataset provides consistent formats and predefined splits to simplify benchmarking and comparison across methods.

tner/mit_movie_trivia is a movie-domain trivia dataset containing question–answer pairs about films, with associated metadata (e.g., film title, category, and contextual fields when available). It is intended for training and evaluating question answering, knowledge extraction, and retrieval models focused on factual movie knowledge and commonsense reasoning about cinematic topics.

desc: WNUT-17 (Emerging and Rare Entities) is a named entity recognition dataset of noisy user-generated text (Twitter/social media) collected for the WNUT 2017 shared task. It contains token-level annotations (BIO-style) for emerging and rare entities, covering categories such as person, location, organization/corporation, product, creative work and group. Designed to benchmark NER systems on informal language, misspellings, novel surface forms and unseen entities, WNUT-17 is commonly used to develop and evaluate models that must generalize to low-resource and rapidly changing entity distributions.

WikiLingua is a large-scale multilingual abstractive summarization dataset built from WikiHow articles, providing aligned article–summary pairs across multiple languages (including English). Each example pairs procedural/how-to content with a concise abstractive summary, and the dataset includes parallel cross-lingual splits to support monolingual, cross-lingual and multilingual summarization research. WikiLingua is useful for training and evaluating abstractive summarizers, studying transfer and low-resource performance, and benchmarking models on multilingual and cross-lingual summarization tasks.

Citilink-Minutes is a corpus of meeting records consisting of raw audio, time-aligned transcripts, human-written minutes, speaker labels, timestamps, and annotated action items/topics. It is designed to support supervised learning and evaluation for meeting summarization (extractive and abstractive), key‑information and action‑item extraction, agenda/topic segmentation, and multi‑speaker diarization. The dataset captures realistic conversational structure and speech variability to benchmark robustness of summarization and information‑extraction systems in multi‑participant meeting scenarios.

sucx3_ner is a token-level named-entity recognition dataset built from the SUC family of Swedish corpora, annotated in three complementary passes to produce BIO-style entity labels (e.g., PER, ORG, LOC, MISC). It spans multiple genres (news, web, discussion) to support robust supervised training and cross-domain evaluation of sequence-labeling models. Distributed in common CoNLL/BIO formats with standard splits, sucx3_ner is intended for benchmarking NER performance using precision/recall/F1 metrics and for experiments in transfer and domain adaptation for Swedish.

RCC-MSU/collection3 is a curated benchmark dataset from Michigan State University containing real-world samples with expert annotations for supervised machine learning. Provided with standardized train/validation/test splits and accompanying metadata, it supports development and evaluation of models for tasks such as classification, detection, and segmentation within the target application domain. The collection is intended to facilitate reproducible research and comparative benchmarking across architectures and training procedures.

SecretMask v2 is a benchmark dataset for evaluating privacy-preserving and mask-handling algorithms on face and object imagery. It contains 600 test examples of images with diverse, realistic occlusion masks (both synthetic and captured) paired with pixel-level mask annotations and original unmasked ground truth where available. The dataset is suited for tasks such as mask detection/segmentation, masked-face recognition, mask removal/inpainting, and robustness testing of downstream vision models under anonymization. SecretMask v2 emphasizes varied lighting, poses, and demographic diversity to assess generalization of privacy and reconstruction methods.

Azerbaijani NER Dataset is a sentence-level corpus of Azerbaijani text with manually annotated entity spans and category labels (e.g., PERSON, LOCATION, ORGANIZATION, MISC). It is intended for training and evaluating sequence-labeling models for named entity recognition, benchmarking NER performance in a low-resource language, and supporting multilingual and cross-lingual transfer experiments. The data are provided in standard token-label formats suitable for supervised learning and evaluation.

mim_gold_ner is a gold‑standard named entity recognition dataset containing manually curated entity span annotations and type labels over texts from the MIM collection. It provides token- and span-level labels (standard entity categories such as PERSON, ORGANIZATION, LOCATION, plus any domain-specific types present) formatted for supervised NER training and evaluation. With high-quality annotations, mim_gold_ner is suitable for benchmarking NER models, conducting error analysis, and supporting transfer-learning or domain-adaptation experiments.

Rodrigo1771/symptemist-ner is a named-entity recognition dataset focused on symptom and related clinical entity mentions from patient-facing or clinical texts. It contains span-level annotations with entity labels for symptoms and contextual attributes (e.g., severity, duration), enabling supervised training and evaluation of NER models. The dataset is suitable for building and benchmarking symptom extraction systems, clinical information retrieval, and downstream tasks such as symptom normalization and clinical decision support in medical NLP.

turkish_ner is a Turkish-language named entity recognition dataset providing token-level annotations for common entity types (e.g., PERSON, LOCATION, ORGANIZATION, MISC) using a scheme such as BIO. It contains sentence-segmented Turkish text with gold-standard entity spans, suitable for training and evaluating sequence-labeling models. The corpus is intended for supervised NER, benchmarking model performance, and research in Turkish NLP, cross-lingual transfer, and domain adaptation.

Beijuka/Luganda_Monolingual_PII_dataset is a Luganda-language corpus annotated for personally identifiable information (PII). It provides monolingual text samples with span-level labels for common PII categories (e.g., person names, locations, organizations, dates, numeric identifiers, phone numbers, emails, and addresses), enabling supervised training and evaluation of PII detection and de-identification systems in Luganda. The dataset is suited for NER-style model development, privacy-preserving NLP, and compliance-focused tools for low-resource language settings.

bc4chemd_ner is a benchmark corpus for chemical named entity recognition that contains biomedical text (e.g., PubMed abstracts) annotated with span-level chemical entity mentions. It provides labeled examples and standard splits for training and evaluating supervised NER models in the chemical/biomedical domain, supporting tasks such as chemical mention detection, entity linking, and information extraction.

PAN-X is a multilingual token-classification dataset for named entity recognition that provides sentence-level annotations of entity spans across multiple languages. It is designed to support research in cross-lingual transfer and multilingual representation learning by offering aligned, human-annotated NER examples that enable training and evaluation of models on diverse language typologies. PAN-X facilitates benchmarking of zero-shot and few-shot transfer, robustness of multilingual encoders, and development of language-agnostic entity extraction systems.

surrey-nlp/PLOD-filtered is a cleaned, quality-filtered subset of the PLOD corpus curated for natural language processing research. The release provides preprocessed text entries and accompanying metadata after removing noisy, low-quality, or irrelevant records, making it better suited for training and evaluation of language models and downstream tasks (e.g., classification, retrieval, summarization). By reducing noise and standardizing formatting, the dataset aims to improve reproducibility and model performance while retaining the original corpus’s topical coverage.

wl is a curated benchmark dataset of real-world images with image-level labels and region-level annotations intended for supervised computer vision research. It emphasizes diversity across scenes, lighting conditions, and object scales to evaluate model robustness and generalization on tasks such as classification, detection, and segmentation. wl is designed for training and comparative evaluation of architectures and algorithms using standard metrics.

ConLL-2002 is a benchmark dataset for named entity recognition (NER) released for the CoNLL-2002 shared task. It contains manually annotated Spanish and Dutch newswire text with four entity types (PER, LOC, ORG, MISC) labeled in the BIO/IOB format and is split into training, development, and test sets. The dataset is widely used for supervised sequence-labeling experiments, cross-lingual NER research, and evaluation of models on token-level entity identification and segmentation.

ViHOS is a video-based human–object segmentation dataset that provides temporally annotated frames with pixel-level instance masks and interaction labels for hands/people and manipulated objects. It is designed to support supervised training and evaluation of segmentation, detection, tracking, and hand–object interaction models in dynamic, occluded, and real-world scenes, enabling research on robust perception of person–object interactions in video.

PLOD-unfiltered is the unfiltered release of the PLOD corpus from Surrey NLP: a large-scale, raw text collection aggregated from diverse web and document sources for language-model pretraining and NLP research. It preserves original formatting and noise (duplications, HTML artifacts, OCR errors, etc.), making it suitable for studying the effects of noisy training data, data filtering and cleaning methods, robustness and domain generalization, and large-scale self-supervised training. Researchers can use it to evaluate preprocessing pipelines, denoising algorithms, and the impact of unfiltered corpora on model bias and downstream task performance.

samirmsallem/wiki_def_de_multitask is a German-language multitask dataset derived from German Wikipedia, containing article titles paired with concise definition texts, contextual sentences, and auxiliary annotations formatted for multiple supervision objectives. It is designed to train and evaluate models on tasks such as definition generation, definition selection/ranking, and context-conditioned definition understanding in German. The dataset supports multitask training regimes for lexical-semantic modeling, dictionary-style generation, and downstream applications like QA or lexical simplification in German.

udpos28 is a multilingual part-of-speech tagging dataset derived from Universal Dependencies v2.8. It provides token-level UPOS annotations across many languages with standard train/dev/test splits, and includes accompanying lemma and morphological feature fields where available. Designed for supervised sequence labeling and cross-lingual transfer research, it serves as a benchmark for training and evaluating POS taggers and multilingual representations.

ConLL-2002 is a benchmark dataset for named entity recognition (NER) released for the CoNLL-2002 shared task. It contains manually annotated Spanish and Dutch newswire text with four entity types (PER, LOC, ORG, MISC) labeled in the BIO/IOB format and is split into training, development, and test sets. The dataset is widely used for supervised sequence-labeling experiments, cross-lingual NER research, and evaluation of models on token-level entity identification and segmentation.

token_classification_v2 is a token-level sequence labeling dataset for training and evaluating models on tasks such as named entity recognition, part-of-speech tagging, and chunking. It provides tokenized text sequences with per-token annotations (commonly encoded in BIO/BILOU-style schemes), standard train/validation/test splits, and label mappings for span reconstruction. The dataset is prepared to work with modern tokenizers and subword alignment strategies, enabling supervised learning and benchmarking of token classification models using metrics like token-level/ entity-level precision, recall, and F1.

disease is a curated medical dataset of de-identified clinical samples paired with ground-truth disease labels, combining modalities such as medical images, laboratory results, and/or structured electronic health-record features. It is designed for supervised learning tasks including disease classification, localization/segmentation, and prognostic risk prediction. The dataset enables benchmarking of diagnostic accuracy, robustness, calibration, and generalization across patient subgroups, and supports development of models for early detection, differential diagnosis, and outcome stratification. Data use is governed by privacy and consent constraints to ensure compliance with clinical and ethical standards.

This shared task focuses on identifying unusual, previously-unseen entities in the context of emerging discussions. Named entities form the basis of many modern approaches to other tasks (like event clustering and summarisation), but recall on them is a real problem in noisy text - even among annotators. This drop tends to be due to novel entities and surface forms. Take for example the tweet “so.. kktny in 30 mins?” - even human experts find entity kktny hard to detect and resolve. This task will evaluate the ability to detect and classify novel, emerging, singleton named entities in noisy text. The goal of this task is to provide a definition of emerging and of rare entities, and based on that, also datasets for detecting these entities.

The ICPR 2022 CHART Competition dataset is a benchmark collection of chart and plot images (e.g., bar, line, pie, scatter) with rich ground-truth annotations—chart type labels, element-level bounding boxes (axes, legends, labels, ticks, series, markers), text transcriptions, and corresponding data values where available. It combines synthetic and real-world visualizations to support tasks such as chart classification, element detection/segmentation, text recognition, and end-to-end data extraction. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating algorithms that convert visual charts into structured, machine-readable representations.

EconBiz is a corpus of bibliographic records harvested from the EconBiz academic search portal, covering economics and business literature. Records include metadata such as titles, abstracts/descriptions, authors, publication year, subjects/keywords, publishers and identifiers, often in German and English. The dataset is suited for information retrieval and ranking, topic or genre classification, metadata enrichment, recommendation, entity linking and other scholarly NLP tasks, providing a domain-specific benchmark for models operating on academic and economic text.

CHIME-R is a speech dataset focused on reverberation and robust automatic speech recognition. It provides simulated and real reverberant multi-microphone recordings derived from clean utterances convolved with room impulse responses (and often combined with noise), together with corresponding clean references. CHIME-R is intended for training and evaluating speech enhancement, dereverberation, beamforming, and ASR systems under realistic room acoustics and multi-channel recording conditions.

finer-139 is a fine-grained visual recognition benchmark containing 139 closely related object categories. It provides curated images with per-instance class labels and instance-level annotations (e.g., bounding boxes and part/attribute labels) to support training and evaluation of classification, localization, and retrieval models. Designed to challenge models with subtle inter-class differences and strong intra-class variation, finer-139 is suited for developing and benchmarking fine-grained recognition, metric learning, and attention-based architectures.

german-ler is a German-language dataset of sentence and phrase pairs annotated for lexical entailment relations (e.g., entails / contradicts / neutral). It provides human-labeled examples for training and evaluating models on lexical semantic inference, paraphrase/contradiction detection, and related NLI tasks in German, making it suitable for benchmarking representation learning and fine-tuning multilingual or language-specific models.

PAN-X.es is the Spanish subset of the PAN-X multilingual named entity recognition dataset used in the XTREME benchmark. It provides tokenized sentences with token-level BIO annotations for common entity types (PER, LOC, ORG, MISC), organized into predefined train/validation/test splits and sourced from Wikipedia. The set is intended for training and evaluating NER models and for studying cross-lingual transfer and multilingual encoder performance on sequence labeling tasks.

HiNER Original is a human-annotated named entity recognition (NER) dataset containing diverse-domain texts labeled at token level with standard BIO-style entity spans and multiple common entity classes (e.g., PER, ORG, LOC). It provides train/validation/test splits and consistent annotation guidelines to support supervised training and benchmarking of sequence-labeling models. HiNER Original is intended for evaluating model accuracy, generalization across domains and text styles, and research on transfer learning and domain adaptation in NER.

jxner is a token-level named entity recognition (NER) dataset compiled from mixed-domain text (news and user-generated content) and annotated with fine-grained entity categories such as PERSON, ORGANIZATION, LOCATION, PRODUCT, DATE/TIME, EVENT and MISC. Annotations follow a BIO tagging scheme with standardized train/validation/test splits. Designed to support supervised sequence-labeling and transfer-learning research, jxner emphasizes realistic challenges—informal language, ambiguous boundaries, and varied mention forms—making it suitable for benchmarking NER model robustness and domain adaptation.

wildreceipt is a real-world receipt image dataset for robust document analysis and OCR. It contains photographs of receipts captured in varied conditions (lighting, perspective, folds, blur, cluttered backgrounds) with annotations for receipt detection, text line/word localization, and transcriptions suitable for end-to-end recognition and layout analysis. Designed to train and evaluate models for receipt detection, text recognition, and information extraction in unconstrained mobile-capture scenarios, wildreceipt emphasizes robustness to distortion and diverse formatting common in practical receipt-processing applications.

BioNLP2004 is a curated biomedical text corpus from the BioNLP 2004 workshop containing sentences and abstracts annotated with domain-specific entities (e.g., genes/proteins) and their relationships/interactions. It is designed for supervised training and evaluation of biomedical information extraction tasks such as named entity recognition, relation and interaction extraction, and event detection. The dataset enables development and benchmarking of NLP models that must handle specialized vocabulary, complex syntactic constructs, and domain-specific annotation schemes common in biomedical literature.

hi_ner-original is a Hindi named‑entity recognition dataset comprising Hindi sentences annotated with entity spans and labels (e.g., PERSON, LOCATION, ORGANIZATION, MISC) at the token level in Devanagari script. It is intended for supervised training and evaluation of sequence‑labeling models and supports research in Hindi NER, cross‑lingual transfer, and handling language‑specific morphology and script features. The dataset serves as a benchmark for developing and comparing named‑entity extraction systems for Hindi.

tner/ttc is a token-level named entity recognition (NER) dataset containing text sequences annotated with entity spans and class labels in the TNER annotation format. It provides pre-split examples for training, validation, and testing, enabling supervised learning and benchmarking of sequence-labeling models (e.g., CRF, BiLSTM-CRF, Transformer token classifiers). The dataset is suitable for research in NER, entity extraction, and evaluation of model generalization and domain adaptation.

favsbot is a dataset of social "favorite"/like interactions collected from an online platform, pairing posts (text and optional media) with user profiles, timestamps, and interaction metadata. It includes curated labels indicating automated (bot) vs. genuine accounts, session-level sequences, and derived relational features (follow/friend graphs, interaction rates). Designed for supervised and temporal tasks—bot detection, engagement prediction, recommendation, and anomaly detection—favsbot supports evaluation of models that exploit behavioral, temporal, and network patterns under realistic, imbalanced distributions with predefined train/validation/test splits.

cord-layoutlmv3 is a processed version of the CORD receipt dataset formatted for LayoutLMv3-style multimodal models. It pairs receipt images with OCR tokens, token bounding boxes, and token-level/segment-level semantic labels (merchant, totals, line items, dates, etc.), and includes visual features compatible with layout-aware transformers. The dataset is intended for supervised training and evaluation of document understanding tasks such as key-value extraction, semantic labeling, and end-to-end information extraction from receipts using combined text, layout, and image cues.

mp-02/cord-sroie is a receipts OCR and information-extraction dataset that combines the CORD and SROIE collections. It contains photographed and scanned retail receipts with dense annotations: word- and line-level bounding boxes, transcriptions, and structured key‑value labels (e.g., merchant, date, total, item lines). The dataset is suited for training and evaluating text detection, recognition, layout analysis, and end-to-end key‑value extraction models for real-world receipt understanding.

username170904/datasaur-MjU0NTk3M2U-MDY0YTNiMjE is an annotation dataset exported from the Datasaur platform containing human-labeled text examples and associated annotation metadata. It includes labeled documents and span-level or document-level labels (stored in common export formats such as JSON/CSV) together with the annotation schema and reviewer/workflow information. The dataset is intended for supervised training and evaluation of NLP tasks such as classification, named entity recognition, and sequence labeling, and for reproducing or extending the original annotation work.

KenCorpus (Dholuo) is a curated corpus of Dholuo (Luo) language text assembled to support NLP research and language technology development. It provides cleaned, domain-diverse Dholuo text (with aligned bilingual segments where available) for training and evaluating language models, machine translation, and other downstream tasks such as POS tagging and text classification. Designed for low-resource language work, KenCorpus facilitates development, benchmarking, and preservation of Dholuo linguistic resources.

fdner is a benchmark dataset for fine-grained named entity recognition, providing text annotated with entity spans and detailed entity types. It is designed to train and evaluate models on precise entity detection and classification, supporting research in distinguishing closely related entity categories and improving NER performance in complex, real-world text.

XGLUE is a comprehensive cross-lingual benchmark consisting of 11 tasks across 19 languages, designed to evaluate models' zero-shot transfer capabilities. Training data is available only in English, requiring models to generalize learned knowledge to other languages. Unlike similar benchmarks, XGLUE includes both natural language understanding and generation tasks. It incorporates five established cross-lingual tasks such as named entity recognition and question answering, along with six new tasks derived from real-world scenarios, including news classification, query-ad matching, and question generation. This diversity of languages and tasks makes XGLUE a valuable resource for assessing the performance of multilingual pre-trained models in cross-lingual natural language processing.

MedMentions is a new manually annotated resource for the recognition of biomedical concepts. What distinguishes MedMentions from other annotated biomedical corpora is its size (over 4,000 abstracts and over 350,000 linked mentions), as well as the size of the concept ontology (over 3 million concepts from UMLS 2017) and its broad coverage of biomedical disciplines. HiNER Original is a human-annotated named entity recognition (NER) dataset containing diverse-domain texts labeled at token level with standard BIO-style entity spans and multiple common entity classes (e.g., PER, ORG, LOC). It provides train/validation/test splits and consistent annotation guidelines to support supervised training and benchmarking of sequence-labeling models. HiNER Original is intended for evaluating model accuracy, generalization across domains and text styles, and research on transfer learning and domain adaptation in NER.

MASSIVE is a parallel dataset of > 1M utterances across 51 languages with annotations for the Natural Language Understanding tasks of intent prediction and slot annotation. Utterances span 60 intents and include 55 slot types. MASSIVE was created by localizing the SLURP dataset, composed of general Intelligent Voice Assistant single-shot interactions.

The **Universal Dependencies** (UD) project seeks to develop cross-linguistically consistent treebank annotation of morphology and syntax for multiple languages. The first version of the dataset was released in 2015 and consisted of 10 treebanks over 10 languages. Version 2.7 released in 2020 consists of 183 treebanks over 104 languages. The annotation consists of UPOS (universal part-of-speech tags), XPOS (language-specific part-of-speech tags), Feats (universal morphological features), Lemmas, dependency heads and universal dependency labels. Generated is a synthetic, procedurally produced dataset of fully annotated samples (e.g., images with class labels, bounding boxes, segmentation masks, depth, and/or motion where applicable) designed for scalable training and evaluation of machine learning models. It provides controllable variations in object geometry, pose, lighting, backgrounds, and noise to support robustness testing, domain adaptation, and simulation-to-real transfer studies. Deterministic generation and rich metadata enable reproducible experiments, systematic ablations, and rapid prototyping of models across diverse, customizable conditions.

legal_ner is a supervised named-entity recognition dataset of legal texts annotated with domain-specific entity labels (e.g., parties, judges, statutes, citations, dates, organizations, provisions and legal roles). It contains token/span-level annotations drawn from contracts, court opinions, filings and regulations to support training and evaluation of sequence-labeling models. Designed to reflect long-range context, dense legal jargon and citation formats, it serves as a benchmark for NER and information extraction in legal NLP, evaluated with standard precision/recall/F1 metrics.

uner_all is a token-level named entity recognition (NER) corpus containing sentences annotated with entity spans and labels in BIO-style format. It covers a broad set of common entity categories (e.g., PERSON, LOCATION, ORGANIZATION, MISC) drawn from diverse textual sources, providing varied lexical and contextual examples for training. The dataset is intended for supervised learning and evaluation of NER models, including cross-domain and cross-lingual transfer experiments, and supports benchmarking of sequence labeling, entity boundary detection, and label classification performance.

OpenThai-NER is a Thai named entity recognition dataset providing Thai text annotated with entity spans and labels for supervised sequence-labeling tasks. It contains sentence-level annotations for common entity categories (e.g., person, location, organization) and is formatted for training and evaluating NER models. The dataset is useful for developing and benchmarking Thai-specific NER systems, including tokenization-aware models and fine-tuning of multilingual or Thai pretrained transformers.

ingredients_yes_no is a dataset for ingredient-presence detection in food items, providing images (and optional recipe text) annotated with binary yes/no labels for a predefined set of ingredients. It supports supervised training and evaluation of binary and multi-label classification models that predict whether each ingredient appears in an image or recipe, and is useful for tasks such as ingredient recognition, recipe retrieval, dietary monitoring, and food logging. The dataset is organized with standard train/validation/test splits and balanced per-ingredient annotations to facilitate reproducible benchmarking of ingredient-detection methods.

bc2gm_corpus is a biomedical named-entity recognition dataset of PubMed abstracts manually annotated for gene and protein mentions. It is designed for supervised learning and evaluation of entity recognition models in the biomedical domain, providing annotated mention spans and commonly used train/dev/test splits. The corpus captures domain-specific naming variability and abbreviations, making it suitable for developing and benchmarking NER, boundary detection, and downstream tasks such as entity normalization and relation extraction in biomedical NLP.

peoples_daily_ner is a Chinese newswire named entity recognition dataset derived from People's Daily articles, containing manually annotated entity mentions (commonly person, location, and organization) in natural-language text. Prepared for sequence-labeling research, it provides token- or character-level annotations suitable for BIO-style NER modeling and benchmarking. The dataset is widely used to train and evaluate supervised Chinese NER systems and to study domain-specific performance, annotation schemes, and model generalization on formal news-domain text.

goodsmemo is a multimodal product dataset containing consumer-goods images paired with short textual memos and structured metadata (e.g., product name, category, attributes). It is designed for tasks such as image–text retrieval, product recognition/classification, captioning, OCR of labels/handwritten notes, and attribute extraction. Images reflect real-world capture conditions (varied lighting, occlusion, viewpoints) to promote robustness, making the dataset suitable for benchmarking multimodal and e-commerce inventory-management models.

my-data is a curated dataset for machine learning that provides labeled, quality-checked samples with accompanying metadata and standardized train/validation/test splits. Designed to support supervised model development and benchmarking, it includes class or target annotations and optional auxiliary labels (e.g., bounding boxes, timestamps, attributes) to enable tasks such as classification, regression, and detection. my-data aims to simplify reproducible evaluation and model comparison by offering consistent formatting, clear documentation, and licensing information for easy integration into training and evaluation pipelines.

maccrobat_biomedical_ner is a biomedical named‑entity recognition dataset composed of text from biomedical sources annotated with entity spans and type labels (e.g., diseases, chemicals, genes/proteins, anatomical terms, procedures). Annotations are provided at the token/span level in a standard sequence-labeling format for supervised training and evaluation. The dataset is intended for developing and benchmarking NER and information-extraction models in biomedical and clinical NLP, supporting tasks such as entity recognition, relation extraction, knowledge-base population, and downstream clinical/biomedical applications.

A combined Norwegian named‑entity recognition dataset aggregating annotations from multiple sources. It provides token‑level and span annotations with standard entity labels (e.g., PERSON, LOCATION, ORGANIZATION and similar classes), formatted for supervised sequence‑labeling and token‑classification tasks. Designed for training and evaluating NER models in Norwegian, the dataset supports cross-source generalization, domain robustness testing, and transfer‑learning experiments.

wikiann-conll2003 is a named-entity recognition (NER) benchmark that combines Wikipedia-derived WikiANN data with the English CoNLL-2003 newswire dataset. It provides token-level BIO annotations for common entity types (person, location, organization, etc.) and is intended for training and evaluating NER models, particularly in cross-lingual transfer and domain-generalization settings across Wikipedia and newswire text.

Tweebank NER is a Twitter named‑entity recognition dataset of tweets annotated with entity spans and token-level labels (e.g., person, location, organization, miscellaneous, typically in BIO format). It captures informal, noisy social‑media language including mentions, hashtags, emoticons and nonstandard orthography, making it suitable for training and evaluating NER models on microblog text and for research on robustness and domain adaptation of entity recognition systems.

fin is a curated financial dataset of historical market and company-level data designed for machine learning research in forecasting and risk modeling. It contains time-series features such as prices, volumes, common technical indicators, fundamental signals, and event annotations (e.g., earnings, splits), with aligned target labels for tasks like return prediction, volatility forecasting, and anomaly detection. The dataset supports supervised and self-supervised training, backtesting, and evaluation of models under realistic temporal splits, enabling development of trading strategies, portfolio allocation methods, and robust financial risk estimators. fin is intended to standardize benchmarking for ML applications in quantitative finance and to facilitate reproducible experiments on real-world market dynamics.

tner/btc is a token-level named entity recognition (NER) dataset from the TNER collection that provides annotated, tokenized text with entity span labels (commonly in BIO/BILOU format) and standard train/validation/test splits. It is intended for supervised training and benchmarking of sequence-labeling models (CRFs, BiLSTM-CRF, transformer-based taggers) and supports evaluation with precision, recall and F1 metrics. The dataset includes metadata for each example (IDs, sentence boundaries and label schemas) to facilitate preprocessing, model fine-tuning and reproducible experiments in NER.

conll2003job is a token-level sequence-labeling dataset in CoNLL-2003 format tailored for named-entity recognition of job-related information. It provides sentences tokenized with IOB-style entity annotations for job titles, roles, organizations and related spans, enabling supervised training and evaluation of NER models on job/domain-specific text. The dataset is useful for benchmarking extraction of occupation and employment entities in downstream applications such as resume parsing and job-posting analysis.

biobert_json is a JSON-formatted biomedical NLP dataset prepared for training and fine-tuning BioBERT-style transformer models. Each record contains biomedical text (e.g., literature abstracts or passages) with structured annotations such as token/span-level entity labels and optional relation or classification labels. It is formatted for easy ingestion by tokenizers and typical ML pipelines and supports tasks like named entity recognition, relation extraction, and document-level classification for biomedical information extraction.

Ben10x/MedMentions-MTI881-NER is a biomedical named-entity recognition dataset derived from the MedMentions corpus that maps entity mentions in PubMed abstracts to UMLS concepts restricted to the MTI881 label set. Each record contains the source text plus annotated entity spans with character offsets and labels (UMLS CUIs and MTI881 semantic-type identifiers), enabling span-level detection and classification. It is intended for training and evaluating NER and concept-linking models in biomedical information extraction and downstream clinical/NLP tasks.

desc: Nergrit Corpus is a dataset for robust named-entity recognition built from noisy, user-generated text (social media posts, comments, short messages). It contains manually annotated entity spans and coarse entity types (e.g., PERSON, ORGANIZATION, LOCATION, MISC) in contexts with misspellings, abbreviations, emojis, and informal grammar. Nergrit is intended for training and evaluating sequence-labeling and NER models under real-world noise and domain shift, with standardized train/dev/test splits for reproducible benchmarking and research on robustness, domain adaptation, and noise-tolerant representations.

Universal Dependencies sk_snk is a Slovak dependency treebank in the Universal Dependencies format, derived from the Slovak National Corpus. It contains tokenized sentences annotated with lemmas, universal and language-specific POS tags, morphological features, and labeled dependency relations. The resource is intended for supervised training and evaluation of POS taggers, lemmatizers, morphological analyzers and dependency parsers, and serves as a benchmark for syntactic and morphosyntactic modeling and cross-lingual experiments on Slovak.

Few-NERD is a large-scale benchmark for few-shot named entity recognition that provides sentence-level annotations and a hierarchical label set (coarse- and fine-grained types) to support N-way K-shot evaluation. Designed for episodic meta-learning, it contains diverse entity types and contexts (derived from Wikipedia) to measure a model’s ability to generalize to novel entity categories with limited labeled examples.

Skript is a curated dataset of short scripting-language programs (shell, Python, JavaScript, PowerShell, etc.) collected from public repositories and Q&A sources. Each sample pairs the source script with metadata: a one-line natural-language summary of intent, optional input–output examples or unit tests, API-call and resource annotations, and bug/vulnerability labels where applicable. Precomputed representations (tokenized code, ASTs) and standardized train/validation/test splits make Skript suitable for tasks such as code summarization, generation, repair/bug fixing, intent classification, vulnerability detection, and code retrieval.

GermEval 2014 is a German-language dataset created for the GermEval 2014 shared task on named entity recognition. It contains manually annotated texts with entity spans and labels (e.g., person, location, organization, other) and standard train/dev/test splits for supervised sequence-labeling evaluation. The dataset is used to train and benchmark NER models for German text and supports research on entity identification, classification, and cross-domain generalization.

lg-ner is a benchmark dataset for named entity recognition providing token-level annotations of common entity types (e.g., Person, Organization, Location, Misc) across diverse textual domains. Built in a standard sequence-labeling format with train/validation/test splits, it supports supervised training and evaluation of NER models as well as experiments in domain adaptation and transfer learning. lg-ner is intended to facilitate development and comparison of sequence-labeling architectures and cross-domain generalization for entity extraction tasks.

**CoNLL-2003** is a named entity recognition dataset released as a part of CoNLL-2003 shared task: language-independent named entity recognition. The data consists of eight files covering two languages: English and German. For each of the languages there is a training file, a development file, a test file and a large file with unannotated data. The English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus. This corpus consists of Reuters news stories between August 1996 and August 1997. For the training and development set, ten days worth of data were taken from the files representing the end of August 1996. For the test set, the texts were from December 1996. The preprocessed raw data covers the month of September 1996. The text for the German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus. This corpus consists of texts in many languages. The portion of data that was used for this task, was extracted from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundshau. All three of the training, development and test sets were taken from articles written in one week at the end of August 1992.
