desc: SecretMask v2 is a benchmark dataset for evaluating privacy-preserving and mask-handling algorithms on face and object imagery. It contains 600 test examples of images with diverse, realistic occlusion masks (both synthetic and captured) paired with pixel-level mask annotations and original unmasked ground truth where available. The dataset is suited for tasks such as mask detection/segmentation, masked-face recognition, mask removal/inpainting, and robustness testing of downstream vision models under anonymization. SecretMask v2 emphasizes varied lighting, poses, and demographic diversity to assess generalization of privacy and reconstruction methods.

nerde is a benchmark dataset for named-entity recognition and entity disambiguation in noisy, real-world text. It provides token-level entity annotations paired with canonical entity identifiers (linking to a knowledge base), enabling supervised training and evaluation of end-to-end extraction and linking systems. nerde is designed to test robustness to informal language, abbreviations and ambiguity, and is useful for developing and comparing NER, entity linking, and joint NER+EL models.

tner/bionlp2004 is a biomedical named-entity recognition dataset containing sentences from biomedical literature annotated with entity mentions (e.g., proteins/genes, RNAs, cell types). It is intended for supervised sequence-labeling and information-extraction tasks, supporting development and evaluation of NER models and domain-specific entity normalization in the biomedical domain.

Invoices is a dataset of scanned and photographed invoice documents paired with structured annotations for document-understanding tasks. It includes diverse vendor templates and layout variations and provides OCR transcriptions, bounding-box or polygon labels for key fields (e.g., vendor, recipient, invoice number, dates, totals, line items), table-structure annotations, and key–value mappings. Designed for training and evaluating OCR, layout analysis, semantic segmentation, table recognition, and information-extraction models, the dataset benchmarks end-to-end document parsing and robustness across real-world invoice formats.

ade_drug_effect_ner is a named‑entity recognition dataset for extracting drug and adverse‑effect mentions from biomedical text. It provides sentence‑level annotations of entity spans and types (e.g., Drug, Effect) derived from case reports and biomedical literature, enabling supervised training and evaluation of sequence‑labeling models. The dataset is intended for pharmacovigilance and clinical information‑extraction research, supporting downstream tasks such as adverse drug event detection and relation extraction.

nubes is a curated dataset of annotated cloud imagery for computer vision and remote sensing tasks. It contains RGB sky and satellite images paired with pixel-level cloud segmentation masks, categorical cloud-type labels, and auxiliary metadata (timestamp, location, sensor parameters). Designed for supervised learning of cloud detection, semantic segmentation, cloud-cover estimation and classification, nubes captures diverse illumination, seasonal and atmospheric conditions to challenge generalization and robustness. The dataset supports development and evaluation of models for weather analysis, solar forecasting, and scene understanding in meteorological and earth-observation applications.

Caner is a curated dataset for cancer-related machine learning tasks, containing medical images with expert-provided diagnostic labels and region-level annotations. It is designed to support supervised training and evaluation for classification, localization and segmentation of malignant tissue across diverse imaging conditions. Caner serves as a practical benchmark for developing and comparing models for cancer detection, quantification and clinically relevant interpretation.

FACT2020 is a benchmark dataset for automated fact-checking and claim verification. It comprises real-world claims paired with retrieved or curated evidence and human veracity labels, along with metadata such as sources and timestamps. The dataset supports supervised learning and evaluation across tasks including claim detection, evidence retrieval/ranking, and verdict classification, facilitating development and assessment of NLP models for reliable real-world fact-checking.

Inspec is a widely used benchmark dataset for automatic keyword extraction from text documents. It comprises scientific abstracts primarily in English, focusing on identifying key terms and phrases that succinctly represent the main topics of each document. The dataset is designed to facilitate the development and evaluation of keyword extraction methods, which aim to improve information retrieval, document summarization, and indexing. Inspec presents challenges typical of natural language processing tasks, such as handling multi-word expressions, varying term frequencies, and linguistic ambiguity. Evaluation metrics commonly reported on Inspec include precision, recall, and F-measure, reflecting the accuracy and completeness of extracted keywords relative to human annotations. Due to its domain specificity and well-established use, Inspec serves as a critical resource for both supervised and unsupervised keyword extraction approaches, enabling comparisons across diverse algorithmic strategies and fostering advances in linguistic and graph-based feature integration.

LINNAEUS is a general-purpose dictionary matching software, capable of processing multiple types of document formats in the biomedical domain (MEDLINE, PMC, BMC, OTMI, text, etc.). It can produce multiple types of output (XML, HTML, tab-separated-value file, or save to a database). It also contains methods for acting as a server (including load balancing across several servers), allowing clients to request matching over a network. nbroad/company_names is a curated corpus of company and organization names along with common variants, abbreviations, and alternate spellings harvested from public directories and web sources. It provides paired canonical names and alias forms to support supervised and evaluation tasks in named-entity recognition, entity linking, record linkage/deduplication, fuzzy matching, and corporate name normalization. The dataset is useful for training models that perform brand detection, entity resolution, information extraction, and data-cleaning pipelines involving organizational mentions.

violations is a labeled benchmark dataset for automated detection and classification of rule/policy violations across real-world examples. It provides annotated instances marked by violation presence and category (and where applicable localization or text spans), enabling supervised training and evaluation of classifiers, detectors, and moderation systems. The dataset is designed to reflect realistic, diverse violation scenarios to test model accuracy, robustness and generalization for applications such as compliance monitoring, safety enforcement, content moderation and automated auditing.

DrugTEMIST-cat is a benchmark dataset of transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images of biological samples exposed to different chemical/drug treatments, annotated with categorical labels denoting treatment class or phenotypic response. Designed for supervised classification and phenotype-recognition tasks, it enables development and evaluation of models that detect drug-induced ultrastructural changes. The dataset covers diverse cell types and imaging conditions to encourage robustness and generalization, making it useful for automated phenotyping, drug screening, and toxicity assessment in bioimage analysis.

CataCCC-drugs is a curated dataset of C–C cross-coupling reactions involving drug-like substrates, including reactant and product SMILES, catalyst/ligand identities, reaction conditions, and experimentally measured yields. It is designed to support supervised learning for reaction outcome prediction, yield regression, condition recommendation, and retrosynthesis planning in medicinal chemistry contexts. By focusing on pharmaceutically relevant scaffolds and realistic catalytic systems, CataCCC-drugs enables development and evaluation of models that generalize to drug discovery workflows and condition optimization for cross-coupling transformations.

Internal test set is a private, held-out dataset used for final evaluation of models. It contains labeled examples representative of production or target-domain data but is excluded from training and validation to provide unbiased estimates of generalization and robustness. The set is intended for performance benchmarking, model selection, and readiness assessment under realistic distributional conditions; it is not publicly released.

symptemist-8-ner is a named‑entity recognition dataset for extracting symptom- and health-related entities from text. Instances are annotated with eight entity categories (e.g., symptoms, conditions, treatments, temporal or contextual modifiers), provided as span-level labels suitable for training and evaluating sequence-labeling NER models. It is intended for research and applications in clinical/health information extraction, symptom detection, and downstream tasks like concept normalization and clinical event extraction.

Beijuka/Multilingual_PII_NER_dataset is a multilingual, span‑annotated corpus for detecting personally identifiable information (PII) in text. It labels common PII categories (e.g., names, addresses/locations, identifiers, contact details, dates) across multiple languages to support supervised training and evaluation of NER and de‑identification systems. The dataset is suitable for benchmarking multilingual PII detection, cross‑lingual transfer studies, and privacy-preserving text-processing pipelines.

Custom Invoice Dataset is a collection of scanned and digitally generated invoice images paired with structured annotations for document-understanding tasks. Annotations include word- and line-level bounding boxes, OCR transcriptions, semantic field labels (e.g., vendor, invoice number, dates, totals), table/line-item structure and key–value mappings. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating OCR, layout analysis, key‑value extraction, and end-to-end invoice-parsing models across diverse templates, languages, and imaging conditions, with annotations provided in common machine-readable formats (e.g., JSON).

WikiAnn sk is the Slovak subset of the WikiAnn (PAN-X) multilingual named-entity recognition corpus, providing token-level NER annotations (typically PER, LOC, ORG) automatically projected from Wikipedia/Wikidata. Distributed in a CoNLL-style format, it is intended for training, evaluation and cross-lingual transfer experiments for Slovak NER, and is commonly used for benchmarking sequence-labeling models in low-resource or multilingual settings.

movie_releases is a structured dataset of films and their distribution events, containing metadata such as titles, release dates by region, formats (theatrical, streaming, home video), genres, production and distribution companies, cast/crew, runtime, language, ratings, synopsis text, and commercial indicators (box office, opening weekend). It is designed for temporal and multimodal tasks like box-office forecasting, release-schedule optimization, recommendation and trend analysis, genre or success prediction, and NLP on synopses or reviews. Time-stamped, region-specific release records make the dataset suitable for studying market dynamics, seasonality, and cross-region rollout strategies.

pv_dataset is a time-series dataset of photovoltaic (PV) system power measurements paired with contextual metadata and meteorological observations (e.g., solar irradiance, ambient temperature, wind, cloud cover, timestamps and site/panel orientation). It supports supervised forecasting of short- and long-term PV output, performance modeling across multiple sites and resolutions, and anomaly/fault detection. The dataset is intended for developing and evaluating ML models for solar generation forecasting, grid integration studies, and PV system monitoring.

Species800 is a named entity recognition (NER) dataset focused on clinical and biomedical text, designed for identifying and classifying entities such as persons, organizations, and locations in medical and healthcare documentation. The dataset comprises annotated text samples using BIO tagging, where B- and I- tags denote the start and continuation of named entities, and O denotes non-entity tokens. It is specifically tailored for training and evaluating NER models in high-stakes domains like clinical note analysis and biomedical research. The dataset supports benchmarking against established challenges such as i2b2/VA concept extraction, n2c2 de-identification, and medication extraction. Due to its domain-specific nature and structured annotation, Species800 enables the development of accurate, production-grade NER systems that perform competitively against commercial solutions like AWS Medical Comprehend and Google Cloud Healthcare API. ner-tr is a Turkish named entity recognition dataset containing token-level annotations for common entity types (e.g., PERSON, ORGANIZATION, LOCATION). It provides standard train/dev/test splits for supervised sequence-labeling evaluation and is suitable for training and benchmarking CRF-, BiLSTM-CRF-, and Transformer-based NER models. The dataset supports research in Turkish NLP, cross-lingual transfer, and entity extraction from diverse Turkish text sources.

ade_drug_dosage_ner is a named‑entity recognition dataset for pharmacovigilance that annotates drug mentions together with their dosage expressions (amounts and units) in adverse drug event texts. It provides sentence‑level span annotations for training and evaluating supervised NER models to extract dosing information from clinical narratives, case reports, and patient‑generated text. The dataset supports tasks such as dose normalization, relation extraction between drugs and doses, and automated adverse event monitoring.

cord-layoutlmv is a receipt document dataset prepared for training and evaluating layout-aware multimodal transformers (e.g., LayoutLMv variants). It contains scanned/photographed receipts with OCR-extracted tokens, token-level bounding boxes, and semantic annotations for entities and key–value pairs (merchant, date, total, item lines, etc.). The data is provided in a format suitable for sequence-labeling and document-level information extraction tasks, enabling supervised training and benchmarking of models that combine textual content and spatial layout for receipt parsing, key-value extraction, and downstream document understanding.

Pharmaconer is a Spanish-language dataset for pharmaceutical named-entity recognition consisting of clinical and biomedical texts manually annotated with drug-related entities (e.g., active ingredients, brand names, formulations and drug groups). Annotations follow standard token-level labeling (BIO-style) and are produced by domain-expert annotators to support reliable supervised training and evaluation. The dataset is intended for developing and benchmarking NER, entity linking and pharmacovigilance information-extraction systems in Spanish clinical and biomedical domains.

desc: tiagoblima/punctuation-tedtalk2012-full-text-bert is a punctuation restoration dataset derived from TED Talks (TEDTalk2012) prepared for BERT-style sequence labeling. It contains full-text transcripts tokenized into BERT WordPiece tokens with aligned punctuation labels (e.g., period, comma, question) for each token, formatted for supervised fine-tuning. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating models that predict punctuation in automatic speech recognition or raw text normalization pipelines, enabling standard sequence-labeling metrics (precision/recall/F1) for performance assessment.

Babelscape/multinerd is a multilingual dataset of span-level entity annotations designed for named entity recognition and entity linking. Each mention is labeled with fine-grained entity types and grounded to BabelNet identifiers, enabling joint NER+EL training and evaluation. The resource supports sequence-labeling, cross-lingual transfer, and fine-grained entity-typing research by providing multilingual, KB-linked annotations for robust entity understanding and grounding.

UD Nheengatu CompLin is a Universal Dependencies treebank for Nheengatu (an Amazonian Tupí-Guaraní language) produced by the CompLin group. Sentences are annotated in UD CONLL format with tokenization, lemmas, UPOS/XPOS tags, morphological features, and gold dependency heads and relations. The resource supports supervised training and evaluation of POS taggers, morphological analyzers, and dependency parsers, and is intended for low-resource NLP research, cross-lingual transfer, and typological studies of indigenous Amazonian languages.

MultiNERD (English) is a multi-domain, fine-grained named entity recognition dataset in English. It contains span-level annotations across a broad taxonomy of entity types drawn from diverse text sources, enabling evaluation of models on varied contexts and granular categories. The dataset is intended for supervised training and benchmarking of NER systems, with emphasis on cross-domain generalization, robustness to label granularity, and transfer/domain-adaptation research.

FEW-NERD is a large-scale few-shot named entity recognition benchmark of human-annotated sentences labeled with a rich hierarchical ontology of entity types (coarse and fine granularity). It is organized for episodic few-shot evaluation with predefined support/query splits and sampling protocols (intra- and cross-domain), enabling research on meta-learning, prototypical, and prompt-based methods that must recognize novel entity categories from very few labeled examples.

OntoNotes 5 is a large, multi-genre, multilingual corpus with layered linguistic annotations including part-of-speech, syntactic structure (constituency), predicate-argument/semantic role labels (PropBank), word senses, named entities, and coreference. Covering genres such as newswire, broadcast, conversations, weblogs and more in English, Chinese, and Arabic, it provides unified annotations that support training and standardized evaluation of coreference resolution, NER, parsing, semantic role labeling, and joint/multi-task NLP models.

Drugtemist-it-9-ner is an Italian-language named entity recognition dataset focused on medication and therapeutic information. It provides span-level annotations across nine entity categories related to drugs and treatment (e.g., drug names, dosage and administration details, adverse effects, and related clinical concepts) for supervised sequence-labeling tasks. The corpus is intended for training and evaluating NER and information-extraction models in pharmacovigilance, clinical NLP, and medication-related knowledge extraction, and is distributed in standard token/label sequence formats suitable for common NER pipelines.

drugtemist-en-fasttext-8-ner is an English named-entity recognition dataset for the pharmaceutical/drug domain. It contains token-level annotations for drug-relevant entities (e.g., drug names, dosages, formulations) and comes with precomputed fastText-8 token embeddings, formatted for token-classification workflows. The dataset is organized with standard train/validation/test splits and common BIO-style labeling, making it suitable for training and evaluating NER models that leverage pretrained word vectors, transfer learning, or embedding-based feature experiments in domain-specific entity extraction.

WikiANN English is the English portion of the WikiANN (PAN-X) named entity recognition corpus: a large-scale, automatically annotated dataset of Wikipedia sentences with token-level entity spans mapped to three categories (PER, LOC, ORG) via Wikidata links. KazNERD (Augmented) is a Kazakh Named Entity Recognition dataset that pairs tokenized sentences with BIO-style entity annotations. It extends the original human-annotated corpus with synthetic augmentations (e.g., back-translation, entity substitution, and cross-lingual transfers) to increase class balance and lexical diversity. The dataset covers standard entity types (person, organization, location, etc.) and is intended for training and evaluating NER models, studying augmentation strategies, and improving robustness for low-resource Kazakh NLP.

mlner2021 is a multilingual named‑entity recognition benchmark consisting of sentences annotated with entity spans and types (e.g., PER, ORG, LOC, MISC) using token‑level IOB labels and standard train/validation/test splits. Sourced from diverse domains, it enables supervised, cross‑lingual transfer and zero‑shot evaluation of NER systems, supporting comparison of multilingual models and assessment of generalization across languages and domains.

HiNER Collapsed is a flattened variant of a hierarchical/nested NER corpus in which nested or hierarchical entity annotations have been collapsed into single-span, coarse entity labels. The dataset provides tokenized text with sequence-label annotations (e.g., BIO/BILOU) reflecting the collapsed entity classes, enabling training and evaluation of flat NER models. It is intended for benchmarking model performance after reducing annotation granularity, for comparing flat vs. hierarchical approaches, and for studying the impact of collapsing nested entities on segmentation and classification accuracy.

xtreme_en_token_drift is a benchmark dataset for evaluating English-language NLP model robustness to token-level distribution shift. It contains English text samples partitioned into in-distribution and out-of-distribution splits where token frequencies, rare-word occurrences, or token mappings are systematically altered to simulate realistic and synthetic drift. The dataset is intended for tasks such as text classification, sequence labeling, and representation evaluation, allowing measurement of performance degradation, calibration, and adaptation methods under vocabulary and token-distribution changes. xtreme_en_token_drift enables controlled experiments on domain shift, continual learning, and robustness interventions for models deployed in changing language environments.

toydata is a small synthetic dataset designed for rapid prototyping, debugging, and baseline evaluation of machine learning models. It provides low-dimensional, controllable feature-label pairs with known ground-truth structure and configurable noise levels, enabling reproducible experiments for classification, regression, or clustering tasks. Its simplicity makes it well suited for unit tests, algorithmic comparisons, and educational demonstrations before scaling to real-world datasets.

HAREM is a Portuguese annotated corpus and benchmark for named-entity recognition created for the HAREM evaluation campaign. It contains manually labeled texts from varied genres (primarily news) with coarse and fine-grained entity categories (person, organization, location, date, value, etc.) and provides standardized splits including Mini‑HAREM and Full‑HAREM. The dataset supports development and evaluation of NER and entity classification systems for Portuguese and serves as a reference benchmark in Portuguese NLP.

tapaco is a corpus of tables paired with contextual sentences and captions mined from web sources (e.g., Wikipedia) to support learning alignments between structured tabular data and natural language. Each instance links table cells or rows to natural-language text that references table content, enabling tasks such as table question answering, table-to-text generation, cell tagging, and table grounding. tapaco is commonly used for pretraining and benchmarking table-aware language models and for weakly supervised extraction of table–text alignments.

drug_bill_layoutv3 is a document layout dataset of pharmaceutical invoices and bills annotated for supervised layout analysis and information extraction. It provides bounding-box and semantic labels for common invoice elements (vendor/header, patient/customer, date, invoice number, line-item rows, quantities, unit prices, totals, tax, signatures/stamps) and table structure annotations for itemized sections. The corpus is intended for training and evaluating OCR, key–value extraction, table parsing, and document segmentation models under realistic scanning and photographic conditions.

data_set is a curated benchmark dataset for supervised machine learning that provides labeled examples and standardized train/validation/test splits with accompanying metadata. It contains diverse, real-world-like samples designed to capture challenging variations relevant to tasks such as classification, detection, and segmentation. The dataset supports training, evaluation, and fair comparison of models, and is useful for research on model robustness, generalization, and practical deployment in applied settings.

desc: shared-task is a benchmark dataset created for a community competition to enable standardized comparison of machine learning methods. It provides curated input samples with task-specific ground-truth annotations and predefined training, validation, and held-out test splits, together with a clear evaluation protocol and metrics. Designed to support supervised learning for a particular problem (e.g., classification, detection, segmentation, or sequence prediction), shared-task facilitates reproducible research, fair benchmarking, and rapid iteration of models under challenge-style conditions.

SourceData is a curated multimodal dataset of original (source) media paired with processed or altered variants and rich metadata. It contains diverse, real-world content (images, audio, and text) alongside their unmodified originals and documented transformations (compression, resizing, filtering, editing). Designed for training and benchmarking models for source attribution, provenance analysis, forgery/manipulation detection, and restoration, SourceData supports supervised, contrastive, and domain-adaptation tasks that require recovering, identifying, or reasoning about the true origin of data.

FUNSD (Form Understanding in Noisy Scanned Documents) is a dataset consisting of 199 real, fully annotated scanned forms characterized by noise and diverse appearances. It is designed to support multiple document understanding tasks such as text detection, optical character recognition, spatial layout analysis, and entity labeling and linking. The dataset aims to facilitate research in form understanding under challenging conditions typical of scanned documents.

plod-filtered is a curated, filtered subset of the PLOD object-detection collection that provides cleaned bounding-box annotations and class labels for supervised detection tasks. Noisy, duplicate, and low-quality annotations/images have been removed and labels standardized to improve training stability and benchmark reliability. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating object detectors, studying robustness to annotation noise, and benchmarking model generalization on real-world images.

NKJP1M is a one-million-token subset of the Narodowy Korpus Języka Polskiego (National Corpus of Polish) intended as a compact, representative sample of Polish text. It provides sentence-segmented and tokenized text with morphosyntactic annotations (lemmas and POS/morphology tags) across a range of genres and domains. NKJP1M is suitable for training and evaluating language models, POS taggers, lemmatizers, morphological analyzers, and other Polish NLP tools, and for frequency/lexical studies and downstream tasks that require annotated Polish text.

pos_tag_100k is a supervised part-of-speech tagging dataset containing approximately 100,000 manually annotated word tokens drawn from diverse text sources. Each token is labeled with POS tags and the corpus is provided with standard train/validation/test splits to support model development and evaluation. It is suited for training and benchmarking sequence-labeling models, measuring tagging accuracy, and studying transfer learning and domain adaptation in POS tagging tasks.

__main__ is the primary benchmark split intended as the central training and evaluation set for a larger dataset collection. It contains a diverse, curated set of labeled examples with standardized annotations and predefined train/validation/test splits to support reproducible supervised learning and model comparison. Designed for broad compatibility, __main__ includes metadata and evaluation protocols to facilitate benchmarking across architectures and tasks, enabling consistent development and assessment of models on the dataset's core examples.

data_loader is a modular dataset utility that standardizes loading, preprocessing, augmentation, and batching of samples and labels for machine learning experiments. It provides configurable transforms, efficient I/O with parallel loading and optional caching, and built-in train/validation/test split handling to support reproducible workflows. Designed to streamline dataset preparation and benchmarking, data_loader enables rapid prototyping and consistent evaluation of models across tasks by delivering reliable, preprocessed data pipelines.

my_csv_dataset3 is a structured tabular dataset provided as one or more CSV files containing rows of observations with feature columns and one or more target columns. It is intended for supervised learning and benchmarking of tabular models (classification and/or regression) and includes a mix of numerical and categorical features that may require preprocessing (imputation, encoding, scaling). The dataset is suitable for model prototyping, baseline comparisons, feature engineering experiments, and cross‑validation-based evaluation using standard tools (pandas, scikit‑learn).

uner_dan_ddt is a multi-domain dataset for dynamic scene understanding and cross-domain evaluation. It provides synchronized RGB sequences with corresponding depth maps and per-frame annotations (bounding boxes, segmentation masks, optical flow) collected across diverse scenes, lighting conditions, and sensor configurations. Designed to benchmark supervised and domain-adaptive models, the dataset targets tasks such as depth estimation, motion segmentation, and object tracking under real-world variations (motion blur, occlusion, sensor noise), enabling evaluation of model accuracy and generalization across domains.

uner_slo_snk is a Slovenian named-entity recognition (NER) dataset formatted to the UNER annotation scheme. It provides token-level entity labels (e.g., PERSON, LOCATION, ORGANIZATION, DATE) over contemporary Slovenian text sources, enabling supervised training and evaluation of sequence-labeling models. The dataset is suitable for benchmarking NER performance, multilingual or cross-lingual transfer, and domain-adaptation experiments on Slovene language data.

DisTEMIST-cat is a labeled subset of the DisTEMIST corpus curated for image-level disease categorization in medical imaging. Each case is paired with one or more categorical diagnostic labels covering clinically relevant conditions, enabling single- and multi-label classification tasks. The collection captures realistic class imbalance and imaging variability to support training, validation, and benchmarking of supervised classifiers and domain-generalization studies in clinical AI.

CataCCC-diseases is a curated medical dataset of cases labeled for multiple disease conditions, each case paired with expert annotations and accompanying clinical metadata. It contains diverse imaging modalities and standardized labels to support supervised tasks such as disease classification, localization, segmentation, and severity scoring. Designed as a benchmark, the dataset enables development and evaluation of diagnostic algorithms, assessment of robustness across disease classes and sites, and reproducible comparisons through consistent annotation protocols and metadata for stratified analysis.

root_b: rodrigo1771 combined train distemist dev ner
desc: Rodrigo1771/combined-train-distemist-dev-ner is a combined training dataset for Spanish clinical named entity recognition, merging the training and development splits from the Distemist corpus. It contains clinical text annotated for named entities relevant to de-identification and clinical NLP (e.g., personal identifiers, dates, locations, institutions, professions and other PHI and clinical mentions). The split is intended for supervised training and fine-tuning of NER and de-identification models on Spanish medical records and for benchmarking entity extraction performance in real-world clinical scenarios.

root_b: rodrigo1771 combined train drugtemist dev ner
desc: Combined-train-drugtemist-dev-ner is a biomedical named-entity recognition dataset that combines training annotations from DrugTemist with a held-out development split. It contains token- and span-level annotations for drug-related entities (e.g., drug names, brands, compounds, formulations) in clinical and biomedical text. The dataset is intended for supervised training and evaluation of NER systems—including fine-tuning transformer-based sequence-labeling models—and for benchmarking models in pharmacovigilance, drug mention detection, and related biomedical NLP tasks.

Rodrigo1771/distemist-ner is a human-annotated Spanish medical named-entity recognition (NER) dataset derived from clinical and biomedical texts. It provides span-level entity annotations (in BIO/IOB-style token labels) for common clinical concept types (e.g., diseases, symptoms, treatments, anatomical terms), suitable for sequence-labeling tasks. The corpus is intended for supervised training and evaluation of NER models, domain adaptation and transfer learning experiments in Spanish clinical NLP, and for developing systems that extract structured medical information from unstructured text.

DrugTemist-NER is a named-entity recognition dataset focused on drug-related text, containing token-level annotations for pharmaceutical entities (e.g., drug names, dosages, formulations, adverse events and related attributes) in unstructured drug-domain documents. It is formatted for supervised NER training with standard BIO labels and split into train/validation/test subsets to facilitate model development and evaluation. The dataset is intended for tasks such as pharmacovigilance, drug labeling extraction, and biomedical literature mining to enable accurate extraction of structured drug information from free text.

drugtemist-en-75-ner is an English named-entity recognition dataset containing token-level/entity-span annotations across texts for 75 fine-grained entity types focused on drug- and treatment-related concepts. It is designed to train and evaluate supervised NER models that must distinguish a wide range of pharmacological and clinical entities (e.g., drug names, formulations, dosages, adverse events, procedures, and related concepts), enabling development and benchmarking of high-resolution biomedical NER systems.

root_b: rodrigo1771 combined train distemist dev 85 ner
desc: Combined-train-distemist-dev-85-ner is a labeled corpus for supervised named-entity recognition in the clinical/biomedical domain, created by merging training data from the DISTEMIST collection with a designated development split (dev-85) to form a larger training set. It contains clinical texts annotated with entity spans and class labels (e.g., medical conditions, medications, procedures), formatted for token- or span-level NER model training and evaluation. The dataset is intended to support development and benchmarking of sequence labeling models, domain adaptation experiments, and improvements in clinical information extraction for Spanish-language medical texts.

root_b: rodrigo1771 combined train drugtemist dev 85 ner
desc: combined-train-drugtemist-dev-85-ner is a biomedical named entity recognition (NER) dataset that aggregates drug-related corpora into a combined training set with a held-out development split of 85 examples. It provides token-level entity annotations for drug- and chemistry-related mentions (e.g., medications, compounds, dosages and related biomedical terms) in a standard NER labeling scheme (e.g., BIO), suitable for supervised training and validation. The dataset is intended for developing and evaluating NER models for pharmacological text mining, clinical information extraction, and related biomedical NLP tasks.

Rodrigo1771/symptemist-fasttext-75-ner is a labeled named-entity recognition dataset for extracting symptom-related mentions from health-oriented text. Each example pairs token sequences with BIO-style NER labels and precomputed 75-dimensional fastText token embeddings, and is provided with standard train/validation/test splits for supervised training and evaluation. The dataset is intended for benchmarking embedding-based sequence-tagging models on symptom detection and related entity extraction in clinical notes or health-related social media.

symptemist-fasttext-85-ner is a token-level named entity recognition dataset for extracting symptom and clinical-related entities from text. Each example includes sentences with BIO entity annotations alongside FastText-85 token embeddings (precomputed 85-dimensional FastText vectors) to streamline model input. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating sequence-labeling models for symptom extraction and related clinical NER tasks, enabling rapid experimentation with FastText-based representations.

Rodrigo1771/drugtemist-en-fasttext-75-ner is an English named-entity recognition dataset focused on drug and medication mentions, provided with token-level NER annotations and accompanying FastText 75-dimensional word embeddings. It is intended for training and evaluating supervised NER models in the pharmaceutical/biomedical domain, enabling experiments that leverage pretrained FastText features for improved representations and faster convergence when extracting drug-related entities.

WikiAnn Arabic is the Arabic portion of the WikiAnn multilingual named entity recognition dataset, automatically annotated (silver-standard) from Wikipedia/Wikidata links. It provides token-level entity span annotations in Arabic for three coarse classes (PER, ORG, LOC), formatted for sequence-labeling tasks. The corpus is large-scale and noisy due to automatic annotation, making it useful for training and evaluating Arabic NER models and for cross-lingual transfer and low-resource research.

dataset_node: Custom dataset - formato BIO␟Named Entity Recognition
desc: Custom dataset - formato BIO is a token-level annotated corpus formatted using the BIO tagging scheme (Begin, Inside, Outside) for sequence labeling tasks such as named entity recognition, chunking, or slot filling. Each sentence is tokenized with one token-per-line and a blank line separating sentences; tokens are paired with BIO tags that indicate entity boundaries and types (custom-defined). The dataset is intended for supervised model training and evaluation (e.g., BiLSTM-CRF, Transformer-based NER), is compatible with common toolchains that accept BIO input, and supports standard metrics like precision, recall, and F1 for entity-level evaluation.

desc: arrow is a dataset of arrow symbols collected across diverse scenes and styles, annotated for tasks such as detection, segmentation and orientation estimation. It includes varied arrow shapes, sizes, rotations, occlusions and backgrounds to encourage robustness to visual variability. Designed for training and evaluating models on directional symbol recognition, pose/orientation recovery and scene understanding, arrow is useful for applications in sign interpretation, HCI, robotics and navigation.

plo_dunfiltered_config is a collection of raw, unfiltered configuration snapshots captured from the PLO service across environments. Each sample contains timestamped configuration files and key–value entries (JSON/YAML/text) plus metadata, preserving real-world noise, duplicates, and partial or malformed entries. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating models for configuration anomaly detection, change prediction, root-cause analysis, and automated configuration repair or synthesis in production-like settings.

ChnSentiCorp is a Chinese sentiment analysis dataset designed for classifying the polarity of textual reviews into positive, negative, or neutral categories. It consists of a large collection of Chinese product and service reviews, providing a diverse and realistic corpus for training and evaluating sentiment classification models. The dataset is particularly valuable for developing and benchmarking pre-trained language models in low-resource, Chinese-language NLP tasks. It has been widely used to assess the performance of models such as BERT, RoBERTa, and MacBERT, with evaluations conducted using standard metrics like accuracy, F1-score, and precision. Due to its domain-specific nature and linguistic characteristics, ChnSentiCorp supports fine-grained sentiment analysis and helps improve model generalization in real-world Chinese text. The dataset reflects the challenges of domain variability, noise, and class imbalance common in user-generated content, making it a critical resource for advancing

article100v1_wikigold_split is a small benchmark for keyphrase extraction consisting of 100 English Wikipedia articles paired with gold-standard (WikiGold) keyphrase annotations, provided in a train/validation/test split. Each entry contains the article text and its manually annotated keyphrases, enabling supervised training, evaluation, and ranking of keyphrase extraction and assignment models. Its compact size makes it suitable for benchmarking, ablation studies, and few‑shot or transfer-learning experiments.

article100v3_wikigold_split is a curated benchmark of 100 Wikipedia articles paired with human-annotated gold keyphrases from the WikiGold corpus, provided in a standardized train/validation/test split (v3). It supplies full article text along with reference keyphrase sets to support supervised training and evaluation of keyphrase extraction, content-selection, and short-form summarization models. The split is intended for reproducible comparison of models on keyword/keyphrase prediction and related information‑retrieval tasks.

article250v5_wikigold_split is a benchmark dataset for supervised keyphrase extraction and generation. It pairs Wikipedia article texts truncated to 250 tokens with human-annotated keyphrases from the WikiGold corpus. Version 5 applies standardized preprocessing (tokenization and normalization) and provides predefined train/validation/test splits. The dataset is suited for training and evaluating extractive tagging, sequence-to-sequence generation, and ranking models, and is typically evaluated with precision/recall/F1 or generation-oriented metrics.

article500v3_wikigold_split is a benchmark dataset of 500 Wikipedia articles paired with gold-standard human summaries and a predefined train/validation/test split (v3). It is designed for development and evaluation of extractive and abstractive document summarization models, supporting supervised training, evaluation of summary quality, and comparison across methods. The dataset emphasizes real-world encyclopedic content and stable splits to enable reproducible experiments and metric-based benchmarking.

tagged_one50v1_wikigold_split is a token-level sequence-labeling benchmark derived from the WikiGold corpus. It provides sentences with gold-standard annotations using the one50v1 tagset (BIO-style) organized into a standardized train/validation/test split. The dataset is intended for supervised training and evaluation of named-entity and other sequence-tagging models, enabling reproducible benchmarking on Wikipedia-derived text.

tagged_one50v2_wikigold_split is a token-level sequence-labeling dataset derived from Wikipedia text, with each token annotated with linguistic tags and arranged according to the WikiGold evaluation split. It is intended for supervised training and benchmarking of sequence models (e.g., POS tagging, NER, chunking) on realistic wiki-domain language. The split provides standard train/validation/test partitions to facilitate reproducible evaluation and comparison of tagging systems.

tagged_uni500v3_wikigold_split is a token-level tagged corpus derived from the Uni500 v3 collection and split following the WikiGold partitioning. It provides annotated mentions with named-entity labels and (where available) canonical Wikipedia links, organized into train/dev/test splits for supervised learning. The dataset is intended for benchmarking sequence-labeling and entity-disambiguation models (NER and entity linking), enabling evaluation with standard precision/recall/F1 metrics on real-world Wikipedia-derived text.

i2b22014 is a de-identified clinical-text corpus released for the 2014 i2b2 shared tasks, consisting of electronic health record narratives (e.g., discharge summaries) manually annotated for clinical concepts, their attributes, and inter-concept relations (including temporal information). It is designed to support supervised learning and evaluation of clinical NLP systems for tasks such as named entity recognition, relation extraction, assertion/status classification, and temporal ordering, serving as a benchmark for extracting structured information from EHR narratives while preserving patient privacy.

invoice_layoutlmv3 is a dataset of invoice images paired with OCR transcriptions, token-level bounding boxes, and field-level annotations for key entities (e.g., vendor, invoice number, dates, totals, addresses, and line items). It is designed for layout-aware document information extraction and key–value parsing, enabling training and evaluation of multimodal transformers like LayoutLMv3. The collection covers diverse invoice templates and visual conditions to benchmark robust layout analysis, entity recognition, and end-to-end document understanding systems.

biocreative_gene_mention is a annotated corpus of biomedical text for gene/protein named entity recognition, derived from MEDLINE abstracts as part of the BioCreative challenge. It provides sentence-level texts with span annotations marking gene and protein mentions, enabling supervised training and evaluation of NER models in the biomedical domain. The dataset targets common challenges of biomedical entity recognition—ambiguous names, synonyms, abbreviations, and domain-specific morphology—and is commonly used for benchmarking entity detection, downstream normalization, and information extraction workflows.

data_registros_layoutv3 is a document-layout dataset of scanned or photographed records annotated with layout elements (bounding boxes/polygons and class labels for fields, labels, tables, lines, etc.). It pairs page images with structured layout annotations to support supervised training and evaluation of layout detection, semantic segmentation, table/field extraction, and form understanding models. The dataset is intended for developing end-to-end document parsing and information-extraction systems applied to record-keeping, archival, and administrative documents.

kh_pos is a dataset for Khmer part-of-speech tagging, comprising Khmer sentences tokenized and annotated with token-level POS tags. It is intended for supervised sequence-labeling research and evaluation, enabling training and benchmarking of POS taggers, morphological analyzers, and downstream Khmer NLP systems. Data are provided as sentence-aligned token/POS pairs in standard formats to facilitate reproducible experiments on a low-resource language.

cne-layoutlmv3-data is a curated multimodal document dataset for training and evaluating LayoutLMv3-style models. It pairs document images with OCR-extracted text, token-level bounding boxes, and structured annotations (layout categories, entity labels, and key–value relations) to support document parsing and information extraction. The dataset is intended for tasks such as form/receipt key–value extraction, entity recognition, and layout-aware classification, enabling supervised fine-tuning and benchmarking of visual–textual transformer models for real-world document understanding.

cne-layoutlmv3 is a Chinese document understanding dataset for training and evaluating LayoutLMv3-style multimodal models on named entity recognition and information extraction. It pairs document images with OCR-extracted tokens, token-level bounding boxes, and entity labels, enabling models to learn joint visual–layout–text representations. The dataset is intended for supervised training and benchmarking of layout-aware NER, key information extraction, and other document-level extraction tasks across diverse Chinese document types.

bgglue is a Bulgarian language understanding benchmark modeled after GLUE, providing a suite of diverse NLP tasks (e.g., text classification, natural language inference, paraphrase detection, named entity recognition, and reading comprehension) with standardized train/dev/test splits and evaluation metrics. It enables consistent evaluation and comparison of Bulgarian and multilingual language models on core semantic and sequence-labeling problems, supporting research on fine-tuning, transfer learning, robustness, and cross-domain generalization for Bulgarian.

TLUnified is a large-scale, multi-source dataset for traffic-light perception in driving environments. It provides images and video frames annotated with bounding boxes, light-state labels (e.g., red/yellow/green/off/blinking), and temporal IDs across diverse weather, lighting and viewpoint conditions. TLUnified supports training and evaluation of detection, state classification, segmentation and tracking models for autonomous driving and traffic-signal analytics.

LayoutLMv3 is a multimodal document dataset and pretraining corpus that pairs scanned document images with token-level OCR, 2D layout coordinates, and visual features to enable unified modeling of text, layout, and appearance. It is designed to support pretraining and fine-tuning of transformer-based document-understanding models and covers diverse document types and annotations for tasks such as form/key‑value extraction, document classification, and visual question answering. The dataset facilitates learning spatial-textual-visual representations for robust information extraction and layout-aware document understanding.

indonlu_nergrit is an Indonesian named-entity recognition dataset in the IndoNLU benchmark containing token-level annotations (BIO/IOB) for entity types such as PERSON, LOCATION, ORGANIZATION, and MISC. It is intended for training and evaluating sequence-labeling models on Indonesian text, enabling benchmarking of NER performance and model generalization in downstream Indonesian NLP tasks.

plod-cw is a benchmark dataset for object detection and robustness research that emphasizes cross-weather (cw) variability. It contains high-resolution outdoor images annotated with bounding boxes and class labels across common object categories, sampled under diverse conditions such as rain, fog, low light, and glare, with abundant occlusions and scale variation. The dataset provides standardized train/validation/test splits and evaluation protocols to support development and comparison of detectors, domain-adaptation methods, and robustness-focused architectures.

shipping_label_ner is a dataset of shipping-label texts (with optional scanned label images) annotated for named-entity recognition. It provides OCR-extracted transcriptions with span-level labels for common shipping entities—sender and recipient names and addresses, company, tracking/airway-bill numbers, postal codes and countries, phone numbers, dates, package weight/dimensions, service type, and reference/invoice IDs. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating sequence-tagging and document-level information-extraction models for logistics automation, enabling robust entity extraction from noisy OCR output and varied label layouts.

datasetprepfrom_gcp is a standardized, preprocessed dataset exported from Google Cloud Platform designed to accelerate reproducible ML experiments and benchmarking. It contains raw inputs transformed into a consistent schema with cleaning, normalization, and feature engineering applied, accompanied by metadata and provenance from the GCP export. The package includes predefined train/validation/test splits and common storage formats (e.g., CSV, TFRecord) so models can be trained and evaluated out-of-the-box. It is suitable for pipeline testing and benchmarking across supervised tasks where labels are provided, and for validating end-to-end cloud-to-model workflows.

wild is a dataset of images captured in unconstrained, real-world conditions intended to benchmark model robustness and generalization. It contains diverse scenes with varying lighting, weather, viewpoints, motion blur and occlusion to reflect practical deployment challenges. Annotated for common vision tasks (e.g., classification, detection, segmentation), wild supports evaluation of algorithms under natural domain shifts and encourages development of models resilient to real-world variability.

uner_cro_set is a dataset for image cropping and thumbnail generation that pairs full-resolution images with multiple human-annotated crop candidates and associated aesthetic/utility quality scores. Designed for supervised learning and evaluation of automatic cropping, ranking, and region-proposal models, it covers diverse scenes, aspect ratios, and object scales to encourage robust generalization. The dataset supports development and benchmarking of composition-aware cropping algorithms, thumbnail selection, and data-augmentation strategies that preserve salient content.

UNER English EWT is a token-level named-entity annotation of the Universal Dependencies English Web Treebank (EWT). It provides BIO-style entity labels mapped to a universal/fine-grained NER tagset and aligned to UD tokenization for web and user-generated text. The corpus is intended for training and evaluating NER and sequence-labeling models, and for UD-aligned experiments in information extraction and cross-lingual transfer.

uner_por_bos is a bilingual named‑entity recognition (NER) dataset for Portuguese (por) and Bosnian (bos). It contains tokenized sentences annotated with BIO entity labels (e.g., PERSON, LOCATION, ORGANIZATION, MISC) for supervised sequence labeling. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating NER models and for cross‑lingual transfer and multilingual representation experiments, provided in a CoNLL‑style format with standard train/dev/test splits.

anno_ctr is a dataset of object center annotations designed for training and evaluating center-based localization and counting models. Each entry pairs an image with precise pixel coordinates of object centers (and optional class/visibility tags), enabling supervised learning of center regression, heatmap prediction, and density estimation. It supports benchmarking keypoint-driven detectors, crowd counting, and lightweight localization methods, focusing evaluation on center localization and counting accuracy.

CarD-T-NER is a benchmark dataset for named entity recognition in the automotive domain. It comprises transcribed driver–assistant dialogues and vehicle service reports annotated with domain-specific entity types (e.g., vehicle_make, model, part, fault, service_action, location, date/time). Capturing conversational and technical language, abbreviations, and noisy transcription artifacts, the dataset supports training and evaluation of NER models for in-car assistants, diagnostic tools, and domain-adaptation research.

Rodrigo1771/drugtemist-en-ner is an English named‑entity recognition dataset of drug-related text, with span-level annotations for drug mentions and related biomedical entities (e.g., active ingredients, brand names, formulations, dosages). It is intended for supervised training and evaluation of NER models for pharmacovigilance, biomedical information extraction, and clinical NLP. The data is provided in a token-level sequence-labeling-friendly format (commonly IOB/BIO) and is suitable for fine-tuning and benchmarking transformer and sequence models on drug-focused entity extraction tasks.

symptemist-75-ner is a span-annotated named-entity recognition corpus focused on symptoms and related clinical concepts, with a fine-grained ontology of 75 entity categories. The dataset provides token/span-level annotations suitable for supervised training and evaluation of NER models in biomedical and patient-reported text. It is intended for benchmarking and developing systems for automated symptom identification, clinical text mining, and downstream tasks such as relation extraction and decision support.

symptemist-85-ner is a small annotated corpus for symptom named‑entity recognition that contains span-level labels for symptom mentions in short clinical or consumer-health texts. The dataset provides token-level BIO tags and character offsets for each symptom entity, making it suitable for training and evaluating NER models that extract symptom mentions from medical notes, patient-reported text, or social-media health posts. It is intended as a lightweight benchmark for model development, error analysis, and transfer learning in clinical NLP.

Symptemist-9-NER is a named-entity recognition dataset annotated with nine entity classes focused on symptoms and related clinical concepts. It provides text spans labeled for these classes to support supervised sequence-labeling model training and evaluation in health-related NLP. The corpus is intended for tasks such as symptom extraction, clinical information retrieval, and downstream relation extraction or normalization, serving as a benchmark for fine-grained clinical entity recognition.

Rodrigo1771/cantemist-85-ner is a Spanish clinical named‑entity recognition dataset drawn from the CANTEMIST corpus, containing 85 annotated clinical case reports. It provides token‑level annotations (commonly in BIO format) for oncology‑related entities (e.g., tumor mentions and related clinical concepts), formatted for supervised training and evaluation of NER and information‑extraction models in the biomedical/clinical domain. The dataset supports development and benchmarking of models for entity identification, clinical text understanding, and downstream tasks such as normalization and relation extraction.

distemist-85-ner is a Spanish clinical named‑entity recognition dataset derived from the DISTEMIST collection. It contains clinical texts with token‑level span annotations for medical concepts (e.g., diseases, symptoms, treatments and anatomical terms), formatted for sequence‑labeling NER models. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating supervised NER systems and benchmarking information extraction from Spanish clinical narratives.

DrugTemist-85-NER is a named entity recognition dataset focused on drug-related text, containing token-level span annotations for entities such as medication names, dosages, routes, frequencies, and adverse effects. It is provided in a BIO-style labeling format suitable for supervised training and evaluation of sequence labeling models and transformer-based NER systems. The dataset is intended for research and benchmarking in biomedical information extraction, pharmacovigilance, and automated structuring of drug-related clinical or literature text.

Rodrigo1771/symptemist-fasttext-8-ner is a token-level named entity recognition dataset focused on symptom and medical mention extraction. Each example contains tokenized text annotated with entity labels in a common sequence-labeling format (e.g., BIO/IOB) and comes with precomputed 8-dimensional FastText embeddings for each token. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating supervised NER models and for experimenting with feature-based or embedding-augmented sequence-labeling approaches in clinical or symptom-focused information extraction.

symptemist-fasttext-9-ner is a named-entity recognition dataset of clinical/medical texts annotated for nine entity categories (symptoms and related clinical concepts) and preprocessed for use with fastText-style token-level training. It provides tokenized sentences with corresponding entity labels in a fastText-compatible format, enabling supervised training and evaluation of NER models for symptom extraction and clinical information retrieval. The dataset is suitable for benchmarking entity-level precision/recall/F1 and for developing pipelines for clinical text mining, cohort selection, and downstream diagnostic support.

drugtemist-it-fasttext-8-ner is an Italian named-entity recognition dataset focused on drug- and pharmaceutical-related text. It provides token-level NER annotations (e.g., drug names, dosages, formulations) and includes precomputed fastText-8 embedding features to simplify model input. The dataset is intended for supervised training and evaluation of sequence-labeling models in Italian biomedical and pharmaceutical domains.

Rodrigo1771/drugtemist-it-fasttext-9-ner is an Italian-language named‑entity recognition dataset focused on drug- and medication-related text. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating sequence-labeling models and domain-adapted NER systems in pharmaceutical and clinical Italian text.

Rodrigo1771/drugtemist-en-fasttext-9-ner is an English named‑entity recognition dataset focused on drug and pharmacology–related text. Each example provides tokenized sentences with BIO-style entity annotations across nine entity classes plus precomputed fastText token features, making it suitable for training and evaluating sequence‑labeling models that leverage subword/embedding inputs. The resource is useful for research in biomedical/drug entity extraction, embedding‑based NER architectures, and domain adaptation experiments.

Rodrigo1771/distemist-fasttext-75-ner is a token-level named-entity recognition dataset that pairs annotated tokens with precomputed 75-dimensional FastText embeddings. Designed for supervised sequence-labeling experiments, it enables training and evaluation of NER models that consume embedding features (feature-based or neural) without requiring users to generate embeddings themselves. The dataset is useful for rapid prototyping, embedding ablation studies, and lightweight token-classification workflows.

DrugTemist-fasttext-75-ner is a token-level named-entity recognition dataset for detecting drug-related entities in text. Each example includes tokenized text with BIO-formatted entity labels and precomputed 75-dimensional FastText embeddings for tokens, along with standard train/validation/test splits. Rodrigo1771/cantemist-fasttext-75-ner is a Spanish clinical named-entity recognition dataset derived from the CANTEMIST oncology corpus, preprocessed for sequence-labeling experiments using 75-dimensional FastText word embeddings. It contains cancer-related clinical texts annotated with entity spans (tumor and related biomedical mentions) along with token-level labels and corresponding FastText vector representations, enabling rapid training of supervised NER models. The dataset is suitable for evaluating and benchmarking NER architectures on Spanish medical language, domain adaptation with subword embeddings, and experiments that leverage precomputed dense token features to accelerate model development.

Mountain-NER-Dataset is a domain-specific named entity recognition corpus focused on mountains and related geographic and trip-planning information. It contains natural-language text (e.g., guidebooks, trip reports, Wikipedia entries) annotated with labels such as PEAK, RANGE, PASS, TRAIL, PARK, LOCATION, ELEVATION, COUNTRY, COORDINATES, DATE, and PERSON. The dataset is intended to train and evaluate NER models for extracting structured mountain-related facts for applications like GIS population, route planning, travel assistants, and domain adaptation research. It provides a challenging benchmark for entity disambiguation and relation-aware extraction in a geospatial outdoor domain.

orchid_corpus is a curated multi-modal dataset of orchid observations comprising high-resolution images paired with species labels and accompanying metadata (captions, collection location, date, and morphological notes). It is designed for fine-grained visual recognition, species identification, and multi-modal retrieval or captioning tasks, supporting supervised learning and evaluation of biodiversity monitoring models. The corpus enables research on domain adaptation, few-shot classification, and automated phenology or distribution analysis for plant conservation and ecological studies.

MasakhaNER is a multilingual named entity recognition dataset for multiple low-resource African languages. It contains human-annotated text labeled with standard entity categories (PERSON, LOCATION, ORGANIZATION, MISC) and provides train/dev/test splits for supervised training and evaluation. datasaur-dev/datasaur-MTFiZjUwM2Q-ZWJiZDRmNGI is a human-annotated text dataset exported from the Datasaur annotation platform. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating models that require structured, human-verified text labels and for benchmarking annotation quality and inter-annotator agreement in document labeling workflows.

VN-SLU Augmented Dataset is a Vietnamese spoken language understanding corpus of utterances annotated with intent labels and slot/sequence tags, enriched with synthetic and augmented variants (e.g., paraphrasing, back-translation, noise injection, and TTS→ASR reconstructions) to increase lexical and acoustic diversity. It covers multiple conversational domains and is designed for training and evaluating intent classification, slot filling, joint SLU and end-to-end ASR+NLU models, with an emphasis on robustness and generalization in low-resource Vietnamese settings.

Resume NER is a dataset of resumes annotated for named entity recognition, labeling tokens with entities such as NAME, EMAIL, PHONE, ADDRESS, EDUCATION, DEGREE, UNIVERSITY, SKILL, JOB_TITLE, COMPANY, DURATION, and CERTIFICATION. It is designed to train and evaluate sequence-labeling models for resume parsing, candidate profiling, automated CV screening, and anonymization, with token-level BIO-formatted annotations suitable for common NER frameworks.

xtreme_en is the English portion of the XTREME evaluation suite, providing English splits of diverse NLP tasks (classification, structured prediction, question answering, and sentence retrieval) drawn from the XTREME benchmark (e.g., XNLI, PAWS-X, POS tagging, NER, XQuAD/MLQA/TyDiQA, BUCC, Tatoeba). It is intended to measure model performance on core English tasks and to serve as a reference point for cross-lingual transfer experiments by comparing monolingual and multilingual models under shared task formulations.

wikigold_splits is a standardized split of the WikiGold corpus providing predefined train/validation/test partitions of Wikipedia sentences annotated with entity mention spans and their links to canonical Wikipedia entities. It is intended for supervised training and reproducible evaluation of named entity recognition and entity linking systems, supporting tasks such as mention detection, entity disambiguation, and end-to-end entity resolution.

article50v0_wikigold_split is a curated split of Wikipedia articles paired with gold-standard reference summaries (Wikigold) and predefined train/validation/test partitions (version v0). The dataset is intended for training and benchmarking extractive and abstractive summarization models and for reproducible evaluation on encyclopedic text.

article50v1_wikigold_split is a derived split of the WikiGold keyphrase extraction dataset. It provides Wikipedia article-level instances in the article50 v1 format (articles normalized to 50-token windows) paired with gold-standard keyphrase annotations and standard train/validation/test partitions. The split is intended for supervised keyphrase extraction, phrase ranking, and evaluation of information retrieval or short-form summarization models on Wikipedia content.

article50v2_wikigold_split is an extractive summarization benchmark derived from WikiGold: Wikipedia articles paired with human-annotated sentence-level relevance labels. The article50 v2 split provides predefined train/validation/test partitions for reproducible evaluation. Each example contains full article text and gold sentence selections, making the dataset suitable for training and evaluating sentence-ranking, salience-detection, and extractive summarization models using standard metrics (e.g., ROUGE, precision/recall).

article50v3_wikigold_split is a split of the WikiGold corpus containing Wikipedia articles paired with human-annotated gold summaries (sentence-level reference labels). The "article50v3" configuration structures input articles into 50-unit contexts and provides standard train/validation/test splits, enabling supervised training and evaluation of extractive summarization and content-selection models on encyclopedic text.

article50v4_wikigold_split is a curated split that pairs the Article50 v4 collection of short Wikipedia article excerpts with the WikiGold human annotations. Each example contains an article excerpt and corresponding gold labels (keyphrases and/or extractive summary sentences), organized into standard train/validation/test splits. It is intended for supervised training and evaluation of keyphrase extraction, extractive summarization, and related information-retrieval or ranking models on compact, Wikipedia-derived texts.

article50v5_wikigold_split is a versioned benchmark derived from the WikiGold corpus that provides article-level train/validation/test splits for supervised keyphrase extraction and related document-level NLP tasks. It contains Wikipedia articles paired with human-curated WikiGold keyphrase annotations, organized according to the v5 split to enable consistent training and evaluation. The dataset is intended for developing and comparing models for keyphrase extraction, phrase labeling, and document summarization under realistic, article-scale conditions.

article50v6_wikigold_split is a benchmark dataset of Wikipedia article excerpts (each truncated to 50 tokens) paired with human-validated WikiGold annotations and provided as predefined train/validation/test splits. It supplies input–label pairs where the inputs are short article segments and the labels are gold-standard target segments or annotations from the WikiGold corpus, making it suitable for supervised tasks such as extractive summarization, sentence splitting/paraphrasing, and evaluation of content-selection models. The split enables consistent training and evaluation of models on concise, real-world encyclopedic text.

article50v7_wikigold_split is a sentence-level extractive summarization dataset built from Wikipedia articles segmented or truncated to 50-sentence units (version 7) with splits aligned to the WikiGold annotation scheme. Each example pairs article text with gold-standard sentence labels indicating salient sentences for summarization, enabling supervised training and evaluation of sentence scoring, selection, and ranking models. It provides standardized train/validation/test splits for reproducible benchmarking on Wikipedia-style content and is suitable for developing and comparing extractive summarizers and content-selection methods.

article50v8_wikigold_split is a curated Wikipedia-based corpus of fixed-length (50-unit) article segments paired with WikiGold human reference annotations and provided train/validation/test splits. It is designed for supervised research on extractive summarization, sentence selection and importance/keyphrase labeling, enabling reproducible evaluation of content-selection and retrieval models on encyclopedic text.

article50v9_wikigold_split is a benchmark collection of 50 Wikipedia articles (v9) with gold-standard keyphrase annotations aligned to the WikiGold protocol and partitioned into predefined train/validation/test splits. It provides raw article text together with ground-truth keyphrases to support supervised evaluation of keyphrase extraction, phrase-level retrieval, topic detection, and document-level summarization models, enabling reproducible comparisons across methods.

article100v0_wikigold_split is a supervised NLP benchmark of 100 Wikipedia articles aligned with WikiGold human annotations and precomputed train/validation/test splits. article100v2_wikigold_split is a dataset of 100 Wikipedia articles paired with human-curated, gold-standard keyphrase annotations from the WikiGold corpus. article100v4_wikigold_split is a curated benchmark (version 4) of 100 Wikipedia articles aligned with WikiGold human annotations and provided with predefined train/validation/test splits. article100v5_wikigold_split is a benchmark split of 100 Wikipedia articles (version 5) annotated with WikiGold gold-standard keyphrases. article100v6_wikigold_split is a benchmark split of 100 Wikipedia articles (v6) paired with WikiGold gold-standard annotations of important phrases. article100v7_wikigold_split is a small benchmark corpus of 100 articles (version 7) manually annotated with gold-standard mention spans and corresponding Wikipedia entity links, provided with predefined train/validation/test splits. article100v8_wikigold_split is a small benchmark of 100 Wikipedia articles (version 8 release) paired with WikiGold gold‑standard keyphrase annotations and provided as train/validation/test splits. article100v9_wikigold_split is a benchmark corpus of 100 Wikipedia articles (version 9) annotated with gold-standard WikiGold labels and provided with predefined train/validation/test splits. article250v0_wikigold_split is a benchmark dataset of Wikipedia articles truncated to 250 tokens (v0) paired with WikiGold gold-standard summaries or sentence-level annotations. article250v1_wikigold_split is a text simplification dataset consisting of Wikipedia articles truncated to 250 tokens paired with human-written simplified references from the WikiGold corpus, provided with train/validation/test splits. article250v2_wikigold_split is a curated dataset of 250 Wikipedia articles aligned with WikiGold gold‑standard annotations and predefined train/validation/test splits. article250v3_wikigold_split is a preprocessed benchmark of Wikipedia articles paired with WikiGold gold-standard keyphrase annotations. article250v4_wikigold_split is a compact benchmark of 250 Wikipedia articles (v4) annotated with gold-standard span-level entity mentions and resolved Wikipedia identifiers, partitioned into train/validation/test according to the WikiGold split. article250v6_wikigold_split is a sentence-level extractive summarization dataset derived from Wikipedia articles with human salience annotations from the WikiGold corpus. article250v7_wikigold_split is a text dataset of Wikipedia-derived articles truncated to 250 words (version 7) with gold-standard keyphrase annotations aligned to the WikiGold split. article250v8_wikigold_split is a curated dataset of Wikipedia articles aligned with WikiGold human annotations, provided as a version‑8 release with predefined train/validation/test splits. article250v9_wikigold_split is a small benchmark of 250 Wikipedia articles (version 9) partitioned according to the WikiGold splitting protocol. article500v0_wikigold_split is a benchmark dataset of 500 Wikipedia articles paired with gold-standard human annotations from the WikiGold corpus, provided as a predefined train/validation/test split (version v0). article500v1_wikigold_split is a benchmark dataset of 500 Wikipedia articles paired with gold-standard WikiGold keyphrase annotations and a predefined train/validation/test split. article500v2_wikigold_split is a benchmark dataset for supervised keyphrase extraction and generation. article500v4_wikigold_split is a curated NLP benchmark of 500 Wikipedia articles (version 4) annotated with WikiGold-style, human‑verified keyphrase/phrase-level labels and provided with predefined train/validation/test splits. article500v5_wikigold_split is a dataset of 500 Wikipedia articles with human-annotated gold keyphrases, provided as version v5 with pre-defined train/validation/test splits aligned to the WikiGold evaluation setup. article500v8_wikigold_split is a curated corpus of 500 Wikipedia articles (v8) paired with WikiGold human annotations and predefined train/validation/test splits. article500v9_wikigold_split is a dataset of 500 Wikipedia articles with manually curated gold-standard keyphrase annotations, organized according to the WikiGold train/validation/test split conventions. tagged_one50v0_wikigold_split is a token-level sequence-labeling dataset derived from the WikiGold corpus. tagged_one100v0_wikigold_split is a labeled dataset derived from the WikiGold corpus, providing gold-standard token-level named entity annotations with a predefined train/validation/test split.
