It groups scientific documents into topical clusters (based on arXiv subject labels) using paper text (titles/abstracts and metadata), providing many classes and fine-grained, domain-specific vocabulary. The dataset tests models’ ability to produce embeddings that separate closely related scientific topics and to support downstream clustering and topic-assignment tasks in scholarly text domains.

MTEB AskUbuntuDupQuestions is a dataset of question pairs drawn from the Ask Ubuntu Stack Exchange, annotated for duplicate relationships. It provides user-written technical questions and labels indicating whether pairs are duplicates, making it suitable for evaluating semantic similarity, duplicate detection, retrieval, and reranking of QA content. The dataset is useful for benchmarking embedding models and retrieval systems on domain-specific paraphrase and semantic equivalence in technical support contexts.

MTEB MindSmallReranking (default) is a reranking benchmark derived from the MIND news recommendation corpus. It provides queries (user contexts or headlines) paired with a small set of candidate news articles and relevance labels for supervised ranking. The dataset is intended to evaluate embedding-based retrieval and reranking models (bi-encoders and cross-encoders) using ranking metrics such as NDCG and MRR in a news-domain relevance setting.

MTEB BSARDRetrieval (default) is a retrieval benchmark in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) that provides query–document pairs with relevance labels under the default task configuration. It evaluates embedding models’ ability to retrieve and rank semantically relevant items, using standard retrieval metrics (e.g., recall@k, MRR). The dataset is intended for assessing and comparing embedding-based semantic search and ranking performance.

BiorxivClusteringP2P is a clustering benchmark from the MTEB suite consisting of bioRxiv preprints (titles/abstracts) organized into topical clusters. It evaluates embedding models’ ability to group semantically related biomedical papers (paper-to-paper clustering) using unsupervised clustering metrics such as NMI and ARI. The dataset targets biomedical and life-science language understanding, enabling assessment of embeddings for topic discovery, literature organization, and downstream biomedical retrieval tasks.

BiorxivClusteringS2S is a dataset of bioRxiv scientific abstracts grouped into topical clusters for evaluating sequence-to-sequence and embedding-based clustering methods within the MTEB benchmark. It provides domain-specific, semantically related text instances to measure an embedding model’s ability to group and separate research topics (e.g., via clustering metrics such as NMI or purity) and to assess semantic representation quality on scientific language. The dataset targets realistic challenges of domain vocabulary, topical overlap, and fine-grained distinctions common in biomedical literature.

MTEB BlurbsClusteringP2P (default) is a benchmark dataset of short, informal text blurbs annotated with cluster labels for evaluating embedding models’ ability to group semantically similar microtexts. Designed for clustering and pairwise similarity evaluation within the MTEB suite, it emphasizes compact, noisy, real-world language (e.g., social posts, product blurbs) to test robustness of representations on fine-grained topical grouping. The default configuration provides canonical train/validation/test splits and metrics for clustering quality (e.g., NMI, ARI) and pairwise retrieval, enabling standardized comparison of embedding and clustering methods.

MTEB BlurbsClusteringS2S (default) is a benchmark of short textual blurbs grouped into semantic clusters, presented in a sequence-to-sequence format. Each example pairs a blurb with a target cluster identifier or canonical cluster description, enabling evaluation of models on mapping short texts to their semantic groupings. It is intended to assess embedding quality, cluster-aware retrieval and generation, and a model’s ability to produce cluster labels or representative descriptions from concise inputs.

MTEB CLSClusteringP2P (default) is a benchmark task from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that evaluates embedding models on clustering-driven classification using pairwise point-to-point relationships. The task provides labeled text instances and measures how well embeddings group semantically similar items into clusters and support cluster-based label assignment, with evaluation using clustering and pairwise classification metrics. It targets embedding compactness and separability, stressing performance of unsupervised or nearest-neighbor style downstream methods in the default configuration.

MTEB CLSClusteringS2S (default) is a benchmark task from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that evaluates models’ ability to group semantically related texts using a sequence-to-sequence formulation. It provides collections of texts with cluster assignments expressed as target sequences, enabling evaluation of both S2S models and embedding+clustering pipelines. The task measures how well representations separate semantic clusters using clustering and classification metrics (e.g., NMI, ARI), and is useful for assessing semantic grouping, document organization, and downstream retrieval or summarization workflows.

MTEB CQADupStackAndroidRetrieval (default) is a retrieval benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark built on the CQADupStack Android Stack Exchange data. It provides a corpus of Android developer question posts, query sets, and relevance judgments that mark duplicate or semantically related questions, enabling evaluation of embedding and semantic-search models on domain-specific Q&A retrieval. It is suited for benchmarking embedding quality, nearest-neighbor retrieval, and duplicate-question detection in technical forum content.

MTEB CQADupstackEnglishRetrieval (default) is an English-language retrieval benchmark derived from the CQADupStack collection of StackExchange forum posts. It contains questions across multiple subforums with annotated duplicate or related question pairs, formatted as queries and candidate documents with ground-truth relevance. The set is designed to evaluate text embedding and semantic retrieval models on duplicate detection and ranking (e.g., recall, MRR) in real-world forum QA content.

MTEB CQADupStackGamingRetrieval is a retrieval dataset from the CQADupStack collection (Gaming Stack Exchange) included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains real user questions with labeled duplicate relationships, formatted for semantic search and duplicate-question retrieval tasks. The dataset evaluates embedding models on retrieval accuracy and ranking in a domain with colloquial and technical gaming vocabulary.

MTEB CQADupStackGisRetrieval (default) is a retrieval benchmark drawn from the CQADupStack GIS Stack Exchange subset, consisting of real user questions and labeled duplicate/relevant pairs. It is designed to evaluate embedding models and semantic search systems on duplicate-question retrieval in the geographic information systems domain, using question titles and bodies as query/document text. The dataset challenges models with domain-specific terminology and varied phrasing, supporting development and assessment of embedding-based retrieval, semantic similarity, and duplicate-detection methods.

MTEB CQADupstackMathematicaRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark derived from the CQADupStack collection for the Mathematica StackExchange. It provides user questions paired with candidate posts and duplicate/non-duplicate relevance labels to evaluate semantic search, duplicate detection, and embedding-based ranking. Included in MTEB’s default tasks, it is suited for assessing embedding and dense-retrieval models on technical Q&A content using ranking metrics such as MRR and nDCG.

MTEB CQADupstackPhysicsRetrieval (default) is a retrieval benchmark drawn from the Physics section of the CQADupStack corpus (Stack Exchange). It contains community Q&A posts and annotated duplicate/non-duplicate relationships, formatted for semantic search and duplicate-question retrieval evaluation. The dataset challenges embedding models with short, technical, domain-specific text and realistic paraphrases, making it suitable for assessing embeddings' ability to capture fine-grained semantic similarity in scientific Q&A contexts under the benchmark's default retrieval configuration.

MTEB CQADupstackProgrammersRetrieval (default) is a retrieval benchmark drawn from the CQADupStack collection of Stack Exchange posts, containing questions and their labeled duplicates from the Programmers community. It is designed to evaluate embedding models on semantic retrieval and duplicate-question identification by providing queries, candidate documents, and relevance labels. The dataset is used within MTEB to measure retrieval performance (e.g., MRR, Recall@k) for models producing dense text representations in a programming-domain QA setting.

CQADupStackRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark from MTEB built from Stack Exchange question threads, where queries are mapped to semantically equivalent or duplicate questions within a pool of candidate posts. It evaluates sentence- and document-level embedding models on duplicate detection and semantic retrieval in technical QA domains, using labeled positives per query to assess ranking and recall metrics. The dataset spans multiple Stack Exchange communities and is useful for benchmarking embedding quality on real-world, domain-specific question retrieval tasks.

MTEB CQADupStackStatsRetrieval is a retrieval-style subset of the CQADupStack collection derived from the Stack Exchange “stats” community, formatted for the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It provides real user questions as queries and corresponding forum posts as candidate documents with relevance judgments indicating duplicates or related answers. The dataset is intended to evaluate embedding models and retrieval systems on semantic search, duplicate-question detection, and ranking performance in a technical, domain-specific QA setting.

CQADupStackTexRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark built from the TeX/LaTeX subset of the CQADupStack question-pair corpus. It contains TeX Stack Exchange questions with labeled duplicate and non-duplicate relationships, formatted for retrieval/evaluation: given a query question, systems must retrieve semantically equivalent or related questions from a candidate set. The split targets evaluation of text embedding and ranking models on domain-specific technical Q&A retrieval and duplicate-question detection.

MTEB CQADupStackUnixRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark drawn from the CQADupStack collection (Unix forum) designed to evaluate embedding and semantic retrieval models on duplicate-question detection. Each example pairs a query question with a pool of candidate questions drawn from Unix StackExchange, with annotations indicating true duplicates. It targets tasks such as nearest-neighbor retrieval, ranking (Recall@k, MRR), and semantic search, and is useful for assessing embedding quality, retrieval effectiveness, and duplicate-question discovery in technical Q&A domains.

MTEB CQADupstackWebmastersRetrieval (default) is a retrieval benchmark drawn from the CQADupStack collection for the Webmasters Stack Exchange community. It provides forum questions and annotated duplicate relationships, formatted as query-to-document retrieval tasks for evaluating text embedding models on semantic similarity and duplicate-question detection. The default split supplies queries and candidate pools for k-NN retrieval, enabling evaluation with ranking and recall-based metrics on technical Q&A forum content.

MTEB CQADupstackWordpressRetrieval (default) is a retrieval benchmark drawn from the CQADupStack Wordpress forum subset, designed to evaluate semantic search and duplicate-question retrieval using text embeddings. It contains user questions as queries and a corpus of prior forum posts, with labeled duplicate or relevant pairs indicating ground-truth retrieval targets. The default configuration provides standard train/validation/test splits and retrieval metrics (e.g., MRR, Recall@k) for consistent embedding-model comparison. This dataset is suited for benchmarking and tuning dense retrieval, semantic search, and duplicate-detection systems on technical community Q&A content.

MTEB ClimateFEVER (default) is a climate-focused claim verification dataset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It pairs climate-related claims with candidate evidence passages labeled as supporting, refuting, or insufficient, enabling supervised evaluation of fact-checking and entailment. The dataset is intended to test embedding quality for evidence retrieval, semantic search, and domain-specific reasoning on climate science statements.

MTEB CmedqaRetrieval (default) is a medical-domain retrieval benchmark within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It pairs medical questions as queries with a corpus of candidate question–answer items annotated for relevance, enabling evaluation of embedding-based semantic search and ranking models. The dataset assesses retrieval accuracy, robustness to domain-specific language, and suitability of embeddings for downstream clinical QA, information retrieval, and decision-support applications.

MTEB CovidRetrieval (default) is a retrieval benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark containing COVID-19–related queries paired with labeled relevant documents or passages drawn from scientific and clinical texts. It is designed to evaluate embedding-based semantic search and dense retrieval models on domain-specific, high-recall information needs, using standard retrieval metrics (e.g., recall, MRR, nDCG). The dataset supports development and comparison of embedding models and retrieval pipelines for pandemic-era biomedical literature and question-driven discovery.

MTEB DBPedia (default) is a short-text classification dataset derived from DBpedia/Wikipedia, consisting of article titles or abstracts paired with ontology topic labels. It is used in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark to evaluate embedding quality on tasks such as k‑NN classification, semantic retrieval, and clustering, measuring how well embeddings capture topical and semantic distinctions in concise texts.

MTEB DuRetrieval (default) is a retrieval benchmark within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark focused on duplicate/semantically-equivalent retrieval. It provides query–candidate pairs with labeled positives (duplicates or paraphrases) and negatives, enabling evaluation of embedding-based dense retrieval and re-ranking systems. The task measures a model’s ability to bring semantically matching texts together and separate non-matching ones using metrics such as recall@k, MRR, and MAP, and covers diverse domains and language styles to assess generalization.

MTEB EcomRetrieval (default) is an e-commerce product retrieval dataset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark designed to evaluate semantic search and embedding-based retrieval models. It contains user queries paired with candidate product entries and relevance labels, enabling assessment of how well embeddings match search intent to product listings. The task focuses on ranking and retrieval performance in the commercial/product domain, typically measured with metrics like recall@k, MRR, and nDCG. This dataset is useful for benchmarking embedding models on product search, recommendation, and catalog matching scenarios.

MTEB FEVER (default) is a fact verification dataset adapted for embedding evaluation. It pairs natural-language claims with candidate evidence sentences extracted from Wikipedia and labels each claim as Supported, Refuted, or NotEnoughInfo. In the MTEB setup it is used to evaluate embedding-based retrieval and reranking—retrieving relevant evidence sentences for a claim and supporting downstream verification/classification—making it a benchmark for semantic search, dense retrieval, and factual-consistency of text embeddings.

FiQA2018 (MTEB default) is a financial-domain benchmark of short text snippets (e.g., news headlines, tweets, or sentences) annotated with continuous quality/informativeness scores and fine-grained sentiment/aspect labels from the FiQA shared task. It is used in MTEB as a regression-style evaluation to measure how well sentence embeddings capture subtle, domain-specific sentiment and relevance signals for scoring, ranking, and retrieval in finance. The dataset challenges models to produce representations that reflect nuanced financial semantics and informativeness in compact texts.

GeoreviewClusteringP2P (MTEB, default) is a benchmark dataset of place- or business-related text reviews organized by location IDs to evaluate text embeddings on clustering and pairwise retrieval tasks. It provides groups of reviews for the same geographic entity, enabling assessment of embedding quality for grouping similar reviews, nearest-neighbor retrieval, and cluster purity using pair-to-pair (P2P) metrics. The dataset is intended to test how well embedding models capture fine-grained semantic similarity in real-world, location-grounded user-generated text.

MTEB GerDaLIR (default) is a German-language retrieval benchmark within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It contains German queries and candidate documents or passages paired with relevance annotations to evaluate semantic search and dense retrieval embeddings. The dataset is designed to assess embedding quality for information retrieval tasks in German, emphasizing lexical variation, morphology, and domain-specific phrasing. It is useful for benchmarking and tuning multilingual and language-specific embedding models for search and ranking applications.

GermanDPR (default) is a German dense-passage retrieval benchmark in MTEB comprising user queries paired with relevant German Wikipedia passages and relevance labels. It is designed to evaluate and train dense embedding models for passage-level search and retrieval in German, supporting assessment of bi-encoder embeddings and reranking approaches for real-world open-domain QA and information retrieval tasks.

MTEB GermanQuAD-Retrieval is a German-language passage retrieval dataset derived from the GermanQuAD question-answering corpus, packaged for the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It provides German questions as queries paired with candidate passages and relevance labels, enabling evaluation of semantic search and embedding-based retrieval models. The dataset is used to benchmark embedding quality on retrieval metrics (e.g., recall, MRR) under MTEB’s default retrieval settings.

MTEB HALClusteringS2S (default) is a clustering benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark designed to evaluate sentence- and short-text embedding models on their ability to group semantically similar texts. The dataset provides texts labeled by cluster membership in a sequence-to-sequence format (input texts with associated cluster identifiers) using the standard MTEB preprocessing and splits. It is intended for measuring unsupervised or downstream clustering quality (e.g., ARI, NMI, F1) and comparing embedding representations on topical and semantic grouping tasks.

MTEB HotpotQA (default) is the HotpotQA multi-hop question-answering subset formatted for the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains multi-hop questions with corresponding answers and annotated supporting facts, requiring reasoning across multiple documents. The split is used to evaluate embedding models on retrieval and semantic matching tasks—assessing their ability to encode multi-step relationships, retrieve relevant passages, and support downstream QA or retrieval-augmented generation. It serves as a benchmark for measuring embedding quality in multi-document reasoning and dense retrieval settings.

MTEB LEMBNarrativeQARetrieval is a retrieval benchmark derived from NarrativeQA within the MTEB LEMB suite. It provides question queries and a corpus of narrative passages with relevance annotations indicating which passages contain the answers. Designed to evaluate embedding-based semantic retrieval and ranking on long-form narrative content, it stresses models’ ability to retrieve answer-bearing excerpts and handle story-level context and reasoning.

MTEB LEMBNeedleRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) suite focused on needle-related biomedical/surgical text. It provides query–document pairs with relevance annotations to evaluate embedding models’ ability to retrieve semantically matching passages about needles (procedures, devices, or related clinical text). The task emphasizes fine-grained, domain-specific semantic retrieval and is intended for benchmarking and improving embedding-based search, ranking, and information-retrieval systems in clinical/biomedical contexts using the default train/validation/test splits.

MTEB LEMBPasskeyRetrieval (default) is a retrieval benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark designed to evaluate embedding models on a passkey retrieval task. The dataset contains short queries paired with a large corpus of anonymized passkey-related entries and binary/graded relevance labels, enabling evaluation of semantic matching and ranking performance. It is intended to measure retrieval metrics such as recall@k, MAP, and NDCG for embeddings in scenarios requiring precise similarity-based lookup of compact, authentication-style records.

MTEB LEMBQMSumRetrieval (default) is a retrieval benchmark derived from the QMSum meeting-summary dataset, cast for embedding-based retrieval. It contains meeting transcripts and query–relevant-segment annotations; given a natural-language query the task is to retrieve the most relevant transcript segments. The dataset evaluates embedding models’ ability to capture semantic relevance in long, spoken-domain documents using standard retrieval metrics (e.g., Recall@k, MRR, nDCG).

MTEB LEMBSummScreenFDRetrieval (default) is a retrieval benchmark within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) derived from the SummScreenFD collection. It pairs summary-style queries with a corpus of screen or dialogue segments and labeled relevant documents, enabling evaluation of semantic retrieval performance. The task measures how well embedding models retrieve supporting screen content for abstractive or conversational summaries, emphasizing robust semantic matching across paraphrase and abstraction. It is suited for benchmarking dense retrieval, vector-search systems, and embedding quality for downstream summarization and information-retrieval applications.

MTEB LEMBWikimQARetrieval (default) is a retrieval benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) focused on open-domain question-to-Wikipedia-passage retrieval. It provides question queries paired with relevant Wikipedia passages and candidate corpora, enabling evaluation of embedding-based semantic search and dense retrieval methods. The task is to rank passages by relevance to each question; common metrics include MRR, Recall@k and nDCG. It uses the MTEB default splits and settings to compare embedding models on real-world QA retrieval performance in the Wikipedia domain.

MTEB MLQARetrieval (deu-deu) is a German-language retrieval benchmark derived from the MLQA dataset and included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It provides German questions paired with German passages and relevance annotations indicating which passages answer each question. The set is designed to evaluate embedding-based and dense retrieval models for semantic search, passage ranking, and retrieval-augmented QA in a mono-lingual German setting.

MTEB MLQARetrieval (deu-spa) is a bilingual retrieval benchmark derived from the MLQA question-answering corpus, designed to evaluate cross-lingual sentence/passage retrieval between German and Spanish. It provides German and Spanish queries aligned with relevant passages in the other language (both retrieval directions), with annotated relevance labels for supervised evaluation. The task measures embedding and retrieval models’ ability to match semantically equivalent content across German and Spanish, supporting development and comparison of multilingual and cross-lingual retrieval systems.

MTEB MLQARetrieval (deu-eng) is a cross-lingual passage retrieval dataset derived from the MLQA benchmark, pairing German queries with English candidate passages and relevance labels. It is designed to evaluate multilingual and cross-lingual embedding and retrieval models on their ability to match questions in German to relevant English contexts. The dataset supports supervised benchmarking of retrieval quality using standard metrics (e.g., recall, MRR) and helps assess model performance on real-world multilingual question answering and information retrieval tasks.

MLQARetrieval (spa-deu) is a cross-lingual retrieval benchmark derived from MLQA that pairs Spanish queries with German passages and relevance labels. It evaluates multilingual embedding and retrieval models on their ability to retrieve correct German context given Spanish questions, supporting metrics such as recall@k and MRR. The dataset is intended for developing and benchmarking dense and sparse cross-lingual retrieval, zero-shot transfer, and multilingual semantic search systems.

MTEB MLQARetrieval (spa-spa) is the Spanish–Spanish retrieval subset of the MLQA Retrieval benchmark within MTEB. It pairs Spanish questions with relevant and non-relevant Spanish passages (derived from the MLQA multilingual QA dataset, based on Wikipedia) to evaluate semantic search and passage-ranking performance. The split is designed for assessing embedding and retrieval models on Spanish-language retrieval tasks such as dense/sparse retrieval, semantic similarity, and QA pipelines using standard ranking metrics (e.g., recall@k, MRR, nDCG).

MTEB MLQARetrieval (spa-eng) is a bilingual retrieval benchmark derived from the MLQA question-answering corpus, designed to evaluate Spanish↔English multilingual embedding and semantic search models. It provides natural question queries paired with candidate passages and relevance labels across Spanish and English, enabling assessment of cross-lingual retrieval accuracy, ranking quality, and embedding alignment. The dataset is suited for testing semantic search, zero-shot transfer, and multilingual representation learning in retrieval settings.

MTEB MLQARetrieval (eng-deu) is a cross-lingual retrieval benchmark derived from the MLQA dataset, pairing English questions with German candidate passages and relevance labels. It evaluates embedding and retrieval models on their ability to match semantically equivalent content across languages, supporting metrics like recall, MRR and nDCG. The dataset is useful for benchmarking multilingual sentence and passage embeddings, dense and sparse retrieval systems, and cross-lingual re-ranking approaches.

MTEB MLQARetrieval (eng-spa) is a bilingual retrieval benchmark derived from the MLQA dataset for evaluating multilingual sentence and passage embeddings on English–Spanish retrieval. It contains English and Spanish question queries paired with candidate passages and relevance labels, supporting monolingual and cross-lingual setups (e.g., English query → Spanish document). The dataset is intended to measure semantic search, cross-lingual transfer, and embedding alignment quality for models tasked with retrieving relevant content across English and Spanish.

MTEB MLQARetrieval (eng-eng) is an English retrieval benchmark derived from the MLQA question-answering dataset. It pairs English questions as queries with relevant Wikipedia passages as target documents to evaluate semantic retrieval and embedding-based nearest-neighbor search for question-to-context matching. The task stresses semantic understanding beyond lexical overlap and is used to benchmark dense retrieval and reranking models using metrics such as Recall@k and MRR.

MTEB MLSUMClusteringP2P (de) is a German-language clustering benchmark derived from the MLSUM news corpus, formatted for the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It contains German news articles with ground-truth cluster labels (e.g., topics or sources) and is designed to evaluate sentence/document embedding models on their ability to group semantically similar news items. The task focuses on point-to-point clustering/semantic grouping, providing a real-world news-domain test of embedding quality for tasks like unsupervised clustering, topic discovery, and downstream retrieval.

MTEB MLSUMClusteringP2P (fr) is the French split of the MLSUM-based clustering task in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains French news articles organized by topical labels and is designed to evaluate document-embedding models’ ability to group related articles. Evaluation uses pairwise (P2P) clustering metrics (precision/recall/F1) to assess how well embeddings separate topics, making it useful for benchmarking multilingual and French-specific clustering and representation methods.

MTEB MLSUMClusteringP2P (ru) is a Russian-language evaluation set from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that uses MLSUM news content to assess embedding models on clustering and pairwise (point-to-point) semantic tasks. It provides Russian news articles with cluster labels and paired examples for measuring how well embeddings group topical content and rank semantically similar items. The dataset is intended for benchmarking document/sentence embedding quality on clustering, retrieval and semantic similarity in Russian news domains.

MTEB MLSUMClusteringP2P (es) is a Spanish-language clustering benchmark derived from the MLSUM news corpus and included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It provides Spanish news articles with ground-truth cluster labels (e.g., topic or source) to evaluate the quality of document/sentence embeddings for unsupervised clustering. The task measures an embedding model’s ability to group semantically similar news items into coherent clusters, enabling comparison of models on topical separation and representation quality in Spanish news text.

MTEB MLSUMClusteringS2S (de) is a German-language clustering benchmark derived from the MLSUM news corpus prepared for the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark’s sequence-to-sequence clustering task. It contains German news articles with ground-truth topic cluster labels, enabling evaluation of document/sentence embeddings via clustering metrics. The set is designed to test representation quality and topical grouping performance of embedding models (especially sequence-to-sequence encoders) on news-domain German text.

MTEB MLSUMClusteringS2S (fr) is a French cluster-level summarization dataset derived from the MLSUM news corpus, formatted for sequence-to-sequence evaluation. It groups related French news articles into topical clusters and provides reference cluster summaries or representative headlines, enabling assessment of models that must both produce abstractive summaries and induce coherent clusterings. The dataset is useful for benchmarking multilingual S2S summarization, evaluating embedding quality for topic clustering, and testing end-to-end pipelines that combine clustering with summary generation.

MLSUMClusteringS2S (ru) is a Russian-language subset derived from the MLSUM news corpus, containing news articles grouped into topical clusters paired with reference summaries. It is designed for benchmarking embedding models on cluster-based retrieval and sequence-to-sequence summarization tasks in Russian, enabling evaluation of topic clustering quality and generation of concise abstractive summaries from clustered news content.

MLSUMClusteringS2S (es) is the Spanish split of the MTEB MLSUMClusteringS2S benchmark. It comprises Spanish news articles grouped into topic-based clusters with representative texts/labels for each cluster, and is designed to evaluate embedding and sequence-to-sequence models on semantic document clustering and cluster-level summarization or label generation. The dataset is used to benchmark document/sentence embedding quality, clustering performance, and S2S generation for topical grouping in Spanish-language news.

MTEB MMarcoReranking (default) is a re-ranking benchmark derived from the MS MARCO passage-ranking dataset within the Massive Text Embeddings Benchmark. It contains search queries paired with candidate passages and relevance labels, designed to evaluate and train embedding-based re-rankers and retrieval models. The task measures a model’s ability to reorder a short list of retrieved passages for a query (commonly using metrics such as MRR and NDCG), making it suitable for benchmarking dense retrieval, re-ranking, and cross-encoder systems.

MTEB MMarcoRetrieval (default) is a large-scale retrieval benchmark based on the MS MARCO passage collection, intended to evaluate text embedding models on web search–style passage retrieval. It provides real user queries paired with a large corpus of candidate passages and relevance judgments, enabling assessment of embedding quality for dense retrieval and ranking. Common evaluation metrics include MRR and recall@k, making it suitable for benchmarking models in ad-hoc search and information retrieval tasks.

MTEB MSMARCO (default) is a large-scale passage retrieval dataset derived from the MS MARCO corpus and included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It provides real user queries paired with candidate passages and human relevance judgments, offering a realistic, high-volume benchmark for evaluating semantic retrieval and ranking with text embeddings. The default configuration uses standard MS MARCO train/dev/test splits and is commonly used to assess and compare dense retrieval, embedding quality, and re-ranking models.

MTEB MasakhaNEWSClusteringP2P (amh) is a benchmark dataset for evaluating embedding models on clustering Amharic news text. It contains Amharic news articles from the MasakhaNEWS collection grouped into topical clusters with ground-truth cluster labels, enabling assessment of how well embeddings capture semantic similarity and topical structure. The set is intended for unsupervised clustering and cluster-quality evaluation (e.g., ARI, NMI) and supports comparison of embedding models and clustering algorithms in a low-resource, morphologically rich language setting.

MasakhaNEWSClusteringP2P (hau) is a Hausa subset of the MasakhaNEWS collection curated for the MTEB clustering (pair-to-pair) evaluation. It contains Hausa news articles annotated with topic labels, enabling evaluation of text embedding models by grouping semantically similar items and measuring cluster quality. The split targets low-resource language performance, making it useful for benchmarking embedding generalization, unsupervised topic discovery, and downstream tasks like document retrieval and classification in Hausa.

MTEB MasakhaNEWSClusteringP2P (ibo) is a pairwise clustering evaluation set drawn from the MasakhaNEWS corpus in Igbo. It provides news article pairs labeled as same-topic or different-topic, enabling assessment of text embedding models’ ability to capture topical similarity and support clustering. The task focuses on real-world news text in a low-resource African language and is used to evaluate embedding quality via pairwise classification and clustering metrics (e.g., accuracy/F1, NMI, ARI).

MasakhaNEWSClusteringP2P (lin) is an MTEB benchmark subset that evaluates multilingual sentence/document embeddings on pair-to-pair clustering and retrieval using the MasakhaNEWS corpus of African news. It contains news text pairs annotated for cluster membership or semantic equivalence across target languages and uses a linear-probe ("lin") evaluation protocol to assess how well fixed embeddings support clustering, pairwise retrieval, and cross-lingual transfer. It is intended for benchmarking embedding quality and robustness on low-resource African languages.

MasakhaNEWSClusteringP2P (lug) is a Luganda subset of the MasakhaNEWS corpus formatted for the MTEB clustering (point-to-point) task. It contains Luganda news texts with cluster membership information used to evaluate semantic grouping and pairwise similarity of document embeddings. The split enables benchmarking of multilingual and low-resource embedding models on unsupervised clustering, topic separation, and retrieval-style pairwise evaluations in Luganda news domains.

MasakhaNEWSClusteringP2P (orm) is the Oromo subset of the MasakhaNEWS clustering benchmark used in MTEB, consisting of Oromo-language news texts annotated with topical cluster labels. It is designed to evaluate text-embedding models on pairwise similarity and clustering tasks—measuring how well embeddings group semantically related news items in a low-resource African language—facilitating benchmarking of multilingual and cross-lingual representation and clustering performance (e.g., NMI/ARI).

MasakhaNEWSClusteringP2P (pcm) is a Nigerian Pidgin (pcm) subset of the MasakhaNEWS corpus prepared for the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) to evaluate embedding quality on news-topic clustering. It contains news articles annotated by topic and converted into a pairwise (point-to-point) format where text pairs are labeled as same- or different-cluster. The task measures how well embeddings capture topical similarity using clustering and pairwise metrics (e.g., ARI, NMI, pairwise F1), facilitating evaluation of multilingual and low-resource semantic representations for news grouping and unsupervised organization.

MasakhaNEWSClusteringP2P (run) is a clustering task from the MTEB suite built on the MasakhaNEWS corpus of African-language news articles. It evaluates embedding models by measuring pairwise similarity and clustering quality to determine how well representations group articles by topic in multilingual, low-resource settings. The task is intended to benchmark and compare embedding approaches for downstream applications such as topic grouping, document organization, and cross-lingual retrieval in African languages.

MTEB MasakhaNEWSClusteringP2P (sna) is a Shona-language pairwise clustering dataset derived from MasakhaNEWS. It contains news article pairs annotated for whether they belong to the same topic cluster, enabling evaluation of sentence/document embeddings on clustering and topical grouping. The task assesses embedding quality for clustering, retrieval, and downstream topic-analysis in a low-resource African language setting within the MTEB benchmark.

MTEB MasakhaNEWSClusteringP2P (som) is a Somali-language subset of the MasakhaNEWS corpus formatted for the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark’s clustering task. It contains Somali news texts with topic-based cluster annotations, enabling evaluation of semantic embeddings on unsupervised clustering quality. The dataset is intended to benchmark and compare embedding models’ ability to group semantically related Somali news items, supporting metrics such as clustering purity, NMI, and ARI, and helping assess performance in a low-resource African language setting.

MTEB MasakhaNEWSClusteringP2P (swa) is a Swahili clustering benchmark drawn from the MasakhaNEWS corpus within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It provides Swahili news texts with cluster labels and pairwise cluster relationships for evaluating sentence/document embeddings on clustering and pairwise similarity tasks. Designed for low-resource language evaluation, it measures embedding quality using clustering- and retrieval-style metrics (e.g., NMI, ARI, pairwise accuracy).

MTEB MasakhaNEWSClusteringP2P (tir) is a clustering benchmark drawn from the MasakhaNEWS Tigrinya news corpus and included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It provides Tigrinya news texts organized into topic-based clusters to evaluate the ability of text embeddings to group semantically similar documents. The subset is intended for assessing clustering quality and semantic grouping in a low-resource, multilingual setting, useful for benchmarking embedding models on Tigrinya news content.

MasakhaNEWSClusteringP2P (xho) is the Xhosa-language subset of the MasakhaNEWS collection used in the Multilingual Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It comprises Xhosa news articles annotated with topic labels and organized for clustering evaluation with pairwise cluster-membership ground truth. The set is intended to benchmark embedding and clustering methods on semantic grouping and topic discovery in a low-resource African language.

MasakhaNEWSClusteringP2P (yor) is a Yoruba-language clustering benchmark in the MTEB suite, derived from MasakhaNEWS news articles and annotated with topic/group labels. It evaluates sentence- and document-level embeddings on clustering and pairwise semantic grouping tasks in a low-resource, real-world news domain. The dataset is intended to test embedding quality for grouping semantically similar Yoruba texts, supporting development and comparison of multilingual and African-language representation models.

MasakhaNEWSClusteringS2S (amh) is an Amharic-language subset of the MasakhaNEWS corpus formatted for clustering evaluation in MTEB. It contains news articles grouped and labeled by topic and presented in a sequence-to-sequence style for clustering/assignment tasks. The dataset is intended to benchmark embedding and representation models on topical separation, document grouping, and retrieval in a low-resource language, supporting evaluation of multilingual and Amharic-specific text representations.

MasakhaNEWSClusteringS2S (hau) is a Hausa-language news dataset derived from MasakhaNEWS and formatted for MTEB’s ClusteringS2S task. It contains Hausa news texts organized into topical/story clusters to evaluate sentence- and document-level representations and sequence-to-sequence clustering approaches. The set is intended for benchmarking multilingual embedding models, clustering algorithms, and transfer learning in a low-resource news domain.

MasakhaNEWSClusteringS2S (ibo) is the Igbo subset of the MasakhaNEWS clustering sequence-to-sequence dataset used in MTEB. It contains Igbo news articles grouped into topical clusters and formatted for sequence-to-sequence clustering evaluation, where models generate cluster labels or representative summaries for each cluster. The dataset enables benchmarking of multilingual embedding and generative models on semantic grouping and cluster-aware generation in a low-resource African language, supporting evaluation of clustering quality, semantic coherence, and cross-lingual transfer.

MTEB MasakhaNEWSClusteringS2S (lin) is a clustering benchmark derived from the MasakhaNEWS multilingual news corpus, formatted for the MTEB sequence-to-sequence clustering task with a linear-probing evaluation. It contains news articles in multiple African languages labeled by topic and is intended to test how well sentence/document embeddings support unsupervised clustering and simple linear classification of topics in low-resource, cross-lingual settings. Evaluation focuses on clustering quality (e.g., ARI, NMI, clustering F1) to compare embedding models’ ability to separate topical classes and generalize across diverse African languages.

MasakhaNEWSClusteringS2S (lug) is a Luganda subset of the MasakhaNEWS collection adapted for the MTEB clustering (sequence-to-sequence) task. It contains short news articles in Luganda with topic labels and is designed to evaluate embedding and seq2seq models on their ability to group semantically related news items. The dataset supports benchmarking of multilingual and low-resource models on clustering quality, topic separation, and representation coherence, enabling assessment of model performance in real-world news clustering and downstream tasks like topic discovery and document organization in Luganda.

MTEB MasakhaNEWSClusteringS2S (orm) is a clustering-oriented subset of the MasakhaNEWS corpus in Oromo, formatted for sequence-to-sequence evaluation. It provides Oromo news texts grouped by topical clusters to benchmark representation learning, clustering quality, and cluster-aware generation in a low-resource language. The split enables evaluation of embedding-based clustering, unsupervised topic discovery, and downstream S2S tasks (e.g., cluster-conditioned summarization or label generation), making it useful for assessing multilingual embedding models and clustering methods on real-world news content in Oromo.

MasakhaNEWSClusteringS2S (pcm) is a Nigerian Pidgin (pcm) subset of the MasakhaNEWS collection formatted for MTEB’s clustering-as-sequence-to-sequence task. It contains short news texts labeled by topical clusters and is intended to evaluate models’ ability to produce cluster assignments or representative cluster summaries in a low-resource language setting. The dataset supports benchmarking embedding quality and sequence-to-sequence approaches for topic clustering and grouping of news content.

MasakhaNEWSClusteringS2S (run) is an MTEB task built on the MasakhaNEWS multilingual African news collection, framed as a sequence-to-sequence clustering problem. It pairs news articles in multiple African languages with topic groupings, enabling evaluation of models that generate cluster assignments or cluster labels from text. The task benchmarks multilingual embeddings and seq2seq approaches on clustering quality and cross-lingual generalization in low-resource settings, supporting development of representation learning, clustering-by-generation, and transfer learning methods.

MasakhaNEWSClusteringS2S (sna) is a Shona-language subset of the MasakhaNEWS corpus formatted for clustering and sequence-to-sequence evaluation. It contains Shona news texts organized into topic clusters with paired input–target examples for S2S tasks, enabling assessment of semantic clustering, topic separation, and sequence-to-sequence generation in a low-resource African language. Designed for the MTEB benchmark, it supports development and evaluation of multilingual embeddings, clustering algorithms, and S2S models on realistic news content, measuring representation quality, cluster coherence, and generation fidelity.

MasakhaNEWSClusteringS2S (som) is a Somali news clustering dataset derived from the MasakhaNEWS corpus and formatted for sequence-to-sequence evaluation in MTEB. It contains Somali news articles paired with cluster annotations, enabling assessment of embedding and clustering models on a low-resource, news-domain language. The dataset is intended for benchmarking representation quality in tasks like topic clustering, cluster assignment generation, and downstream retrieval or classification in Somali.

MasakhaNEWSClusteringS2S (swa) is a Swahili news clustering dataset derived from the MasakhaNEWS corpus and formatted for the MTEB clustering (S2S) task. It contains Swahili news texts grouped into topic clusters with ground-truth cluster labels, enabling evaluation of embedding and sequence-to-sequence models on clustering, topic coherence, and semantic retrieval. The dataset is aimed at benchmarking representation quality in a low-resource language and supports common clustering metrics (NMI, ARI, purity) for comparing models on real-world Swahili news content.

MasakhaNEWSClusteringS2S (tir) is the Tigrinya subset of the MasakhaNEWS corpus prepared for the MTEB sequence-to-sequence clustering benchmark. It contains Tigrinya news texts grouped by topical labels and formatted for S2S-style clustering evaluation, enabling assessment of representation quality and cluster assignment performance. The dataset is intended to benchmark embedding and sequence-to-sequence models on unsupervised clustering and topical grouping in a low-resource African language.

MasakhaNEWSClusteringS2S (xho) is a Xhosa-language subset of the MTEB benchmark derived from the MasakhaNEWS corpus, formatted for sequence-to-sequence clustering evaluation. It contains news articles grouped by topical clusters with cluster labels, enabling assessment of embedding and S2S models on topic separation and grouping in a low-resource African language. The split is intended for benchmarking clustering quality, semantic grouping, and cross-lingual transfer of sentence/document representations.

MasakhaNEWSClusteringS2S (yor) is a Yoruba-language subset of the MasakhaNEWS collection prepared for sequence-to-sequence clustering tasks. It contains news articles grouped into topic clusters with cluster labels or representative summaries, enabling models to learn to map documents to cluster identifiers or generate concise cluster descriptions. The dataset is intended for evaluating multilingual/low-resource seq2seq models and embedding methods on document grouping, cluster-label generation, and topic-level representation quality in Yoruba.

MTEB MedicalRetrieval (default) is a medical-domain retrieval dataset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark containing medical queries paired with relevant documents or passages and non‑relevant distractors. It is designed to evaluate embedding models on semantic search and ranking in clinical and biomedical language, measuring performance and generalization for tasks such as literature search, clinical question answering, and information access in specialized medical terminology.

MedRxivClusteringP2P (MTEB, default) is a biomedical document clustering dataset built from medRxiv preprints, pairing related research papers to form clusterable groups. It evaluates embedding models on their ability to capture fine-grained semantic relationships in clinical and medical research text (titles and abstracts), supporting unsupervised clustering and retrieval tasks. The dataset is useful for benchmarking representations for literature mapping, topic discovery, and semantic search in the biomedical domain.

MedrxivClusteringS2S is a biomedical clustering benchmark drawn from medRxiv preprints. It provides article texts (titles and abstracts) paired with cluster labels representing research topics, formatted for sequence-to-sequence evaluation. The dataset is designed to evaluate embedding, representation learning, and clustering methods on domain-specific semantic grouping, testing a model’s ability to group related medical research for tasks like retrieval, topic organization, and downstream analysis.

MintakaRetrieval (de) is a German-language retrieval dataset in the Massive Text Embeddings Benchmark (MTEB). It provides German queries paired with candidate passages/documents and relevance labels to evaluate semantic retrieval and ranking performance of embedding models. The dataset is designed for benchmarking monolingual semantic search, passage ranking, and embedding-based retrieval systems in German, supporting comparisons of retrieval quality and generalization across models.

MTEB MintakaRetrieval (es) is a Spanish-language retrieval benchmark within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) consisting of query–document pairs with relevance annotations. It is designed to evaluate semantic search and embedding-based retrieval methods for Spanish, supporting dense and sparse retrieval, reranking, and zero-shot embedding evaluation using standard retrieval metrics (e.g., Recall@k, MRR, nDCG). The dataset is intended for training and benchmarking models for Spanish semantic search, cross-lingual retrieval experiments, and comparison of embedding encoders on real-world retrieval tasks.

MTEB NFCorpus (default) is a text corpus within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark designed to evaluate embedding models on semantic retrieval and similarity tasks. It provides documents paired with queries and relevance labels (default split) to assess performance on semantic search, nearest-neighbor retrieval, clustering, and reranking. NFCorpus emphasizes topical diversity and realistic language variation, making it useful for benchmarking embedding quality and downstream retrieval performance.

MTEB NQ (default) is a retrieval benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark built on Google’s Natural Questions. It consists of real user queries paired with relevant Wikipedia passages (long-answer passages) and ground-truth relevance labels, used to evaluate embedding quality for dense retrieval, semantic search, and passage ranking on realistic open-domain QA queries.

MTEB QuoraRetrieval (default) is a retrieval benchmark drawn from Quora question pairs, providing queries and a candidate pool with relevance labels that indicate duplicate or semantically related questions. Included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB), it is designed to evaluate sentence- and passage-level embeddings for semantic retrieval tasks using metrics such as MRR and Recall@k. The dataset is useful for benchmarking and developing embedding models for duplicate question detection, semantic search, and retrieval-oriented QA systems.

MTEB RedditClustering (default) is a clustering benchmark composed of Reddit posts grouped into ground-truth clusters, intended to evaluate text embedding models’ ability to capture semantic similarity in short, informal social-media text. It is used to test unsupervised clustering performance (e.g., ARI/AMI/NMI) and robustness of embeddings on noisy, topical, and conversational language, making it useful for assessing embedding quality and downstream clustering or topic-discovery methods.

MTEB RedditClusteringP2P is a clustering benchmark drawn from Reddit posts, where texts are grouped into topical clusters (e.g., by subreddit or discussion thread). It provides diverse, real-world short-to-medium length social media posts spanning many topics and styles, intended to evaluate embedding models and unsupervised clustering methods. The dataset measures how well representations separate semantically related posts and supports development and comparison of clustering algorithms, dimensionality reduction, and community/topic discovery techniques in noisy, conversational text.

RiaNewsRetrieval (default) is a news retrieval dataset drawn from RIA Novosti articles, used in the MTEB suite to evaluate embedding-based semantic search and ad-hoc document retrieval. It provides queries (typically headlines or short queries) paired with candidate news documents and relevance judgments on the default evaluation split. The dataset focuses on the Russian news domain and is intended to benchmark embedding models on ranking metrics such as recall, MAP, and nDCG for realistic news search scenarios.

MTEB RuBQReranking (default) is a Russian-language reranking benchmark included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It comprises queries paired with candidate passages and relevance labels derived from the RuBQ corpus, with standard train/dev/test splits for the default configuration. The dataset is intended to evaluate embedding-based retrieval and reranking models on Russian semantic ranking tasks, supporting comparison using common ranking metrics (e.g., nDCG, MRR).

RuBQRetrieval is a Russian-language retrieval dataset in the MTEB suite containing user queries paired with candidate documents/passages and relevance annotations. It is designed to evaluate semantic retrieval and dense embedding models on Russian IR tasks, supporting benchmarking of vector search, ranking, and semantic similarity. The default configuration provides standard train/validation/test splits with relevance labels for consistent comparison of retrieval performance across models.

RuSciBenchGRNTIClusteringP2P is a Russian scientific-text dataset in the MTEB suite designed to evaluate embedding models on clustering and pairwise similarity tasks using GRNTI (Russian scientific subject classification) labels. It contains scientific documents (e.g., titles and abstracts) annotated with GRNTI topic codes, enabling assessment of how well embeddings group texts by research domain. The dataset is intended for benchmarking semantic clustering, retrieval, and topic grouping performance on Russian scientific literature.

RuSciBenchOECDClusteringP2P (MTEB, default) is a benchmark dataset of Russian scientific texts labeled with OECD subject categories, designed to evaluate embedding models on semantic clustering and pairwise similarity tasks. It contains short scientific documents (titles and/or abstracts) mapped to topical classes, enabling assessment of how well embeddings group related research and separate distinct topics. The dataset is used within MTEB’s clustering/P2P evaluation to test representation quality for domain-specific semantic organization and peer-to-peer retrieval in Russian scientific literature.

SCIDOCS is a scientific-document retrieval dataset in the MTEB benchmark that pairs real scholarly queries with candidate documents and relevance labels. It is designed to evaluate embedding models and semantic-search systems on retrieval and ranking of scientific literature, emphasizing fine-grained semantic matching across domain-specific vocabulary and diverse research topics. SCIDOCS is commonly used to benchmark embedding quality for semantic search, reranking, and downstream academic IR tasks.

MTEB STS17 (en-en) is the English subset of the Semantic Textual Similarity 2017 task included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It consists of English sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores (e.g., 0–5) and is used to evaluate sentence and text embedding models by measuring correlation (Pearson/Spearman) between model-predicted similarities (e.g., cosine) and human judgments. It benchmarks fine-grained semantic similarity capability for tasks like paraphrase detection, semantic search, clustering, and similarity-based retrieval.

MTEB STS17 (es-en) is a cross-lingual semantic textual similarity subset used in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains Spanish–English sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores, typically on a 0–5 scale, for assessing semantic closeness across languages. The set is intended to evaluate multilingual sentence and text embeddings on tasks such as semantic similarity, retrieval, and clustering, and is commonly used with correlation metrics (Pearson/Spearman) to compare model outputs against human judgments.

MTEB STS17 (en-de) is a cross-lingual semantic textual similarity dataset containing English–German sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores from the SemEval 2017 STS task. Included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, it is used to evaluate how well sentence embedding models capture semantic equivalence across English and German for tasks such as similarity scoring, retrieval, and cross-lingual clustering. The dataset helps measure alignment and robustness of multilingual embeddings on fine-grained semantic judgments.

MTEB STS17 (es-es) is a Spanish Semantic Textual Similarity subset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It comprises Spanish sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores (typically on a 0–5 scale) and is used to evaluate how well sentence embeddings capture nuanced semantic similarity. Common evaluation protocols measure correlation (Spearman/Pearson) between embedding-derived similarity (e.g., cosine) and human judgments.

MTEB STS17 (fr-en) is a cross-lingual semantic textual similarity dataset comprising French–English sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores. Included in the MTEB benchmark, it evaluates multilingual and cross-lingual sentence embeddings and retrieval systems by measuring how well embedding-based similarity correlates with human judgments, making it suitable for benchmarking semantic matching, retrieval, and embedding quality across languages.

MTEB STS22 (zh-en) is a cross-lingual semantic textual similarity dataset from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that contains Chinese–English sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores. It is designed to evaluate multilingual and cross-lingual sentence embeddings on semantic similarity, retrieval, and clustering tasks, measuring how well embeddings align meaning across languages using gold-standard similarity labels (typically on a 0–5 scale).

MTEB STS22 (zh) is the Chinese subset of the Semantic Textual Similarity 2022 tasks within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains Chinese sentence pairs annotated with continuous similarity scores (typically measuring semantic relatedness on a 0–5 scale) and is intended to evaluate sentence and text embedding models on semantic similarity, ranking, and retrieval. The dataset is used to benchmark embedding quality for Chinese-language tasks such as paraphrase detection, semantic search, and clustering, helping assess models’ ability to capture fine-grained semantic relatedness in Chinese.

MTEB STS22 (es) is the Spanish subset of the Semantic Textual Similarity 2022 task within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains Spanish sentence pairs with human-annotated similarity scores (typically on a 0–5 scale), providing gold-standard labels for semantic relatedness. The set is used to evaluate and compare sentence and text embedding models on semantic similarity tasks (e.g., computing embedding similarity, ranking, correlation with human judgments) and to assess cross-lingual or language-specific embedding quality for Spanish.

MTEB STS22 (fr) is a French semantic textual similarity benchmark within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains French sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores, used to evaluate how well sentence or text embeddings capture semantic closeness. The dataset is intended for intrinsic evaluation of embedding models, with performance typically measured by correlation (Pearson/Spearman) between model-derived similarity scores and human judgments. It is useful for benchmarking and tuning multilingual or French-specific embedding models on semantic similarity tasks.

MTEB STS22 (de-fr) is a cross-lingual semantic textual similarity dataset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, containing German–French sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores. It is designed to evaluate multilingual and cross-lingual sentence embedding models on their ability to measure semantic relatedness across languages. The data supports benchmarking via correlation metrics (e.g., Spearman/Pearson), and is useful for tasks such as cross-lingual retrieval, clustering, and evaluation of transfer learning for multilingual representations.

MTEB STS22 (pl-en) is a cross-lingual Semantic Textual Similarity subset of the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark containing Polish–English sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores (typically on a continuous 0–5 scale). It is designed to evaluate and compare multilingual sentence embedding models on their ability to capture semantic equivalence across languages, supporting tasks like cross-lingual retrieval, clustering, and semantic search.

MTEB STS22 (pl) is the Polish subset of the Semantic Textual Similarity 2022 task included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains pairs of Polish sentences annotated with continuous human similarity scores, covering diverse domains and writing styles. The dataset is designed to evaluate and compare sentence- and embedding-based models via correlation metrics (e.g., Pearson/Spearman) on semantic similarity, supporting development of Polish embeddings for tasks like semantic search, paraphrase detection, and retrieval.

MTEB STS22 (en) is an English semantic textual similarity dataset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores (continuous, typically 0–5) drawn from diverse domains, and is designed to evaluate how well sentence or text embeddings capture semantic relatedness. The dataset is commonly used to measure correlation between embedding-based similarity metrics (e.g., cosine) and human judgments, providing a standard benchmark for embedding model quality on STS tasks.

MTEB STS22 (ru) is the Russian-language subset of the Semantic Textual Similarity 2022 task within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It comprises Russian sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores and is intended to evaluate the semantic fidelity of sentence embeddings and models for fine-grained semantic relatedness. The dataset is used to benchmark and compare embedding models on tasks such as semantic retrieval, clustering, paraphrase identification, and cross-lingual transfer for Russian.

MTEB STS22 (de) is the German subset of the Semantic Textual Similarity 2022 task within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It comprises German sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores and is used to evaluate sentence and text embedding models by comparing embedding-derived similarity (e.g., cosine) to human judgments. The dataset benchmarks models’ ability to capture fine-grained semantic relatedness in German, relevant for tasks like semantic search, paraphrase detection, and clustering.

MTEB STS22 (fr-pl) is a cross-lingual Semantic Textual Similarity subset from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark containing French–Polish sentence pairs with human-annotated similarity scores. It is designed to evaluate how well sentence embedding models capture semantic equivalence across languages, using correlation metrics (e.g., Spearman) against gold similarity labels. The dataset is useful for benchmarking and developing multilingual and cross-lingual embedding models, transfer learning, and zero-shot semantic understanding between French and Polish.

MTEB STS22 (de-pl) is a cross-lingual semantic textual similarity subset from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark containing German–Polish sentence pairs with human-annotated similarity scores. It is designed to evaluate multilingual sentence embeddings and cross-lingual semantic retrieval by measuring fine-grained semantic alignment between German and Polish sentences, useful for benchmarking embedding models on cross-lingual understanding, transfer, and zero-shot similarity tasks.

MTEB STS22 (es-en) is a cross-lingual semantic textual similarity dataset containing Spanish–English sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores (normally on a 0–5 scale). It is part of the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark and is intended to evaluate multilingual and cross-lingual sentence embeddings by measuring correlation between embedding-based similarity (e.g., cosine) and human judgments. The split supports benchmarking for tasks such as cross-lingual semantic search, retrieval, and paraphrase identification.

MTEB STS22 (de-en) is a cross-lingual semantic textual similarity dataset from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark consisting of German–English sentence pairs with human-annotated similarity scores (typically on a 0–5 scale). It is designed to evaluate multilingual and cross-lingual sentence embedding models by measuring how well embeddings capture semantic equivalence across languages. The dataset is commonly used with correlation metrics (e.g., Pearson/Spearman) for benchmarking embedding quality in tasks such as retrieval, clustering, and semantic search across German and English text.

MTEB STSBenchmarkMultilingualSTS (fr) is the French subset of the Semantic Textual Similarity component in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It consists of French sentence pairs with human-annotated similarity scores used to evaluate the semantic alignment of sentence embeddings. The dataset is intended for benchmarking multilingual embedding models on tasks such as semantic search, paraphrase detection, clustering, and correlation-based evaluation (e.g., Pearson/Spearman) of embedding quality in French.

MTEB STSBenchmarkMultilingualSTS (en) is the English subset of the Semantic Textual Similarity benchmarks included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It consists of sentence pairs with human-annotated similarity scores (continuous) for evaluating sentence embeddings and semantic similarity models. The dataset is commonly used to assess embedding quality for tasks such as semantic retrieval, ranking, and regression on fine-grained semantic relatedness between sentences.

MTEB SciDocsRR is a scientific document relevance-ranking benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains queries (e.g., paper titles or abstracts) paired with candidate scholarly documents and graded relevance labels, designed to evaluate semantic search, embedding quality, and dense retrieval models on scholarly literature. The dataset is intended for ranking and retrieval metrics (nDCG, MAP, recall) and helps compare and develop embeddings and retrieval systems for scientific document search.

MTEB SciFact is a scientific fact‑checking dataset adapted for embedding evaluation. It pairs scientific claims with supporting or refuting evidence drawn from research abstracts and sentence-level evidence annotations labeled as supports, refutes, or not enough information. In the MTEB default setting it benchmarks text embeddings on retrieval and semantic matching tasks in a domain-specific (scientific/biomedical) context, evaluating models’ ability to retrieve relevant evidence and discriminate claim–evidence relationships.

SpanishNewsClusteringP2P (default) is an MTEB clustering benchmark of Spanish-language news articles with ground-truth topic clusters. It evaluates embedding models’ ability to group semantically related news items by measuring cluster quality (e.g., NMI/ARI) in a pairwise clustering evaluation. The task assesses topical coherence and separation of document/sentence embeddings within the Spanish news domain.

SpanishPassageRetrievalS2S (default) is an MTEB benchmark for Spanish semantic passage retrieval. It provides Spanish query–passage pairs formatted for a sequence-to-sequence (sentence-to-sentence) retrieval setup, enabling evaluation of embedding and retrieval models on relevance ranking and semantic search in Spanish under the MTEB default configuration.

StackExchangeClustering (MTEB, default) is a clustering benchmark built from Stack Exchange Q&A content where posts are grouped into topical clusters. It evaluates the semantic coherence of text embeddings and clustering algorithms on short, technical question-and-answer language across multiple communities. The dataset is suitable for unsupervised clustering, cluster-quality evaluation (e.g., ARI/NMI), and comparing representation methods for topic separation and retrieval in real-world Q&A text.

MTEB StackExchangeClusteringP2P is a clustering benchmark of Stack Exchange question posts designed to evaluate text embedding models on topic grouping and pairwise semantic grouping. The dataset provides raw text (titles and/or bodies) paired with ground-truth topic/community labels and semantically related pairs, enabling evaluation of clustering quality (e.g., ARI/NMI) and pairwise semantic separation. It is intended for assessing embedding-based clustering, community detection, and downstream retrieval or grouping performance on real-world forum data.

MTEB StackOverflowDupQuestions (default) is a benchmark dataset of StackOverflow question pairs labeled as duplicates or not, intended to evaluate text embeddings on semantic similarity, duplicate detection, and retrieval tasks. Each example pairs two question texts (title and/or body) with a binary label indicating whether they are duplicates. Included as part of the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, the dataset is used to measure embedding models’ ability to identify paraphrases and near-duplicate technical Q&A content under the benchmark’s standard train/validation/test splits.

MTEB SyntecReranking (default) is a re-ranking benchmark within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) that provides query–candidate document pairs with relevance labels for evaluating embedding-based re-ranking models. Designed to assess the ability of embeddings and lightweight rankers to refine initial retrieval results, it measures ranking quality using standard metrics (e.g., NDCG, MRR). The dataset follows MTEB’s default preprocessing and splits, enabling consistent comparison of models on re-ranking performance in realistic retrieval scenarios.

SyntecRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark in MTEB designed to evaluate text embedding models on domain-specific technical search. It pairs technical queries with candidate documents and relevance labels to test semantic matching under specialized vocabulary, abbreviations, and varied query formulations. The dataset assesses embedding quality for ranking and retrieval metrics in technical information-seeking scenarios, useful for benchmarking zero-shot and fine-tuned models on robustness to lexical gaps and domain terminology.

MTEB T2Reranking (default) is a reranking benchmark within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that evaluates embedding models on query-to-document reranking tasks. It provides queries paired with pre-retrieved candidate lists and graded relevance labels, enabling assessment of how well embeddings reorder search results (typical metrics: NDCG, MAP, MRR). The dataset covers diverse domains and difficulty levels and is intended to measure embedding quality for downstream retrieval and reranking scenarios under the MTEB default evaluation settings.

MTEB T2Retrieval (default) is a retrieval-focused subset of the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark designed to evaluate embedding models on text-to-document retrieval tasks. It provides query–candidate pools drawn from diverse domains and datasets, enabling assessment of semantic search and dense retrieval quality using metrics such as Recall@k, MRR and nDCG. The suite is intended for benchmarking and comparing embedding encoders on their ability to rank relevant documents for natural-language queries in practical IR scenarios.

MTEB TRECCOVID (default) is an information-retrieval benchmark from the TREC-COVID challenge incorporated into the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It comprises a corpus of COVID-19–related scientific articles, topic queries, and relevance judgments, enabling evaluation of embedding models on semantic search and ranked retrieval tasks. The dataset is used to measure retrieval effectiveness, ranking quality, and generalization of embedding-based search systems on domain-specific biomedical literature.

TenKGnadClusteringP2P (default) is an MTEB clustering benchmark containing ~10,000 text items with ground-truth cluster labels provided in a point-to-point (P2P) format. It is designed to evaluate the quality of sentence/document embeddings for unsupervised clustering and grouping tasks, supporting common clustering metrics (e.g., ARI, NMI) and enabling comparison of embedding models on their ability to separate topical/semantic clusters.

MTEB TenKGnadClusteringS2S is a clustering benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark containing roughly 10,000 text instances derived from the GNAD corpus presented in a sequence-to-sequence format. Each example includes a text and a ground-truth cluster label, enabling evaluation of embedding models on semantic grouping and clustering quality. The dataset is intended to assess how well representations capture topic/intent similarity for unsupervised clustering, cluster-oriented retrieval, and comparison of clustering algorithms and embedding methods.

MTEB ThuNewsClusteringP2P is a pairwise news-clustering dataset derived from the THU news collection, where each example is a pair of articles labeled as belonging to the same topical cluster or not. It is intended to evaluate text embedding models' ability to capture topic-level similarity for tasks such as pairwise retrieval, binary cluster membership classification, and downstream clustering. The default split provides balanced positive and negative pairs across news topics to benchmark embedding quality on topical grouping and similarity discrimination.

ThuNewsClusteringS2S is a Chinese news clustering dataset derived from the ThuNews corpus and formatted for sequence-to-sequence evaluation. Each example pairs a news article (input) with a target sequence representing its cluster assignment or cluster-related label, enabling evaluation of embedding models and seq2seq systems on topical grouping and semantic clustering. It is intended for benchmarking clustering quality, topic coherence, and representation transfer in Chinese-language settings.

MTEB Touche2020 (default) is a retrieval and ranking dataset from the Touche 2020 challenge included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains queries paired with candidate documents and relevance judgments, enabling evaluation of semantic search and dense/sparse retrieval models. The dataset is used to assess embedding quality for ranking metrics (e.g., recall, MRR, nDCG) on short query–to–document matching tasks and serves as a benchmark for embedding-based retrieval and re-ranking approaches.

MTEB TwentyNewsgroupsClustering (default) is a clustering benchmark derived from the classic 20 Newsgroups corpus, containing ~18,846 newsgroup posts across 20 topical categories. It provides short-to-medium length documents with ground-truth labels to evaluate embedding-based unsupervised clustering and topic separation. The default setting supplies the full collection for clustering experiments and is commonly measured with clustering metrics such as Adjusted Rand Index, Normalized Mutual Information, and purity. This dataset is useful for assessing the semantic grouping quality of sentence- and document-level embeddings and representation learning models.

MTEB VideoRetrieval (default) is a benchmark task for evaluating cross-modal retrieval between text queries and video clips. It provides collections of videos paired with relevance-labeled text queries and standard splits under the default configuration, enabling comparison of embedding models on retrieval metrics such as recall@k, mean reciprocal rank, and nDCG. The task assesses the ability of text, video, and joint embedding methods to retrieve relevant videos from large corpora in both zero-shot and supervised settings.

MTEB XMarket (en) is the English subset of the XMarket e‑commerce dataset used in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains English product titles and descriptions from multiple marketplaces, paired for retrieval and matching tasks. The split is designed to evaluate sentence embeddings on product search, cross-market product matching, and semantic retrieval in e‑commerce settings, emphasizing real-world variability in naming and description styles.

MTEB XMarket (de) is the German subset of the XMarket e-commerce dataset used in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains product titles and descriptions (and often parallel entries across marketplaces) labeled for relevance or matching, enabling evaluation of semantic text embeddings on retrieval, product matching, and classification in an e-commerce domain. The dataset is intended to test embedding quality on domain-specific, multilingual product data, measuring robustness for tasks such as cross-lingual retrieval, duplicate detection, and clustering in German-language commerce content.

XMarket (es) is the Spanish subset of the XMarket e-commerce dataset used in MTEB. It contains Spanish product titles and associated metadata with labeled relevance/product-matching pairs for retrieval and classification.
