The dataset is designed to evaluate text embedding models on Spanish e-commerce tasks—semantic search, product matching, clustering, and categorization—and to assess embedding quality and cross-lingual transfer when combined with other language splits.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (deu-deu) is a German monolingual retrieval benchmark within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) that evaluates semantic search and retrieval of question–answer pairs or passages. It provides German query–document relevance pairs for assessing embedding models’ ability to match user queries to relevant answers/passages in German. The dataset is intended for development and evaluation of dense retrieval and semantic search systems, enabling comparison using common retrieval metrics (e.g., MRR, Recall, nDCG) and benchmarking model performance on German-language retrieval tasks.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (deu-eng) is a cross-lingual question–answer retrieval dataset within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that evaluates German↔English semantic search. It contains question–passage pairs where queries in one language must retrieve relevant answer passages in the other, enabling assessment of embedding alignment and cross-lingual retrieval performance (e.g., recall@k, MRR). The task supports benchmarking and developing multilingual retrieval and semantic embedding models for cross-lingual QA scenarios.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (eng-deu) is a cross-lingual retrieval dataset within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, pairing English queries with German candidate passages and relevance annotations for question–answer retrieval. It is designed to evaluate and benchmark multilingual and cross-lingual sentence or passage embedding models on their ability to align semantic representations across English and German for retrieval and ranking tasks. The dataset supports development and assessment of retrieval pipelines, dense/sparse embedding methods, and techniques for semantic matching in multilingual information retrieval and QA applications.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (eng-pol) is a cross-lingual retrieval benchmark pairing English queries with Polish passages annotated for relevance. It evaluates the ability of multilingual embedding and retrieval models to match English questions to relevant Polish documents (and vice versa), measuring retrieval quality for cross-language QA scenarios. The dataset is intended for benchmarking dense and sparse retrieval, representation learning, and cross-lingual transfer, using metrics like recall and MRR to assess embedding alignment and retrieval effectiveness between English and Polish.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (eng-cmn) is a cross-lingual retrieval subset of the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that evaluates embedding models on English-to-Mandarin question-to-passage retrieval. It contains English queries paired with Mandarin Chinese candidate passages and relevance annotations, enabling assessment of multilingual embedding spaces on retrieval metrics (e.g., recall, MRR). The dataset is intended for benchmarking and developing models for cross-lingual QA retrieval, search, and related semantic matching tasks.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (eng-spa) is a cross-lingual retrieval dataset within the MTEB benchmark containing English queries paired with Spanish candidate passages and relevance labels for question–answer retrieval. It is designed to evaluate multilingual and cross-lingual embedding and retrieval models on the task of retrieving Spanish answers for English questions. The dataset is suited for benchmarking dense/sparse retrieval, bilingual sentence embeddings, and ranking algorithms using standard IR metrics.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (eng-fra) is a cross-lingual retrieval benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that evaluates English↔French retrieval between queries and candidate passages. It provides paired English queries and French documents with relevance labels to measure the effectiveness of multilingual sentence embeddings and dense retrieval models (metrics: recall@k, MRR), enabling assessment of semantic alignment, cross-lingual transfer, and retrieval performance without relying on translation.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (pol-eng) is a cross-lingual retrieval benchmark in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark family that evaluates how well embeddings support semantic search between Polish and English. It provides Polish–English query–passage pairs with relevance annotations (bidirectional: Polish→English and English→Polish) for assessing retrieval effectiveness. The dataset is intended for evaluating and comparing multilingual sentence/passage embeddings, cross-lingual semantic search, and retrieval-oriented fine-tuning strategies.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (pol-pol) is a Polish-language retrieval benchmark within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It provides Polish queries paired with relevant passages (and distractors) to evaluate semantic search and dense retrieval models in a monolingual setting. The dataset is designed to assess the quality of text embeddings and vector-ranking methods for Polish information retrieval, supporting development and comparison of embedding models, ANN index strategies, and end-to-end retrieval pipelines.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (cmn-eng) is a cross-lingual retrieval benchmark for evaluating multilingual sentence embeddings on Mandarin↔English question–passage retrieval. It provides queries in one language and candidate passages in the other with relevance labels, enabling measurement of retrieval metrics (e.g., recall, MRR) for cross-lingual semantic matching. The dataset is intended to assess embedding models’ ability to retrieve correct answers across Mandarin and English in QA-style retrieval scenarios.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (cmn-cmn) is a Mandarin retrieval benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains Chinese questions and a corpus of Chinese passages where target passages contain the answers. The task is to rank passages so that answer-containing passages appear at the top, enabling evaluation of embedding and retrieval models’ ability to capture semantic relevance for open-domain/extractive QA in Chinese. It is useful for assessing dense retrieval, embedding quality, and QA retrieval pipelines in Mandarin.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (spa-eng) is a cross-lingual retrieval benchmark in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark suite that pairs Spanish queries with English candidate question–answer passages and relevance labels. It is designed to evaluate multilingual sentence and passage embeddings on their ability to retrieve relevant English answers for Spanish queries. The dataset is suitable for assessing and comparing embedding-based retrieval, dense retrieval and reranking models on cross-lingual transfer, and is typically evaluated with retrieval metrics such as recall@k and MRR.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (spa-spa) is a monolingual Spanish retrieval benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, containing Spanish questions and pools of candidate passages/answers for semantic search. It evaluates embedding-based retrieval and ranking quality on QA-style tasks using metrics like recall@k and MRR. The dataset is intended for developing and comparing Spanish-language sentence/document embeddings, dense retrieval models, and semantic QA systems.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (fra-eng) is a cross-lingual retrieval benchmark containing French–English query–document pairs with relevance labels, derived for evaluating semantic matching across languages. It measures how well multilingual sentence embeddings and retrieval systems can match French queries to English passages (and vice versa), focusing on cross-lingual semantic search and question–answer retrieval. The dataset is intended for benchmarking embedding models, retrieval pipelines, and multilingual transfer capabilities in information retrieval settings.

MTEB STS17 (en-tr) is a cross-lingual semantic textual similarity subset from the STS 2017 shared task included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains English–Turkish sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores (typically 0–5), designed to evaluate how well sentence embedding models capture semantic relatedness across languages. Commonly used for benchmarking cross-lingual embeddings, the dataset supports evaluation via correlation metrics (Pearson/Spearman) and is useful for tasks like cross-lingual retrieval, clustering, and transfer learning.

MTEB STS17 (it-en) is a cross-lingual Semantic Textual Similarity dataset of Italian–English sentence pairs with human-annotated similarity scores (from the SemEval/STS 2017 resource). Included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, it is used to evaluate multilingual and cross-lingual sentence embeddings on their ability to measure semantic equivalence across languages. The dataset is suitable for benchmarking models on correlation metrics (e.g., Pearson/Spearman) and for assessing cross-lingual retrieval, similarity ranking, and transfer performance.

MTEB STS17 (nl-en) is the Dutch–English subset of the Semantic Textual Similarity 2017 tasks included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains Dutch–English sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores and is intended to evaluate cross-lingual sentence embeddings on semantic similarity. The dataset is used for benchmarking multilingual encoders and cross-lingual retrieval/semantic search systems, typically evaluated with correlation metrics (Pearson/Spearman) against human judgments.

MTEB STS17 (en-ar) is the English–Arabic subset of the Semantic Textual Similarity 2017 tasks included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It consists of English–Arabic sentence pairs annotated with continuous similarity scores (typically 0–5) indicating semantic relatedness. The dataset is used to evaluate cross-lingual sentence embeddings and models on similarity regression, semantic retrieval, and ranking across English and Arabic.

MTEB BIOSSES is a biomedical semantic similarity subset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, consisting of expert-annotated sentence pairs from biomedical text with graded similarity scores. It is designed to evaluate embedding models on domain-specific semantic textual similarity (STS) tasks, measuring how well representations capture nuanced meanings in biomedical language. The dataset is useful for benchmarking and fine-tuning embeddings for biomedical NLP tasks such as retrieval, clustering, and semantic search.

MTEB SICK-R is the SICK Relatedness subset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains sentence pairs with human-annotated semantic relatedness scores, used to evaluate sentence embeddings on semantic textual similarity as a regression task. The dataset emphasizes compositional semantics and fine-grained degrees of relatedness (paraphrase, entailment, partial overlap), making it suitable for benchmarking embedding quality via correlation metrics such as Pearson and Spearman.

MTEB STS12 is the STS 2012 subset within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, comprising sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores for evaluating semantic textual similarity. It spans multiple domains (e.g., news, blogs, forums) and is intended to benchmark sentence and text embedding models by measuring correlation (Pearson/Spearman) with human judgments. The suite supports comparison of embedding quality for tasks requiring fine-grained semantic understanding and model selection in embedding-based pipelines.

MTEB STS13 is the SemEval-2013 Semantic Textual Similarity subset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains sentence pairs from diverse domains annotated with continuous similarity scores (typically 0–5) reflecting degrees of semantic equivalence. The set is used to evaluate sentence and text embedding models by measuring correlation (Pearson/Spearman) between embedding-based similarity (e.g., cosine) and human judgments, making it useful for benchmarking embeddings for retrieval, clustering, and semantic search.

MTEB STS14 is a semantic textual similarity dataset of sentence pairs annotated with graded human similarity scores (typically 0–5). Spanning multiple domains (e.g., news, headlines, images, forums), it is used to evaluate text- and sentence-embedding models by measuring how well embedding-based similarity (e.g., cosine) correlates with human judgments, making it a standard benchmark for fine-grained semantic relatedness.

MTEB STS15 is the STS 2015 subset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, comprising sentence pairs annotated with human-judged semantic similarity scores (typically on a 0–5 scale). It is used to evaluate sentence and text embedding quality by measuring correlation (e.g., Pearson/Spearman) between embedding-based similarity (usually cosine) and human judgments, providing a fine-grained benchmark for semantic similarity and paraphrase detection across diverse domains.

MTEB STS16 is the Semantic Textual Similarity 2016 subset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, consisting of sentence pairs with human-annotated graded similarity scores (typically 0–5). It covers diverse English domains (news, headlines, answers, forums) to test semantic alignment across varying genres. Used to evaluate embedding and sentence-pair models, performance is measured by correlation (Pearson/Spearman) between model similarity scores and human judgments, making it a standard benchmark for assessing semantic representation quality.

STSBenchmark (as used in MTEB) is a semantic textual similarity dataset of sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores on a continuous scale (commonly 0–5). It provides train/dev/test splits across multiple domains to evaluate how well sentence or text embeddings capture graded semantic relatedness. Common evaluation measures are Pearson/Spearman correlation between predicted similarity (e.g., cosine similarity of embeddings) and gold scores, making it a standard benchmark for embedding quality on STS tasks.

SummEval is a human-annotated summarization evaluation dataset containing document–summary pairs with expert quality judgments across dimensions such as coherence, consistency, fluency, and relevance. It is designed to benchmark and train automatic summarization evaluation metrics and embedding-based systems by measuring how well model scores correlate with human assessments, supporting research on summary quality estimation and metric learning.

AFQMC (Ant Financial Question Matching Corpus) is a Chinese sentence-pair dataset for semantic similarity/paraphrase identification. It contains question/query pairs labeled for semantic equivalence and is included in MTEB to evaluate text-embedding models’ ability to capture fine-grained semantic relationships in Chinese. AFQMC is useful for benchmarking embeddings on tasks such as semantic textual similarity, paraphrase detection, retrieval, clustering, and downstream classification.

MTEB ATEC is a sentence-pair dataset for evaluating text embeddings on semantic similarity and relevance. It contains short text pairs annotated with graded similarity/relevance labels, emphasizing fine-grained distinctions between closely related texts. Included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB), ATEC is used to benchmark embedding quality for tasks such as semantic textual similarity, semantic search, and retrieval-based ranking.

MTEB BQ is a query–document relevance dataset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It contains real short search queries paired with candidate documents and relevance judgments, designed to evaluate embedding models on semantic retrieval and ranking tasks. The dataset emphasizes short-form query understanding and is suited for measuring embedding quality in nearest-neighbor search, semantic search, and retrieval-oriented downstream applications.

MTEB LCQMC is the LCQMC (Large-scale Chinese Question Matching Corpus) subset used in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains roughly 260k Chinese sentence pairs labeled with binary annotations indicating semantic equivalence (paraphrase/duplicate vs. non-duplicate). Designed for evaluating and training sentence embeddings and paraphrase detection models, it supports tasks such as semantic similarity scoring, retrieval, and binary classification in Chinese-language settings.

MTEB PAWSX is the PAWS-X paraphrase dataset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark for evaluating multilingual sentence embeddings. It contains sentence pairs labeled as paraphrase or non-paraphrase with challenging high lexical overlap and word-order perturbations across multiple languages (e.g., English, German, Spanish, French, Japanese, Korean, Chinese). It is used to test embedding models on paraphrase identification, semantic similarity, robustness to word-order/lexical overlap, and cross-lingual transfer.

MTEB QBQTC is a dataset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark composed of short query–title pairs annotated with relevance/class labels. It is designed to evaluate embedding models on semantic similarity, retrieval and classification of short texts by testing their ability to match user queries to candidate titles or categories. The dataset is useful for benchmarking embedding quality, ranking performance, and downstream classification on concise, real-world query–title examples.

MTEB STSB is the Semantic Textual Similarity (STS-B) task included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark: a collection of sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores (typically 0–5). It evaluates sentence-embedding models by comparing embedding-based similarity (e.g., cosine) to human judgments using correlation metrics (Pearson/Spearman). Drawn from SemEval STS sources across varied domains, it benchmarks a model’s ability to capture fine-grained semantic relatedness and paraphrase strength.

MTEB SICKFr is a French version of the SICK (Sentences Involving Compositional Knowledge) dataset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It comprises French sentence pairs annotated with human semantic relatedness scores and entailment labels, enabling evaluation of sentence embeddings on semantic textual similarity, entailment recognition, retrieval, and clustering tasks. The dataset is intended for benchmarking and comparing embedding models’ ability to capture fine-grained semantic relations in French.

SummEvalFr is a French summarization evaluation dataset in MTEB that provides documents with multiple system-generated and reference summaries accompanied by crowd-sourced human ratings across quality dimensions (consistency, relevance, coherence, fluency). Derived from the SummEval benchmark and localized to French, it is intended to benchmark embedding-based methods and evaluation metrics by measuring correlation between embedding similarities and human judgments, supporting research on summary quality assessment and multilingual summarization evaluation.

MTEB MIRACLRetrieval (ru) is the Russian-language subset of the MIRACL retrieval benchmark included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It comprises Russian queries paired with candidate documents/paragraphs and relevance annotations, designed to evaluate text-embedding models on monolingual semantic search and ranking. The dataset is intended for benchmarking dense retrieval, embedding quality, and downstream search applications in Russian.

MTEB AILACasedocs (default) is a legal-domain benchmark of case documents and associated queries/annotations for evaluating text embedding models on retrieval and semantic tasks. It contains long-form court opinions and case metadata with relevance labels suitable for semantic search, reranking, clustering, and similarity evaluation. The dataset stresses domain-specific language, long-context representation, and fine-grained semantic distinctions common in legal texts, making it useful for benchmarking embedding quality, domain adaptation, and zero-shot retrieval performance in legal information access.

AILAStatutes (default) is a legal-domain benchmark in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) containing statutory provisions and associated metadata for evaluating text embeddings. It is designed to test models on legal semantic understanding and retrieval tasks—such as semantic search, similarity, clustering, and classification—by challenging embeddings with domain-specific vocabulary, hierarchical structure, and varying passage lengths. The dataset is useful for benchmarking and developing embeddings that must capture nuanced legal meanings and relationships.

MTEB ARCChallenge (default) is the ARC Challenge subset from the AI2 Reasoning Challenge adapted for the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It comprises grade-school-level, multiple-choice science questions that require reasoning beyond surface-level retrieval, with each question paired to candidate answers and a labeled correct answer. The default configuration provides query–candidate data and evaluation protocols to assess embedding models on tasks like retrieval, semantic matching, and answer selection, making it a challenging benchmark for embedding quality on reasoning-intensive QA.

AlphaNLI (default) is a natural language inference (NLI) dataset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It comprises premise–hypothesis pairs annotated with entailment, contradiction, or neutral labels to evaluate sentence-level semantic understanding. The dataset contains challenging, adversarial-style examples to assess robustness and generalization of embedding models. In MTEB it serves as a standard task for measuring embedding quality on NLI-style classification and semantic retrieval.

ArxivClusteringP2P.v2 is a benchmarking dataset from MTEB for evaluating text embedding models on clustering of scientific papers. It contains arXiv paper texts (typically titles and abstracts) grouped into ground-truth topic clusters derived from arXiv subject categories, enabling assessment of how well embeddings capture topical similarity. Designed for pairwise/point-to-point clustering evaluation, the dataset measures clustering quality and topic separation for applications like topic discovery and corpus organization; v2 reflects updated preprocessing and label refinement.

MTEB BigPatentClustering (default) is a large-scale clustering benchmark drawn from the BigPatent corpus, containing patent titles and abstracts paired with patent classification labels (e.g., CPC). It evaluates embedding and clustering methods on domain-specific, technical texts with many fine-grained, imbalanced classes, testing semantic representation quality, scalability, and cluster coherence. The dataset is intended for unsupervised clustering and representation benchmarking within MTEB.

MTEB FaithDial (default) is a dataset for evaluating faithfulness and factual grounding in multi-turn dialogue: it pairs conversational contexts and candidate responses with reference knowledge passages and human annotations indicating whether responses faithfully reflect the referenced information. Designed for embedding-based retrieval, response ranking and faithfulness-detection tasks, it enables evaluation and development of models that must generate or select dialogue outputs consistent with source knowledge.

FeedbackQARetrieval is a retrieval benchmark in MTEB that pairs user questions with a pool of candidate answers or feedback items labeled for relevance. It is designed to evaluate text embedding and dense retrieval models on their ability to retrieve and rank semantically relevant answers in a QA/feedback setting, using metrics such as recall@k and MRR. The dataset supports development and comparison of embedding-based semantic search and retrieval systems for interactive question-answering and feedback retrieval scenarios.

MTEB STS22 (tr) is the Turkish subset of the Semantic Textual Similarity task from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB), containing Turkish sentence pairs annotated with graded similarity scores (typically 0–5). It is designed to evaluate text embedding models by measuring how well embedding-based similarity estimates correlate with human judgments (e.g., Pearson/Spearman), enabling benchmarking of semantic equivalence and semantic search performance in Turkish.

MTEB STS22 (it) is the Italian subset of the Semantic Textual Similarity 2022 task within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains Italian sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores, intended to evaluate sentence embeddings and semantic similarity models. The dataset is used to benchmark embedding quality via correlation metrics (e.g., Pearson/Spearman) for tasks such as semantic search, clustering, and paraphrase detection in Italian.

MTEB STS22 (ar) is the Arabic portion of the Semantic Textual Similarity (STS) 2022 subset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains Arabic sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores (typically on a 0–5 scale) and is intended to evaluate how well embedding models capture fine-grained semantic similarity at the sentence level. The split is used for benchmarking and comparing embedding quality using correlation metrics (e.g., Pearson/Spearman) and is useful for downstream tasks such as semantic search, clustering, duplicate detection, and paraphrase identification in Arabic.

MTEB STS22 (es-it) is a semantic textual similarity subset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark comprising Spanish–Italian sentence pairs annotated with human similarity scores. It is designed to evaluate cross-lingual and multilingual embedding models by measuring how well embedding-based similarity estimates align with human judgments (commonly via Spearman/Pearson correlation). The split is useful for benchmarking embedding quality for cross-lingual semantic search, retrieval, paraphrase detection, and transfer across Romance languages.

WikiCitiesClustering is an MTEB clustering dataset comprising Wikipedia city articles grouped into clusters that reflect geographic or semantic associations (e.g., cities by country or region). It benchmarks the ability of text embedding models to produce representations that cluster semantically and geographically related city descriptions, enabling evaluation of unsupervised clustering quality and embedding separability for document-level retrieval and grouping tasks.

MTEB AppsRetrieval (default) is a retrieval benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that evaluates embedding models on app-store search. It contains user queries paired with candidate app metadata (titles and descriptions) and ground-truth relevance labels, allowing measurement of semantic search and ranking performance in an app-discovery setting. The default split provides query-to-candidate pairs for computing retrieval metrics (e.g., recall, MAP, nDCG), useful for benchmarking and tuning dense and sparse embedding–based retrieval systems.

MTEB COIRCodeSearchNetRetrieval (python) is a retrieval benchmark derived from the CodeSearchNet corpus that pairs Python function-level code snippets with natural-language queries or descriptions. It provides ground-truth relevance annotations for evaluating embedding and retrieval models on semantic code search and ranking tasks. The dataset is intended to assess how well text-code embeddings capture cross-modal semantics for practical code search, recommendation, and code-understanding applications.

MTEB COIRCodeSearchNetRetrieval (javascript) is a code-search retrieval benchmark drawn from the CodeSearchNet corpus and included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It contains natural-language queries paired with function-level JavaScript code snippets to evaluate embedding-based retrieval models. The dataset is designed to measure semantic matching between queries and code (e.g., recall@k, MRR), supporting development and comparison of models that embed code and text into a shared vector space for accurate code search and retrieval.

MTEB COIRCodeSearchNetRetrieval (go) is a code-search retrieval dataset derived from CodeSearchNet for the Go programming language. It pairs natural-language queries (typically function docstrings or user queries) with corresponding Go code snippets to benchmark semantic retrieval and embedding models. Designed for evaluating embedding quality on code search tasks, it is commonly used to measure retrieval metrics such as MRR and Recall@k and to develop semantic code search and similarity systems.

MTEB COIRCodeSearchNetRetrieval (ruby) is a retrieval benchmark derived from the CodeSearchNet corpus for the Ruby programming language. It contains natural-language queries (e.g., docstrings, comments or search phrases) paired with candidate Ruby code snippets and ground-truth relevance labels, enabling evaluation of semantic code search and embedding-based retrieval systems. Used within MTEB to assess embedding quality on text-to-code retrieval and ranking tasks, the dataset tests models on code-specific vocabulary, identifier variability and contextual semantics from real-world GitHub projects.

MTEB COIRCodeSearchNetRetrieval (java) is a Java code-search retrieval dataset derived from CodeSearchNet for the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It pairs natural-language queries with Java code snippets and relevance labels to evaluate embedding-based semantic search and retrieval models for query-to-code matching. It is intended for training and benchmarking code-search encoders and rankers using metrics such as MRR and recall@k, and presents challenges like domain-specific vocabulary and syntactic variability.

MTEB COIRCodeSearchNetRetrieval (php) is the PHP subset of the CodeSearchNet retrieval benchmark included in MTEB. It contains PHP function source code paired with natural-language queries and docstrings extracted from open-source repositories, enabling supervised evaluation of text-to-code and code-to-text retrieval. The dataset is designed for training and benchmarking embedding-based semantic code search and ranking models using metrics such as MRR and recall@k, supporting research in code understanding, semantic retrieval, and developer tooling.

MTEB CodeFeedbackMT (default) is a dataset of code snippets paired with reviewer feedback or comments, provided across multiple human and programming languages. It is designed to evaluate embeddings on tasks such as semantic similarity, retrieval, and cross-lingual alignment between code and natural-language feedback. The dataset supports development and benchmarking of models for code search, automated code review, feedback retrieval, and multilingual code–text understanding.

MTEB CodeFeedbackST (default) is a dataset of short code snippets paired with concise reviewer feedback or comments, designed to evaluate embedding models’ ability to capture semantic relationships between code and short textual feedback. It supports tasks such as cross-modal retrieval, semantic similarity, and clustering between code and feedback texts, enabling assessment of embedding quality for code understanding, code-search, and automated review assistance.

MTEB CodeSearchNetCCRetrieval (python) is a code–comment retrieval benchmark derived from the CodeSearchNet corpus for evaluating embedding models on Python code search. Each example pairs a natural-language comment or docstring with candidate Python code snippets, enabling evaluation of semantic similarity and retrieval quality (e.g., MRR, recall@k). The task assesses how well text and code embeddings align for practical code search and natural-language-to-code retrieval scenarios.

MTEB CodeSearchNetCCRetrieval (javascript) is a JavaScript code-search retrieval benchmark derived from the CodeSearchNet corpus and packaged for the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It pairs natural-language function descriptions or docstrings as queries with corresponding JavaScript code snippets as targets to evaluate semantic retrieval and embedding models. The dataset is intended for assessing embedding quality and nearest-neighbor search performance on code understanding tasks, commonly using ranking metrics such as MRR and recall@k.

MTEB CodeSearchNetCCRetrieval (go) is a retrieval benchmark derived from the CodeSearchNet corpus and formatted for the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It pairs Go functions with associated natural-language descriptions (docstrings/comments) to support supervised and evaluation tasks for code–text and text–code retrieval. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating embedding and semantic search models on real-world Go code from public repositories, enabling assessment of ranking quality and cross-modal code understanding.

MTEB CodeSearchNetCCRetrieval (ruby) is a retrieval benchmark derived from the CodeSearchNet corpus for Ruby. It contains Ruby function-level code snippets paired with natural-language docstrings and query–code pairs to evaluate embedding models on code search and code↔text retrieval tasks. The dataset measures how well embeddings capture functional semantics for ranking and semantic search, enabling comparison of models on code understanding, code retrieval, and query-to-code matching.

MTEB CodeSearchNetCCRetrieval (Java) is a retrieval benchmark derived from the CodeSearchNet corpus for evaluating embedding models on code–comment/code–query matching. It contains Java function-level code snippets paired with natural-language queries or comments and relevance labels, enabling supervised evaluation of semantic code search and retrieval. The dataset is intended to measure embedding quality with retrieval metrics (e.g., recall@k, MRR) and to support development of models for code search, code understanding, and documentation or recommendation tasks.

MTEB CodeSearchNetCCRetrieval (php) is a benchmark dataset for evaluating embedding-based code search and retrieval on PHP code. It pairs PHP functions with natural-language docstrings and relevance annotations to support semantic retrieval, nearest-neighbor search, and embedding-quality evaluations. Included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB), it measures models’ ability to match natural-language queries to relevant PHP code snippets.

MTEB CodeSearchNetRetrieval (python) is a retrieval benchmark derived from the CodeSearchNet corpus, consisting of natural-language queries (often function docstrings or short descriptions) paired with Python code snippets extracted from open-source repositories. It is designed to evaluate embedding models for semantic code search and retrieval by measuring how well vector representations of queries retrieve the relevant code (common metrics: MRR, Recall@K). The dataset supports benchmarking of cross-modal and mono-modal embedding approaches for code understanding, search, and downstream tasks such as code recommendation and snippet ranking.

MTEB CodeSearchNetRetrieval (JavaScript) is a retrieval benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that evaluates embedding models on code search for JavaScript. It contains JavaScript code snippets paired with natural-language queries/docstrings extracted from open-source repositories, and tasks require retrieving relevant code given a query (and vice versa). The dataset is used to assess and compare embedding quality for cross-modal code↔text retrieval using ranking metrics such as MRR and Recall@K, supporting development of code-search and code-understanding systems.

MTEB CodeSearchNetRetrieval (go) is a retrieval benchmark of Go-language functions paired with natural-language queries and docstrings from the CodeSearchNet corpus, prepared for evaluating semantic code–text retrieval. It measures embedding and search model performance on tasks like text→code and code→text retrieval using metrics such as MRR and recall@k, enabling comparison of models’ ability to match developer intent to Go code. Useful for developing and benchmarking code search, code understanding, and semantic retrieval systems.

MTEB CodeSearchNetRetrieval (ruby) is a retrieval benchmark of natural-language queries paired with Ruby code snippets and relevance labels, derived from the CodeSearchNet corpus. It is designed to evaluate embedding and retrieval models on text-to-code and code-to-text semantic search in the Ruby programming language, measuring how well models match intent to implementation for code search applications.

MTEB CodeSearchNetRetrieval (java) is a code-search retrieval benchmark derived from the CodeSearchNet corpus focused on Java. It pairs natural-language queries or docstrings with Java code snippets and labeled relevant targets, enabling evaluation of embedding-based retrieval and cross-modal semantic matching. The dataset is used to benchmark models on tasks like semantic code search using metrics such as MRR and Recall@K, supporting development of vector representations for retrieving relevant Java code given natural language queries.

MTEB CodeSearchNetRetrieval (php) is a code-search retrieval dataset derived from CodeSearchNet focused on PHP. It pairs PHP function-level code snippets with accompanying natural-language descriptions/docstrings to form query–code relevance pairs, split into train/validation/test. Designed for evaluation of embedding and retrieval systems, it measures a model’s ability to rank relevant code given a natural-language query (metrics like MRR/recall). It is intended for benchmarking semantic code search and representation learning on PHP code.

MTEB CodeTransOceanContest (default) is a benchmark within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark focused on code representation and cross-language code translation tasks. It contains paired examples of code snippets (and where available, natural-language descriptions or translated equivalents) across multiple programming languages, enabling evaluation of embedding models on code search, semantic similarity, and translation retrieval. The dataset stresses cross-lingual code understanding and clone detection, providing standardized train/validation/test splits for comparable evaluation of models used in code intelligence and transfer learning.

MTEB CodeTransOceanDL (default) is a benchmark dataset within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark focused on code representation and retrieval. It contains function- or snippet-level examples paired with natural-language descriptions and/or related code instances, enabling evaluation of code-to-text, code search, and semantic similarity tasks. The default split is intended for measuring embedding quality on code understanding, retrieval, and clustering across programming languages and real-world code patterns. It is useful for developing and comparing code embedding models, semantic code search systems, and downstream tools that rely on robust code semantics.

MTEB CosQA (default) is a multiple-choice answer-selection dataset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark designed to evaluate embedding models’ ability to identify the correct answer among distractors using similarity-based retrieval. It provides question–candidate answer pairs with one correct answer and several distractors, enabling assessment of semantic matching, ranking, and robustness to lexical variation in answer selection tasks.

MIRACL Retrieval (ar) is an Arabic retrieval dataset in the MTEB suite for evaluating text embedding models on semantic search and dense retrieval. It provides Arabic queries paired with candidate passages and human relevance labels, enabling supervised evaluation of embedding-based ranking, retrieval, and semantic matching approaches. The dataset covers diverse topics and real-world query formulations, making it useful for benchmarking model performance on Arabic monolingual retrieval and for comparing embedding quality across retrieval scenarios.

MTEB MIRACLRetrieval (bn) is a Bengali information-retrieval benchmark from the MIRACL collection included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It provides Bengali queries paired with a passage corpus and relevance annotations to evaluate semantic search, dense retrieval, and ranking methods. The set is intended to measure the quality and cross-lingual robustness of text embeddings and retrieval models on Bengali retrieval tasks in both supervised and zero-shot settings.

MTEB MIRACLRetrieval (de) is the German subset of the MIRACL retrieval benchmark included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It provides German queries paired with a document/passage corpus and human-annotated relevance labels for passage-level retrieval. Designed to evaluate semantic search and embedding-based retrieval models, it offers standard train/dev/test splits and is used to measure retrieval metrics such as MRR, recall@k, and nDCG, enabling assessment of multilingual and cross-lingual retrieval performance on German-language content.

MTEB MIRACLRetrieval (en) is an English information-retrieval dataset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark designed to evaluate embedding-based semantic search and ranking. It provides queries paired with candidate documents and relevance labels across diverse domains, enabling assessment of embedding models on nearest-neighbor retrieval, ranking metrics (e.g., MRR, NDCG), and generalization to real-world search scenarios. The set is intended for benchmarking and comparing text representation quality for English retrieval tasks.

MTEB MIRACLRetrieval (es) is the Spanish subset of the MIRACL retrieval task in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It comprises Spanish queries paired with candidate passages/documents and relevance labels to evaluate semantic search and dense retrieval systems. The dataset is intended for benchmarking embedding-based models on ranking metrics (e.g., recall@k, MRR, nDCG) and for assessing multilingual and Spanish-specific retrieval performance.

MTEB MIRACLRetrieval (fa) is a Persian (Farsi) retrieval benchmark drawn from the MIRACL dataset and formatted for the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It provides Farsi queries paired with candidate passages and relevance labels to evaluate embedding-based semantic search and ranking models. The dataset is intended to measure representation quality for dense and sparse retrieval methods using ranking metrics (MRR, nDCG), enabling comparison and development of sentence/document embedding models for Persian information retrieval.

MTEB MIRACLRetrieval (fi) is a Finnish-language retrieval dataset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It pairs Finnish queries with candidate documents or passages annotated for relevance to evaluate semantic retrieval and embedding-based search. The set is intended for benchmarking sentence/paragraph embeddings and dense retrieval models on Finnish information-retrieval tasks (e.g., semantic search, passage retrieval), enabling comparison of retrieval accuracy and cross-lingual transfer when used alongside other MTEB subsets.

MTEB MIRACLRetrieval (fr) is the French split of the MIRACL retrieval dataset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, consisting of French queries paired with candidate documents and relevance annotations for assessing semantic search. It is used to evaluate embedding-based retrieval and ranking models on monolingual French information retrieval tasks and to measure encoder transfer and generalization across retrieval scenarios.

MTEB MIRACLRetrieval (hi) is a Hindi monolingual information-retrieval benchmark from the MIRACL collection included in MTEB. It provides Hindi queries paired with candidate passages and relevance labels to evaluate semantic search and retrieval quality of embedding and ranking models. The dataset is suited for testing monolingual and multilingual embeddings, zero-shot transfer, and ranking performance on realistic, web-derived Hindi retrieval queries.

MIRACL Retrieval (id) is a multilingual information retrieval benchmark within MTEB that provides query–document pairs with relevance labels across multiple languages. It is designed to evaluate text embedding models for semantic and cross-lingual retrieval, supporting open-domain and passage-ranking scenarios. The dataset enables assessment of embedding-based retrieval performance using ranking metrics (e.g., Recall@k, MRR, nDCG) and is useful for benchmarking and improving models for semantic search, cross-lingual transfer, and retrieval-based downstream tasks.

MTEB MIRACLRetrieval (ja) is the Japanese subset of the MIRACL retrieval benchmark included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It provides Japanese queries paired with candidate passages and relevance labels to evaluate semantic retrieval and ranking performance of text embeddings. The set is intended for benchmarking Japanese-language embedding models on standard retrieval metrics (e.g., Recall@k, MRR, nDCG) and for assessing their ability to capture semantic similarity in Japanese retrieval scenarios.

MTEB MIRACLRetrieval (ko) is the Korean slice of the MIRACL retrieval dataset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains Korean-language queries paired with candidate passages and relevance labels for supervised evaluation of embedding-based information retrieval and semantic search. The set is intended to benchmark and develop sentence/document embedding models and retrieval systems for Korean, supporting evaluation with ranking metrics (e.g., MRR, Recall@k, nDCG) and enabling both monolingual and cross-lingual retrieval research.

MTEB MIRACLRetrieval (sw) is a multilingual retrieval dataset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that provides query–document pairs across many languages for evaluating semantic retrieval. It focuses on passage/document ranking, measuring retrieval metrics such as MRR and nDCG to assess dense embedding models in monolingual and cross‑lingual settings. The collection is suited for benchmarking embedding-based nearest‑neighbor search and real‑world information‑retrieval performance.

MTEB MIRACLRetrieval (te) is a Telugu-language retrieval dataset from the MIRACL collection adapted for the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It contains queries paired with candidate documents and relevance labels to evaluate semantic search and information retrieval systems in Telugu. The dataset is intended for benchmarking embedding models, dense retrieval and reranking methods on cross-lingual and monolingual retrieval tasks, enabling assessment of representation quality and retrieval effectiveness for Telugu text.

MIRACLRetrieval (th) is the Thai subset of the MIRACL retrieval dataset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It provides Thai-language queries paired with candidate passages/documents and relevance labels for supervised evaluation of semantic retrieval and embedding-based ranking. The data is designed to benchmark dense and sparse retrieval, reranking, and embedding models on Thai text, supporting standard IR metrics (MRR, MAP, nDCG) and assessment of language-specific and cross-lingual retrieval performance.

MIRACLRetrieval (yo) is the Yoruba-language subset of the MIRACL retrieval benchmark included in MTEB. It provides query–document pairs with relevance annotations for evaluating semantic search and embedding-based retrieval in Yoruba. The dataset is intended to benchmark text embedding models on monolingual retrieval performance in a low-resource language, supporting standard retrieval metrics (e.g., MRR, NDCG, recall) and enabling assessment of models’ ability to capture query–document relevance across diverse topics.

MTEB MIRACLRetrieval (zh) is the Chinese subset of the MIRACL retrieval task within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It provides Chinese queries paired with candidate passages and relevance labels to evaluate embedding-based semantic search and ranking. The dataset is intended for benchmarking and training retrieval models (bi-encoders, cross-encoders) on Chinese semantic matching tasks using metrics like recall@k, MRR, and nDCG.

MTEB StackOverflowQA (default) is a benchmark dataset of Stack Overflow programming question–answer pairs prepared for embedding evaluation. Each example pairs a question (title and body, optionally tags) with one or more answers (often the accepted answer), enabling semantic search, retrieval, reranking, and clustering tasks in a technical QA domain. It assesses embedding models’ ability to represent technical language and code-related content and to retrieve relevant answers across diverse programming topics.

MTEB SyntheticText2SQL (default) is a synthetic dataset of natural-language questions paired with corresponding SQL queries generated from templates and diverse schema permutations. It is designed to evaluate embedding models and retrieval systems on semantic alignment between free-form text and structured queries—use cases include retrieval of relevant SQL given an NL question, similarity-based ranking, and assessing embedding quality for semantic parsing. The dataset supports benchmarking and development of NL-to-SQL retrieval, retrieval-augmented generation, and embedding models for structured-query understanding.

MTEB PAWSX is the PAWS-X paraphrase dataset included in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark for evaluating multilingual sentence embeddings. It contains sentence pairs labeled as paraphrase or non-paraphrase with challenging high lexical overlap and word-order perturbations across multiple languages (e.g., English, German, Spanish, French, Japanese, Korean, Chinese). It is used to test embedding models on paraphrase identification, semantic similarity, robustness to word-order/lexical overlap, and cross-lingual transfer.

GeoreviewClusteringP2P is a clustering dataset of geotagged place reviews designed to evaluate embedding models' ability to group texts that refer to the same physical location. Each example contains short review text (and typically geolocation or place identifiers) where the goal is to cluster reviews into place-level groups, testing fine-grained semantic similarity and duplicate detection across noisy, real-world user-generated content. It serves as a benchmark for unsupervised clustering and representation learning, emphasizing robustness to stylistic variation, partial evidence, and geo-semantic ambiguity.

MTEB RiaNewsRetrieval is a retrieval benchmark in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark suite consisting of Russian news articles paired with queries and relevance judgments. It is designed to evaluate embedding-based semantic search and document-ranking systems on real-world news content, enabling comparison of dense and sparse retrieval models, ranking quality, and generalization in the Russian news domain.

MTEB RuBQReranking is a Russian-language reranking benchmark in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It provides queries paired with sets of candidate documents or passages and human-assigned relevance labels for each query-candidate pair, enabling supervised training and evaluation of embedding-based reranking models. The dataset is intended to measure how well retrieval and re-ranking methods improve result ordering for Russian information-retrieval tasks, and is commonly used to compare embedding, cross-encoder, and hybrid approaches using ranking metrics such as nDCG and MRR.

MTEB RuBQRetrieval is a Russian-language retrieval benchmark in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) suite, consisting of Russian queries paired with relevant and non-relevant documents for semantic search evaluation. It is designed to assess and compare embedding models on dense retrieval and ranking tasks in Russian, measuring models’ ability to produce representations that enable accurate document retrieval and semantic matching.

MTEB RuSciBenchGRNTIClusteringP2P is a benchmark for evaluating text embeddings on clustering and pairwise similarity within Russian scientific literature. The dataset comprises Russian scientific documents (titles/abstracts/papers) annotated with GRNTI subject codes; positive pairs are formed by documents sharing the same GRNTI label and negatives by differing labels. It is intended for paper-to-paper (P2P) clustering and pairwise retrieval evaluations in MTEB, measuring how well embeddings capture domain-specific topical similarity for semantic grouping and clustering in the scientific domain.

RuSciBenchOECDClusteringP2P is an MTEB subset for evaluating text embeddings on clustering and pairwise similarity in the Russian/OECD scientific and policy domain. It contains OECD-related documents (reports, abstracts, summaries) with ground-truth cluster labels and curated pairwise (P2P) annotations indicating whether two items belong to the same cluster. The dataset targets assessment of embedding quality for semantic grouping, clustering algorithms, and pairwise retrieval in a specialized, domain-specific Russian-language corpus.

MTEB CMedQAv1-reranking (default) is a reranking benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark focused on medical question-answering. It provides medical queries with a set of candidate answers/documents and relevance labels, enabling evaluation of embedding models’ ability to rank relevant answers above irrelevant ones. Designed for assessing semantic retrieval and reranking performance (e.g., MRR, NDCG) in clinical/medical QA scenarios, it is used to compare and develop embedding encoders and reranker pipelines under MTEB’s default evaluation settings.

CMedQAv2-reranking is a medical question-answering reranking dataset in the MTEB benchmark. Each instance pairs a clinical or consumer medical query with a pool of candidate passages/documents annotated for relevance, enabling evaluation of embedding-based rerankers and retrieval models. The dataset emphasizes domain-specific terminology and strict relevance judgments, making it suitable for assessing and training models to rank clinically relevant answers in biomedical/healthcare QA tasks.

MTEB MIRACLRetrievalHardNegatives (ar) is an Arabic retrieval benchmark within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that provides queries with corresponding relevant passages and deliberately mined hard-negative passages. It is designed to evaluate and stress-test embedding-based retrieval and ranking models under challenging negative examples that are semantically similar to positives. The dataset supports development and comparison of dense retrieval, contrastive training, and re-ranking systems for Arabic information retrieval tasks.

MTEB MLQARetrieval (ara-ara) is a monolingual Arabic retrieval benchmark drawn from the MLQA dataset, providing Arabic queries paired with candidate passages and relevance labels for evaluating semantic search and dense retrieval systems. It is used within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) to assess embedding models on retrieval metrics such as recall@k and MRR in an Arabic-only setting. The dataset supports development and comparison of Arabic semantic retrieval, passage ranking, and embedding-based search methods.

MintakaRetrieval (ar) is an Arabic retrieval dataset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) containing Arabic queries paired with candidate documents/passages and relevance judgments. It is designed to evaluate and benchmark embedding-based semantic search and ranking models for Arabic, supporting common retrieval metrics (e.g., recall@k, nDCG). The dataset is suitable for testing monolingual Arabic retrieval performance, comparing embedding methods, and fine-tuning dense retrieval systems.

MTEB MrTidyRetrieval (arabic) is an Arabic-language retrieval benchmark for evaluating text embedding and semantic search models. It provides Arabic queries paired with candidate documents or passages and relevance labels for supervised evaluation of retrieval and ranking performance. The dataset targets dense vector search and embedding quality (e.g., recall@k, MRR) and challenges models with Arabic-specific morphology and lexical variation. It is intended for training, validating, and comparing multilingual or Arabic-focused retrieval systems.

MTEB SadeemQuestionRetrieval (default) is a question-retrieval benchmark from the MTEB suite that pairs user queries with candidate questions and relevance labels (default split). It is designed to evaluate semantic search and embedding models on retrieval and ranking tasks—such as duplicate question detection, semantic nearest-neighbor search, and answer reranking—using metrics like Recall@K, MRR, and nDCG. The dataset supports development and benchmarking of models for question matching and conversational/QA retrieval scenarios.

XPQARetrieval (ara-ara) is the Arabic monolingual subset of the XPQA retrieval task from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It contains Arabic questions paired with relevant Arabic passages and is designed to evaluate embedding models on semantic retrieval for question answering. The dataset benchmarks dense retrieval and semantic search performance, supporting development and comparison of embedding-based retrieval and re-ranking methods for Arabic QA.

MTEB STS17 (ar-ar) is the Arabic–Arabic subset of the Semantic Textual Similarity 2017 benchmark used in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It contains Arabic sentence pairs annotated with graded similarity scores (e.g., 0–5) that quantify semantic equivalence. The split is intended to evaluate sentence and text embedding models on semantic similarity, retrieval and ranking tasks, typically measured via correlation metrics (Pearson/Spearman) and ranking-based evaluations.

GerDaLIRSmall is a compact German image–caption dataset in the MTEB suite for evaluating cross-modal embeddings. It contains images paired with German-language captions and is intended for text-to-image and image-to-text retrieval tasks. As a small, default benchmark, it enables fast experimentation and comparison of multilingual and multimodal embedding models using standard retrieval metrics.

LeCaRDv2 (MTEB, default) is a retrieval benchmark of query–document relevance judgments designed to evaluate text embedding and dense retrieval models. It provides queries paired with labeled relevant and non‑relevant documents (including hard negatives) to test semantic matching and ranking quality. The dataset is used within MTEB to assess embedding representations for retrieval tasks, measuring how well models separate relevant from irrelevant texts and support end‑to‑end ranking in realistic search scenarios.

LegalBench ConsumerContractsQA (MTEB default) is a benchmark dataset of question–answer pairs grounded in consumer-facing contract documents (e.g., terms of service, warranties, privacy policies). Each instance links a legal question about contract terms, obligations, or consumer rights to a correct answer and the supporting contract passages. It is designed to evaluate embedding models and retrieval/QA pipelines on domain-specific semantic understanding, relevance ranking, and passage retrieval in the legal consumer-contracts setting.

MTEB LegalBenchCorporateLobbying (default) is a legal-domain benchmark for evaluating text embeddings on corporate lobbying detection and related retrieval tasks. It contains legal and policy texts (e.g., filings, reports, regulatory notices, and news excerpts) labeled for whether they pertain to corporate lobbying activities, enabling binary classification, semantic search, and clustering evaluations. Designed for the MTEB suite, it measures embedding quality for compliance, policy analysis, and legal information retrieval applications.

MTEB LegalQuAD (default) is a benchmark dataset of legal question–answer pairs with associated reference passages, curated for evaluating text embedding models on legal-domain retrieval and question-answering tasks. It emphasizes domain-specific semantics and relevance judgment, enabling assessment of embedding quality for semantic search, passage retrieval, and QA in legal texts. The dataset is provided in the default MTEB format for standardized comparison and domain adaptation of embedding models.

MTEB LegalSummarization (default) is a benchmark dataset of legal texts paired with human-written summaries, created to train and evaluate summarization and embedding models in the legal domain. It contains long-form documents (e.g., case opinions, statutes, contract excerpts) with concise reference summaries, emphasizing domain-specific terminology, factual precision, and preservation of legal meaning. The dataset is intended for benchmarking abstractive and extractive summarization, long-context modeling, and embedding-based retrieval or evaluation in legal NLP applications.

MTEB MintakaRetrieval (hi) is a Hindi-language retrieval benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) that provides query-document pairs with relevance labels for evaluating semantic search and dense retrieval models. It contains Hindi queries paired with candidate passages or documents and labeled relevance to measure how well embedding-based encoders capture semantic similarity in Hindi. The dataset is intended for assessing retrieval performance of embedding models using metrics such as recall@k and MRR, supporting development of Hindi-specific or multilingual semantic search systems.

MTEB MintakaRetrieval (it) is an Italian-language retrieval benchmark within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It provides query-document pairs with relevance annotations to evaluate embedding-based semantic search and information retrieval models in Italian. The dataset is designed to assess retrieval quality of bi-encoder and cross-encoder architectures, supporting comparisons of multilingual and monolingual embedding models on realistic search tasks.

MTEB MintakaRetrieval (ja) is a Japanese-language retrieval benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) Mintaka suite. It contains Japanese queries paired with candidate documents or passages and relevance annotations for evaluating semantic retrieval performance. The dataset is intended to assess and compare text embedding models (bi-encoder/ANN) on retrieval metrics such as MRR, nDCG, and recall in a Japanese setting, supporting development of multilingual and language-specific embedding models for search and information retrieval.

MintakaRetrieval (pt) is a Portuguese retrieval benchmark within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) designed to evaluate embedding models on semantic search and dense retrieval in Portuguese. It provides query–document pairs with relevance labels to assess ranking quality (e.g., recall@k, MRR) for tasks such as semantic search, information retrieval, and cross-lingual retrieval. The dataset is intended for benchmarking and comparing embedding models’ ability to capture Portuguese semantic relevance in retrieval and ranking scenarios.

MTEB HellaSwag (default) is a commonsense reasoning multiple-choice subset used in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark to evaluate embedding quality for pragmatic inference. Each instance contains a short context and several candidate endings (one correct, others distractors); the task is to rank or select the most plausible continuation using embedding similarity or classifiers. It stresses everyday physical and social commonsense, making it a challenging benchmark for measuring semantic understanding, robustness to distractors, and downstream performance of sentence embedding models.

PIQA (Physical Interaction QA) in MTEB is a multiple-choice dataset for evaluating text embeddings on commonsense physical reasoning. Each example presents a short everyday physical task and two candidate solutions (one correct), testing knowledge of object affordances, support, friction, and practical action choices. In the MTEB "default" setup it is used to measure an embedding model’s ability to match questions to the correct answer (via similarity/retrieval), making it useful for assessing whether embeddings capture pragmatic physical knowledge. The full dataset contains roughly 16k training, 1.8k validation, and 3k test items.

MTEB Quail (default) is a short-text relevance dataset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark designed to evaluate embedding models on pairwise semantic matching. It contains query–candidate text pairs with relevance labels (binary or graded) to test retrieval, semantic similarity, and question–answer matching performance. The dataset is useful for benchmarking embedding quality on short queries and compact candidate texts in retrieval and ranking scenarios.

MTEB RARbCode (default) is a benchmark dataset within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark focused on code representation and code–text matching. It contains aligned code snippets and accompanying natural-language metadata (e.g., function names, docstrings, or comments) organized into standard train/validation/test splits to evaluate embedding models on tasks such as code search, semantic similarity, duplicate detection, and clustering. The dataset is designed to measure how well models capture semantic relationships between code and text and to enable consistent comparison of embeddings on code-centric retrieval and downstream tasks.

MTEB RARbMath (default) is a math-focused retrieval benchmark in the MTEB suite containing math questions paired with candidate posts (relevant and non-relevant answers or passages) collected from community Q&A. It evaluates embedding models’ ability to capture semantic similarity in formula-rich, notation-heavy text where relevance depends on conceptual and symbolic matching beyond surface wording. Typical uses include retrieval, semantic search, reranking and clustering of mathematical content.

MTEB SpartQA (default) is a question-answering benchmark within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that contains question–answer pairs and associated candidate passages for evaluating embedding models on semantic retrieval and answer ranking. Using the MTEB default split and evaluation protocol, it measures how well sentence or passage embeddings support open-domain QA, semantic search, and answer selection tasks.

TempReasonL1 (default) is a dataset in the MTEB suite for evaluating text embeddings on basic temporal reasoning. It contains short event descriptions and sentence pairs annotated with temporal relations (e.g., before, after, simultaneous/overlap). Designed for embedding-based classification and retrieval evaluations, the dataset assesses models’ ability to encode temporal order and simple causal/sequence relations in language. The default configuration provides standard train/validation/test splits and common metrics (accuracy/F1) for reproducible benchmarking.

TempReasonL2Fact is a temporal reasoning dataset of factual statements annotated for temporal relations and factual consistency. It contains short fact sentences and paired queries or candidate facts labeled by temporal relation (e.g., before/after/same or consistent/inconsistent), designed to evaluate models’ ability to encode and compare time-sensitive factual information. It is used in MTEB to benchmark embedding methods on temporal inference, fact verification, and time-aware semantic retrieval tasks.

MTEB TempReasonL3Fact (default) is a benchmark subset within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark focused on level‑3 temporal reasoning over factual statements. It contains text pairs and retrieval/classification tasks that require multi-step, time-aware inference to judge factual relevance, ordering, or consistency across temporal contexts. The dataset is intended to evaluate and compare embedding models’ ability to capture fine-grained, time-sensitive factual relationships for tasks such as temporal retrieval, ranking, and clustering, using the provided default split for reproducible evaluation.

MTEB TempReasonL3Pure (default) is a benchmark subset of the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark focused on high-difficulty temporal reasoning. It contains short texts and text pairs annotated for complex temporal relations (event order, overlap, duration and causal-temporal chains) with minimal lexical shortcuts, forcing multi-step inference. The split is tuned for embedding-based evaluation of retrieval, clustering, and temporal-relation classification in zero-shot and supervised settings, measuring how well representations capture nuanced temporal semantics.

MTEB WinoGrande (default) is a benchmark dataset for evaluating semantic representations on commonsense coreference resolution. It contains large-scale, crowd-sourced examples of sentences with ambiguous pronouns and labeled correct antecedents, requiring world knowledge and reasoning beyond surface cues. Within MTEB it is used to assess embedding and sentence-representation models’ ability to capture fine-grained semantic and commonsense relations relevant to pronoun disambiguation.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (eng-ara) is a cross-lingual retrieval dataset within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that pairs English queries/questions with Arabic candidate passages and binary or graded relevance labels. It is designed to evaluate multilingual sentence- and passage-embedding models on the task of retrieving relevant Arabic text given English queries (and vice versa), supporting dense retrieval and embedding-based ranking research. Typical evaluation metrics include Recall@k, MRR, and nDCG. The dataset is useful for benchmarking and improving English–Arabic semantic matching in QA and information-retrieval systems.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (ara-eng) is a cross-lingual question-answer retrieval dataset in the MTEB suite that pairs Arabic queries with English candidate passages to evaluate multilingual embedding models on retrieval for QA. It measures models’ ability to rank and retrieve answer-bearing passages across Arabic–English language pairs, supporting development of cross-lingual semantic search and question-answering systems.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (hin-hin) is a Hindi monolingual question-to-passage retrieval dataset in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It provides Hindi queries paired with relevant and non-relevant Hindi passages, with relevance annotations for benchmarking semantic search and dense retrieval systems. The set is intended to evaluate embedding models’ ability to rank and retrieve semantically matching Hindi texts (metrics: recall@k, MRR, nDCG), supporting development and comparison of bi-encoder and retrieval-oriented representations for Hindi.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (eng-hin) is a cross-lingual retrieval benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark designed for English–Hindi retrieval tasks. It pairs English queries with Hindi candidate passages (and relevance labels) to evaluate embedding-based and dense retrieval models on semantic matching across languages. The dataset is intended for assessing cross-lingual semantic search, bilingual retrieval performance, and zero-shot transfer of sentence/document representations between English and Hindi.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (hin-eng) is a cross-lingual retrieval benchmark pairing Hindi queries with English candidate passages and relevance labels. It is designed to evaluate multilingual sentence and passage embeddings on their ability to retrieve semantically equivalent content across Hindi and English. The dataset provides query-document relevance pairs for ranking evaluation (e.g., MRR, nDCG) and supports development and comparison of models for cross-lingual semantic search and information retrieval.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (ita-ita) is a monolingual Italian question–answer retrieval dataset from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. It pairs Italian queries with candidate answer passages and relevance labels to evaluate embedding-based retrieval performance. The task measures a model’s ability to match questions to correct answers in Italian using standard retrieval metrics (e.g., recall@k, MRR), and is suited for benchmarking semantic search, passage retrieval, and QA retrieval systems in Italian.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (eng-ita) is a cross-lingual question-to-passage retrieval dataset within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) that pairs English queries with relevant Italian passages (and/or vice versa). It is designed to evaluate multilingual embedding and retrieval models on semantic matching across English and Italian in a QA setting, measuring retrieval accuracy (e.g., recall@k, MRR) for question answering scenarios. The dataset is useful for benchmarking zero-shot and fine-tuned multilingual search, cross-lingual semantic similarity, and retrieval-based QA systems.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (ita-eng) is a bilingual cross-lingual retrieval benchmark in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that pairs Italian queries with English candidate passages annotated for relevance. It is designed to evaluate multilingual sentence/document embedding models and dense retrieval systems on cross-language question-answer retrieval and semantic search. The dataset is suited for training and benchmarking embedding-based retrieval and reranking approaches, with common evaluation metrics including recall@k, MRR, and nDCG.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (jpn-jpn) is a Japanese monolingual retrieval benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). It provides Japanese questions paired with relevant Japanese passages (positives and negatives) to evaluate embedding-based retrieval in a QA-style setting. The task measures semantic retrieval quality of sentence/document embeddings using metrics such as Recall@k and MRR. It is useful for benchmarking and developing Japanese dense retrieval, semantic search, and QA retrieval models.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (eng-jpn) is a cross-lingual retrieval benchmark within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that evaluates embedding models on English–Japanese question-to-passage retrieval. It contains QA-style queries and candidate passages in English and Japanese (both directions), with labeled relevant passages for each query. The task measures how well dense or sparse embeddings support semantic search and passage retrieval for cross-lingual question answering, using ranking metrics such as recall and MRR to assess performance.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (jpn-eng) is a cross-lingual retrieval benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) that evaluates embedding models on Japanese–English retrieval. It contains query–candidate pairs with relevance labels where queries in one language must retrieve semantically matching texts in the other, focusing on sentence- or passage-level semantic alignment. The dataset is intended to measure multilingual embedding quality for bilingual retrieval and cross-lingual QA scenarios, enabling comparison of models’ ability to retrieve and rank semantically equivalent content across Japanese and English.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (kor-kor) is a Korean monolingual retrieval subset of the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that focuses on question-to-context retrieval. It provides Korean questions paired with relevant passages (answer-containing texts) to evaluate embedding models on ranking and retrieval metrics such as recall and MRR. The dataset is intended for benchmarking and developing Korean-language semantic search, dense retrieval, and question-answer retrieval systems.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (eng-kor) is a cross-lingual retrieval benchmark in the MTEB suite containing English queries paired with Korean passages and relevance annotations. It evaluates embedding models’ ability to match semantically relevant Korean texts to English queries (and vice versa), supporting assessment of multilingual semantic search, ranking, and representation quality using retrieval metrics such as recall and MRR.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (kor-eng) is a cross-lingual retrieval benchmark from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that pairs Korean queries with English candidate passages/answers. It is designed to evaluate multilingual sentence and passage embeddings on the task of retrieving correct English responses given Korean questions (and vice versa). The dataset is used to assess and compare embedding models for cross-lingual information retrieval and open-domain QA via metrics like Recall@K and MRR.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (por-por) is a Portuguese question–answer retrieval dataset within the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark designed to evaluate embedding models’ ability to retrieve relevant answers for Portuguese queries. It contains paired Portuguese queries and candidate answers with relevance annotations to measure semantic retrieval performance (e.g., Recall@K, MRR). The dataset is suited for benchmarking and developing multilingual or language-specific embedding models, retrieval systems, and QA rerankers in Portuguese.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (eng-por) is a cross-lingual retrieval benchmark that pairs English questions with Portuguese candidate passages and relevance annotations. It is designed to evaluate multilingual embedding and dense retrieval models on their ability to match semantically equivalent content across English and Portuguese, supporting tasks like cross-lingual semantic search and QA-context retrieval. The dataset enables benchmarking of embedding alignment, retrieval accuracy, and generalization of models in English–Portuguese retrieval scenarios.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (por-eng) is a cross-lingual retrieval dataset from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that pairs Portuguese queries with English question–answer items. It is designed to evaluate multilingual embedding and retrieval models on their ability to match semantically relevant English QA content given Portuguese queries. The dataset is useful for benchmarking and developing cross-lingual information retrieval, multilingual QA retrieval pipelines, and embedding alignment methods.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (tam-tam) is a retrieval benchmark for evaluating semantic retrieval of answer passages given a question. It comprises question queries paired with a pool of candidate passages drawn from the tam-tam collection, with relevance annotations for supervised evaluation. The dataset is designed to test embedding-based retrievers (dense and sparse) on passage-level QA retrieval, including cross-lingual/multilingual scenarios, and is commonly used to measure metrics such as recall and MRR at multiple cutoffs.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (eng-tam) is a cross-lingual retrieval benchmark focused on English–Tamil question–answer retrieval. It contains English queries and Tamil QA candidates with relevance annotations to evaluate how well embedding models retrieve semantically matching Tamil answers from English queries (and vice versa). The dataset is intended to measure multilingual and cross-lingual dense retrieval performance, robustness of sentence/paragraph embeddings, and effectiveness of models on low-resource language retrieval tasks.

MTEB XPQARetrieval (tam-eng) is a cross-lingual QA retrieval subset of the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark that evaluates retrieval and semantic matching between Tamil and English. It contains QA-style queries and candidate passages with relevance labels across the two languages, enabling benchmarking of multilingual sentence and passage embeddings for cross-language retrieval tasks. The dataset is suited for measuring retrieval performance (e.g., recall@K, MRR) and robustness of models in low-resource and code-switched settings.

HellaSwag is a large-scale commonsense natural language inference dataset designed to evaluate models' ability to understand everyday situations. It consists of multiple-choice questions where models must select the most plausible continuation of a given context.
